tasmātsamastalokānāṃ hitameva mayocyate /
harināmaparānmartyānna kalirbādhartakvacit //
meaning:
तस्मात्समस्तलोकानां हितमेव मयोच्यते /
हरिनामपरान्मर्त्यान्न कलिर्बाधर्तक्वचित् //
text_mt: Therefore only the welfare of all worlds is spoken by me: / Kali never afflicts mortals devoted to the name of Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
harernāmaiva nāmaiva nāmaiva mama jīvanam /
kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā //
meaning:
हरेर्नामैव नामैव नामैव मम जीवनम् /
कलौ नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरन्यथा //
text_mt: Only the name of Hari, only the name, only the name is my life! / In Kali there is no other recourse, none at all, none otherwise.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
evaṃ sa nārado viprāḥ sanakena prabodhitaḥ /
parāṃ nirvṛttimāpannaḥ punaretaduvāca ha //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
एवं स नारदो विप्राः सनकेन प्रबोधितः /
परां निर्वृत्तिमापन्नः पुनरेतदुवाच ह //
text_mt: Sūta said: / Thus enlightened by Sanaka, O brāhmaṇas, Nārada, / having attained supreme serenity, spoke this once more:

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvaśāstrajña svayātikaruṇātmanā /
prakāśitaṃ jagajjyotiḥ paraṃ brahma sanātanam //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वशास्त्रज्ञ स्वयातिकरुणात्मना /
प्रकाशितं जगज्ज्योतिः परं ब्रह्म सनातनम् //
text_mt: Nārada said: / O Lord, knower of all scriptures, by you of very compassionate nature / the light of the universe, the supreme eternal Brahman, has been revealed.

sanskrit_iast:
etadeva paraṃ puṇyametadeva paraṃ tapaḥ /
yaḥ smaretpuṇḍarīkākṣaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam //
meaning:
एतदेव परं पुण्यमेतदेव परं तपः /
यः स्मरेत्पुण्डरीकाक्षं सर्वपापविनाशनम् //
text_mt: This alone is supreme merit, this alone is supreme austerity, / that one remembers the lotus-eyed Lord, the destroyer of all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmannānājagañcaitadekacitsaṃprakāśitam /
tvayoktaṃ tatpratīye 'haṃ kathaṃ dṛṣṭāntamantarā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मन्नानाजगञ्चैतदेकचित्संप्रकाशितम् /
त्वयोक्तं तत्प्रतीये ऽहं कथं दृष्टान्तमन्तरा //
text_mt: O Brahman, that this manifold universe is illuminated by a single consciousness / has been spoken by you; how can I comprehend that without an illustration?

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādyena yathā brahma pratītaṃ bodhitena tu /
tadākhyāhi yathā cittaṃ sīdatsthitimavāpnuyāt //
meaning:
तस्माद्येन यथा ब्रह्म प्रतीतं बोधितेन तु /
तदाख्याहि यथा चित्तं सीदत्स्थितिमवाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: Therefore tell me how and by what [means] Brahman is comprehended by one instructed, / so that my faltering mind may attain stability.

sanskrit_iast:
etacchrutvā vaco viprā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ /
sanakaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ smarannārāyaṇaṃ param //
meaning:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो विप्रा नारदस्य महात्मनः /
सनकः प्रत्युवाचेदं स्मरन्नारायणं परम् //
text_mt: Having heard this speech of the great-souled Nārada, O brāhmaṇas, / Sanaka replied this, remembering the supreme Nārāyaṇa:

sanskrit_iast:
sanaka uvāca
brahmannahaṃ dhyānaparo bhaveyaṃ sanandanaṃ pṛccha yathābhilāṣam /
vedāntaśāstre kuśalastavāyaṃ nivartayedvā paramāryavandyaḥ //
meaning:
सनक उवाच
ब्रह्मन्नहं ध्यानपरो भवेयं सनन्दनं पृच्छ यथाभिलाषम् /
वेदान्तशास्त्रे कुशलस्तवायं निवर्तयेद्वा परमार्यवन्द्यः //
text_mt: Sanaka said: / O brāhmaṇa, I am intent upon meditation; ask Sanandana according to your wish. / Skilled in the Vedānta scripture, worthy of worship by the foremost noble ones, he will resolve [your doubt].

sanskrit_iast:
itīritaṃ samākarṇya sanakasya sa nāradaḥ /
sanandanaṃ mokṣadharmānpraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde nāmamahātmyannāmaikacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
इतीरितं समाकर्ण्य सनकस्य स नारदः /
सनन्दनं मोक्षधर्मान्प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे नाममहात्म्यन्नामैकचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Hearing this spoken by Sanaka, Nārada / proceeded to ask Sanandana about the principles of liberation.

Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named 'The Eulogy of Greatness of the Name', in the first quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīnārada uvāca
kutaḥ sṛṣṭamidaṃ brahmañjagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
pralaye ca kamabhyeti tanme brūhi sanandana //
meaning:
श्रीनारद उवाच
कुतः सृष्टमिदं ब्रह्मञ्जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् /
प्रलये च कमभ्येति तन्मे ब्रूहि सनन्दन //
text_mt: Glorious Nārada said: / Whence was this world of moving and unmoving beings created, O brāhmaṇa, / and to whom does it go in the cosmic dissolution? Tell me that, O Sanandana!

sanskrit_iast:
sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ sabalāhakaḥ /
sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavano loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ //
meaning:
ससागरः सगगनः सशैलः सबलाहकः /
सभूमिः साग्निपवनो लोको ऽयं केन निर्मितः //
text_mt: Together with oceans, skies, mountains, and clouds, / together with earth, fire, and wind, by whom was this world fashioned?

sanskrit_iast:
kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ /
śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmavidhiḥ katham //
meaning:
कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः /
शौचाशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मविधिः कथम् //
text_mt: How were the beings created? How the divisions of class? / What of their purity and impurity? How the rules of righteousness and unrighteousness?

sanskrit_iast:
kīdṛśo jīvatāṃ jīvaḥ kva vā gacchanti ye mṛtāḥ /
asmāllokādamuṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ śaṃsatu me bhavān //
meaning:
कीदृशो जीवतां जीवः क्व वा गच्छन्ति ये मृताः /
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं सर्वं शंसतु मे भवान् //
text_mt: What is the individual soul of living beings? Where do they go who die / from this world to the world beyond? Explain everything to me!

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi cetihāsaṃ purātanam /
bhṛguṇābhihitaṃ śāstraṃ bharadvājāya pṛcchate //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि चेतिहासं पुरातनम् /
भृगुणाभिहितं शास्त्रं भरद्वाजाय पृच्छते //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / Listen, Nārada, I shall tell an ancient history / of the teaching proclaimed by Bhṛgu to Bharadvāja when he inquired.

sanskrit_iast:
kailāsaśikhare dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānaṃ mahaujasam /
bhṛgumaharṣimāsīnaṃ bharadvājo 'nvapṛcchata //
meaning:
कैलासशिखरे दृष्ट्वा दीप्यमानं महौजसम् /
भृगुमहर्षिमासीनं भरद्वाजो ऽन्वपृच्छत //
text_mt: Having seen the great sage Bhṛgu, radiant and of great splendor, / seated upon the peak of Kailāsa, Bharadvāja questioned him:

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
kathaṃ jīvo vicarati nānāyoniṣu saṃtatam /
kathaṃ muktiśca saṃsārājjāyate tasya mānada //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
कथं जीवो विचरति नानायोनिषु संततम् /
कथं मुक्तिश्च संसाराज्जायते तस्य मानद //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / How does the individual soul wander continuously in various wombs? / And how does liberation from saṃsāra arise for it, O honor-giver?

sanskrit_iast:
yaśca nārāyaṇaḥ sraṣṭā svayaṃbhūrbhagavansvayam /
sevyasevakabhāvena vartete iti tau sadā //
meaning:
यश्च नारायणः स्रष्टा स्वयंभूर्भगवन्स्वयम् /
सेव्यसेवकभावेन वर्तेते इति तौ सदा //
text_mt: And the creator Nārāyaṇa, the self-born Lord himself— / do the two always exist in the relation of worshipped and worshipper?

sanskrit_iast:
praviśanti laye sarve yamīśaṃ sacarācarāḥ /
lokānāṃ ramaṇaḥ so 'yaṃ nirguṇaśca nirañjanaḥ //
meaning:
प्रविशन्ति लये सर्वे यमीशं सचराचराः /
लोकानां रमणः सो ऽयं निर्गुणश्च निरञ्जनः //
text_mt: The Lord into whom all moving and unmoving beings enter at the dissolution, / he is the delight of the worlds, devoid of qualities and taintless.

sanskrit_iast:
anīrdaśyo 'pratarkyaśca kathaṃ jñāyeta kairmune /
kathamenaṃ parātmānaṃ kālaśaktiduranvayam //
meaning:
अनीर्दश्यो ऽप्रतर्क्यश्च कथं ज्ञायेत कैर्मुने /
कथमेनं परात्मानं कालशक्तिदुरन्वयम् //
text_mt: Indescribable and unthinkable—how can he be known, and by whom, O sage? / How [can one know] this supreme Self, whose power of time is difficult to follow?

sanskrit_iast:
atarkyacaritaṃ vedāḥ stuvanti kathamādarāt /
jīvo jīvatvamullaṅghya kathaṃ brahma samanvayāt //
meaning:
अतर्क्यचरितं वेदाः स्तुवन्ति कथमादरात् /
जीवो जीवत्वमुल्लङ्घ्य कथं ब्रह्म समन्वयात् //
text_mt: How do the Vedas devoutly praise him whose conduct is beyond thought? / Transcending individuality, how does the individual soul attain Brahman?

sanskrit_iast:
etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tanme brūhi kṛpānirgha /
evaṃ sa bhagavānpṛṣṭo bharadvājena saṃśayam //
meaning:
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि कृपानिर्घ /
एवं स भगवान्पृष्टो भरद्वाजेन संशयम् //
text_mt: I wish to hear this; tell it to me, O compassionate, sinless one! / When the Lord was thus asked about his doubt by Bharadvāja,

sanskrit_iast:
maharṣirbrahmasaṃkāśaḥ sarvaṃ tasmai tato 'bravīt /
bhṛguruvāca
mānaso nāma yaḥ pūrvo viśruto ve maharṣibhiḥ //
meaning:
महर्षिर्ब्रह्मसंकाशः सर्वं तस्मै ततो ऽब्रवीत् /
भृगुरुवाच
मानसो नाम यः पूर्वो विश्रुतो वे महर्षिभिः //
text_mt: the great sage, resembling Brahmā, then told him everything. / Bhṛgu said: / He who was called 'the Mind-born' first, celebrated among the great sages,

sanskrit_iast:
anādinidhano devastathā tebhyo 'jarāmaraḥ /
avyakta iti vikhyātaḥ śāśvato 'thākṣayo 'vyayaḥ //
meaning:
अनादिनिधनो देवस्तथा तेभ्यो ऽजरामरः /
अव्यक्त इति विख्यातः शाश्वतो ऽथाक्षयो ऽव्ययः //
text_mt: is the God without beginning or end, and unaging and immortal to them, / renowned as the unmanifest, eternal, imperishable, and immutable.

sanskrit_iast:
yataḥ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni jāyante ca mriyanti ca /
so 'mṛjatprathamaṃ devo mahāntaṃ nāma nāmataḥ //
meaning:
यतः सृष्टानि भूतानि जायन्ते च म्रियन्ति च /
सो ऽमृजत्प्रथमं देवो महान्तं नाम नामतः //
text_mt: From whom created beings are born and die, / that God first created that known by the name of Mahat.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśamiti vikhyātaṃ sarvabhūtadharaḥ prabhuḥ /
ākāśādabhavadvāri salilādagnimārutau //
meaning:
आकाशमिति विख्यातं सर्वभूतधरः प्रभुः /
आकाशादभवद्वारि सलिलादग्निमारुतौ //
text_mt: The Lord, bearer of all beings, [created] that renowned as space; / from space water arose, and from water fire and wind;

sanskrit_iast:
agnimārutasaṃyogāttataḥ samabhavanmahī /
tatastejo mayaṃ divyaṃ padmaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā //
meaning:
अग्निमारुतसंयोगात्ततः समभवन्मही /
ततस्तेजो मयं दिव्यं पद्मं सृष्टं स्वयंभुवा //
text_mt: from the conjunction of fire and wind the earth then arose. / Then a divine lotus consisting of light was created by the self-born [Lord].

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātpadmātsamabhavadvrahmā vedamayo vidhiḥ /
ahṝṅkāra iti khyātaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtakṛt //
meaning:
तस्मात्पद्मात्समभवद्व्रह्मा वेदमयो विधिः /
अहॄङ्कार इति ख्यातः सर्वभूतात्मभूतकृत् //
text_mt: From that lotus arose Brahmā, the creator consisting of the Vedas, / known as the ego-sense, the maker of the beings who constitute all elements.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmā vai sa mahātejā ya ete pañca dhātavaḥ /
śailāstasyāsthisaṃdhāstu medo masiṃ ca medinī //
meaning:
ब्रह्मा वै स महातेजा य एते पञ्च धातवः /
शैलास्तस्यास्थिसंधास्तु मेदो मसिं च मेदिनी //
text_mt: Brahmā indeed is of great splendor, from whom are these five elements: / the mountains are his bone-joints; the earth is his fat and flesh;

sanskrit_iast:
samudrāstasya rudhiramākāśamudaraṃ tathā /
pavanaścaiva niśvāsastejo 'gnirnimnagāḥ śirāḥ //
meaning:
समुद्रास्तस्य रुधिरमाकाशमुदरं तथा /
पवनश्चैव निश्वासस्तेजो ऽग्निर्निम्नगाः शिराः //
text_mt: the oceans are his blood, and space is his belly; / the wind is his breath; fire is his energy; the rivers are his veins;

sanskrit_iast:
agnīṣomau ca candrākārai nayane tasya viśrute /
nabhaścordhvaśirastasya kṣitiḥ padau bhujau diśaḥ //
meaning:
अग्नीषोमौ च चन्द्राकारै नयने तस्य विश्रुते /
नभश्चोर्ध्वशिरस्तस्य क्षितिः पदौ भुजौ दिशः //
text_mt: Agni and Soma, the sun and the moon, are renowned as his eyes; / the sky is his head above, the earth his feet, and the directions his arms.

sanskrit_iast:
durvijñeyo hyacintyātmā siddhairapi na saṃśayaḥ /
sa eṣa bhagavānviṣṇurananta iti viśrutaḥ //
meaning:
दुर्विज्ञेयो ह्यचिन्त्यात्मा सिद्धैरपि न संशयः /
स एष भगवान्विष्णुरनन्त इति विश्रुतः //
text_mt: He is difficult to know and unthinkable in nature, even by perfected beings, without doubt. / This is the Lord Viṣṇu, celebrated as Ananta,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtātmabhūtastho durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ /
ahṝṅkārasya yaḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtabhaghavāyavai /
tataḥ samabhavadviśvaṃ pṛṣṭo 'haṃ yadiha tvayā //
meaning:
सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थो दुर्विज्ञेयो ऽकृतात्मभिः /
अहॄङ्कारस्य यः स्रष्टा सर्वभूतभघवायवै /
ततः समभवद्विश्वं पृष्टो ऽहं यदिह त्वया //
text_mt: dwelling in all beings as their inner self, difficult to know by the undisciplined. / He who is the creator of the ego-sense, the Lord of all beings, / from him the universe arose, concerning which I was asked here by you.

sanskrit_iast:
bhagdvāja uvāca
gaganasya diśāṃ caiva bhūtalasvānilasya ca /
kānyatra parimāṇāni saṃśayaṃ chindhi tattvataḥ //
meaning:
भग्द्वाज उवाच
गगनस्य दिशां चैव भूतलस्वानिलस्य च /
कान्यत्र परिमाणानि संशयं छिन्धि तत्त्वतः //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / Of the sky and the directions, of the surface of the earth and the wind, / what are the measurements here? Sever my doubt according to truth!

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
anantametadākāśaṃ siddhadaivatasovitam /
ramyaṃ nānāśrayākīrṇaṃ yasyāṃ to nādhigamyate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
अनन्तमेतदाकाशं सिद्धदैवतसोवितम् /
रम्यं नानाश्रयाकीर्णं यस्यां तो नाधिगम्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / Infinite is this space, frequented by perfected beings and gods, / delightful, filled with various abodes, whose end is not reached.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrdhvaṃ gateradhastāttu candrādityau na paśyataḥ /
tatra devāḥ svayaṃ dīptā bhāskarābhāgnivarcasaḥ //
meaning:
ऊर्ध्वं गतेरधस्तात्तु चन्द्रादित्यौ न पश्यतः /
तत्र देवाः स्वयं दीप्ता भास्कराभाग्निवर्चसः //
text_mt: Above the reach of their course, the sun and moon do not behold down below; / there the gods shine by themselves, possessing the splendor of the sun and fire.

sanskrit_iast:
te cāpyantaṃ na paśyanti nabhasaḥ prathitaujasaḥ /
durgamatvādanantatvāditi me vada mānada //
meaning:
ते चाप्यन्तं न पश्यन्ति नभसः प्रथितौजसः /
दुर्गमत्वादनन्तत्वादिति मे वद मानद //
text_mt: And they too, though celebrated in splendor, do not see the end of the sky, / because of its impassability and infinitude—tell me this, O honor-giver!

sanskrit_iast:
upariṣṭopariṣṭāttu pjvaladbhiḥ svayaṃprabhaghaiḥ /
niruddhametadākāśaṃ hyaprameyaṃ surairapi //
meaning:
उपरिष्टोपरिष्टात्तु प्ज्वलद्भिः स्वयंप्रभघैः /
निरुद्धमेतदाकाशं ह्यप्रमेयं सुरैरपि //
text_mt: Above and still above, it is occupied by blazing [deities] shining by themselves; / this space is indeed immeasurable even by the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
prathivyante samudrāstu samudrānte tamaḥ smṛtam /
tamasoṃ'te jalaṃ prāhurjalasyānte 'gnireva ca //
meaning:
प्रथिव्यन्ते समुद्रास्तु समुद्रान्ते तमः स्मृतम् /
तमसोंऽते जलं प्राहुर्जलस्यान्ते ऽग्निरेव च //
text_mt: At the end of the earth are the oceans, and at the end of the oceans darkness is recorded; / at the end of darkness they speak of water, and at the end of water, fire indeed.

sanskrit_iast:
rasātalānte salilaṃ jalānte pannagādhipāḥ /
tadante punarākāśamākāśānte punarjalam //
meaning:
रसातलान्ते सलिलं जलान्ते पन्नगाधिपाः /
तदन्ते पुनराकाशमाकाशान्ते पुनर्जलम् //
text_mt: At the end of Rasātala is water, and at the end of the water are the serpent lords; / at their end is space once more, and at the end of space is water again.

sanskrit_iast:
evamantaṃ bhagavataḥ pramāṇaṃ salilasya ca /
agnimārutatoyebhyo durjñeyaṃ daivatairapi //
meaning:
एवमन्तं भगवतः प्रमाणं सलिलस्य च /
अग्निमारुततोयेभ्यो दुर्ज्ञेयं दैवतैरपि //
text_mt: In this way the limit and the measure of the blessed lord and of water / are difficult to comprehend even for the gods, because of fire, wind, and water.

sanskrit_iast:
agnimārutatoyānāṃ varṇā kṣititalasya ca /
ākāśasadṛśā hyete bhidyante tattvadaśanāt //
meaning:
अग्निमारुततोयानां वर्णा क्षितितलस्य च /
आकाशसदृशा ह्येते भिद्यन्ते तत्त्वदशनात् //
text_mt: The colors of fire, wind, water, / and of the surface of the earth resemble space, but they are distinguished by perceiving truth.

sanskrit_iast:
paṭhanti caiva munayaḥ śāstreṣu vividheṣu ca /
trailokye sāgare caiva pramāṇaṃ vihitaṃ yathā //
meaning:
पठन्ति चैव मुनयः शास्त्रेषु विविधेषु च /
त्रैलोक्ये सागरे चैव प्रमाणं विहितं यथा //
text_mt: Sages also recite in various treatises / the measure that has been laid down for the three worlds and for the ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
adṛśyo yastvagamyo yaḥ kaḥ pramāṇa mudīrayet /
siddhānāṃ devatānāṃ ca parimītā yadā gatiḥ //
meaning:
अदृश्यो यस्त्वगम्यो यः कः प्रमाण मुदीरयेत् /
सिद्धानां देवतानां च परिमीता यदा गतिः //
text_mt: Who can declare the measure of that which is invisible and inaccessible, / when the reach of the perfected beings and the deities is limited?

sanskrit_iast:
tadāgaṇyamanantasya nāmānanteti viśrutam /
nāmadheyānurupasya mānasasya mahātmanaḥ //
meaning:
तदागण्यमनन्तस्य नामानन्तेति विश्रुतम् /
नामधेयानुरुपस्य मानसस्य महात्मनः //
text_mt: Therefore, the name of the immeasurable, boundless one is famed as Ananta, / appropriate to the name of the great-souled mind-born lord.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā tu divyaṃ yadrūpaṃ hrasate varddhate punaḥ /
ko 'nyastadvedituṃ śakyo yo 'pi syāttadvidho 'paraḥ //
meaning:
यदा तु दिव्यं यद्रूपं ह्रसते वर्द्धते पुनः /
को ऽन्यस्तद्वेदितुं शक्यो यो ऽपि स्यात्तद्विधो ऽपरः //
text_mt: When his divine form diminishes and then expands again, / who else could know that, even if another were similar to him?

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ puṣkarataḥ saṣṭaḥ sarvajño mūrtimānprabhuḥ /
brahmā dharmamayaḥ pūrvaḥ prajāpatiranuttamaḥ //
meaning:
ततः पुष्करतः सष्टः सर्वज्ञो मूर्तिमान्प्रभुः /
ब्रह्मा धर्ममयः पूर्वः प्रजापतिरनुत्तमः //
text_mt: Then from the lotus the omniscient, embodied Lord was created— / Brahmā, full of righteousness, the first, unsurpassed lord of creatures.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
puṣkaro yadi saṃbhūto jyeṣṭaṃ bhavati puṣkaram /
brahmāṇaṃ pūrvajaṃ cāha bhavānsaṃdeha eva me //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
पुष्करो यदि संभूतो ज्येष्टं भवति पुष्करम् /
ब्रह्माणं पूर्वजं चाह भवान्संदेह एव मे //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / If the lotus was created, the lotus must be the eldest, / and you say that Brahmā is the first-born; herein lies my doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
mānasasyeha yā mūrtirbrahmatvaṃ samupāgatā /
tasyāsanavidhānārthaṃ pṛthivī padmamucyate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
मानसस्येह या मूर्तिर्ब्रह्मत्वं समुपागता /
तस्यासनविधानार्थं पृथिवी पद्ममुच्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / That form of the mind-born lord which attained the status of Brahmā here— / the earth is called the lotus to serve as a seat for him.

sanskrit_iast:
karṇikā tasya padmasya merurgaganamucchritaḥ /
tasya madhye sthito lokānsṛjatyeṣa jagadvidhiḥ //
meaning:
कर्णिका तस्य पद्मस्य मेरुर्गगनमुच्छ्रितः /
तस्य मध्ये स्थितो लोकान्सृजत्येष जगद्विधिः //
text_mt: The pericarp of that lotus is Meru, elevated into the sky; / standing in its center, this ordainer of the universe creates the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ kathaṃ sa sṛjati prabhuḥ /
merumadhye sthito brahmā tadvahirdvijasattama //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
प्रजाविसर्गं विविधं कथं स सृजति प्रभुः /
मेरुमध्ये स्थितो ब्रह्मा तद्वहिर्द्विजसत्तम //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / How does that Lord, standing in the center of Meru, / create the diverse emission of creatures outside it, O best of the twice-born?

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ mānaso manasāsṛjat /
saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
प्रजाविसर्गं विविधं मानसो मनसासृजत् /
संरक्षणार्थं भूतानां सृष्टं प्रथमतो जलम् //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / The mind-born lord created the diverse emission of creatures with his mind. / First water was created for the protection of all beings,

sanskrit_iast:
yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam /
yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ varddhante yena ca prajāḥ //
meaning:
यत्प्राणाः सर्वभूतानां सृष्टं प्रथमतो जलम् /
यत्प्राणाः सर्वभूतानां वर्द्धन्ते येन च प्रजाः //
text_mt: water was created first, which is the breath of life of all beings, / and by which creatures thrive.

sanskrit_iast:
parityaktāśca na śyanti tenadaṃ sarvamāvṛttam /
pṛthivī parvatā meghā mūrtimantaśca ye pare /
sarvaṃ tadvāruṇaṃ jñeyamāpastastaṃbhire punaḥ //
meaning:
परित्यक्ताश्च न श्यन्ति तेनदं सर्वमावृत्तम् /
पृथिवी पर्वता मेघा मूर्तिमन्तश्च ये परे /
सर्वं तद्वारुणं ज्ञेयमापस्तस्तंभिरे पुनः //
text_mt: Abandoned by it, they perish; by it all this is pervaded. / The earth, mountains, clouds, and whatever other embodied forms exist— / all that is to be known as watery; the waters then solidified.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
kathaṃ salilamutpannaṃ kathaṃ caivāgnimārutau /
kathaṃ vā medinī sṛṣṭetyatra me saṃśayo mahān //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
कथं सलिलमुत्पन्नं कथं चैवाग्निमारुतौ /
कथं वा मेदिनी सृष्टेत्यत्र मे संशयो महान् //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / How was water produced, and how were fire and wind? / And how was the earth created? In this I have great doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
brahmakalpe purā brahman brahmarṣīṇāṃ samāgame /
lokasaṃbhavasaṃdehaḥ samutpanno mahātmanām //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
ब्रह्मकल्पे पुरा ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मर्षीणां समागमे /
लोकसंभवसंदेहः समुत्पन्नो महात्मनाम् //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / In a former Brahma-kalpa, O brahmin, at an assembly of brahmin seers, / a doubt concerning the origin of the world arose among those great-souled ones.

sanskrit_iast:
te 'tiṣṭandhyānamālaṃbya maunamāsthāya niścalāḥ /
tyaktāhārāḥ sparddhamānā divyaṃ virṣaśataṃ dvijāḥ //
meaning:
ते ऽतिष्टन्ध्यानमालंब्य मौनमास्थाय निश्चलाः /
त्यक्ताहाराः स्पर्द्धमाना दिव्यं विर्षशतं द्विजाः //
text_mt: Resorting to meditation, observing silence, motionless, / abandoning food, and striving eagerly, those twice-born stayed for a hundred divine years.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ brahmamayī vāṇī sarveṣāṃ śrotramāgamat /
divyā sarasvatī tatra saṃbabhūva nabhastalāt //
meaning:
तेषां ब्रह्ममयी वाणी सर्वेषां श्रोत्रमागमत् /
दिव्या सरस्वती तत्र संबभूव नभस्तलात् //
text_mt: A voice consisting of Brahman reached the ears of all of them; / the divine Sarasvatī appeared there from the vault of heaven:

sanskrit_iast:
purāstimitamākāśamanantamacalopamam /
naṣṭacandrārkapavanaṃ prasuptamiva saṃbabhau //
meaning:
पुरास्तिमितमाकाशमनन्तमचलोपमम् /
नष्टचन्द्रार्कपवनं प्रसुप्तमिव संबभौ //
text_mt: ‘Formerly, space was motionless, boundless, like a mountain; / bereft of moon, sun, and wind, it appeared as though asleep.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ salilamutpannaṃ tamasīva tamaḥ param /
tasmāñca salilotpīḍādudatiṣṭata mārutaḥ //
meaning:
ततः सलिलमुत्पन्नं तमसीव तमः परम् /
तस्माञ्च सलिलोत्पीडादुदतिष्टत मारुतः //
text_mt: Then water arose, like supreme darkness within darkness; / and from that compression of water, wind arose.

sanskrit_iast:
yathābhavanamacchidraṃ niḥśabdamiva lakṣyate /
tañcābhasā pūryamāṇaṃ saśabdaṃ kurute 'nilaḥ //
meaning:
यथाभवनमच्छिद्रं निःशब्दमिव लक्ष्यते /
तञ्चाभसा पूर्यमाणं सशब्दं कुरुते ऽनिलः //
text_mt: Just as a hollow space without an opening appears to be silent, / but when being filled with water, the wind makes a sound,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā salilasaṃruddhe nabhasoṃ'taṃ nirantare /
bhittvārṇavatalaṃ vāyuḥ samutpatati ghoṣavān //
meaning:
तथा सलिलसंरुद्धे नभसोंऽतं निरन्तरे /
भित्त्वार्णवतलं वायुः समुत्पतति घोषवान् //
text_mt: so, when the interior of space was enclosed by water without gap, / the wind, bursting through the floor of the ocean, rose up roaring.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣu vā carate vāyurarṇavotpīḍasaṃbhavaḥ /
ākāśasthānamāsādya praśāntiṃ nādhigacchati //
meaning:
एषु वा चरते वायुरर्णवोत्पीडसंभवः /
आकाशस्थानमासाद्य प्रशान्तिं नाधिगच्छति //
text_mt: This wind, born from the pressure of the ocean, moves about; / having reached the realm of space, it finds no rest.

sanskrit_iast:
tasminvāyvambusaṃgharṣe dīptatejā mahābalaḥ /
prādurāsīdūrdhvaśikhaḥ kṛtvā nistimiraṃ tamaḥ //
meaning:
तस्मिन्वाय्वम्बुसंघर्षे दीप्ततेजा महाबलः /
प्रादुरासीदूर्ध्वशिखः कृत्वा निस्तिमिरं तमः //
text_mt: In that friction between wind and water, [fire] of blazing brilliance and great power / appeared with upward flames, dispelling the gloom of darkness.

sanskrit_iast:
agniḥ pavanasaṃyuktaḥ khaṃ samākṣipate jalam /
tadagnivāyusaṃparkāddhanatvamupapadyate //
meaning:
अग्निः पवनसंयुक्तः खं समाक्षिपते जलम् /
तदग्निवायुसंपर्काद्धनत्वमुपपद्यते //
text_mt: Fire, combined with wind, hurled water into the sky; / through contact with fire and wind, it attained solidity.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyākāśaṃ nipatitaḥ snehāttiṣṭati yo 'paraḥ /
sa saṃghātatvamāpanno bhūmitvamanugacchati //
meaning:
तस्याकाशं निपतितः स्नेहात्तिष्टति यो ऽपरः /
स संघातत्वमापन्नो भूमित्वमनुगच्छति //
text_mt: That which fell from the sky and remained other[wise] through moisture, / having attained compactness, developed into the condition of earth.

sanskrit_iast:
rasānāṃ sarvagandhānāṃ snehānāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā /
bhūmiryo niriyaṃ jñeyā yasyāḥ sarvaṃ prasūyate //
meaning:
रसानां सर्वगन्धानां स्नेहानां प्राणिनां तथा /
भूमिर्यो निरियं ज्ञेया यस्याः सर्वं प्रसूयते //
text_mt: The earth is to be known as the womb of tastes, of all fragrances, / of moistures, and likewise of living beings; from it everything is brought forth.’

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
ya ete dhātavaḥ pañca rakṣyā yānasṛjatprabhuḥ /
āvṛtā yairime lokā mahābhūtābhisaṃjñitaiḥ //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
य एते धातवः पञ्च रक्ष्या यानसृजत्प्रभुः /
आवृता यैरिमे लोका महाभूताभिसंज्ञितैः //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / These five elements to be protected which the Lord created, / by which these worlds are enveloped, designated as the great elements—

sanskrit_iast:
yadāsṛjatsahasrāṇi bhūtānāṃ sa mahāmatiḥ /
paścātteṣveva bhūtatvaṃ kathaṃ samupapadyate //
meaning:
यदासृजत्सहस्राणि भूतानां स महामतिः /
पश्चात्तेष्वेव भूतत्वं कथं समुपपद्यते //
text_mt: when that wise one created thousands of beings, / how thereafter does the nature of elements apply to them?

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
amitāni mahāṣṭāni yānti bhūtāni saṃbhavam /
atasteṣāṃ mahābhūtaśabdo 'yamupapadyate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
अमितानि महाष्टानि यान्ति भूतानि संभवम् /
अतस्तेषां महाभूतशब्दो ऽयमुपपद्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / Countless beings of great magnitude come into existence; / therefore, the term ‘great element’ (mahābhūta) applies to them.

sanskrit_iast:
ceṣṭā vāyuḥ khamākāśamūṣmāgniḥ salilaṃ dravaḥ /
pṛthivī cātra saṃghātaḥ śarīraṃ pāñcabhautikam //
meaning:
चेष्टा वायुः खमाकाशमूष्माग्निः सलिलं द्रवः /
पृथिवी चात्र संघातः शरीरं पाञ्चभौतिकम् //
text_mt: Movement is wind, space is void, heat is fire, fluid is water, / and earth is the solid mass here; the body consists of the five elements.

sanskrit_iast:
ityataḥ pañcabhiryuktairyuktaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam /
śrotre ghrāṇo rasaḥ sparśo dṛṣṭiścendriyasaṃjñitāḥ //
meaning:
इत्यतः पञ्चभिर्युक्तैर्युक्तं स्थावरजङ्गमम् /
श्रोत्रे घ्राणो रसः स्पर्शो दृष्टिश्चेन्द्रियसंज्ञिताः //
text_mt: Thus, the stationary and the moving are endowed with the five elements; / the ear, nose, taste, touch, and sight are designated as the sense faculties.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
pañcabhiryadi bhūtaistu yuktāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ /
sthāvarāṇāṃ na dṛśyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
पञ्चभिर्यदि भूतैस्तु युक्ताः स्थावरजङ्गमाः /
स्थावराणां न दृश्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / If stationary and moving beings are endowed with the five elements, / the five elements are not perceived in the body of stationary beings.

sanskrit_iast:
anūṣmaṇāmaceṣṭānāṃ ghanānāṃ caiva tattvataḥ /
vṛkṣāṇāṃ nopalabhyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
meaning:
अनूष्मणामचेष्टानां घनानां चैव तत्त्वतः /
वृक्षाणां नोपलभ्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः //
text_mt: Since they lack heat and motion, and are completely solid, / the five elements are not observed in the bodies of trees.

sanskrit_iast:
va śṛṇvanti na paśyanti na gandharasavedinaḥ /
na ca sparśaṃ hi jānanti te kathaṃ pañca dhātavaḥ //
meaning:
व शृण्वन्ति न पश्यन्ति न गन्धरसवेदिनः /
न च स्पर्शं हि जानन्ति ते कथं पञ्च धातवः //
text_mt: They do not hear, they do not see, nor do they perceive smell or taste; / nor indeed do they feel touch. How can they consist of the five elements?

sanskrit_iast:
adravatvādanignitvādabhūmitvādavāyutaḥ /
ākāśasyāprameyatvādṛkṣāṇāṃ nāsti bhautikam //
meaning:
अद्रवत्वादनिग्नित्वादभूमित्वादवायुतः /
आकाशस्याप्रमेयत्वादृक्षाणां नास्ति भौतिकम् //
text_mt: Because they lack liquidity, fire, earth, and wind, / and because space cannot be grasped, trees have no elemental nature.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
ghanānāmapi vṛkṣaṇāmākāśo 'sti na saṃśayaḥ /
teṣāṃ puṣpapalavyaktirnityaṃ samupapadyate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
घनानामपि वृक्षणामाकाशो ऽस्ति न संशयः /
तेषां पुष्पपलव्यक्तिर्नित्यं समुपपद्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / Even in dense trees there is space, without doubt; / the emergence of their flowers and fruits occurs perpetually.

sanskrit_iast:
ūṣmato mlāyate parṇaṃ tvakphalaṃ puṣpameva ca /
mlāyate śīryate cāpi sparśastenātra vidyate //
meaning:
ऊष्मतो म्लायते पर्णं त्वक्फलं पुष्पमेव च /
म्लायते शीर्यते चापि स्पर्शस्तेनात्र विद्यते //
text_mt: Leaf, bark, fruit, and flower wither from heat; / they wither and fall, and therefore touch exists in them.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyyagnyaśaninirdhoṣaiḥ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ viśīryate /
śrotreṇa gṛhyate śabdastasmācchṛṇvanti pādapāḥ //
meaning:
वाय्यग्न्यशनिनिर्धोषैः फलं पुष्पं विशीर्यते /
श्रोत्रेण गृह्यते शब्दस्तस्माच्छृण्वन्ति पादपाः //
text_mt: By the sounds of wind, fire, and thunder, fruit and flower fall; / sound is grasped by the ear, therefore trees hear.

sanskrit_iast:
vallī veṣṭayate vṛkṣānsarvataścaiva gacchati /
nahyadṛṣṭaśca mārgo 'sti tasmātpaśyanti pādapāḥ //
meaning:
वल्ली वेष्टयते वृक्षान्सर्वतश्चैव गच्छति /
नह्यदृष्टश्च मार्गो ऽस्ति तस्मात्पश्यन्ति पादपाः //
text_mt: A creeper twines around trees and moves in every direction; / and there is no path without sight, therefore trees see.

sanskrit_iast:
puṇyāpuṇyaistathā gadhairdhūpaiśca vividhairapi /
arogāḥ puṣpitāḥ saṃti tasmājjighranti pādapāḥ //
meaning:
पुण्यापुण्यैस्तथा गधैर्धूपैश्च विविधैरपि /
अरोगाः पुष्पिताः संति तस्माज्जिघ्रन्ति पादपाः //
text_mt: By pleasant and unpleasant fragrances, as well as various incenses, / they become free of disease and bloom; therefore trees smell.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaduḥkhayorgrahaṇācchinnasya ca virohaṇāt /
jīvaṃ paśyāmi vṛkṣāṇāmacaitanyaṃ na vidyate //
meaning:
सुखदुःखयोर्ग्रहणाच्छिन्नस्य च विरोहणात् /
जीवं पश्यामि वृक्षाणामचैतन्यं न विद्यते //
text_mt: From their apprehension of pleasure and pain, and from the healing of what is cut, / I see life in trees; they are not devoid of consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
tena tajjalamādatte jarayatyagnimārutau /
āhārapariṇāmāñca snaho vṛddhiśca jāyate //
meaning:
तेन तज्जलमादत्ते जरयत्यग्निमारुतौ /
आहारपरिणामाञ्च स्नहो वृद्धिश्च जायते //
text_mt: Thereby it drinks that water, and digests it through fire and wind; / and from the digestion of food, moisture and growth are produced.

sanskrit_iast:
jaṅgamānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śarīre paṃñca dhātavaḥ /
pratyekaśaḥ prabhidyante yaiḥ śarīraṃ viceṣṭate //
meaning:
जङ्गमानां च सर्वेषां शरीरे पंञ्च धातवः /
प्रत्येकशः प्रभिद्यन्ते यैः शरीरं विचेष्टते //
text_mt: And in the bodies of all moving beings the five elements / are individually differentiated, by means of which the body moves.

sanskrit_iast:
tvak ca māṃsaṃ tathāsthīni majjā snāyuśca pañcamaḥ /
ityetadiha saṃghātaṃ śarīre pṛthivīmaye //
meaning:
त्वक् च मांसं तथास्थीनि मज्जा स्नायुश्च पञ्चमः /
इत्येतदिह संघातं शरीरे पृथिवीमये //
text_mt: Skin, flesh, bones, marrow, and sinew as the fifth— / such is the aggregate here in the body made of earth.

sanskrit_iast:
tejo hyagnistathā krodhaścakṣuruṣmā tathaiva ca /
agnirjanayate yañca pañcāgneyāḥ śarīriṇaḥ //
meaning:
तेजो ह्यग्निस्तथा क्रोधश्चक्षुरुष्मा तथैव च /
अग्निर्जनयते यञ्च पञ्चाग्नेयाः शरीरिणः //
text_mt: Splendour, fire, anger, the eye, and warmth, / and that which fire digests—these five in the embodied soul originate from fire.

sanskrit_iast:
śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ tathāsyaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ koṣṭameva ca /
ākāśātprāṇināmete śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
meaning:
श्रोत्रं घ्राणं तथास्यं च हृदयं कोष्टमेव च /
आकाशात्प्राणिनामेते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः //
text_mt: The ear, the nose, and the mouth, the heart and the internal cavity— / these five elements in the body of living beings arise from space.

sanskrit_iast:
śleṣmā pittamatha svedo vasā śoṇitameva ca /
ityāpaḥ pañcadhā dehe bhavanti prāṇināṃ sadā //
meaning:
श्लेष्मा पित्तमथ स्वेदो वसा शोणितमेव च /
इत्यापः पञ्चधा देहे भवन्ति प्राणिनां सदा //
text_mt: Phlegm, bile, sweat, fat, and blood— / in these five ways water is constantly present in the body of living beings.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇātprīṇayate prāṇī vyānāvdyāyacchate tathā //
meaning: प्राणात्प्रीणयते प्राणी व्यानाव्द्यायच्छते तथा //
text_mt: Through the prāṇa the creature is gratified, and through the vyāna it exerts itself.

sanskrit_iast:
gacchatyapāno 'dhaścaiva samāno hyadyavasthitaḥ /
udānāducchvasitīti pañca (prati)bhadāñca bhāṣate /
ityete vāyavaḥ pañca veṣṭayantīhadehinam //
meaning:
गच्छत्यपानो ऽधश्चैव समानो ह्यद्यवस्थितः /
उदानादुच्छ्वसितीति पञ्च (प्रति)भदाञ्च भाषते /
इत्येते वायवः पञ्च वेष्टयन्तीहदेहिनम् //
text_mt: The apāna moves downward, and the samāna resides within. / Through the udāna it exhales; thus are spoken the five distinctions. / In this way, these five vital airs envelop the embodied soul here.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmergandhaguṇānvetti rasaṃ cādūbhyaḥ śarīravān /
tasya gandhasya vakṣyāmi vistarābhihitānguṇān //
meaning:
भूमेर्गन्धगुणान्वेत्ति रसं चादूभ्यः शरीरवान् /
तस्य गन्धस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तराभिहितान्गुणान् //
text_mt: The embodied soul knows the quality of smell from earth, and taste from water. / I shall explain in detail the declared qualities of that smell:

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭaścānuṣṭagandhaśca madhuraḥ kaṭureva ca /
nirhārī saṃhataḥ snigdho rukṣo viśada eva ca //
meaning:
इष्टश्चानुष्टगन्धश्च मधुरः कटुरेव च /
निर्हारी संहतः स्निग्धो रुक्षो विशद एव च //
text_mt: Pleasant and unpleasant smell, sweet and pungent, / diffusive, compact, oily, dry, and pure.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ navavidho jñeyaḥ pārthivo gandhavistaraḥ /
jyotiḥ paśyati cakṣurbhyaḥ sparśaṃ vetti ca vāyunā //
meaning:
एवं नवविधो ज्ञेयः पार्थिवो गन्धविस्तरः /
ज्योतिः पश्यति चक्षुर्भ्यः स्पर्शं वेत्ति च वायुना //
text_mt: Thus, the extension of earthy smell is known to be ninefold. / One sees fire through the eyes and knows touch by means of air.

sanskrit_iast:
śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca rasaścāpi guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
rasajñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu //
meaning:
शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसश्चापि गुणाः स्मृताः /
रसज्ञानं तु वक्ष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु //
text_mt: Sound, touch, form, and taste are recorded as qualities. / But I shall explain the knowledge of taste; listen to that as I speak.

sanskrit_iast:
raso bahuvidhaḥ prokta ṛṣibhiḥ prathitātmabhiḥ /
madhuro lavaṇastiktaḥ kaṣāyo 'mlaḥ kaṭustathā //
meaning:
रसो बहुविधः प्रोक्त ऋषिभिः प्रथितात्मभिः /
मधुरो लवणस्तिक्तः कषायो ऽम्लः कटुस्तथा //
text_mt: Taste has been declared to be manifold by celebrated sages: / sweet, salty, bitter, astringent, sour, and pungent.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa ṣaḍidhavistāro raso vārimayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaśca triguṇaṃ jyotirucyate //
meaning:
एष षडिधविस्तारो रसो वारिमयः स्मृतः /
शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपश्च त्रिगुणं ज्योतिरुच्यते //
text_mt: This sixfold expansion of taste is recorded as watery. / Fire is said to have three qualities: sound, touch, and form.

sanskrit_iast:
jyotiḥ paśyati rūpāṇi rūpaṃ ca bahudhā smṛtam /
hrasvo dīrdhastathā sthūlaścaturasro 'ṇuvṛttavān //
meaning:
ज्योतिः पश्यति रूपाणि रूपं च बहुधा स्मृतम् /
ह्रस्वो दीर्धस्तथा स्थूलश्चतुरस्रो ऽणुवृत्तवान् //
text_mt: Fire perceives forms, and form is recorded as manifold: / short, long, gross, square, subtle, round,

sanskrit_iast:
śuklaḥ kṛṣṇastathā rakto nīlaḥ pīto 'ruṇastathā /
kaṭhinaścikkaṇaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ picchilo mṛdu dāruṇaḥ //
meaning:
शुक्लः कृष्णस्तथा रक्तो नीलः पीतो ऽरुणस्तथा /
कठिनश्चिक्कणः श्लक्ष्णः पिच्छिलो मृदु दारुणः //
text_mt: white, black, red, blue, yellow, and reddish-brown, / hard, smooth, polished, slimy, soft, and rough.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ ṣoḍaśavistāro jyotīrupaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tatraikaguṇamākāśaṃ śabda ityeva tatsmṛtam //
meaning:
एवं षोडशविस्तारो ज्योतीरुपगुणः स्मृतः /
तत्रैकगुणमाकाशं शब्द इत्येव तत्स्मृतम् //
text_mt: Thus the quality of form belonging to fire is remembered as sixteenfold. / In that respect, space possesses a single quality; it is remembered as sound alone.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya śabdasya vakṣyāmi vistaraṃ vividhātmakam /
ṣaḍjo ṛṣabhagāndhārau madhyamodhaivatastathā //
meaning:
तस्य शब्दस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तरं विविधात्मकम् /
षड्जो ऋषभगान्धारौ मध्यमोधैवतस्तथा //
text_mt: I shall explain the diverse extension of that sound: / ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, and dhaivata,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamaścāpi vijñeyastathā cāpi niṣādavān /
eṣa saptavidhaḥ prokto guṇa ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चमश्चापि विज्ञेयस्तथा चापि निषादवान् /
एष सप्तविधः प्रोक्तो गुण आकाशसंभवः //
text_mt: pañcama should also be known, as well as niṣāda. / This quality arising from space is declared to be sevenfold.

sanskrit_iast:
aiśvaryyeṇa tu sarvatra sthito 'pi payahādiṣu /
mṛdaṅgabherīśaṅkhānāṃ stanayitno rathasya ca //
meaning:
ऐश्वर्य्येण तु सर्वत्र स्थितो ऽपि पयहादिषु /
मृदङ्गभेरीशङ्खानां स्तनयित्नो रथस्य च //
text_mt: Yet by its sovereignty, though residing everywhere—in clouds and so on— / of mṛdaṅga-drums, bherī-drums, conches, thunder, and chariots,

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ bahuvidhākāraḥ śabda ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ /
vāyavyastu guṇaḥ sparśaḥ sparśaśca bahudhā smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
एवं बहुविधाकारः शब्द आकाशसंभवः /
वायव्यस्तु गुणः स्पर्शः स्पर्शश्च बहुधा स्मृतः //
text_mt: sound arising from space has such manifold forms. / Touch is the quality belonging to wind, and touch is recorded as manifold:

sanskrit_iast:
uṣṇaḥ śītaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ snigdho viśada eva ca /
tathā kharo mṛduḥ ślakṣṇo lavurgurutaro 'pi ca //
meaning:
उष्णः शीतः सुखं दुःखं स्निग्धो विशद एव च /
तथा खरो मृदुः श्लक्ष्णो लवुर्गुरुतरो ऽपि च //
text_mt: hot, cold, pleasant, painful, oily, and pure, / likewise rough, soft, polished, light, and heavier.

sanskrit_iast:
śabdasparśau tu vijñeyau dviguṇau vāyurityuta /
evamekādaśavidho vāyavyo guṇa ucyate //
meaning:
शब्दस्पर्शौ तु विज्ञेयौ द्विगुणौ वायुरित्युत /
एवमेकादशविधो वायव्यो गुण उच्यते //
text_mt: Sound and touch are to be known as having two qualities in air. / Thus the quality belonging to air is said to be elevenfold.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśajaṃ śabdamāhurebhirvāyuguṇaiḥ saha /
avyāhataiścetayate naveti viṣamā gatiḥ //
meaning:
आकाशजं शब्दमाहुरेभिर्वायुगुणैः सह /
अव्याहतैश्चेतयते नवेति विषमा गतिः //
text_mt: They declare that sound is born of space, along with these qualities of air. / With these unhindered, one perceives; its uneven course is ninefold.

sanskrit_iast:
āpyāyante ca te nityaṃ dhātavastaistu dhātubhiḥ /
āpo 'gnirmāruścaiva nityaṃ jāgrati dehiṣu //
meaning:
आप्यायन्ते च ते नित्यं धातवस्तैस्तु धातुभिः /
आपो ऽग्निर्मारुश्चैव नित्यं जाग्रति देहिषु //
text_mt: And those bodily elements are constantly nourished by those very elements. / Water, fire, and wind remain perpetually awake within embodied beings.

sanskrit_iast:
mūlamete śarīrasya vyāpya prāṇāniha sthitāḥ /
pārthivaṃ dhātumāsādya yathā ceṣṭayate balī //
meaning:
मूलमेते शरीरस्य व्याप्य प्राणानिह स्थिताः /
पार्थिवं धातुमासाद्य यथा चेष्टयते बली //
text_mt: These, the roots of the body, abide here pervading the vital breaths. / Having reached the earthy element, just as the powerful one moves about,

sanskrit_iast:
śrito mūrddhānamagnistu śarīraṃ paripālayet /
prāṇo mūrddhani vāgnau ca vartamāno viceṣṭate //
meaning:
श्रितो मूर्द्धानमग्निस्तु शरीरं परिपालयेत् /
प्राणो मूर्द्धनि वाग्नौ च वर्तमानो विचेष्टते //
text_mt: so fire, residing in the head, protects the body. / Prāṇa, existing in the head and in the fire, is set in motion.

sanskrit_iast:
sa jantuḥ sarvabhūtātmā puruṣaḥ sa sanātanaḥ /
mano buddhirahṝṅkāro bhūtāni viṣayaśca saḥ //
meaning:
स जन्तुः सर्वभूतात्मा पुरुषः स सनातनः /
मनो बुद्धिरहॄङ्कारो भूतानि विषयश्च सः //
text_mt: That creature is the Self of all beings, the eternal Puruṣa; / it is the mind, intellect, egoity, the elements, and the sense objects.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ tviha sa sarvatra prāṇaistu paripālyate /
pṛṣṭatastu samānena svāṃ svāṃ gatimupāśritaḥ //
meaning:
एवं त्विह स सर्वत्र प्राणैस्तु परिपाल्यते /
पृष्टतस्तु समानेन स्वां स्वां गतिमुपाश्रितः //
text_mt: Thus indeed it is protected on all sides here by the vital breaths, / and from behind by samāna, each resorting to its own course.

sanskrit_iast:
vastimūlaṃ gudaṃ caiva pāvakaṃ samupāśritaḥ /
vahanmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vāpyapānaḥ parivartate //
meaning:
वस्तिमूलं गुदं चैव पावकं समुपाश्रितः /
वहन्मूत्रं पुरीषं वाप्यपानः परिवर्तते //
text_mt: Resorting to the bladder-base, the anus, and the digestive fire, / bearing urine or faeces, the apāna revolves.

sanskrit_iast:
prayatne karmaniyame yaca ekastriṣu vartate /
udāna iti taṃ prāhuradhyātmajñānakovidāḥ //
meaning:
प्रयत्ने कर्मनियमे यच एकस्त्रिषु वर्तते /
उदान इति तं प्राहुरध्यात्मज्ञानकोविदाः //
text_mt: That single one which operates across the three in effort and the restraint of action / is called udāna by those skilled in the knowledge of the supreme Self.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃdhiṣvapi ca sarveṣu saṃniviṣṭastathānilaḥ /
śarīreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāna ityupadiśyate //
meaning:
संधिष्वपि च सर्वेषु संनिविष्टस्तथानिलः /
शरीरेषु मनुष्याणां व्यान इत्युपदिश्यते //
text_mt: The wind stationed within all the joints / in the bodies of human beings is taught to be vyāna.

sanskrit_iast:
bāhuṣvagnistu vitataḥ samānena samīritaḥ /
rasānvāru doṣāṃśca vartayannati ceṣṭate //
meaning:
बाहुष्वग्निस्तु विततः समानेन समीरितः /
रसान्वारु दोषांश्च वर्तयन्नति चेष्टते //
text_mt: The fire extended in the arms, impelled by the samāna, / acts vigorously, circulating the bodily humours and the fluids of digested food.

sanskrit_iast:
apānaprāṇayormadhye prāṇāpānasamīhitaḥ /
samanvitastvadhiṣṭānaṃ samyak pacati pāvakaḥ //
meaning:
अपानप्राणयोर्मध्ये प्राणापानसमीहितः /
समन्वितस्त्वधिष्टानं सम्यक् पचति पावकः //
text_mt: Between the apāna and prāṇa, impelled by prāṇa and apāna, / the fire, conjoined with its seat, digests [food] properly.

sanskrit_iast:
āspaṃhi pāyuparyantamante syādgudasaṃjñite /
retastasmātprajāyante sarvasrotāṃsi dehinām //
meaning:
आस्पंहि पायुपर्यन्तमन्ते स्याद्गुदसंज्ञिते /
रेतस्तस्मात्प्रजायन्ते सर्वस्रोतांसि देहिनाम् //
text_mt: From the mouth up to the anus, which terminates in what is called the rectum, / from that, semen and all the bodily channels of embodied beings are produced.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇānāṃ sannipātāśca sannipātaḥ prajāyate /
ūṣmā cāgirīti jñeyo yo 'nnaṃ pacati dehinām //
meaning:
प्राणानां सन्निपाताश्च सन्निपातः प्रजायते /
ऊष्मा चागिरीति ज्ञेयो यो ऽन्नं पचति देहिनाम् //
text_mt: From the conjunction of the vital breaths, a union is produced; / and the heat is to be known as the fire that digests the food of embodied beings.

sanskrit_iast:
agnivegavahaḥ prāṇo gudānte pratihanyate /
sa ūrdhvamāgamya punaḥ samutkṣipati pāvakam //
meaning:
अग्निवेगवहः प्राणो गुदान्ते प्रतिहन्यते /
स ऊर्ध्वमागम्य पुनः समुत्क्षिपति पावकम् //
text_mt: The prāṇa, bearing the force of the fire, is checked at the end of the rectum; / going upward again, it propels the fire.

sanskrit_iast:
pakvāśayastvadho nābhyā ūrdhvamāmāśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
nābhimūle śarīrasya sarve prāṇāśca saṃsthitāḥ //
meaning:
पक्वाशयस्त्वधो नाभ्या ऊर्ध्वमामाशयः स्मृतः /
नाभिमूले शरीरस्य सर्वे प्राणाश्च संस्थिताः //
text_mt: The seat of digested food is below the navel, and the stomach is recorded as above. / All the vital breaths are situated at the navel-root of the body.

sanskrit_iast:
prasthitā hṛdayātsarve tiryagūrdhdamadhastathā /
vahṝntyannarasānnāḍyo daśaprāṇapracoditāḥ //
meaning:
प्रस्थिता हृदयात्सर्वे तिर्यगूर्ध्दमधस्तथा /
वहॄन्त्यन्नरसान्नाड्यो दशप्राणप्रचोदिताः //
text_mt: Setting out from the heart transversely, upward, and downward, / the channels, impelled by the ten vital breaths, carry the essence of food.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa mārgo 'pi yogānāṃ yena gacchanti tatpadam /
jitaklamāḥ samā dhīrā mūrddhanyātmānamādadhan //
meaning:
एष मार्गो ऽपि योगानां येन गच्छन्ति तत्पदम् /
जितक्लमाः समा धीरा मूर्द्धन्यात्मानमादधन् //
text_mt: This is also the path of yogins by which they go to that abode; / their fatigue overcome, composed and steadfast, they place the self in the crown of the head.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ sarveṣu vihitaprāṇāpāneṣu dehinām /
tasminsamidhyate nityamagniḥ sthālyāmivāhitaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bhṛgubharadvājasaṃvāde jagadutpattivarṇanaṃ nāma dvicatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एवं सर्वेषु विहितप्राणापानेषु देहिनाम् /
तस्मिन्समिध्यते नित्यमग्निः स्थाल्यामिवाहितः //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे भृगुभरद्वाजसंवादे जगदुत्पत्तिवर्णनं नाम द्विचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
In this way, when all the prāṇa and apāna breaths are regulated in embodied beings, / the fire within is constantly kindled, like one placed in a pot.

Thus ends the forty-second chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Universe', in the dialogue between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja, in the second quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadi prāṇapatirvāyurvāyureva viceṣcate /
śvasityābhāṣate caiva tato jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यदि प्राणपतिर्वायुर्वायुरेव विचेष्चते /
श्वसित्याभाषते चैव ततो जीवो निरर्थकः //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / If wind is the master of the breath, and wind alone moves, / breathes, and speaks, then the soul is useless.

sanskrit_iast:
ya ūṣmabhāva āgneyo vahninaivopalabhyate /
agnirjarayate caitattadā jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
meaning:
य ऊष्मभाव आग्नेयो वह्निनैवोपलभ्यते /
अग्निर्जरयते चैतत्तदा जीवो निरर्थकः //
text_mt: If the condition of heat belongs to fire and is perceived by fire alone, / and fire digests this [food], then the soul is useless.

sanskrit_iast:
jantoḥ pramniyamāṇasya jīvo naivopalabhyate /
vāyureva jahātyenamūṣmabhāvaśca naśyati //
meaning:
जन्तोः प्रम्नियमाणस्य जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते /
वायुरेव जहात्येनमूष्मभावश्च नश्यति //
text_mt: When a living creature is dying, the soul is not perceived at all; / it is wind alone that leaves it, and the state of heat perishes.

sanskrit_iast:
yadi vāthumayo jīvaḥ saṃśleṣo yadi vāyunā /
vāyumañjalavatpaśyedgacchetsaha marudguṇaiḥ //
meaning:
यदि वाथुमयो जीवः संश्लेषो यदि वायुना /
वायुमञ्जलवत्पश्येद्गच्छेत्सह मरुद्गुणैः //
text_mt: If the soul consists of wind, or if it is joined with wind, / one would see the wind like water in the hollow of the hands, and it would depart along with the host of winds.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃśleṣo yadi vā tena yadi tasmātpraṇaśyati /
mahārṇavavimuktatvādanyatsalilabhājanam //
meaning:
संश्लेषो यदि वा तेन यदि तस्मात्प्रणश्यति /
महार्णवविमुक्तत्वादन्यत्सलिलभाजनम् //
text_mt: Or if there is a union with it, and if it perishes from that, / [it would be] like another vessel of water released into the great ocean.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛpe vā salilaṃ dadyātpradīpaṃ vā hutāśane /
kṣipraṃ praviśya naśyeta yathā naśyatyasau tathā //
meaning:
कृपे वा सलिलं दद्यात्प्रदीपं वा हुताशने /
क्षिप्रं प्रविश्य नश्येत यथा नश्यत्यसौ तथा //
text_mt: Or if one should pour water into a well, or [place] a lamp into fire, / having entered it quickly vanishes, just as that one would vanish.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcadhāraṇake hyasmiñcharīre jīvitaṃ kṛtam /
yeṣāmanyatarābhāvāñcaturṇāṃ nāsti saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चधारणके ह्यस्मिञ्छरीरे जीवितं कृतम् /
येषामन्यतराभावाञ्चतुर्णां नास्ति संशयः //
text_mt: Life is established in this body which holds the five [elements]; / without doubt, in the absence of any one of them, the [other] four cannot remain.

sanskrit_iast:
naśyantyāpo hyanāhārādvāyurucchvāsanigrahāt /
naśyate koṣṭabhedārthamagrirnaśyatyabhojanāt //
meaning:
नश्यन्त्यापो ह्यनाहाराद्वायुरुच्छ्वासनिग्रहात् /
नश्यते कोष्टभेदार्थमग्रिर्नश्यत्यभोजनात् //
text_mt: For water perishes from lack of food, and wind from the restraint of breathing; / from the rupturing of the internal cavity fire is destroyed, and it perishes from lack of eating.

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhitraṇaparikleśairmedinī caiva śīryate /
pīḍite 'nyatare hyeṣāṃ saṃghāto yāti pañcatām //
meaning:
व्याधित्रणपरिक्लेशैर्मेदिनी चैव शीर्यते /
पीडिते ऽन्यतरे ह्येषां संघातो याति पञ्चताम् //
text_mt: And the earth decays through the distress of diseases and wounds. / Indeed, when any one of these is afflicted, the aggregate meets dissolution into the five elements.

sanskrit_iast:
tasminpañcatvamāpanne jīvaḥ kimanudhāvati /
kiṃ khedayati vā jīvaḥ kiṃ śṛṇoti bravīti ca //
meaning:
तस्मिन्पञ्चत्वमापन्ने जीवः किमनुधावति /
किं खेदयति वा जीवः किं शृणोति ब्रवीति च //
text_mt: When that [body] has attained dissolution into the five elements, what does the living soul pursue? / Or what causes sorrow to the soul, what does it hear, and what does it speak?

sanskrit_iast:
eṣā gauḥ paralokasthaṃ tārayiṣyatimāmiti /
yo dattvā mriyate jantuḥ sā gauḥ kaṃ tārayiṣyati //
meaning:
एषा गौः परलोकस्थं तारयिष्यतिमामिति /
यो दत्त्वा म्रियते जन्तुः सा गौः कं तारयिष्यति //
text_mt: "This cow will carry me across when I am in the other world"— / when a creature dies after giving [such a gift], whom will that cow carry across?

sanskrit_iast:
gauścapratigrahītā ca dātā caiva samaṃ yadā /
ihaiva vilayaṃ yānti kutasteṣāṃ samāgamaḥ //
meaning:
गौश्चप्रतिग्रहीता च दाता चैव समं यदा /
इहैव विलयं यान्ति कुतस्तेषां समागमः //
text_mt: When the cow, the recipient, and the giver together / dissolve right here in this world, whence comes their reunion?

sanskrit_iast:
vihagairupabhuktasya śailāgrātpatitasya ca /
agninā copayuktasya kutaḥ saṃjīvanaṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
विहगैरुपभुक्तस्य शैलाग्रात्पतितस्य च /
अग्निना चोपयुक्तस्य कुतः संजीवनं पुनः //
text_mt: For one eaten by birds, or fallen from a mountain peak, / or consumed by fire, whence can there be life again?

sanskrit_iast:
chinnasya yadi vṛkṣasya na mūlaṃ pratirohati /
jīvanyasya pravartante mṛtaḥ kva punareṣyati //
meaning:
छिन्नस्य यदि वृक्षस्य न मूलं प्रतिरोहति /
जीवन्यस्य प्रवर्तन्ते मृतः क्व पुनरेष्यति //
text_mt: If a felled tree does not sprout again from its root, / [and only] others living proceed, where will the dead one go again?

sanskrit_iast:
jīvamātraṃ purā sṛṣṭaṃ yadetatparivartate /
mṛtāḥ praṇaśyanti bījādbījaṃ praṇaśyati //
meaning:
जीवमात्रं पुरा सृष्टं यदेतत्परिवर्तते /
मृताः प्रणश्यन्ति बीजाद्बीजं प्रणश्यति //
text_mt: Only the living soul was created formerly, which revolves here; / the dead perish, and seed perishes from seed.

sanskrit_iast:
iti me saṃśayo brahmanhṛdaye paridhāvati /
ta nivartaya sarvajña yatastvāmāśrito hyaham //
meaning:
इति मे संशयो ब्रह्मन्हृदये परिधावति /
त निवर्तय सर्वज्ञ यतस्त्वामाश्रितो ह्यहम् //
text_mt: Thus this doubt rushes through my heart, O sage; / dispel it, O omniscient one, for indeed I have taken refuge in you.

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
evaṃ pṛṣṭastadānena sa bhṛgarbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
punarāhu muniśreṣṭha tatsaṃdehanivṛttaye //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
एवं पृष्टस्तदानेन स भृगर्ब्रह्मणः सुतः /
पुनराहु मुनिश्रेष्ठ तत्संदेहनिवृत्तये //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / Being thus questioned at that time by him, that Bhṛgu, son of Brahmā, / spoke again, O best of sages, for the dispelling of his doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
na prāṇāḥ santi jīvasya dattasya ca kṛtasya ca /
yāti dehāntaraṃ prāṇī śarīraṃ tu viśīryate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
न प्राणाः सन्ति जीवस्य दत्तस्य च कृतस्य च /
याति देहान्तरं प्राणी शरीरं तु विशीर्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / There are no vital breaths of the living soul, nor of what is given or done; / the living being goes to another body, but the physical body falls away.

sanskrit_iast:
na śarīrāśrito jīvastasminnaṣṭe praṇaśyati /
samidhāmagnidagdhānāṃ yathāgrirddaśyate tathā //
meaning:
न शरीराश्रितो जीवस्तस्मिन्नष्टे प्रणश्यति /
समिधामग्निदग्धानां यथाग्रिर्द्दश्यते तथा //
text_mt: The living soul residing in the body does not perish when that is destroyed, / just as fire is seen when firewood is consumed by fire.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
agneryathā tasya nāśāttadvināśo na vidyate /
indhanasyopayogānte sa vāgnirnopalabhyate //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
अग्नेर्यथा तस्य नाशात्तद्विनाशो न विद्यते /
इन्धनस्योपयोगान्ते स वाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / As with fire, there is no destruction of it through its destruction; / [yet] at the end of the consumption of fuel, that fire is not perceived.

sanskrit_iast:
naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam /
gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate //
meaning:
नश्यतीत्येव जानामि शान्तमग्निमनिन्धनम् /
गतिर्यस्य प्रमाणं वा संस्थानं वा न विद्यते //
text_mt: I know only that fire, extinguished and devoid of fuel, perishes, / [a fire] whose movement, measure, or place of resting is not found.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
samidhāmupayogānte sa cāgnirnopalabhyate /
naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
समिधामुपयोगान्ते स चाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते /
नश्यतीत्येव जानामि शान्तमग्निमनिन्धनम् //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / At the end of the consumption of firewood, that fire is not perceived; / I know that the extinguished fire, devoid of fuel, [merely seems to] perish.

sanskrit_iast:
gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate /
samidhāmupayogānte yathāgnirnopalabhyate //
meaning:
गतिर्यस्य प्रमाणं वा संस्थानं वा न विद्यते /
समिधामुपयोगान्ते यथाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: Its movement, measure, or place of resting is not found; / as fire is not perceived at the end of the consumption of firewood,

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśānugatatvāddhi durgrāhyo hi nirāśrayaḥ /
tathā śarīrasaṃtyāge jīvo hyākāśavatsthitaḥ //
meaning:
आकाशानुगतत्वाद्धि दुर्ग्राह्यो हि निराश्रयः /
तथा शरीरसंत्यागे जीवो ह्याकाशवत्स्थितः //
text_mt: because it has merged into space, it is indeed difficult to grasp, being without support; / likewise, upon abandonment of the body, the living soul remains like space.

sanskrit_iast:
na naśyate susūkṣmatvādyathā jyotirna saṃśayaḥ /
prāṇāndhārayate hyagniḥ sa jīva upadhāryatām //
meaning:
न नश्यते सुसूक्ष्मत्वाद्यथा ज्योतिर्न संशयः /
प्राणान्धारयते ह्यग्निः स जीव उपधार्यताम् //
text_mt: It does not perish because of its extreme subtlety, just like light; there is no doubt. / Fire indeed sustains the vital breaths; let that be understood as the living soul.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyusaṃdhāraṇo hyagnirnaśyatyucchvāsanigrahāt /
tasminnaṣṭe śarīrāgnau tato dehamacetanam //
meaning:
वायुसंधारणो ह्यग्निर्नश्यत्युच्छ्वासनिग्रहात् /
तस्मिन्नष्टे शरीराग्नौ ततो देहमचेतनम् //
text_mt: Fire is sustained by wind, and perishes through the cessation of breath; / when that bodily fire is destroyed, then the body is unconscious.

sanskrit_iast:
patitaṃ yāti bhūmitvamayanaṃ tasya hi kṣitiḥ /
jagamānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca //
meaning:
पतितं याति भूमित्वमयनं तस्य हि क्षितिः /
जगमानां हि सर्वेषां स्थावराणां तथैव च //
text_mt: Fallen, it turns into earth, for the earth is its destination; / indeed of all moving and likewise of unmoving beings.

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśaṃ pavano 'nveti jyotistamanugacchati /
teṣāṃ trayāṇāmekatvādvayaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭitam //
meaning:
आकाशं पवनो ऽन्वेति ज्योतिस्तमनुगच्छति /
तेषां त्रयाणामेकत्वाद्वयं भूमौ प्रतिष्टितम् //
text_mt: Wind follows space, and light follows it; / because of the oneness of those three, the body is established on earth.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra khaṃ tatra pavanastatrāgniryatra mārutaḥ /
amūrtayaste vijñeyā mūrtimantaḥ śarīriṇaḥ //
meaning:
यत्र खं तत्र पवनस्तत्राग्निर्यत्र मारुतः /
अमूर्तयस्ते विज्ञेया मूर्तिमन्तः शरीरिणः //
text_mt: Where there is space, there is wind; where there is wind, there is fire; / they are to be known as formless, while embodied beings have form.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadyagnimārutau bhūmiḥ khamāpaśca śarīriṣu /
jīvaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇastatretyetadācakṣva me 'nagha //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यद्यग्निमारुतौ भूमिः खमापश्च शरीरिषु /
जीवः किंलक्षणस्तत्रेत्येतदाचक्ष्व मे ऽनघ //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / If fire and wind, earth, space, and water are in embodied beings, / then what is the characteristic of the living soul there? Tell me this, O sinless one!

sanskrit_iast:
pañcātmake pañcaratau pañcavijñānasaṃjñake /
śarīre prāṇināṃ jīvaṃ vettubhicchāmi yādṛśam //
meaning:
पञ्चात्मके पञ्चरतौ पञ्चविज्ञानसंज्ञके /
शरीरे प्राणिनां जीवं वेत्तुभिच्छामि यादृशम् //
text_mt: Consisting of the five [elements], delighting in the five, named for fivefold perception: / in such a body of living beings, I wish to know of what sort the living soul is.

sanskrit_iast:
māṃsaśoṇitasaṃghāte medaḥsnāyvasthisaṃcaye /
bhidyamāne śarīre tu jīvo naivopalabhyate //
meaning:
मांसशोणितसंघाते मेदःस्नाय्वस्थिसंचये /
भिद्यमाने शरीरे तु जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: In an aggregate of flesh and blood, a heap of fat, sinews, and bones, / when the body is dissected, the living soul is not found at all.

sanskrit_iast:
yadyajīvaśarīraṃ tu pañcabhūtasamanvitam /
śarīre mānase duḥkha kastāṃ vedayate rujam //
meaning:
यद्यजीवशरीरं तु पञ्चभूतसमन्वितम् /
शरीरे मानसे दुःख कस्तां वेदयते रुजम् //
text_mt: If the body endowed with the five elements were without a living soul, / then in bodily and mental pain, who experiences that ache?

sanskrit_iast:
śṛṇoti kathitaṃ jīvaḥ karṇābhyāṃna śṛṇoti tat /
maharṣe manasi vyagre tasmājjīvo nirarthakaḥ //
meaning:
शृणोति कथितं जीवः कर्णाभ्यांन शृणोति तत् /
महर्षे मनसि व्यग्रे तस्माज्जीवो निरर्थकः //
text_mt: The living soul hears what is spoken; it does not hear it through the ears / when the mind is agitated, O great sage; therefore, is the living soul useless?

sanskrit_iast:
sarve paśyanti yadṛśyaṃ manoyuktena cakṣuṣā /
manasi vyākule cakṣuḥ paśyannapi na paśyati //
meaning:
सर्वे पश्यन्ति यदृश्यं मनोयुक्तेन चक्षुषा /
मनसि व्याकुले चक्षुः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति //
text_mt: All see an object of sight with the eye joined with the mind; / when the mind is distracted, the eye, even though looking, does not see.

sanskrit_iast:
na paśyati na cāghrāti na śṛṇoti na bhāṣate /
na ca smarśamasau vetti nidrāvaśagataḥ punaḥ //
meaning:
न पश्यति न चाघ्राति न शृणोति न भाषते /
न च स्मर्शमसौ वेत्ति निद्रावशगतः पुनः //
text_mt: It does not see, nor does it smell, nor does it hear, nor does it speak; / and fallen under the sway of sleep, it does not perceive touch again.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛṣyati kruddhyate ko 'tra śocatyudvijate ca kaḥ /
icchati dhyāyati dveṣṭi vākyaṃ vācayate ca kaḥ //
meaning:
हृष्यति क्रुद्ध्यते को ऽत्र शोचत्युद्विजते च कः /
इच्छति ध्यायति द्वेष्टि वाक्यं वाचयते च कः //
text_mt: Who rejoices here, who grows angry, who grieves, and who becomes agitated? / Who desires, meditates, hates, and utters speech?

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
taṃ pañcasādhāraṇamatra kiñciccharīrameko vahateṃ'tarātmā /
sa vetti gandhāṃśca rasāñchutīśca sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca guṇāṃśca ye 'lye //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
तं पञ्चसाधारणमत्र किञ्चिच्छरीरमेको वहतेंऽतरात्मा /
स वेत्ति गन्धांश्च रसाञ्छुतीश्च स्पर्शं च रूपं च गुणांश्च ये ऽल्ये //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / A single inner Self bears that body here, which is the common property of the five [elements]; / it perceives smells, tastes, sounds, touch, form, and whatever other qualities there are.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcātmake pañcaguṇapradarśī sa sarvagātrānugatoṃ'tarātmā /
saveti duḥkhāni sukhāni cātra tadviprayogāttu na vetti deham //
meaning:
पञ्चात्मके पञ्चगुणप्रदर्शी स सर्वगात्रानुगतोंऽतरात्मा /
सवेति दुःखानि सुखानि चात्र तद्विप्रयोगात्तु न वेत्ति देहम् //
text_mt: Discerning the five qualities in that which consists of the five [elements], that inner Self permeates all the limbs; / it experiences pleasures and pains here, but upon separation from it, [the person] does not know the body.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā na rūpaṃ na sparśo noṣyabhavaśca pāvake /
tadā śānte śarīrāgnau dehatyāgena naśyati //
meaning:
यदा न रूपं न स्पर्शो नोष्यभवश्च पावके /
तदा शान्ते शरीराग्नौ देहत्यागेन नश्यति //
text_mt: When there is no form, no touch, and no presence of heat in fire, / then, when the bodily fire is extinguished, it departs through abandonment of the body.

sanskrit_iast:
āpomayamidaṃ sarvamāpomūrtiḥ śarīriṇām /
tatrātmā mānaso brahmā sarvabhūteṣu lokakṛt //
meaning:
आपोमयमिदं सर्वमापोमूर्तिः शरीरिणाम् /
तत्रात्मा मानसो ब्रह्मा सर्वभूतेषु लोककृत् //
text_mt: All this is composed of water; water is the form of embodied beings; / there the mental Self, Brahmā, is the world-maker in all beings.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ taṃ vijānīhi sarvalokahitātmakam /
tasminyaḥ saṃśrito dehe hyabbinduriva puṣkare //
meaning:
आत्मानं तं विजानीहि सर्वलोकहितात्मकम् /
तस्मिन्यः संश्रितो देहे ह्यब्बिन्दुरिव पुष्करे //
text_mt: Know that Self, whose nature is the welfare of all the worlds; / that which resides in that body is like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ lokahitātmakam /
tamorajaśca sattvaṃ ca viddhi jīvaguṇānimām //
meaning:
क्षेत्रज्ञं तं विजानीहि नित्यं लोकहितात्मकम् /
तमोरजश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि जीवगुणानिमाम् //
text_mt: Know it to be the knower of the field, eternally having the welfare of the world as its nature; / know darkness, passion, and goodness to be these qualities of the living soul.

sanskrit_iast:
acetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam /
ataḥ paraṃ kṣetravido vadanti prāvartayadyo bhuvanāni sapta //
meaning:
अचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति स चेष्टते चेष्टयते च सर्वम् /
अतः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति प्रावर्तयद्यो भुवनानि सप्त //
text_mt: They call the quality of the living soul insentient; it moves and sets everything in motion; / higher than this, the knowers of the field speak of that which set the seven worlds in motion.

sanskrit_iast:
na jīvanāśo 'sti hi dehabhede mithyaitadāhurmuna ityabuddhāḥ /
jīvastu dehāntaritaḥ prayāti daśārddhatastasya śarīrabhedaḥ //
meaning:
न जीवनाशो ऽस्ति हि देहभेदे मिथ्यैतदाहुर्मुन इत्यबुद्धाः /
जीवस्तु देहान्तरितः प्रयाति दशार्द्धतस्तस्य शरीरभेदः //
text_mt: There is no destruction of the living soul upon the dissolution of the body; fools who are not wise say this falsely; / but the living soul departs, separated from the body; the dissolution of its body is from the five [elements].

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣu gūḍhaścarati sarvadā /
dṛśyate tvagryā budhyāsūkṣmayā tattvadarśibhiḥ //
meaning:
एवं भूतेषु सर्वेषु गूढश्चरति सर्वदा /
दृश्यते त्वग्र्या बुध्यासूक्ष्मया तत्त्वदर्शिभिः //
text_mt: Thus it moves, hidden in all beings at all times; / but it is seen by the seers of truth with a subtle, supreme intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ pūrvāpararātreṣu yuñjānaḥ satataṃ budhaḥ /
labdhāhāro viśuddhātmā paśyatyātmānamātmani //
meaning:
तं पूर्वापररात्रेषु युञ्जानः सततं बुधः /
लब्धाहारो विशुद्धात्मा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि //
text_mt: The wise one who constantly yokes it in the earlier and later parts of the night, / having taken food, with a purified self, sees the Self in the self.

sanskrit_iast:
cittasya hi prasādena hitvā karma śubhāśubham /
prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukhamānantyamaśnute //
meaning:
चित्तस्य हि प्रसादेन हित्वा कर्म शुभाशुभम् /
प्रसन्नात्मात्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमानन्त्यमश्नुते //
text_mt: Through the serenity of the mind, having abandoned auspicious and inauspicious action, / with a serene self, abiding in the Self, he attains endless bliss.

sanskrit_iast:
mānaso 'gniḥ śarīreṣu jīva ityabhidhīyate /
sṛṣṭiḥ prajāpatereṣā bhūtādhyātmaviniścaye //
meaning:
मानसो ऽग्निः शरीरेषु जीव इत्यभिधीयते /
सृष्टिः प्रजापतेरेषा भूताध्यात्मविनिश्चये //
text_mt: The fire belonging to the mind in bodies is called the living soul; / this is the creation of Prajāpati in the ascertainment of the elements and the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
asṛjadbrāhmaṇāneva pūrvaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ /
ātmatejo 'bhinir vṛttānbhāskarāgnisamaprabhān //
meaning:
असृजद्ब्राह्मणानेव पूर्वं ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः /
आत्मतेजो ऽभिनिर् वृत्तान्भास्कराग्निसमप्रभान् //
text_mt: First Prajāpati Brahmā created only Brāhmaṇas, / brought forth from his own splendor, equal in radiance to the sun and fire.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca tathā brahma ca śāśvatam /
ācāraṃ caiva śaucaṃ ca svargāya vidadhe prabhuḥ //
meaning:
ततः सत्यं च धर्मं च तथा ब्रह्म च शाश्वतम् /
आचारं चैव शौचं च स्वर्गाय विदधे प्रभुः //
text_mt: Then the Lord ordained truth, righteousness, eternal sacred wisdom, / good conduct, and purity for the sake of heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
devadāna vagandharvā daityāsuramahoragāḥ /
yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca piśācā manujāstathā //
meaning:
देवदान वगन्धर्वा दैत्यासुरमहोरगाः /
यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च पिशाचा मनुजास्तथा //
text_mt: Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Daityas, Asuras, great serpents, / Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Nāgas, Piśācas, and humans—

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāṇāmasitastathā /
bharadvāja uvāca
cāturvarṇyasya varṇena yadi varṇo vibhidyate //
meaning:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राणामसितस्तथा /
भरद्वाज उवाच
चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य वर्णेन यदि वर्णो विभिद्यते //
text_mt: Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and likewise the dark [class] of Śūdras. / Bharadvāja said: / If caste is distinguished by the color of the four castes,

sanskrit_iast:
svedamūtrapurīṣāṇi śleṣmā pitta saśoṇitam /
tvantaḥ kṣarati sarveṣāṃ kasmādvarṇo vibhajyate //
meaning:
स्वेदमूत्रपुरीषाणि श्लेष्मा पित्त सशोणितम् /
त्वन्तः क्षरति सर्वेषां कस्माद्वर्णो विभज्यते //
text_mt: sweat, urine, feces, phlegm, bile, along with blood, / flow within all of them, why then is caste divided?

sanskrit_iast:
jaṅgamānāmasaṃkhyeyāḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jātayaḥ /
teṣāṃ vividhavarṇānāṃ kuto varṇaviniścayaḥ //
meaning:
जङ्गमानामसंख्येयाः स्थावराणां च जातयः /
तेषां विविधवर्णानां कुतो वर्णविनिश्चयः //
text_mt: Countless are the species of moving and unmoving beings; / of those possessing various colors, whence is the determination of caste?

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
na viśeṣo 'sti varṇānāṃ sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ jagat /
brahmaṇā pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ hi karmaṇā varṇatāṃ gatam //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
न विशेषो ऽस्ति वर्णानां सर्वं ब्रह्ममयं जगत् /
ब्रह्मणा पूर्वसृष्टं हि कर्मणा वर्णतां गतम् //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / There is no distinction among the castes; the entire world consists of Brahman; / for, originally created by Brahmā, it attained the status of caste through action.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmabhogāḥ priyāstīkṣṇāḥ krodhatāpriyasāhasāḥ /
tyaktasvakarmaraktāṅgāste dvijāḥ kṣatratāṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
कामभोगाः प्रियास्तीक्ष्णाः क्रोधताप्रियसाहसाः /
त्यक्तस्वकर्मरक्ताङ्गास्ते द्विजाः क्षत्रतां गताः //
text_mt: Those twice-born who loved desires and sensual pleasures, who were fierce, fond of anger and daring deeds, / and who abandoned their own duties, red-limbed, attained the status of Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit_iast:
gobhyo vṛttiṃ samāsthāya pītāḥ kṛṣyupajīvinaḥ /
svadharṃmannānutiṣṭanti te dvijā vaiśyatāṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
गोभ्यो वृत्तिं समास्थाय पीताः कृष्युपजीविनः /
स्वधर्ंमन्नानुतिष्टन्ति ते द्विजा वैश्यतां गताः //
text_mt: Those twice-born who, adopting their livelihood from cows, becoming yellow [in complexion], subsist on agriculture / and do not adhere to their own duty, have attained the status of Vaiśyas.

sanskrit_iast:
rhisānṛtaparā lubdhāḥ sarvakarmopajīvinaḥ /
kṛṣṇāḥ śaucapāribhrāṣṭāste dvijāḥ śūdratāṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
र्हिसानृतपरा लुब्धाः सर्वकर्मोपजीविनः /
कृष्णाः शौचपारिभ्राष्टास्ते द्विजाः शूद्रतां गताः //
text_mt: Those twice-born who are devoted to violence and falsehood, greedy, subsisting on all kinds of occupations, / black [in complexion], and fallen from ritual purity, have attained the status of Śūdras.

sanskrit_iast:
ityetaiḥ karmabhirvyāptā dvijā varṇāntaraṃ gatāḥ /
brāhmaṇā dharmatantrasthāstapasteṣāṃ na naśyati //
meaning:
इत्येतैः कर्मभिर्व्याप्ता द्विजा वर्णान्तरं गताः /
ब्राह्मणा धर्मतन्त्रस्थास्तपस्तेषां न नश्यति //
text_mt: Occupied with these actions, twice-born men have entered different classes. / For Brahmins established in the system of dharma, their ascetic power does not perish.

sanskrit_iast:
brahma dhārayatāṃ nityaṃ vratāni niyabhāṃstathā /
brahma caiva purā sṛṣṭaṃ yena jānanti tadvidaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्म धारयतां नित्यं व्रतानि नियभांस्तथा /
ब्रह्म चैव पुरा सृष्टं येन जानन्ति तद्विदः //
text_mt: For those who constantly uphold Brahman, vows, and observances, / Brahman was created of old, by which those who know it perceive [the truth].

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāṃ bahuvidhāstvanyāstatra tatra dvijātayaḥ /
piśācajā rākṣasāḥ pretā vividhā mlecchajātayaḥ /
sā sṛṣṭirmānasī nāma dharmatantraparāyaṇā //
meaning:
तेषां बहुविधास्त्वन्यास्तत्र तत्र द्विजातयः /
पिशाचजा राक्षसाः प्रेता विविधा म्लेच्छजातयः /
सा सृष्टिर्मानसी नाम धर्मतन्त्रपरायणा //
text_mt: Various other twice-born groups appeared here and there among them— / Piśācas, Rākṣasas, Pretas, and diverse kinds of Mlecchas. / That was called the mind-born creation, devoted to the order of dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
brāhmaṇaḥ kena bhavati kṣatriyo vā dvijottama /
vaiśyaḥ śūdraśca viprarṣe tadbrūhi vadatāṃ vara //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
ब्राह्मणः केन भवति क्षत्रियो वा द्विजोत्तम /
वैश्यः शूद्रश्च विप्रर्षे तद्ब्रूहि वदतां वर //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / By what does one become a Brahmin or a Kṣatriya, O best of the twice-born? / And how a Vaiśya and a Śūdra, O Brahmin sage? Tell that, O best among speakers.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
jātakarmādibhiryastu saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ śuciḥ /
vedādhyayanasaṃpanno brahmakarmasvavasthitaḥ //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
जातकर्मादिभिर्यस्तु संस्कारैः संस्कृतः शुचिः /
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नो ब्रह्मकर्मस्ववस्थितः //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / But he who is purified by the rites of passage beginning with the birth-ceremony, who is clean, / endowed with the study of the Vedas, and established in the duties of Brahman;

sanskrit_iast:
śaucācārasthitaḥ samyagvidyābhyāsī gurupriyaḥ /
nityavratī satyaparaḥ sa vai brāhmaṇa ucyate //
meaning:
शौचाचारस्थितः सम्यग्विद्याभ्यासी गुरुप्रियः /
नित्यव्रती सत्यपरः स वै ब्राह्मण उच्यते //
text_mt: Established properly in ritual purity and conduct, engaged in learning, dear to his teacher, / constant in vows, and devoted to truth—he indeed is called a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
satyaṃ dānamatho 'droha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṛpā ghṛṇā /
tapasyāṃ dṛśyate yatra sa brāhmaṇa iti smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
सत्यं दानमथो ऽद्रोह आनृशंस्यं कृपा घृणा /
तपस्यां दृश्यते यत्र स ब्राह्मण इति स्मृतः //
text_mt: Truth, charity, freedom from malice, harmlessness, compassion, tenderness, / and asceticism—in whom these are seen, he is recorded as a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣatrajaṃ sevate karma vedādhyayanasaṃgataḥ /
dānādānaratiryastu sa vai kṣatriya ucyate //
meaning:
क्षत्रजं सेवते कर्म वेदाध्ययनसंगतः /
दानादानरतिर्यस्तु स वै क्षत्रिय उच्यते //
text_mt: He who pursues the occupation arising from the martial order, engaged in the study of the Vedas, / and delights in giving and receiving—he indeed is called a Kṣatriya.

sanskrit_iast:
viśatyāśu paśubhyaśca kṛṣyādānaratiḥ śuciḥ /
vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sa vaiśya iti saṃjñitaḥ //
meaning:
विशत्याशु पशुभ्यश्च कृष्यादानरतिः शुचिः /
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नः स वैश्य इति संज्ञितः //
text_mt: He who quickly turns to cattle, delights in agriculture and commerce, is pure, / and is endowed with Vedic study—he is termed a Vaiśya.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaghabhakṣaratirnityaṃ sarvakarmakaro 'śuciḥ /
tyaktavedastvanācāraḥ sa vai śūdra iti smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वघभक्षरतिर्नित्यं सर्वकर्मकरो ऽशुचिः /
त्यक्तवेदस्त्वनाचारः स वै शूद्र इति स्मृतः //
text_mt: He who habitually delights in eating all foods, performs all types of work, is impure, / has abandoned the Vedas, and is without right conduct—he indeed is recorded as a Śūdra.

sanskrit_iast:
śūdre caitadbhavellakṣma dvije tacca na vidyate /
na vai śūdro bhavecchūdro brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇo na ca //
meaning:
शूद्रे चैतद्भवेल्लक्ष्म द्विजे तच्च न विद्यते /
न वै शूद्रो भवेच्छूद्रो ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणो न च //
text_mt: If this characteristic exists in a Śūdra and is absent in a twice-born man, / then a Śūdra would not be a Śūdra, nor would a Brahmin be a Brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvopāyaistu lobhasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ /
etatpavitraṃ jñānānāṃ tathā caivātmasaṃyamaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वोपायैस्तु लोभस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः /
एतत्पवित्रं ज्ञानानां तथा चैवात्मसंयमः //
text_mt: The restraint of greed and anger by all means, / and self-control—this is the purifier of all kinds of knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
varjyau sarvātmanā tau hi śreyoghātārthamudyatau /
nityakrodhācchriyaṃ rakṣettapo rakṣettu matsarāt //
meaning:
वर्ज्यौ सर्वात्मना तौ हि श्रेयोघातार्थमुद्यतौ /
नित्यक्रोधाच्छ्रियं रक्षेत्तपो रक्षेत्तु मत्सरात् //
text_mt: For those two must be shunned with one's whole self, as they are intent upon destroying the highest good. / One should protect prosperity from constant anger, and asceticism from envy;

sanskrit_iast: vidyāṃ mānāpamānābhaghyāmātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ //
meaning: विद्यां मानापमानाभघ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः //
text_mt: Knowledge from honour and dishonour, and the self from heedlessness.

sanskrit_iast:
yasya sarve samāraṃbhaghā nirāśīrbandhanā dvija /
tyāge yasya hutaṃ sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān //
meaning:
यस्य सर्वे समारंभघा निराशीर्बन्धना द्विज /
त्यागे यस्य हुतं सर्वं स त्यागी स च बुद्धिमान् //
text_mt: He whose undertakings are all free from the bond of desire, O twice-born, / and to whom everything is offered up in renunciation—he is a renouncer, and he is wise.

sanskrit_iast:
ahiṃstraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ maitrāyaṇa gataścaret /
parigrahātparityajya bhavedbaddhyā jitendriyaḥ //
meaning:
अहिंस्त्रः सर्वभूतानां मैत्रायण गतश्चरेत् /
परिग्रहात्परित्यज्य भवेद्बद्ध्या जितेन्द्रियः //
text_mt: Harmless to all beings, he should wander about, benevolent to all; / abandoning possessions, he should become one who has mastered his senses by means of intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
aśokasthānamāti vediha cāmutra cābhayam /
taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmamanā //
meaning:
अशोकस्थानमाति वेदिह चामुत्र चाभयम् /
तपोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्ममना //
text_mt: The sorrowless state brings fearlessness both here and in the hereafter / for the sage who is constant in austerity, subdued, and self-controlled.

sanskrit_iast:
ajitaṃ jetukāmena vyāsaṃgeṣu hyasaṃginā /
indriyairgṛhyate yadyattattavdyaktamiti sthitiḥ //
meaning:
अजितं जेतुकामेन व्यासंगेषु ह्यसंगिना /
इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद्यत्तत्तव्द्यक्तमिति स्थितिः //
text_mt: For one desiring to conquer the unconquered, unattached in the midst of attachments— / whatever is perceived by the senses, that is the manifest: such is the principle.

sanskrit_iast:
avyaktamiti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyamatīndriyam /
aviśraṃbheṇa mantavyaṃ viśraṃbhe dhārayenmanaḥ //
meaning:
अव्यक्तमिति विज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् /
अविश्रंभेण मन्तव्यं विश्रंभे धारयेन्मनः //
text_mt: Beyond the senses and graspable by inference, it should be known as the unmanifest. / One should reflect with vigilance; one should fix the mind in steadfast trust.

sanskrit_iast:
manaḥ prāṇena gṛhṇīyātprāṇaṃ brahmaṇi dhārayet /
nivedādeva nirvāṇaṃ na ca kiñcidviccitayet //
meaning:
मनः प्राणेन गृह्णीयात्प्राणं ब्रह्मणि धारयेत् /
निवेदादेव निर्वाणं न च किञ्चिद्विच्चितयेत् //
text_mt: One should hold the mind with the breath, and fix the breath in Brahman; / liberation comes solely from detachment, and one should think of nothing else.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaṃ vai brahmaṇo brahmannirvedenādhigacchati /
śauce tu satataṃ yuktaḥ sadācārasamanvitaḥ //
meaning:
सुखं वै ब्रह्मणो ब्रह्मन्निर्वेदेनाधिगच्छति /
शौचे तु सततं युक्तः सदाचारसमन्वितः //
text_mt: Through detachment, O Brahmin, one attains the bliss of Brahman. / Constantly engaged in purity and endowed with right conduct,

sanskrit_iast:
svanukrośaśca bhūteṣu taddvijātiṣu lakṣaṇam /
satyaṃvrataṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ satyaṃ visṛjate prajā //
meaning:
स्वनुक्रोशश्च भूतेषु तद्द्विजातिषु लक्षणम् /
सत्यंव्रतं तपः शौचं सत्यं विसृजते प्रजा //
text_mt: Compassionate toward beings—this is the characteristic among the twice-born. / Truth, vows, austerity, and purity—truth brings forth creatures.

sanskrit_iast:
satyena dhāryate lokaḥ svaḥ satyenaiva gacchati /
anṛtaṃ tamaso rūpaṃ tamasā nīyate hyadhaḥ //
meaning:
सत्येन धार्यते लोकः स्वः सत्येनैव गच्छति /
अनृतं तमसो रूपं तमसा नीयते ह्यधः //
text_mt: By truth the world is sustained; by truth alone one goes to heaven. / Falsehood is the form of darkness; by darkness one is led downwards.

sanskrit_iast:
tamograstāna paśyanti prakāśantamasāvṛtāḥ /
suduṣprakāśa ityāhurnarakaṃ tama eva ca //
meaning:
तमोग्रस्तान पश्यन्ति प्रकाशन्तमसावृताः /
सुदुष्प्रकाश इत्याहुर्नरकं तम एव च //
text_mt: Seized by darkness, enveloped in darkness, they do not see the light. / They say that hell is darkness and extremely difficult to illuminate.

sanskrit_iast:
satyānṛtaṃ tadubhaghayaṃ prāpyate jagatīcaraiḥ /
tatrāpyevaṃvidhā loke vṛttiḥ satyānṛte bhavet //
meaning:
सत्यानृतं तदुभघयं प्राप्यते जगतीचरैः /
तत्राप्येवंविधा लोके वृत्तिः सत्यानृते भवेत् //
text_mt: Both truth and falsehood are encountered by those who walk the earth; / even there, such conduct in truth and falsehood exists in the world.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmādharmauṃ prakāśaśca tamo duḥkhasukhaṃ tathā /
śārīrairmānasairduḥkhaiḥ sukhaiścāpyasukhodayaiḥ //
meaning:
धर्माधर्मौं प्रकाशश्च तमो दुःखसुखं तथा /
शारीरैर्मानसैर्दुःखैः सुखैश्चाप्यसुखोदयैः //
text_mt: Righteousness and unrighteousness, light and darkness, as well as pleasure and pain; / by bodily and mental pains, and by pleasures that lead to unhappiness,

sanskrit_iast:
lokasṛṣṭaṃ prapaśyanto na muhyanti vicakṣaṇāḥ /
tatra duḥkhavimokṣārthaṃ prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ //
meaning:
लोकसृष्टं प्रपश्यन्तो न मुह्यन्ति विचक्षणाः /
तत्र दुःखविमोक्षार्थं प्रयतेत विचक्षणः //
text_mt: Discerning people, observing what has been produced in the world, are not bewildered. / Therefore, the discerning person should strive for release from suffering.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaṃ hyanityaṃ bhūtānāmiha loke paratra ca /
rāhugrastasya somasya yathā jyotsnā na bhāsate //
meaning:
सुखं ह्यनित्यं भूतानामिह लोके परत्र च /
राहुग्रस्तस्य सोमस्य यथा ज्योत्स्ना न भासते //
text_mt: Pleasure is indeed impermanent for living beings in this world and in the next. / Just as the moonlight of the moon seized by Rāhu does not shine,

sanskrit_iast: tathā tamobhibhūtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ naśyate sukham //
meaning: तथा तमोभिभूतानां भूतानां नश्यते सुखम् //
text_mt: So the happiness of beings overcome by darkness is destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
tatkhalu dvividhaṃ sukhamucyacate śarīraṃ mānasaṃ ca /
iha khalvamuṣmiṃśca loke vastupravṛttayaḥ sukhārthamabhidhīyante nahītaḥ paratrāparvagaphalādviśiṣṭataramasti /
sa eva kāmyo guṇaviśeṣo dharmārthaguṇāraṃbhagastaddheturasyotpattiḥ sukhaprayojanārthamāraṃbhāḥ /
bharadvāja uvāca
vadaitadbhavatābhihitaṃ sukhānāṃ paramā sthitiriti //
meaning:
तत्खलु द्विविधं सुखमुच्यचते शरीरं मानसं च /
इह खल्वमुष्मिंश्च लोके वस्तुप्रवृत्तयः सुखार्थमभिधीयन्ते नहीतः परत्रापर्वगफलाद्विशिष्टतरमस्ति /
स एव काम्यो गुणविशेषो धर्मार्थगुणारंभगस्तद्धेतुरस्योत्पत्तिः सुखप्रयोजनार्थमारंभाः /
भरद्वाज उवाच
वदैतद्भवताभिहितं सुखानां परमा स्थितिरिति //
text_mt: Indeed, pleasure is said to be of two kinds: bodily and mental. / In this world and in the other world, the pursuits of objects are designated for the sake of happiness; for there is nothing higher than the fruit of final liberation beyond this. / That desirable, distinguished quality itself is the beginning of the qualities of dharma and artha, the cause of which is its production; undertakings are for the sake of happiness. / Bharadvāja said: / Speak of this which was stated by you, that this is the highest state among pleasures.

sanskrit_iast: na tadupagṛhṇīmo na hyeṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ mahati sthitānām //
meaning: न तदुपगृह्णीमो न ह्येषामृषीणां महति स्थितानाम् //
text_mt: We do not accept that, for it does not belong to these sages established in greatness.

sanskrit_iast:
aprāpya eṣa kāmya guṇaviśeṣo na cainamabhiśīlayanti /
tapasi śrūyate trilokakṛdbrahmā prabhurekākī tiṣṭati brahmacārī na kāmasukhoṣvātmānamavadadhāti //
meaning:
अप्राप्य एष काम्य गुणविशेषो न चैनमभिशीलयन्ति /
तपसि श्रूयते त्रिलोककृद्ब्रह्मा प्रभुरेकाकी तिष्टति ब्रह्मचारी न कामसुखोष्वात्मानमवदधाति //
text_mt: This desirable, distinguished quality is unobtainable, and they do not cultivate it. / In austerity, it is heard that the creator of the three worlds, Lord Brahmā, stands alone, chaste, and does not fix his self on the pleasures of desire.

sanskrit_iast: api ca bhagavānviśveśvara umāpatiḥ kāmamabhivartamānamanaṅgatvena samamanayat //
meaning: अपि च भगवान्विश्वेश्वर उमापतिः काममभिवर्तमानमनङ्गत्वेन सममनयत् //
text_mt: Moreover, the venerable Lord of the Universe, the husband of Umā, reduced desire, as it was approaching, to bodilessness.

sanskrit_iast: tasmādbhūmau na tu mahātmabhirañjayati gṛhīto na tveṣa tāvadviśiṣṭo guṇaviśeṣa iti //
meaning: तस्माद्भूमौ न तु महात्मभिरञ्जयति गृहीतो न त्वेष तावद्विशिष्टो गुणविशेष इति //
text_mt: Therefore on earth, it is not joyfully accepted by great-souled persons; nor is this distinguished quality superior.

sanskrit_iast: naitadbhagavataḥ pratyemi bhavatā tūktaṃ sukhānāṃ paramāḥ striya iti lokapravādo hi dvividhaḥ phalodayaḥ sukṛtātsukhamavāpyate 'nyathā duḥkhamiti //
