meaning: नैतद्भगवतः प्रत्येमि भवता तूक्तं सुखानां परमाः स्त्रिय इति लोकप्रवादो हि द्विविधः फलोदयः सुकृतात्सुखमवाप्यते ऽन्यथा दुःखमिति //
text_mt: I do not believe this of the lord; yet it was said by you that women are the supreme among pleasures. For popular saying holds that the fruition of actions is twofold: happiness is attained from good deeds, and suffering otherwise.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
atrocyate anṛtātkhalu tamaḥ prādurbhūtaṃ tatastamograstā adharmamevānuvartante na dharmaṃ krodhalobhamohahiṃsānṛtādibhikhacchannāḥ khalvasmiṃlloke nāmutra sukhamāpnuvanti vividhavyādhirujopatāpairavakīryante vadhabandhanaparikleśādibhiśca kṣutpipāsāśramakṛtairupatāpairupatapyante varṣavātātyuṣṇātiśītakṛtaiśca pratibhayaiḥ śārīrairduḥkhairupatapyante bandhudhanavināśaviprayogakṛtaiśca mānasaiḥ śaukairabhibhūyante jarāmṛtyukṛtaiścānyairiti yastvetaiḥ //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
अत्रोच्यते अनृतात्खलु तमः प्रादुर्भूतं ततस्तमोग्रस्ता अधर्ममेवानुवर्तन्ते न धर्मं क्रोधलोभमोहहिंसानृतादिभिखच्छन्नाः खल्वस्मिंल्लोके नामुत्र सुखमाप्नुवन्ति विविधव्याधिरुजोपतापैरवकीर्यन्ते वधबन्धनपरिक्लेशादिभिश्च क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमकृतैरुपतापैरुपतप्यन्ते वर्षवातात्युष्णातिशीतकृतैश्च प्रतिभयैः शारीरैर्दुःखैरुपतप्यन्ते बन्धुधनविनाशविप्रयोगकृतैश्च मानसैः शौकैरभिभूयन्ते जरामृत्युकृतैश्चान्यैरिति यस्त्वेतैः //
text_mt:
Bhṛgu said:
Here it is said: From falsehood indeed darkness arose; then, seized by darkness, they pursue only adharma, not dharma. Veiled by anger, greed, delusion, violence, falsehood, and the like, they indeed obtain no happiness in this world nor in the next. They are strewn with diverse sicknesses, aches, and afflictions; they are tormented by afflictions caused by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, and by slaughters, bondages, distress, and the like; they are tormented by bodily sorrows born of fear, caused by rain, wind, extreme heat, and extreme cold; they are overwhelmed by mental griefs caused by the destruction and separation from kin and wealth, and by others caused by old age and death. But he who, by these—

sanskrit_iast:
śārīraṃ mānasaṃ nāsti na jarā na ca pātakam /
nityameva sukhaṃ svarge sukhaṃ duḥkhamihobhayam //
meaning:
शारीरं मानसं नास्ति न जरा न च पातकम् /
नित्यमेव सुखं स्वर्गे सुखं दुःखमिहोभयम् //
text_mt: There is no bodily or mental [affliction], nor old age, nor sin; / there is only constant happiness in heaven; here [in this world] there are both happiness and sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
narake duḥkhamevāhuḥ sukhaṃ tatparamaṃ padam /
pṛthivī sarvabhūtānāṃ janitrī tadvidhāḥ striyaḥ //
meaning:
नरके दुःखमेवाहुः सुखं तत्परमं पदम् /
पृथिवी सर्वभूतानां जनित्री तद्विधाः स्त्रियः //
text_mt: In hell, they say, there is only sorrow; that supreme abode is bliss. / The earth is the mother of all beings, and women are of the same nature.

sanskrit_iast:
pumānprajāpatistatraśukraṃ tejomayaṃ viduḥ /
ityetallokanirmātā dharmasya caritasya ca //
meaning:
पुमान्प्रजापतिस्तत्रशुक्रं तेजोमयं विदुः /
इत्येतल्लोकनिर्माता धर्मस्य चरितस्य च //
text_mt: The male is Prajāpati in that regard; they know his semen to be full of fiery energy. / Thus he is the creator of the world, of righteousness, and of good conduct,

sanskrit_iast:
tapasaśca sutaptasya svādhyāyasya hutasya ca /
hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ svādhyāye śāntiruttamā //
meaning:
तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य स्वाध्यायस्य हुतस्य च /
हुतेन शाम्यते पापं स्वाध्याये शान्तिरुत्तमा //
text_mt: and of well-performed austerity, of personal Vedic study, and of oblations. / By oblations sin is pacified; in personal study lies the highest tranquility.

sanskrit_iast:
dānena bhogānityāhusta pasā svargamāpnuyāt /
dānaṃ tu dvividhaṃ prāhuḥ paratrārthamihaiva ca //
meaning:
दानेन भोगानित्याहुस्त पसा स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
दानं तु द्विविधं प्राहुः परत्रार्थमिहैव च //
text_mt: They say that through giving one obtains enjoyments; through austerity one may attain heaven. / But giving they declare to be twofold: for the next world, and for this world alone.

sanskrit_iast:
sadbhyo yaddīyate kiñcittatparatropatiṣṭate /
asadbhyo dīyate yattu taddānamiha bhujyate /
yādṛśaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tādṛśaṃ phalamaśnute //
meaning:
सद्भ्यो यद्दीयते किञ्चित्तत्परत्रोपतिष्टते /
असद्भ्यो दीयते यत्तु तद्दानमिह भुज्यते /
यादृशं दीयते दानं तादृशं फलमश्नुते //
text_mt: Whatever is given to the virtuous waits [for the giver] in the next world; / but what is given to the unvirtuous is enjoyed [as a gift] here in this world. / Just as the gift that is given, so is the fruit that one experiences.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
kiṃ kasya dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃ vā dharmasya lakṣaṇam /
dharmaḥ katividho vāpi tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
किं कस्य धर्मचरणं किं वा धर्मस्य लक्षणम् /
धर्मः कतिविधो वापि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / What is the practice of righteousness for whom, and what is the mark of righteousness? / Or of how many kinds is righteousness? You ought to explain that.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
svadharmācaraṇe yuktā ye bhavanti manīṣiṇaḥ /
teṣāṃ svargapalāvāptiryo 'nyathā sa vimuhyate //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
स्वधर्माचरणे युक्ता ये भवन्ति मनीषिणः /
तेषां स्वर्गपलावाप्तिर्यो ऽन्यथा स विमुह्यते //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / Those wise men who are engaged in practicing their own duty, / attain the fruit of heaven; he who acts otherwise becomes deluded.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadetañcāturāśramyaṃ brahmarṣivihitaṃ purā /
teṣāṃ sve sve samācārāstanme vaktumihārhasi //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यदेतञ्चातुराश्रम्यं ब्रह्मर्षिविहितं पुरा /
तेषां स्वे स्वे समाचारास्तन्मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / This system of four stages of life which was ordained of old by the Brahmin seers— / you ought to tell me here the respective practices proper to them.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
pūrvameva bhagavatā brahmaṇā lokahitamanutiṣṭatā dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthamāśramāścatvāro 'bhinirddiṣṭāḥ //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
पूर्वमेव भगवता ब्रह्मणा लोकहितमनुतिष्टता धर्मसंरक्षणार्थमाश्रमाश्चत्वारो ऽभिनिर्द्दिष्टाः //
text_mt: Bhṛgu said: / In the very beginning, the four stages of life were prescribed by the blessed Lord Brahmā, who was acting for the welfare of the world, for the purpose of preserving righteousness.

sanskrit_iast: tatra gurukulavāsameva prathamamāśramamāharanti samyagatra śaucasaskāraniyamavrataviniyatātmā ubhe saṃdhye bhāskarāgnidaivatānyupasthāya vihāya taddhyālasyaṃ gurorabhivādanavedābyāsaśravaṇapavitraghīkṛtāntarātmā triṣavaṇamupaspṛśya brahmacaryāgniparicaraṇaguruśuśrūṣā nityabhikṣābhaikṣyādisarvaniveditāntarātmā guruvacananideśānuṣṭānāpratikūlo guruprasādalabdhasvādhyāyatatparaḥ syāt //
meaning: तत्र गुरुकुलवासमेव प्रथममाश्रममाहरन्ति सम्यगत्र शौचसस्कारनियमव्रतविनियतात्मा उभे संध्ये भास्कराग्निदैवतान्युपस्थाय विहाय तद्ध्यालस्यं गुरोरभिवादनवेदाब्यासश्रवणपवित्रघीकृतान्तरात्मा त्रिषवणमुपस्पृश्य ब्रह्मचर्याग्निपरिचरणगुरुशुश्रूषा नित्यभिक्षाभैक्ष्यादिसर्वनिवेदितान्तरात्मा गुरुवचननिदेशानुष्टानाप्रतिकूलो गुरुप्रसादलब्धस्वाध्यायतत्परः स्यात् //
text_mt: There, they declare living in the teacher's family to be the first stage of life. In this stage, having his self completely restrained by purity, sacraments, observances, and vows; having worshipped the sun, fire, and deities at both twilights; having cast aside sleep and laziness; having his inner self purified by saluting the teacher, Vedic study, and listening [to instruction]; having bathed at the three junctions of the day; devoted to chastity, attending to the sacred fire, service to the teacher, daily begging for alms, and offering his entire inner self [and food received] from alms and the like; never opposed to following the words and directions of the teacher; he should be intent on personal Vedic study obtained through the teacher's favor.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavati cātra ślokaḥ
guruṃ yastu samārādhya dvijo vedamāvānpuyāt /
tasya svargaphalāvāptiḥ siddhyate cāsya mānasam /
iti gārhasthyaṃ khalu dvitīyamāśramaṃ vadanti //
meaning:
भवति चात्र श्लोकः
गुरुं यस्तु समाराध्य द्विजो वेदमावान्पुयात् /
तस्य स्वर्गफलावाप्तिः सिद्ध्यते चास्य मानसम् /
इति गार्हस्थ्यं खलु द्वितीयमाश्रमं वदन्ति //
text_mt: And there is a verse on this: / But that twice-born man who, having worshipped his teacher, obtains the Veda, / attains the fruit of heaven, and his mental desire is accomplished. / Thus they indeed declare householdership to be the second stage of life.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya sadā cāralakṣaṇaṃ sarvamanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
samāvṛtānāṃ sadācārāṇāṃ sahadharmacaryaphalārthināṃ gṛhāśramo vidhīyate //
meaning:
तस्य सदा चारलक्षणं सर्वमनुव्याख्यास्यामः /
समावृतानां सदाचाराणां सहधर्मचर्यफलार्थिनां गृहाश्रमो विधीयते //
text_mt: We shall expound all the characteristics of its good conduct. / The householder stage is prescribed for those who have returned home [from studenthood], who possess good conduct, and who desire the fruits of joint performance of duty.

sanskrit_iast: dharmārthakāmāvāptirhya.tra trivargasādhanamapekṣyāgarhitakarmaṇā dhanānyādāya svādhyāyopalabdhaprakarṣeṇa vā brahmarṣinirmitena vā adbhiḥ sāgaragatena vā dravyaniyamābhyāsadaivataprasādopalabdhena vā dhanena gṛhastho gārhasthyaṃ vartayet //
meaning: धर्मार्थकामावाप्तिर्ह्य.त्र त्रिवर्गसाधनमपेक्ष्यागर्हितकर्मणा धनान्यादाय स्वाध्यायोपलब्धप्रकर्षेण वा ब्रह्मर्षिनिर्मितेन वा अद्भिः सागरगतेन वा द्रव्यनियमाभ्यासदैवतप्रसादोपलब्धेन वा धनेन गृहस्थो गार्हस्थ्यं वर्तयेत् //
text_mt: For herein lies the attainment of duty, wealth, and pleasure, with a view to the cultivation of the three aims of life. Having acquired wealth through blameless occupations, or by excellence obtained through personal Vedic study, or that established by Brahmin seers, or by crossing the ocean on waters, or by wealth obtained through disciplined pursuit of possessions or the grace of the deities, the householder should maintain householdership.

sanskrit_iast: taddhi sarvāśramaṇāṃ mūlamudāharanti gurukulanivāsinaḥ parivrājakā ye 'nye saṃkalpitavrataniyamadharmānuṣṭāninasteṣāmapyantarā ca bhikṣābalisaṃvibhāgāḥ pravartante //
meaning: तद्धि सर्वाश्रमणां मूलमुदाहरन्ति गुरुकुलनिवासिनः परिव्राजका ये ऽन्ये संकल्पितव्रतनियमधर्मानुष्टानिनस्तेषामप्यन्तरा च भिक्षाबलिसंविभागाः प्रवर्तन्ते //
text_mt: For they declare that to be the foundation of all stages of life. For those dwelling in the teacher's household, for wandering mendicants, and for others who practice vows, observances, and duties they have undertaken—even in between these, the distributions of alms and offerings proceed [from him].

sanskrit_iast: vānaprasthānāṃ ca dravyopaskāra iti prāyaśaḥ khalvete sādhavaḥ sādhupathyodanāḥ svādhyāyaprasaṃginastīrthābhigamanadeśadarśanārthaṃ pṛthivīṃ paryaṭanti //
meaning: वानप्रस्थानां च द्रव्योपस्कार इति प्रायशः खल्वेते साधवः साधुपथ्योदनाः स्वाध्यायप्रसंगिनस्तीर्थाभिगमनदेशदर्शनार्थं पृथिवीं पर्यटन्ति //
text_mt: And there is the provision of materials for forest hermits. For mostly these virtuous men, having wholesome food suitable for the virtuous, engaged in personal study of the Veda, wander the earth for the purpose of visiting sacred fords and seeing various countries.

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ pratyutthānābhigamanamanasūyāvākyadānasukhasatkārāsanasukhaśayanābhyavahārasatkriyā ceti //
meaning: तेषां प्रत्युत्थानाभिगमनमनसूयावाक्यदानसुखसत्कारासनसुखशयनाभ्यवहारसत्क्रिया चेति //
text_mt: For them, there is rising to welcome them, going out to greet them, speaking words free from envy, providing comfortable hospitality, seats, comfortable beds, and food.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavati cātra ślokaḥ
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate /
sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyamādāya gacchati //
meaning:
भवति चात्र श्लोकः
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते /
स दत्त्वा दुष्कृतं तस्मै पुण्यमादाय गच्छति //
text_mt: And there is a verse on this: / A guest who turns away from a house disappointed in his hopes, / having given his bad deeds to that [householder], goes away taking the [householder's] merit.

sanskrit_iast: api cātra yajñakriyābhirdevatāḥ prīyante nivāpena pitaro vidyābhyāsaśravaṇadhāraṇena ṛṣayaḥ apatyotpādanena prajāpatiriti //
meaning: अपि चात्र यज्ञक्रियाभिर्देवताः प्रीयन्ते निवापेन पितरो विद्याभ्यासश्रवणधारणेन ऋषयः अपत्योत्पादनेन प्रजापतिरिति //
text_mt: Moreover, in this stage deities are pleased through sacrificial rites, the ancestors through the libation of water, the seers through the study, hearing, and retention of sacred knowledge, and Prajāpati through the procreation of offspring.

sanskrit_iast:
lokau cātra bhavataḥ
vātsalyāḥ sarvabhūtebhyo vāyoḥ śrotrastathā girā /
paritāpodapaghātaśca pāruṣyaṃ cātra garhitam //
meaning:
लोकौ चात्र भवतः
वात्सल्याः सर्वभूतेभ्यो वायोः श्रोत्रस्तथा गिरा /
परितापोदपघातश्च पारुष्यं चात्र गर्हितम् //
text_mt: And there are two verses on this: / Affection toward all beings, in hearing the wind, and in speech; / and causing torment, injury, and harshness are condemned here.

sanskrit_iast:
avajñānamahṝṅkāro daṃbhaścaiva vigarhitaḥ /
ahiṃsā satyamakrodaṃ sarvāśramagataṃ tapaḥ //
meaning:
अवज्ञानमहॄङ्कारो दंभश्चैव विगर्हितः /
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोदं सर्वाश्रमगतं तपः //
text_mt: Disrespect, egotism, and hypocrisy are also thoroughly condemned; / non-injury, truth, and freedom from anger are the austerity common to all stages of life.

sanskrit_iast: api cātra mālyābharaṇavastrābhyaṅganityopabhoganṛtyagītavāditraśrutisukhanayanasneharāmādarśanānāṃ prāptirbhakṣyabhojyalehyapeyacoṣyāṇāmabhyavahāryyāṇāṃ vividhānāmupabhogaḥ //
meaning: अपि चात्र माल्याभरणवस्त्राभ्यङ्गनित्योपभोगनृत्यगीतवादित्रश्रुतिसुखनयनस्नेहरामादर्शनानां प्राप्तिर्भक्ष्यभोज्यलेह्यपेयचोष्याणामभ्यवहार्य्याणां विविधानामुपभोगः //
text_mt: Moreover, in this stage there is the continuous enjoyment of garlands, ornaments, clothes, and anointing, along with the pleasure of hearing dance, song, and musical instruments, the viewing of charming women that gladdens the eyes, and the consumption of various kinds of edibles: chewables, foodstuffs, licked dishes, beverages, and foods to be sucked.

sanskrit_iast:
svavihārasaṃtoṣaḥ kāmasukhāvāptiriti /
trivargaguṇanirvṛttiryasya nityaṃ gṛhāśrame /
sa sukhānyanubhūyeha śiṣṭānāṃ gatimāpnuyāt //
meaning:
स्वविहारसंतोषः कामसुखावाप्तिरिति /
त्रिवर्गगुणनिर्वृत्तिर्यस्य नित्यं गृहाश्रमे /
स सुखान्यनुभूयेह शिष्टानां गतिमाप्नुयात् //
text_mt: There is satisfaction in one's own pleasures and attainment of the joy of desires. / He in whose household stage the qualities of the three aims of life are constantly fulfilled, / having experienced pleasures here, will attain the destination of the virtuous.

sanskrit_iast:
uñchavṛttirvṛhastho yaḥ svadhama caraṇe rataḥ /
tyaktakāmasukhāraṃbhaḥ svargastasya na durlabhaḥ //
meaning:
उञ्छवृत्तिर्वृहस्थो यः स्वधम चरणे रतः /
त्यक्तकामसुखारंभः स्वर्गस्तस्य न दुर्लभः //
text_mt: The householder who lives by gleaning ears of grain, devoted to practicing his own duty, / who has abandoned the pursuit of sensual pleasure, finds heaven not difficult to attain.

sanskrit_iast: vānaprasthāḥ khalvapi dharmamanusarantaḥ puṇyāni tīrthāni nadīprastravaṇāni svabhakteṣvaraṇyeṣu mṛgavarāhamahiṣa śārdūlavanagajākīrṇeṣu tapasyante anusaṃcaranti //
meaning: वानप्रस्थाः खल्वपि धर्ममनुसरन्तः पुण्यानि तीर्थानि नदीप्रस्त्रवणानि स्वभक्तेष्वरण्येषु मृगवराहमहिष शार्दूलवनगजाकीर्णेषु तपस्यन्ते अनुसंचरन्ति //
text_mt: Moreover, the forest hermits, following duty, practice austerities and wander about sacred fords, rivers, waterfalls, and forests dear to them that are teeming with deer, boars, buffaloes, tigers, and wild elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
tyaktagrāmyavastrābhyavahāropabhogā vanyauṣadhiphalamūlaparṇaparimitavicitraniyatāhārāḥ sthānāsaninobhūpāṣāṇasikatāśarkarāvālukābhasmaśāyinaḥ kāśukuśacarmavalkalasaṃvṛtāṅgāḥ keśaśyaśrunakharomadhāriṇo niyatakālopasparśanāḥśuṣkabalihomakālānuṣṭāyinaḥ /
samitkuśakusumāpahārasaṃmārjanalabdhaviśrāmāḥ śītoṣṇapavanaviṣṭaṃ bhavibhinnasarvatvaco vividhaniyamayogacaryānuṣṭānavihitapariśuṣkamāṃsaśoṇitatvagasthibhūtā dhṛtiparāḥ sattvayogāccharīrāṇyudvahṝnte //
meaning:
त्यक्तग्राम्यवस्त्राभ्यवहारोपभोगा वन्यौषधिफलमूलपर्णपरिमितविचित्रनियताहाराः स्थानासनिनोभूपाषाणसिकताशर्करावालुकाभस्मशायिनः काशुकुशचर्मवल्कलसंवृताङ्गाः केशश्यश्रुनखरोमधारिणो नियतकालोपस्पर्शनाःशुष्कबलिहोमकालानुष्टायिनः /
समित्कुशकुसुमापहारसंमार्जनलब्धविश्रामाः शीतोष्णपवनविष्टं भविभिन्नसर्वत्वचो विविधनियमयोगचर्यानुष्टानविहितपरिशुष्कमांसशोणितत्वगस्थिभूता धृतिपराः सत्त्वयोगाच्छरीराण्युद्वहॄन्ते //
text_mt: They have abandoned village clothing, food, and enjoyments; their food is measured, varied, and strictly regulated, consisting of wild herbs, fruits, roots, and leaves; standing and sitting, they sleep on the earth, stones, gravel, grit, sand, and ashes; their limbs are covered with kāśa grass, kuśa grass, hides, and bark-cloth; they bear hair, beards, nails, and body-hair; bathing at fixed times, observing the times for dry offerings and fire oblations; / finding rest in collecting kindling, kuśa grass, and flowers, and in sweeping; having their entire skin cracked by exposure to cold, heat, and wind; reduced to skin and bones with their flesh and blood dried up by the performance of various rules and practices of yoga; devoted to steadfastness, they bear their bodies through the power of purity.

sanskrit_iast:
yastvetāṃ niyatacaryāṃ brahmarṣivihitāṃ caret /
sa dahedagnivaddoṣāñjayellokāṃśca durjāyān //
meaning:
यस्त्वेतां नियतचर्यां ब्रह्मर्षिविहितां चरेत् /
स दहेदग्निवद्दोषाञ्जयेल्लोकांश्च दुर्जायान् //
text_mt: He who practices this regulated conduct prescribed by the Brahmin seers / will burn away blemishes like fire and conquer worlds that are hard to win.

sanskrit_iast:
parivrājakānāṃ punarācāraḥ tadyathā /
vimucyāgniṃ dhanakalatraparibarhasaṃgeṣvātmānaṃ snehapāśānavadhūya parivrajanti /
samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanāstrivargapravṛtteṣvasaktabuddhayaḥ //
meaning:
परिव्राजकानां पुनराचारः तद्यथा /
विमुच्याग्निं धनकलत्रपरिबर्हसंगेष्वात्मानं स्नेहपाशानवधूय परिव्रजन्ति /
समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनास्त्रिवर्गप्रवृत्तेष्वसक्तबुद्धयः //
text_mt: Now, the conduct of wandering mendicants is as follows: / Having relinquished the sacred fire, having cast off the ties of affection in regard to wealth, wife, and attachments to possessions, they wander forth, / viewing a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal, their minds detached from pursuits concerning the three aims of life.

sanskrit_iast: arimitrodāsīnāṃ tulyadarśanāḥ sthāvarajarāyujāṇḍajasvedajānāṃ bhūtānāṃ vāṅmanṛḥkarmabhiranabhiranabhidrohiṇo 'niketāḥ parvatapulinavṛkṣamūladevāyatanānyanusaṃcaranto vā sārthamupeyurnagaraṃ grāmaṃ vā na krodhadarpalobhamohakārpaṇyadaṃbhaparivādābhimānanirvṛttahiṃsā iti //
meaning: अरिमित्रोदासीनां तुल्यदर्शनाः स्थावरजरायुजाण्डजस्वेदजानां भूतानां वाङ्मनृःकर्मभिरनभिरनभिद्रोहिणो ऽनिकेताः पर्वतपुलिनवृक्षमूलदेवायतनान्यनुसंचरन्तो वा सार्थमुपेयुर्नगरं ग्रामं वा न क्रोधदर्पलोभमोहकार्पण्यदंभपरिवादाभिमाननिर्वृत्तहिंसा इति //
text_mt: Regarding enemies, friends, and indifferent persons with an equal eye; harmless in speech, mind, and action towards living beings that are stationary, womb-born, egg-born, or sweat-born; homeless, wandering through mountains, sandbanks, the roots of trees, and temples; or they may enter a caravan, city, or village; their violence has ceased through the elimination of anger, pride, greed, delusion, miserliness, deceit, slander, and egotism.

sanskrit_iast:
bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā yaścarate muniḥ /
na tasya sarvabhūtebhyo bhayamutpadyate kvacit //
meaning:
भवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाः
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यश्चरते मुनिः /
न तस्य सर्वभूतेभ्यो भयमुत्पद्यते क्वचित् //
text_mt: And there are verses on this: / The sage who wanders having granted safety to all beings— / from no beings does fear arise for him anywhere.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvāgnihotraṃ svaśarīrasaṃsthaṃ śarīramagniṃ svamukhe juhoti /
viprastu bhaikṣopagatairhavirbhiścitā gninā saṃvrajate hi sokān //
meaning:
कृत्वाग्निहोत्रं स्वशरीरसंस्थं शरीरमग्निं स्वमुखे जुहोति /
विप्रस्तु भैक्षोपगतैर्हविर्भिश्चिता ग्निना संव्रजते हि सोकान् //
text_mt: Having established the agnihotra within his own body, he offers his body-fire into his own mouth; / a Brahmin who offers with oblations obtained from alms goes with his accumulated fire to the worlds of light.

sanskrit_iast:
mokṣāśramaṃ yaścarate yathoktaṃ śuciḥ svasaṃkalpitayuktabuddhiḥ /
anindhanaṃ jyotiriva praśāntaṃ sa brahmalokaṃ śrayate dvijātiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bhṛgubharadvājasaṃvāde brāhmaṇācāranirūpaṇaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
मोक्षाश्रमं यश्चरते यथोक्तं शुचिः स्वसंकल्पितयुक्तबुद्धिः /
अनिन्धनं ज्योतिरिव प्रशान्तं स ब्रह्मलोकं श्रयते द्विजातिः //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे भृगुभरद्वाजसंवादे ब्राह्मणाचारनिरूपणं नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
The twice-born who practices the stage of life leading to liberation as taught, pure, with an intellect concentrated on his own intention, / attains the world of Brahmā, tranquil like a fire without fuel.

Thus ends the forty-third chapter, entitled "Exposition of the Conduct of Brāhmaṇas", in the dialogue between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja in the second quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
asmāllokātparo lokaḥ śrūyate nopalabhyate /
tamahaṃ jñātumicchāmi tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
अस्माल्लोकात्परो लोकः श्रूयते नोपलभ्यते /
तमहं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति //
text_mt:
Bharadvāja said:
A world beyond this world is heard of, but not perceived. / I wish to know about it; you ought to tell me that.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛguruvāca
uttare himavatpārśve puṇye sarvaguṇānvite /
puṇyaḥ kṣemyaśca kāmyaśca sa paro loka ucyate //
meaning:
मृगुरुवाच
उत्तरे हिमवत्पार्श्वे पुण्ये सर्वगुणान्विते /
पुण्यः क्षेम्यश्च काम्यश्च स परो लोक उच्यते //
text_mt:
Bhṛgu said:
On the northern side of the Himavat, sacred and endowed with all virtues, / holy, secure, and desirable, that is called the world beyond.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra hyapāpakarmāṇaḥ śucayo 'tyantanirmalāḥ /
lobhamohaparityaktā mānavā nirupadravāḥ //
meaning:
तत्र ह्यपापकर्माणः शुचयो ऽत्यन्तनिर्मलाः /
लोभमोहपरित्यक्ता मानवा निरुपद्रवाः //
text_mt: For there men are of sinless deeds, pure, exceedingly spotless, / free from greed and delusion, and without affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
sa svargasadṛśo deśaḥ tatra hyuktāḥ śubhā guṇāḥ /
kāle mṛtyuḥ prabavati spṛśanti vyādhayo na ca //
meaning:
स स्वर्गसदृशो देशः तत्र ह्युक्ताः शुभा गुणाः /
काले मृत्युः प्रबवति स्पृशन्ति व्याधयो न च //
text_mt: That region is like heaven, for auspicious qualities are declared there. / Death occurs [only] at the appointed time, and diseases do not touch [them].

sanskrit_iast:
na lobaḥ paradāreṣu svadāranirato janaḥ /
nānyo hi vadhyate tatra dravyeṣu ca na vismayaḥ //
meaning:
न लोबः परदारेषु स्वदारनिरतो जनः /
नान्यो हि वध्यते तत्र द्रव्येषु च न विस्मयः //
text_mt: There is no desire for another's wife; people are devoted to their own wives. / Indeed, no other person is slain there, nor is there greed for possessions.

sanskrit_iast:
paro hyadharmo naivāsti saṃdeho nāpi jāyate /
kṛtasya tu phalaṃ tatra pratyakṣamupalabhyate //
meaning:
परो ह्यधर्मो नैवास्ति संदेहो नापि जायते /
कृतस्य तु फलं तत्र प्रत्यक्षमुपलभ्यते //
text_mt: For supreme adharma does not exist at all, nor does doubt arise; / and the fruit of what is done is directly perceived there.

sanskrit_iast:
yānāsanāśanopetā prasādabhavanāśrayāḥ /
sarvakāmairvṛtāḥ keciddhemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ //
meaning:
यानासनाशनोपेता प्रसादभवनाश्रयाः /
सर्वकामैर्वृताः केचिद्धेमाभरणभूषिताः //
text_mt: Endowed with vehicles, seats, and food, dwelling in palaces, / some are surrounded by all desirable things and adorned with golden ornaments.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇadhāraṇamātraṃ tu keṣāñcidupapadyate /
śrameṇa mahatā kecitkurvanti prāṇadhāraṇam //
meaning:
प्राणधारणमात्रं तु केषाञ्चिदुपपद्यते /
श्रमेण महता केचित्कुर्वन्ति प्राणधारणम् //
text_mt: For some, however, only mere sustenance of life is obtained; / some maintain their life only with great toil.

sanskrit_iast:
iha dharmaparāḥ kecitkecinnaiṣkṛtikā narāḥ /
sukhitā duḥkhitāḥ kecinnirdhanā dhanino pare //
meaning:
इह धर्मपराः केचित्केचिन्नैष्कृतिका नराः /
सुखिता दुःखिताः केचिन्निर्धना धनिनो परे //
text_mt: Here [on earth] some men are devoted to dharma, while some are deceitful; / some are happy, some are sorrowful; some are penniless, others wealthy.

sanskrit_iast:
iha śramo bhayaṃ mohaḥ kṣudhā tīvrā ca jāyate /
lobhaścārthakṛto tṝṇāṃ yena muhyantyapaṇḍitāḥ //
meaning:
इह श्रमो भयं मोहः क्षुधा तीव्रा च जायते /
लोभश्चार्थकृतो तॄणां येन मुह्यन्त्यपण्डिताः //
text_mt: Here fatigue, fear, delusion, and intense hunger arise, / as well as greed caused by wealth among men, by which fools are deluded.

sanskrit_iast:
yastadvedo bhayaṃ prājñaḥ pāpmanā na sa lipyate /
sopadhe nikṛtiḥ steyaṃ parivādo 'bhyasūyatā //
meaning:
यस्तद्वेदो भयं प्राज्ञः पाप्मना न स लिप्यते /
सोपधे निकृतिः स्तेयं परिवादो ऽभ्यसूयता //
text_mt: The wise man who knows that danger is not tainted by evil. / Fraud with deception, theft, slander, malice,

sanskrit_iast:
paropaghāto hiṃsā ca paiśunmanṛtaṃ tathā /
etānsaṃsevate yastu tapastasya prahīyate //
meaning:
परोपघातो हिंसा च पैशुन्मनृतं तथा /
एतान्संसेवते यस्तु तपस्तस्य प्रहीयते //
text_mt: injury to others, violence, calumny, and falsehood— / whoever practices these, his austerity diminishes.

sanskrit_iast:
yastvetānācaredvidvānna tapastasya varddhate /
iha cintā bahuvidhā dharmādharmasya karmaṇaḥ //
meaning:
यस्त्वेतानाचरेद्विद्वान्न तपस्तस्य वर्द्धते /
इह चिन्ता बहुविधा धर्माधर्मस्य कर्मणः //
text_mt: And if an educated man practices these, his austerity does not grow. / Here there are many kinds of anxiety concerning actions of dharma and adharma.

sanskrit_iast:
karmabhūmiriyaṃ loke iha kṛtvā śubhāśubham /
śubhaiḥ śubhamavāpnoti tathāśubhamathānyathā //
meaning:
कर्मभूमिरियं लोके इह कृत्वा शुभाशुभम् /
शुभैः शुभमवाप्नोति तथाशुभमथान्यथा //
text_mt: This world is the land of action; having done auspicious and inauspicious deeds here, / one attains good by good [deeds], and likewise bad through the opposite.

sanskrit_iast:
iha prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāstathā /
iṣṭeṣṭatapasaḥ pūtā brahmalokamupāśritāḥ //
meaning:
इह प्रजापतिः पूर्वं देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा /
इष्टेष्टतपसः पूता ब्रह्मलोकमुपाश्रिताः //
text_mt: Here formerly Prajāpati, the gods, and hosts of sages, / having offered sacrifices and performed desired austerities, became purified and resorted to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit_iast:
uttaraḥ pṛthivībhāgaḥ sarvapuṇyatamaḥ śubhaḥ /
ihasthāstatra jāyante ye vai puṇyakṛto janāḥ //
meaning:
उत्तरः पृथिवीभागः सर्वपुण्यतमः शुभः /
इहस्थास्तत्र जायन्ते ये वै पुण्यकृतो जनाः //
text_mt: The northern part of the earth is the most sacred of all and auspicious; / those people living here who perform holy deeds are born there.

sanskrit_iast:
yadi satkāramicchanti tiryagyoniṣu cāpare /
kṣīṇāyuṣastathā cānye naśyanti pṛthivītale //
meaning:
यदि सत्कारमिच्छन्ति तिर्यग्योनिषु चापरे /
क्षीणायुषस्तथा चान्ये नश्यन्ति पृथिवीतले //
text_mt: If they desire honour [they may go there], while others [fall] into animal wombs; / and others, their lifespans exhausted, perish on the surface of the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
anyonyabhakṣaṇāsaktā lobhamohasamanvitāḥ /
ihaiva parivarttante na ca yāntyuttarāṃ diśam //
meaning:
अन्योन्यभक्षणासक्ता लोभमोहसमन्विताः /
इहैव परिवर्त्तन्ते न च यान्त्युत्तरां दिशम् //
text_mt: Addicted to devouring one another, filled with greed and delusion, / they revolve right here and do not go to the northern direction.

sanskrit_iast:
gurūnupāsate ye tu niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ /
panthānaṃ sarvālokānāṃ vijānanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
गुरूनुपासते ये तु नियता ब्रह्मचारिणः /
पन्थानं सर्वालोकानां विजानन्ति मनीषिणः //
text_mt: Those who serve their teachers, disciplined and celibate, / those wise men know the path of all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
ityukto 'yaṃ mayā dharmaḥ saṃkṣipto brahmanirmitaḥ /
dharmādharmauṃ hi lokasya yo vai vetti sa buddhimān //
meaning:
इत्युक्तो ऽयं मया धर्मः संक्षिप्तो ब्रह्मनिर्मितः /
धर्माधर्मौं हि लोकस्य यो वै वेत्ति स बुद्धिमान् //
text_mt: Thus this concise dharma created by Brahmā has been spoken by me; / for whoever knows the dharma and adharma of the world is wise.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca /.
adhyātmaṃ nāma yadidaṃ puruṣasyeha cintyate /
yadadhyātmaṃ yathā caitattanme brūhi tapodhana //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच /.
अध्यात्मं नाम यदिदं पुरुषस्येह चिन्त्यते /
यदध्यात्मं यथा चैतत्तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन //
text_mt:
Bharadvāja said:
What is this that is considered here as the 'self' of man? / Tell me, O ascetic, what this inner self is and how it exists.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
adhyātmamiti viprarṣe yadetadanupṛcchasi /
tadvyākhyāṃsyāmi te tāta śreyaskaratamaṃ sukham //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
अध्यात्ममिति विप्रर्षे यदेतदनुपृच्छसि /
तद्व्याख्यांस्यामि ते तात श्रेयस्करतमं सुखम् //
text_mt:
Bhṛgu said:
Since you ask this, O brahmin sage, concerning the inner self, / I will explain that to you, my dear child, which is most beneficial and brings happiness,

sanskrit_iast:
sṛṣṭipralayasaṃyuktamācāryaiḥ paridarśitam /
yajjñātvā puruṣo loke prītiṃ saukhyaṃ ca vindati //
meaning:
सृष्टिप्रलयसंयुक्तमाचार्यैः परिदर्शितम् /
यज्ज्ञात्वा पुरुषो लोके प्रीतिं सौख्यं च विन्दति //
text_mt: associated with creation and dissolution, shown by the teachers, / knowing which a man finds joy and happiness in the world.

sanskrit_iast:
phalalābhaśca tasya syātsarvabhūtahitaṃ ca tat /
pṛthivī vāyurākāśamāpo jyotiśca pañcamam //
meaning:
फललाभश्च तस्य स्यात्सर्वभूतहितं च तत् /
पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम् //
text_mt: And there will be gain of fruit for him, and that is beneficial to all beings. / Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth—

sanskrit_iast:
mahābhūtāni bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhavāpyayau /
yataḥ sṛṣṭāni tatraiva tāni yānti layaṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
महाभूतानि भूतानां सर्वेषां प्रभवाप्ययौ /
यतः सृष्टानि तत्रैव तानि यान्ति लयं पुनः //
text_mt: these great elements are the origin and dissolution of all beings; / from where they are created, into that very source they dissolve again.

sanskrit_iast:
mahābhūtāni bhūtebhyaḥ sāgarasyormayo yathā /
prasārya ca yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ //
meaning:
महाभूतानि भूतेभ्यः सागरस्योर्मयो यथा /
प्रसार्य च यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः //
text_mt: The great elements [arise] from beings like the waves of the ocean; / and just as a tortoise extends its limbs and withdraws them again,

sanskrit_iast:
tadvad bhūtāni bhūtātmā sṛṣṭāni harate punaḥ /
mahābhūtāni pañcaiva sarvabhūteṣu bhūtakṛt //
meaning:
तद्वद् भूतानि भूतात्मा सृष्टानि हरते पुनः /
महाभूतानि पञ्चैव सर्वभूतेषु भूतकृत् //
text_mt: in the same way the Self of beings withdraws the created beings again. / The Creator of beings made the five great elements in all beings

sanskrit_iast:
akarotteṣu vai samyak taṃ tu jīvo na paśyati /
śabdaḥ śrotraṃ tathā khāni trayamākāśayonijam //
meaning:
अकरोत्तेषु वै सम्यक् तं तु जीवो न पश्यति /
शब्दः श्रोत्रं तथा खानि त्रयमाकाशयोनिजम् //
text_mt: properly within them, but the living soul does not see Him. / Sound, the ear, and the bodily cavities: this triad is born from the womb of space.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyoḥ sparsastathā ceṣṭā tvakcaiva tritayaṃ smṛtam /
rūpaṃ cakṣustathā pākastrividhaṃ teja ucyate //
meaning:
वायोः स्पर्सस्तथा चेष्टा त्वक्चैव त्रितयं स्मृतम् /
रूपं चक्षुस्तथा पाकस्त्रिविधं तेज उच्यते //
text_mt: Touch, movement, and the skin are known as the triad of wind. / Form, the eye, and digestion are declared as the threefold nature of fire.

sanskrit_iast:
rasāḥ kledaśca jihvā ca trayo jalaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ghreyaṃ ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca ete bhūmiguṇāstrayaḥ //
meaning:
रसाः क्लेदश्च जिह्वा च त्रयो जलगुणाः स्मृताः /
घ्रेयं घ्राणं शरीरं च एते भूमिगुणास्त्रयः //
text_mt: Tastes, moisture, and the tongue are remembered as the three qualities of water. / The smellable, the organ of smell, and the body: these are the three qualities of earth.

sanskrit_iast:
mahābhūtāni pacaiva ṣaṣṭaṃ ca mana ucyate /
indriyāṇi manaścaiva vijñātānyasya bhārata //
meaning:
महाभूतानि पचैव षष्टं च मन उच्यते /
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव विज्ञातान्यस्य भारत //
text_mt: The great elements are five, and the mind is called the sixth; / the senses and the mind are known for this [embodied soul], O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit_iast:
saptamī buddhirityāhuḥ kṣetrajñaḥ punaraṣṭamaḥ /
śrotraṃ vai śravaṇārthāya sparśanāya ca tvak smṛtā //
meaning:
सप्तमी बुद्धिरित्याहुः क्षेत्रज्ञः पुनरष्टमः /
श्रोत्रं वै श्रवणार्थाय स्पर्शनाय च त्वक् स्मृता //
text_mt: They say the intellect is the seventh, and the knower of the field is the eighth. / The ear is for hearing, and the skin is known to be for touching;

sanskrit_iast:
rasādānāya rasanā gandhādānāya nāsikā /
cakṣurālokanāyaiva saṃśayaṃ kurute manaḥ //
meaning:
रसादानाय रसना गन्धादानाय नासिका /
चक्षुरालोकनायैव संशयं कुरुते मनः //
text_mt: the tongue is for perceiving taste, and the nose is for perceiving smell; / the eye is for seeing, and the mind produces doubt;

sanskrit_iast:
buddhiradhyavasānāya kṣetrajñaḥ sākṣivatsthitaḥ /
urddhaṃ pādatalābhyāṃ yadavākcodakca paśyati //
meaning:
बुद्धिरध्यवसानाय क्षेत्रज्ञः साक्षिवत्स्थितः /
उर्द्धं पादतलाभ्यां यदवाक्चोदक्च पश्यति //
text_mt: the intellect is for determination, and the knower of the field stands like a witness. / What looks upward from the soles of the feet, and downward and horizontally—

sanskrit_iast:
etena sarvamevedaṃ vibhunā cyāptamantaram /
puruṣairindriyāṇīha veditavyāni kṛtstraśaḥ //
meaning:
एतेन सर्वमेवेदं विभुना च्याप्तमन्तरम् /
पुरुषैरिन्द्रियाणीह वेदितव्यानि कृत्स्त्रशः //
text_mt: all this inside is pervaded by this all-pervading [knower of the field]. / The senses here ought to be known completely by men.

sanskrit_iast:
tamo rajaśca sattvaṃ ca te 'pi bhāvāstadāśritāḥ /
etāṃ buddhiṃ naro buddhā bhūtānāgatiṃ gatim //
meaning:
तमो रजश्च सत्त्वं च ते ऽपि भावास्तदाश्रिताः /
एतां बुद्धिं नरो बुद्धा भूतानागतिं गतिम् //
text_mt: Tamas, rajas, and sattva—these states also depend on that. / A man, having understood this intellect and the origin and passing of beings,

sanskrit_iast:
samavekṣya śanaiścaivaṃ labhate śamamuttamam /
guṇairvinaśyate buddirbuddherevendriyāṇyapi //
meaning:
समवेक्ष्य शनैश्चैवं लभते शममुत्तमम् /
गुणैर्विनश्यते बुद्दिर्बुद्धेरेवेन्द्रियाण्यपि //
text_mt: and reflecting thus gradually, attains supreme peace. / The intellect is destroyed by the qualities (guṇas), and the senses by the intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
manaḥṣaṣṭāni bhūtāni buddhyabāve kuto guṇāḥ /
iti tanmayamevaitatsarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam //
meaning:
मनःषष्टानि भूतानि बुद्ध्यबावे कुतो गुणाः /
इति तन्मयमेवैतत्सर्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् //
text_mt: The elements have the mind as their sixth; in the absence of intellect, whence could the qualities arise? / Thus this entire universe of moving and unmoving beings is made of that.

sanskrit_iast:
pralīyate codbhavati tasmānnirddiśyate tathā /
yena paśyati tañcakṣuḥ śṛṇoti śrotramucyate //
meaning:
प्रलीयते चोद्भवति तस्मान्निर्द्दिश्यते तथा /
येन पश्यति तञ्चक्षुः शृणोति श्रोत्रमुच्यते //
text_mt: It dissolves and emerges; therefore it is designated accordingly. / That by which one sees is the eye; that which hears is called the ear.

sanskrit_iast:
jighrati ghrāṇamityāhuḥ rasaṃ jānāti jihvayā /
tvacā sparśayati sparśaṃ buddhirvikriyate sakṛt //
meaning:
जिघ्रति घ्राणमित्याहुः रसं जानाति जिह्वया /
त्वचा स्पर्शयति स्पर्शं बुद्धिर्विक्रियते सकृत् //
text_mt: They say that by which one smells is the olfactory organ; by the tongue one knows taste; / through the skin one perceives touch; the intellect undergoes modification each time.

sanskrit_iast:
yena prārthayate kiñcittadā bhavati tanmanaḥ /
adhiṣṭānāttu buddherhi pṛthagarthāni pañcadhā //
meaning:
येन प्रार्थयते किञ्चित्तदा भवति तन्मनः /
अधिष्टानात्तु बुद्धेर्हि पृथगर्थानि पञ्चधा //
text_mt: That by which one desires anything is then the mind. / From the location of the intellect, indeed, the fivefold objects are distinct.

sanskrit_iast:
indriyāṇīti tānyāhustānyadṛśyo 'dhitiṣṭati /
puruṣe tiṣṭatī buddhistriṣu bhāveṣu vartate //
meaning:
इन्द्रियाणीति तान्याहुस्तान्यदृश्यो ऽधितिष्टति /
पुरुषे तिष्टती बुद्धिस्त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते //
text_mt: These are called the senses; the unseen [Self] resides within them. / Residing in the person, the intellect operates in three states.

sanskrit_iast:
kadācillabhate prītiṃ kadācidupaśocati /
na sukhena na duḥkhena kadācidapi vartate //
meaning:
कदाचिल्लभते प्रीतिं कदाचिदुपशोचति /
न सुखेन न दुःखेन कदाचिदपि वर्तते //
text_mt: Sometimes it experiences joy, sometimes it grieves; / and sometimes it abides in neither pleasure nor pain.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ narāṇāṃ manasi triṣu bhāveṣu vartate /
seyaṃ bhāvātmikā bhāvāṃstrīnetānativartate //
meaning:
एवं नराणां मनसि त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते /
सेयं भावात्मिका भावांस्त्रीनेतानतिवर्तते //
text_mt: Thus in the mind of human beings it functions in three states; / this [intellect], which consists of these states, transcends these three states.

sanskrit_iast:
saritāṃ sāgaro bhartā velānāmiva vāridhiḥ /
atibhāvagatā buddhirbhāvairmanasi vartate //
meaning:
सरितां सागरो भर्ता वेलानामिव वारिधिः /
अतिभावगता बुद्धिर्भावैर्मनसि वर्तते //
text_mt: Just as the ocean, the lord of rivers, [surpasses] its shorelines, / the intellect, having transcended states, operates in the mind through these states.

sanskrit_iast:
vartamāno munistvevaṃ svabāvamanuvartate /
indriyāṇi hi sarvāṇi pravartayati sā sadā //
meaning:
वर्तमानो मुनिस्त्वेवं स्वबावमनुवर्तते /
इन्द्रियाणि हि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तयति सा सदा //
text_mt: Functioning thus, the sage conforms to his true nature; / for it always activates all the senses.

sanskrit_iast:
prītiḥ sattvaṃ rajaḥ śokastamaḥ krodhastu te trayaḥ /
ye ye ca bhāvā loke 'sminsarve pyeteṣu vai triṣu //
meaning:
प्रीतिः सत्त्वं रजः शोकस्तमः क्रोधस्तु ते त्रयः /
ये ये च भावा लोके ऽस्मिन्सर्वे प्येतेषु वै त्रिषु //
text_mt: Joy is sattva, sorrow is rajas, and anger is tamas: these are the three; / and whatever states exist in this world, they all are indeed within these three.

sanskrit_iast:
iti buddhigatāḥ sarvā vyākhyātāstava bhāvanāḥ /
indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi vijetavyāni dhīmatā //
meaning:
इति बुद्धिगताः सर्वा व्याख्यातास्तव भावनाः /
इन्द्रियाणि च सर्वाणि विजेतव्यानि धीमता //
text_mt: Thus all the mental states belonging to the intellect have been explained to you; / and all the senses must be conquered by the wise person.

sanskrit_iast:
sattvaṃ rajastamaścaiva prāṇināṃ saṃśritāḥ sadā /
triviśvāvedanāścaiva sarvasattveṣu dṛśyate //
meaning:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव प्राणिनां संश्रिताः सदा /
त्रिविश्वावेदनाश्चैव सर्वसत्त्वेषु दृश्यते //
text_mt: Sattva, rajas, and tamas are always situated in living beings; / and a threefold perception is seen in all creatures.

sanskrit_iast:
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti mānada /
sukhasparśaḥ sattvaguṇo duḥkhasparśo rajoguṇaḥ //
meaning:
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति मानद /
सुखस्पर्शः सत्त्वगुणो दुःखस्पर्शो रजोगुणः //
text_mt: It is sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa, O giver of honor. / The quality of sattva is contact with pleasure; the quality of rajas is contact with pain.

sanskrit_iast:
tamoguṇena saṃyuktau bhavato vyāvahārikau /
tava yatprītisaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet //
meaning:
तमोगुणेन संयुक्तौ भवतो व्यावहारिकौ /
तव यत्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत् //
text_mt: Coupled with the quality of tamas, both become worldly. / Whatever in you is accompanied by joy in the body or mind,

sanskrit_iast:
vartate sāttviko bhāva ityācakṣīta tattathā /
atha yadduḥkhasaṃyuktamaprītikaramātmanaḥ //
meaning:
वर्तते सात्त्विको भाव इत्याचक्षीत तत्तथा /
अथ यद्दुःखसंयुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः //
text_mt: one should know to be functioning as a sāttvika state. / Now, whatever is accompanied by sorrow and causes displeasure to oneself,

sanskrit_iast:
pravṛttaṃ raja ityeva jānīhi munisattama /
athayanmohasaṃyuktamavyakta viṣamaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येव जानीहि मुनिसत्तम /
अथयन्मोहसंयुक्तमव्यक्त विषमं भवेत् //
text_mt: know that to have arisen from rajas, O best of sages. / And that which is accompanied by delusion, indistinct and unsteady,

sanskrit_iast:
apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ tamastadupadhārayet /
praharṣaḥ prītirānandaḥ sukhaṃ vā śāntacittatā //
meaning:
अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत् /
प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः सुखं वा शान्तचित्तता //
text_mt: incomprehensible and unknowable, one should understand as tamas. / Exhilaration, delight, bliss, joy, or tranquillity of mind—

sanskrit_iast:
kathañcidabhivartanta ityete sāttvikā guṇāḥ /
atuṣṭiḥ paritāpaśca śoko lobhastathā kṣamā //
meaning:
कथञ्चिदभिवर्तन्त इत्येते सात्त्विका गुणाः /
अतुष्टिः परितापश्च शोको लोभस्तथा क्षमा //
text_mt: if these arise in any way, these are the qualities of sattva. / Dissatisfaction, distress, sorrow, greed, and impatience—

sanskrit_iast:
liṅgāni rajasastāni dṛśyante dehahetubhiḥ /
apamānastathā mohaḥ pramādaḥ svapnatandrite //
meaning:
लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि दृश्यन्ते देहहेतुभिः /
अपमानस्तथा मोहः प्रमादः स्वप्नतन्द्रिते //
text_mt: these marks of rajas are seen caused by bodily concerns. / Disrespect, delusion, negligence, sleep, and sluggishness—

sanskrit_iast:
kathañcidabhivartante vividhāstāmasā guṇāḥ /
dūṣaṇaṃ bahudhāgāmi prārthanāsaṃśayātmakam //
meaning:
कथञ्चिदभिवर्तन्ते विविधास्तामसा गुणाः /
दूषणं बहुधागामि प्रार्थनासंशयात्मकम् //
text_mt: these diverse qualities of tamas manifest somehow. / The mind, which tends to run in many directions and consists of desire and doubt,

sanskrit_iast:
manaḥ svaniyataṃ yasya sa sukhī pretyaceha ca /
sattvakṣetrajñayoretadantaraṃ yasya sūkṣmayoḥ //
meaning:
मनः स्वनियतं यस्य स सुखी प्रेत्यचेह च /
सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेतदन्तरं यस्य सूक्ष्मयोः //
text_mt: when restrained by oneself, brings happiness in this world and the next. / This is the distinction between the subtle sattva and the knower of the field:

sanskrit_iast:
sṛjatehi guṇāneka eko na sṛjate guṇān /
maśakoduṃbarau vāpi saṃprayuktau yathā sadā //
meaning:
सृजतेहि गुणानेक एको न सृजते गुणान् /
मशकोदुंबरौ वापि संप्रयुक्तौ यथा सदा //
text_mt: the one creates the qualities; the other does not create qualities. / Just as a gnat and a fig are always conjoined,

sanskrit_iast:
anyonyametau syātāṃ ca sapraṃyogastathobhayoḥ /
pṛthagbhūtau prakṛtyā tau sapraṃyuktau ca sarvadā //
meaning:
अन्योन्यमेतौ स्यातां च सप्रंयोगस्तथोभयोः /
पृथग्भूतौ प्रकृत्या तौ सप्रंयुक्तौ च सर्वदा //
text_mt: they may be mutual, and there is conjunction between both; / they are distinct by nature, and yet always conjoined.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā matsyo jalaṃ caiva saṃprayukto tathaiva tau /
na guṇā vidurātmānaṃ sa guṇānvetti sarvaśaḥ //
meaning:
यथा मत्स्यो जलं चैव संप्रयुक्तो तथैव तौ /
न गुणा विदुरात्मानं स गुणान्वेत्ति सर्वशः //
text_mt: Just as a fish and water are conjoined, so indeed are the two. / The qualities do not know the Self; the Self knows the qualities entirely.

sanskrit_iast:
paridraṣṭā guṇānāṃ tu saṃstraṣṭā manyate tathā /
indriyastu pradīpārthaṃ kurute buddhisattamaiḥ //
meaning:
परिद्रष्टा गुणानां तु संस्त्रष्टा मन्यते तथा /
इन्द्रियस्तु प्रदीपार्थं कुरुते बुद्धिसत्तमैः //
text_mt: It is the spectator of the qualities, yet is regarded as the creator. / The sense organ acts like a lamp through the best functions of the intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
nirviceṣṭairajānadbhiḥ paramātmā pradīpavān /
sṛjate hi guṇānsattvaṃ kṣetrajñaḥ paripaśyati //
meaning:
निर्विचेष्टैरजानद्भिः परमात्मा प्रदीपवान् /
सृजते हि गुणान्सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञः परिपश्यति //
text_mt: For them who are motionless and unknowing, the Supreme Self serves as a lamp. / For sattva produces the qualities, and the knower of the field beholds them.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃprayogastayoreṣa sattvakṣetrajñayordhruvam /
āśrayo nāsti sattvasya kṣetrajñasya ca kaścana //
meaning:
संप्रयोगस्तयोरेष सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ध्रुवम् /
आश्रयो नास्ति सत्त्वस्य क्षेत्रज्ञस्य च कश्चन //
text_mt: This connection between the two, sattva and the knower of the field, is constant. / There is no other support for sattva, nor for the knower of the field.

sanskrit_iast:
sattvaṃ manaḥ saṃsṛjate na guṇānvai kadācana /
raśmīṃsteṣāṃ sa manasā yadā samyaṅniyacchati //
meaning:
सत्त्वं मनः संसृजते न गुणान्वै कदाचन /
रश्मींस्तेषां स मनसा यदा सम्यङ्नियच्छति //
text_mt: Sattva produces the mind, never the qualities. / When one properly restrains their reins with the mind,

sanskrit_iast:
tadā prakāśate 'syātmā ghaṭe dīpo jvalanniva /
tyaktvā yaḥ prākṛtaṃ karma nityamātmaratirmuniḥ //
meaning:
तदा प्रकाशते ऽस्यात्मा घटे दीपो ज्वलन्निव /
त्यक्त्वा यः प्राकृतं कर्म नित्यमात्मरतिर्मुनिः //
text_mt: then one's Self shines like a lamp burning in a pot. / The sage who has renounced material action, who constantly delights in the Self,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtātmabhūstasmātsa gaccheduttamāṃ gatim /
yathā vāricaraḥ pakṣī salilena na lipyate //
meaning:
सर्वभूतात्मभूस्तस्मात्स गच्छेदुत्तमां गतिम् /
यथा वारिचरः पक्षी सलिलेन न लिप्यते //
text_mt: and who has become the Self of all beings, will therefore attain the supreme state. / Just as an aquatic bird is not smeared by water,

sanskrit_iast:
evameva kṛtaprajño bhūteṣu parivartate /
evaṃ svabhāvamevaitatsvabuddhyā viharennaraḥ //
meaning:
एवमेव कृतप्रज्ञो भूतेषु परिवर्तते /
एवं स्वभावमेवैतत्स्वबुद्ध्या विहरेन्नरः //
text_mt: in the very same way a person of steady wisdom moves among living beings. / Thus a person should live in accordance with true nature through their own intellect,

sanskrit_iast:
aśocannaprahṛṣyaṃśca samo vigatamatsaraḥ /
bhāvayuktyā prayuktastu sa nityaṃ sṛjate guṇān //
meaning:
अशोचन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च समो विगतमत्सरः /
भावयुक्त्या प्रयुक्तस्तु स नित्यं सृजते गुणान् //
text_mt: neither grieving nor rejoicing, even-minded and free from malice. / Employed through the conjunction of mental states, it constantly creates qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
ūrṇanābhiryathā sūtraṃ vijñeyāstantuvadguṇāḥ /
pradhvastā na nivartante nivṛttirnopalabhyate //
meaning:
ऊर्णनाभिर्यथा सूत्रं विज्ञेयास्तन्तुवद्गुणाः /
प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते निवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: Just as a spider produces thread, the qualities should be known like threads; / once destroyed, they do not return, nor is their cessation directly perceived.

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣeṇa parokṣaṃ tadanumānena siddhyati /
evameke vyavasyanti nivṛttiriti cāpare //
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षेण परोक्षं तदनुमानेन सिद्ध्यति /
एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे //
text_mt: That which is beyond direct perception is established by inference. / Some conclude in this way, while others hold cessation [as the truth].

sanskrit_iast:
ubhayaṃ saṃpradhāryaitadvyavasyeta yathāmati /
itīmaṃ hṛdayagrathiṃ buddhicintāmayaṃ dṛḍham //
meaning:
उभयं संप्रधार्यैतद्व्यवस्येत यथामति /
इतीमं हृदयग्रथिं बुद्धिचिन्तामयं दृढम् //
text_mt: Having deliberated upon both, one should make a resolution according to one's wisdom. / Having thus untied this firm knot of the heart composed of intellect and anxiety,

sanskrit_iast:
vimucya sukhamāsīta na śocecchinnasaṃśavaḥ /
malināḥ prāṇnuyuḥ śuddhiṃ yathā pūrṇāṃ nadīṃ narāḥ //
meaning:
विमुच्य सुखमासीत न शोचेच्छिन्नसंशवः /
मलिनाः प्राण्नुयुः शुद्धिं यथा पूर्णां नदीं नराः //
text_mt: one should sit happily and not grieve, with doubts severed. / Just as impure people attain purity [by entering] a full river,

sanskrit_iast:
avagāhya suvidvāṃso viddhi jñānabhide tathā /
mahānadyā hi pārajñastapyate na taranyathā //
meaning:
अवगाह्य सुविद्वांसो विद्धि ज्ञानभिदे तथा /
महानद्या हि पारज्ञस्तप्यते न तरन्यथा //
text_mt: having bathed in it, so know the wise to attain purity through the distinction of knowledge. / For one who knows the other shore of a great river is not afflicted while crossing it;

sanskrit_iast:
na tu tapyati tattvajñaḥ kulajñastu taratyuta /
evaṃ ye viduradhyātmaṃ kaivalyaṃ jñānamuttamam //
meaning:
न तु तप्यति तत्त्वज्ञः कुलज्ञस्तु तरत्युत /
एवं ये विदुरध्यात्मं कैवल्यं ज्ञानमुत्तमम् //
text_mt: nor is the knower of truth afflicted, and one who knows the riverbanks crosses safely. / Thus those who know the inner Self attain solitary liberation, the supreme knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ buddhā naraḥ sarvo bhūtānāmagatiṃ gatim /
avekṣya ca śanairbuddhyā labhate ca śamaṃ tataḥ //
meaning:
एवं बुद्धा नरः सर्वो भूतानामगतिं गतिम् /
अवेक्ष्य च शनैर्बुद्ध्या लभते च शमं ततः //
text_mt: Having thus understood the departure and arrival of living beings, / and having perceived it slowly through intellect, a person thereupon attains peace.

sanskrit_iast:
trivargo yasya viditaḥ prekṣya yaśca vimuñcati /
anviṣya manasā yuktastattvadarśī nirutsukaḥ //
meaning:
त्रिवर्गो यस्य विदितः प्रेक्ष्य यश्च विमुञ्चति /
अन्विष्य मनसा युक्तस्तत्त्वदर्शी निरुत्सुकः //
text_mt: The one by whom the three ends of life are understood, who beholds and abandons [attachment], / seeking with a disciplined mind, sees the truth and is devoid of longing.

sanskrit_iast:
na cātmā śakyate draṣṭumindriyeṣu vibhāgaśaḥ /
tatra tatra visṛṣṭeṣu durvāpeṣvakṛtātmābhiḥ //
meaning:
न चात्मा शक्यते द्रष्टुमिन्द्रियेषु विभागशः /
तत्र तत्र विसृष्टेषु दुर्वापेष्वकृतात्माभिः //
text_mt: The Self cannot be seen separately among the senses, / scattered here and there, difficult to attain by undisciplined minds.

sanskrit_iast:
etad buddhā bhaved buddhaḥ kimanyad buddhalakṣaṇam /
vijñāya taddhi manyante katakṛtyā manīṣiṇaḥ //
meaning:
एतद् बुद्धा भवेद् बुद्धः किमन्यद् बुद्धलक्षणम् /
विज्ञाय तद्धि मन्यन्ते कतकृत्या मनीषिणः //
text_mt: Having understood this, one becomes awakened; what other mark of the awakened is there? / Indeed, having known that, the wise consider their purpose accomplished.

sanskrit_iast:
na bhavati viduṣāṃ tato bhayaṃ yadaviduṣāṃ sumahadbhayaṃ bhavet /
nahi gatiradhikāsti kasyacitsati hi guṇepravadatyatulyatām //
meaning:
न भवति विदुषां ततो भयं यदविदुषां सुमहद्भयं भवेत् /
नहि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचित्सति हि गुणेप्रवदत्यतुल्यताम् //
text_mt: There is no fear for the wise from that which causes immense fear to the ignorant; / for there is no higher path for anyone, since when a quality is present, it reveals inequality.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ karotyanabhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ tacca nirdahati yatpurākṛtam /
nāpriyaṃ tadubhayaṃ kutaḥ priyaṃ tasya tajjanayatīha kurvataḥ //
meaning:
यः करोत्यनभिसंधिपूर्वकं तच्च निर्दहति यत्पुराकृतम् /
नाप्रियं तदुभयं कुतः प्रियं तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वतः //
text_mt: That which one performs without selfish intention burns up what was done in the past; / neither unpleasant nor pleasant is produced here for one who acts thus—whence could it arise?

sanskrit_iast:
lokamāyurabhisūyate janastasya tajjanayatīha kurvantaḥ /
tatra paśya kuśalānna śocate jāyate yadi bhayaṃ padaṃ sadā //
meaning:
लोकमायुरभिसूयते जनस्तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वन्तः /
तत्र पश्य कुशलान्न शोचते जायते यदि भयं पदं सदा //
text_mt: People revile [their allotted] life in this world; it produces that for one who acts in this world. / Behold there: the skilled person does not grieve if the state of fear arises continually.

sanskrit_iast:
bharadvāja uvāca
dhyānayogaṃ samācakṣvamahyaṃ tatpadasiddhaye /
yajjñātvā mucyate brahmannarastrividhatāpataḥ //
meaning:
भरद्वाज उवाच
ध्यानयोगं समाचक्ष्वमह्यं तत्पदसिद्धये /
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते ब्रह्मन्नरस्त्रिविधतापतः //
text_mt: Bharadvāja said: / Explain to me the yoga of meditation for attaining that state, / knowing which, O holy one, a human being is freed from the threefold suffering.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛguruvāca
hṝnta te saṃpravakṣyāmi jñānayogaṃ caturvidham /
yaṃ jñātvā śāśvatīṃ siddhiṃ gacchantīha maharṣayaḥ //
meaning:
भृगुरुवाच
हॄन्त ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानयोगं चतुर्विधम् /
यं ज्ञात्वा शाश्वतीं सिद्धिं गच्छन्तीह महर्षयः //
text_mt:
Bhṛgu said:
Listen! I shall explain to you the fourfold yoga of knowledge, / knowing which the great sages attain eternal perfection in this world.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā svanuṣṭitaṃ dhyānaṃ tathā kurvanti yoginaḥ /
maharṣayo jñānatṛptā nirvāṇagatamānasāḥ //
meaning:
यथा स्वनुष्टितं ध्यानं तथा कुर्वन्ति योगिनः /
महर्षयो ज्ञानतृप्ता निर्वाणगतमानसाः //
text_mt: Yogins practice meditation just as it is prescribed, / [and become] great sages satisfied through knowledge, with their minds dissolved in nirvāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
nāvartante punaścāpi muktāḥ saṃsāradoṣataḥ /
janmadoṣapārīkṣīṇāḥ svabhāve paryavasthitāḥ //
meaning:
नावर्तन्ते पुनश्चापि मुक्ताः संसारदोषतः /
जन्मदोषपारीक्षीणाः स्वभावे पर्यवस्थिताः //
text_mt: They do not return again, freed from the defects of worldly existence; / with the defect of rebirth destroyed, they abide established in their own nature.

sanskrit_iast:
nirdvandvā nityasattvasthā vimuktā niṣparigrahāḥ /
asaṃgānya vidhādīni manaḥ śāntikarāṇi ca //
meaning:
निर्द्वन्द्वा नित्यसत्त्वस्था विमुक्ता निष्परिग्रहाः /
असंगान्य विधादीनि मनः शान्तिकराणि च //
text_mt: Free from dualities, ever established in sattva, liberated, devoid of possessions, / [they cultivate] unattached practices and the like, which pacify the mind.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra dhyānena saṃkliṣṭamekāgraṃ dhārayenmanaḥ /
piṇḍīkṛtyendriyagrāmamāsīnaḥ kāṣṭavanmuniḥ //
meaning:
तत्र ध्यानेन संक्लिष्टमेकाग्रं धारयेन्मनः /
पिण्डीकृत्येन्द्रियग्राममासीनः काष्टवन्मुनिः //
text_mt: Restrained by meditation, the sage, seated like a piece of wood, / drawing together the group of senses, should hold the mind one-pointed.

sanskrit_iast:
śabdaṃ na vindecchrotreṇa tvacā sparśaṃ na vedayet /
rūpaṃ na cakṣuṣā vindyājjihvayā na rasāṃstathā //
meaning:
शब्दं न विन्देच्छ्रोत्रेण त्वचा स्पर्शं न वेदयेत् /
रूपं न चक्षुषा विन्द्याज्जिह्वया न रसांस्तथा //
text_mt: He should not perceive sound with the ear, nor feel touch with the skin; / he should not perceive form with the eye, nor tastes with the tongue.

sanskrit_iast:
ghroyāṇyapi ca sarvāṇi jahyāddhyānena tattvavit /
pañcavargapramāthīni neccheñcaitāni vīryavān //
meaning:
घ्रोयाण्यपि च सर्वाणि जह्याद्ध्यानेन तत्त्ववित् /
पञ्चवर्गप्रमाथीनि नेच्छेञ्चैतानि वीर्यवान् //
text_mt: The knower of truth, through meditation, should also abandon all smells; / powerful, he should not desire these that torment the group of five.

sanskrit_iast:
tato manasi saṃgṛhya pañcavargaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ /
samādadhyānmano bhrāntamindriyaiḥ saha pañcabhiḥ //
meaning:
ततो मनसि संगृह्य पञ्चवर्गं विचक्षणः /
समादध्यान्मनो भ्रान्तमिन्द्रियैः सह पञ्चभिः //
text_mt: Then, gathering the group of five into the mind, the wise man / should concentrate the wandering mind together with the five senses.

sanskrit_iast:
visañcāri nirālambaṃ pañcadvāraṃ balābalam /
pūrvadhyānapathe dhīraḥ samādadhyānmanastvarā //
meaning:
विसञ्चारि निरालम्बं पञ्चद्वारं बलाबलम् /
पूर्वध्यानपथे धीरः समादध्यान्मनस्त्वरा //
text_mt: The steadfast man should promptly concentrate upon the path of primary meditation the mind, / which wanders about, lacks support, has five gates, and fluctuates in strength.

sanskrit_iast:
indriyāṇi manaścaiva yadā piṇḍīkarotyayam /
eṣa dhyānapathaḥ pūrvo bhayā samanuvarṇitaḥ //
meaning:
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव यदा पिण्डीकरोत्ययम् /
एष ध्यानपथः पूर्वो भया समनुवर्णितः //
text_mt: When he draws together the senses and the mind, / this is the primary path of meditation that has been described by me.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya tatpūrvasaṃruddha ātmaṣaṣṭhamanantaram /
sphuriṣyati samudrāntā vidyudambudhare yathā //
meaning:
तस्य तत्पूर्वसंरुद्ध आत्मषष्ठमनन्तरम् /
स्फुरिष्यति समुद्रान्ता विद्युदम्बुधरे यथा //
text_mt: To him, when that [mind] with the self as sixth has subsequently been restrained, / it will flash at the edge of the ocean like lightning in a rain-cloud.

sanskrit_iast:
jalabinduryathā lolaḥ parṇasthaḥ sarvataścalaḥ /
evamevāsya cittaṃ ca bhavati dhyānavartmani //
meaning:
जलबिन्दुर्यथा लोलः पर्णस्थः सर्वतश्चलः /
एवमेवास्य चित्तं च भवति ध्यानवर्त्मनि //
text_mt: Just as a drop of water on a leaf is restless and moving in all directions, / in the very same way does his mind become on the path of meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
samāhitaṃ kṣaṇaṃ kiñjiddhyānavartmani tiṣṭati /
punarvāyupathaṃ bhrāntaṃ mano bhavati vāyuvat //
meaning:
समाहितं क्षणं किञ्जिद्ध्यानवर्त्मनि तिष्टति /
पुनर्वायुपथं भ्रान्तं मनो भवति वायुवत् //
text_mt: For a moment it stays concentrated somewhat on the path of meditation; / then the wandering mind again enters the path of the wind, like the wind itself.

sanskrit_iast:
anirvedo gatakleśo gatatandro hyamatsarī /
samādadhyātpunaśceto dhyānena dhyānayogavit //
meaning:
अनिर्वेदो गतक्लेशो गततन्द्रो ह्यमत्सरी /
समादध्यात्पुनश्चेतो ध्यानेन ध्यानयोगवित् //
text_mt: Free from despondency, with distress gone, with sluggishness gone, free from envy, / the knower of dhyāna-yoga should concentrate the mind again through meditation.

sanskrit_iast:
vicāraśca vitarkaśca vivekaścopajāyate /
muneḥ samādhiyuktasya prathamaṃ dhyānamāditaḥ //
meaning:
विचारश्च वितर्कश्च विवेकश्चोपजायते /
मुनेः समाधियुक्तस्य प्रथमं ध्यानमादितः //
text_mt: Deliberation, reflection, and discernment arise / from the very beginning in the first meditation of the sage engaged in samādhi.

sanskrit_iast:
manasā kliśyamānastu samādhānaṃ ca kārayet /
na nirvedaṃ munirgacchetkuryādevātmano hitam //
meaning:
मनसा क्लिश्यमानस्तु समाधानं च कारयेत् /
न निर्वेदं मुनिर्गच्छेत्कुर्यादेवात्मनो हितम् //
text_mt: Even when afflicted by the mind, he should effect concentration; / the sage should not fall into despondency, but should work for his own welfare.

sanskrit_iast:
pāṃśubhasmakarīṣāṇāṃ yathā vai rāśayaścitāḥ /
sahasā vāriṇā siktā na yānti paribhāvanāḥ //
meaning:
पांशुभस्मकरीषाणां यथा वै राशयश्चिताः /
सहसा वारिणा सिक्ता न यान्ति परिभावनाः //
text_mt: Just as heaps of dust, ashes, and dry cow-dung that have been gathered / do not become thoroughly moistened when suddenly sprinkled with water,

sanskrit_iast:
kiñcit snigdhaṃ yathā ca syācchuṣkaṃ cūrṇamabhāvitam /
krameṇa tu śanairgacchatsarvaṃ tatparibhāvanam //
meaning:
किञ्चित् स्निग्धं यथा च स्याच्छुष्कं चूर्णमभावितम् /
क्रमेण तु शनैर्गच्छत्सर्वं तत्परिभावनम् //
text_mt: and just as dry unsoaked powder remains partially dry, / but by degrees, going slowly, all of it becomes thoroughly permeated,

sanskrit_iast:
evamevendriyagrāmaṃ śanaiḥ śaṃ paribhāvayet /
saṃharetkramaśaścaiva samyak tatpraśamiṣyati //
meaning:
एवमेवेन्द्रियग्रामं शनैः शं परिभावयेत् /
संहरेत्क्रमशश्चैव सम्यक् तत्प्रशमिष्यति //
text_mt: in the very same way one should gradually discipline the group of senses; / and one should withdraw it by degrees; it will become completely pacified.

sanskrit_iast:
svayameva manaścaivaṃ pañcavargaṃ munīśvara /
pūrvaṃ dhyānapathe sthāpya nityayogena śāmyati //
meaning:
स्वयमेव मनश्चैवं पञ्चवर्गं मुनीश्वर /
पूर्वं ध्यानपथे स्थाप्य नित्ययोगेन शाम्यति //
text_mt: O lord of sages, having first established the mind and the group of five / on the path of meditation, it becomes pacified of its own accord through constant practice.

sanskrit_iast:
na tatpuruṣakāreṇa na ca daivena kenacit /
sukhameṣyati tattasya yadevaṃ saṃyatātmanaḥ //
meaning:
न तत्पुरुषकारेण न च दैवेन केनचित् /
सुखमेष्यति तत्तस्य यदेवं संयतात्मनः //
text_mt: Not by human effort nor by any fate / does that bliss come to him, except when he is thus self-controlled.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhena tena saṃyukto raṃsyate dhyānakarmaṇi /
gacchanti yogino hyovaṃ nirvāṇaṃ tu nirāmayam //
meaning:
सुखेन तेन संयुक्तो रंस्यते ध्यानकर्मणि /
गच्छन्ति योगिनो ह्योवं निर्वाणं तु निरामयम् //
text_mt: Endowed with that bliss, he will delight in the practice of meditation; / for yogins thus attain nirvāṇa free from affliction.

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
ityukto bhṛguṇā brahmanbharadvājaḥ pratāpavān /
bhṛguṃ paramadharmātmā vismitaḥ pratyapūjayat //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
इत्युक्तो भृगुणा ब्रह्मन्भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान् /
भृगुं परमधर्मात्मा विस्मितः प्रत्यपूजयत् //
text_mt:
Sanandana said:
Addressed in this way by Bhṛgu, O brāhmaṇa, the glorious Bharadvāja, / supreme in righteousness, full of wonder, worshipped Bhṛgu in return.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa te prasavo vidvan jagataḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ /
nikhilena mahāprājña kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe dvitīyapāde catuścatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एष ते प्रसवो विद्वन् जगतः संप्रकीर्तितः /
निखिलेन महाप्राज्ञ किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे द्वितीयपादे चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
This origin of the world has been proclaimed to you in full, O wise one; / O greatly intelligent one, what more do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter in the second part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
sanandanavacaḥ śrutvā mokṣadharmāśritaṃ dvijāḥ /
punaḥ papraccha tattvajño nārado 'dhyātmasatkathām //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
सनन्दनवचः श्रुत्वा मोक्षधर्माश्रितं द्विजाः /
पुनः पप्रच्छ तत्त्वज्ञो नारदो ऽध्यात्मसत्कथाम् //
text_mt:
Sūta said:
Having heard Sanandana's words concerning the doctrine of liberation, O twice-born ones, / Nārada, the knower of truth, again asked about the sacred discourse on the inner self.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
śrutaṃ mayā mahābhāga mokṣaśāstraṃ tvayoditam /
na ca me jāyate tṛptirbhūyobhūyo 'pi śṛṇvataḥ //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
श्रुतं मया महाभाग मोक्षशास्त्रं त्वयोदितम् /
न च मे जायते तृप्तिर्भूयोभूयो ऽपि शृण्वतः //
text_mt:
Nārada said:
I have heard, O fortunate one, the treatise on liberation spoken by you; / yet my satiety does not arise, even as I listen again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā saṃmucyate janturavidyābandhanānmune /
tathā kathaya sarvajña mokṣadharmaṃ sadāśritam //
meaning:
यथा संमुच्यते जन्तुरविद्याबन्धनान्मुने /
तथा कथय सर्वज्ञ मोक्षधर्मं सदाश्रितम् //
text_mt: O sage, tell me how an embodied soul is completely freed from the bondage of ignorance; / O omniscient one, tell me the everlasting doctrine of liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
yathā mokṣamanuprāpto janako mithilādhipaḥ //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् /
यथा मोक्षमनुप्राप्तो जनको मिथिलाधिपः //
text_mt:
Sanandana said:
Concerning this, they also cite this ancient narrative / of how Janaka, the ruler of Mithilā, attained liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
janako janadevastu mithilāyā adhīśvaraḥ /
aurdhvadehikadharmāṇāmāsīdyukto vicintane //
meaning:
जनको जनदेवस्तु मिथिलाया अधीश्वरः /
और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणामासीद्युक्तो विचिन्तने //
text_mt: Janaka Janadeva, the ruler of Mithilā, / was intent upon pondering duties concerning the afterlife.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya śmaśāna mācāryā vasati satataṃ gṛhe /
darśayantaḥ pṛthagdharmānnānāpāṣañjavādinaḥ //
meaning:
तस्य श्मशान माचार्या वसति सततं गृहे /
दर्शयन्तः पृथग्धर्मान्नानापाषञ्जवादिनः //
text_mt: In his house there constantly lived a hundred teachers, / teachers of various heterodox doctrines, expounding different paths.

sanskrit_iast:
sa teṣāṃ pretyabhāve ca pretya jātau viniścaye /
ādamasthaḥ sa bhūyiṣṭamātmatattvena tuṣaayati //
meaning:
स तेषां प्रेत्यभावे च प्रेत्य जातौ विनिश्चये /
आदमस्थः स भूयिष्टमात्मतत्त्वेन तुषअयति //
text_mt: Regarding their determination of life after death and rebirth after dying, / he, remaining within his own control, was mostly not satisfied with their doctrine of the self.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra pañcaśikho nāma kāpileyo mahāmuniḥ /
paridhāvanmahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mithilāmatha //
meaning:
तत्र पञ्चशिखो नाम कापिलेयो महामुनिः /
परिधावन्महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम मिथिलामथ //
text_mt: Then the great sage named Pañcaśikha, the son of Kapilā, / wandering over the whole earth, arrived at Mithilā.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvasaṃnyāsadharmāṇaḥ tattvajñānaviniścaye /
suparyavasitārthaśca nirdvandvo naṣṭasaṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वसंन्यासधर्माणः तत्त्वज्ञानविनिश्चये /
सुपर्यवसितार्थश्च निर्द्वन्द्वो नष्टसंशयः //
text_mt: Practicing the duties of total renunciation, in the determination of the knowledge of truth / his purpose was thoroughly achieved; he was free from dualities, his doubts destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣīṇāmāhurekaṃ yaṃ kāmādavasitaṃ nṛṣu /
śāśvataṃ sukhamatyantamanvicchansa sudurlabham //
meaning:
ऋषीणामाहुरेकं यं कामादवसितं नृषु /
शाश्वतं सुखमत्यन्तमन्विच्छन्स सुदुर्लभम् //
text_mt: Among the sages they speak of him as the singular one among men who transcended desire, / seeking eternal, ultimate bliss, which is exceedingly difficult to attain.

sanskrit_iast:
yamāhuḥ kapilaṃ sāṃkhyāḥ paramarṣi prajāpatim /
sa manye tena rūpeṇa vikhyāpayati hi svayam //
meaning:
यमाहुः कपिलं सांख्याः परमर्षि प्रजापतिम् /
स मन्ये तेन रूपेण विख्यापयति हि स्वयम् //
text_mt: He whom the Sāṃkhyas call Kapila, the supreme sage and progenitor— / he himself, I think, makes himself known in that form.

sanskrit_iast:
āsureḥ prathamaṃ śiṣyaṃ yamāhuścirajīvinam /
pañcasrotasi yaḥ satramāste varṣasahasrakam //
meaning:
आसुरेः प्रथमं शिष्यं यमाहुश्चिरजीविनम् /
पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रमास्ते वर्षसहस्रकम् //
text_mt: He whom they call the long-lived first disciple of Āsuri, / who performed a sacrificial session for a thousand years at Pañcasrotas—

sanskrit_iast:
pañcasrotasamāgamya kāpilaṃ maṇḍalaṃ mahat /
puruṣāvasthamavyaṅktaṃ paramārthaṃ nyavedayat //
meaning:
पञ्चस्रोतसमागम्य कापिलं मण्डलं महत् /
पुरुषावस्थमव्यङ्क्तं परमार्थं न्यवेदयत् //
text_mt: having arrived at Pañcasrotas, he imparted the supreme truth, / the great Sāṃkhya circle, the unmanifest condition of Puruṣa.

sanskrit_iast:
iṣṭimantreṇa saṃyukto bhūyaśca tapasāsuriḥ /
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorvyaktiṃ vibudhe dehadarśanaḥ //
meaning:
इष्टिमन्त्रेण संयुक्तो भूयश्च तपसासुरिः /
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्व्यक्तिं विबुधे देहदर्शनः //
text_mt: Endowed with sacrificial mantras and further through austerity, Āsuri, / discerning the body, understood the manifestation of the field and the knower of the field.

sanskrit_iast:
yattadekākṣaraṃ brahma nānārūpaṃ pradṛśyate /
āsurirmaṇḍale tasminpratipede tamavyayam //
meaning:
यत्तदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म नानारूपं प्रदृश्यते /
आसुरिर्मण्डले तस्मिन्प्रतिपेदे तमव्ययम् //
text_mt: That which is the single-syllabled Brahman perceived as multiform— / that imperishable [reality] Āsuri realized in that circle.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya pañcaśikhaḥ śiṣyo mānuṣyā payasā bhṛtaḥ /
brāhmaṇī kapilī nāma kācidāsītkuṭumbinī //
meaning:
तस्य पञ्चशिखः शिष्यो मानुष्या पयसा भृतः /
ब्राह्मणी कपिली नाम काचिदासीत्कुटुम्बिनी //
text_mt: Pañcaśikha was his disciple, nourished with human milk; / there was a certain brāhmaṇa householder woman named Kapilā.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyaḥ putratvamāgatya sriyāḥ sa pibagati stanau /
tataśca kāpileyatvaṃ lebhe buddhiṃ ca naiṣṭikīm //
meaning:
तस्यः पुत्रत्वमागत्य स्रियाः स पिबगति स्तनौ /
ततश्च कापिलेयत्वं लेभे बुद्धिं च नैष्टिकीम् //
text_mt: Becoming her son, he drank from the woman's breasts; / and from that he obtained the status of Kapilā's son and resolute intellect.

sanskrit_iast:
etanme bhagavānāha kāpileyasya saṃbhavam /
tasya tatkāpileyatvaṃ sarvavittvamanuttamam //
meaning:
एतन्मे भगवानाह कापिलेयस्य संभवम् /
तस्य तत्कापिलेयत्वं सर्ववित्त्वमनुत्तमम् //
text_mt: The lord told me this origin of Kapilā's son; / hence his status as son of Kapilā and his unsurpassed omniscience.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmātyo janako jñātvā dharmajño jñāninaṃ mune /
upetya śatamācāryānmohayāmāsa hetubhiḥ //
meaning:
सामात्यो जनको ज्ञात्वा धर्मज्ञो ज्ञानिनं मुने /
उपेत्य शतमाचार्यान्मोहयामास हेतुभिः //
text_mt: Janaka, the knower of righteousness, learning together with his ministers of this wise man, O sage, / approached [him, who] confounded the hundred teachers with arguments.

sanskrit_iast:
janakastvabhisaṃraktaḥ kāpi leyānudarśanam /
utsṛjya śatamācāryāmpṛṣṭato 'nujagāma tam //
meaning:
जनकस्त्वभिसंरक्तः कापि लेयानुदर्शनम् /
उत्सृज्य शतमाचार्याम्पृष्टतो ऽनुजगाम तम् //
text_mt: Janaka, deeply attached to the philosophical system of Kapilā's son, / abandoned the hundred teachers and followed after him.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmai paramakalyāṇaṃ praṇatāya ca dharmataḥ /
abravītparamaṃ mokṣaṃ yattatsāṃkhyaṃ vidhīyate //
meaning:
तस्मै परमकल्याणं प्रणताय च धर्मतः /
अब्रवीत्परमं मोक्षं यत्तत्सांख्यं विधीयते //
text_mt: To him, bowed in accordance with righteousness, he expounded the supreme good, / the ultimate liberation which is known as Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit_iast:
jātinirvedamuktvā sa karmanirvedamabravīt /
karmanirvedamuktvā ca sarvanirvedamabravīt //
meaning:
जातिनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा स कर्मनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् /
कर्मनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा च सर्वनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Having spoken of disillusionment with birth, he spoke of disillusionment with action; / and having spoken of disillusionment with action, he spoke of disillusionment with all.

sanskrit_iast:
yadarthaṃ dharmasaṃsargaḥ karmaṇāṃ ca phalo dayaḥ /
tamanāśvāsikaṃ mohaṃ vināśi calamadhruvam //
meaning:
यदर्थं धर्मसंसर्गः कर्मणां च फलो दयः /
तमनाश्वासिकं मोहं विनाशि चलमध्रुवम् //
text_mt: That for the sake of which there is connection with dharma and the rising of the fruits of actions, / that [very object] is devoid of solace, delusion, perishable, unsteady, and transient.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛśyamāne vināśe ca pratyakṣe lokasākṣike /
āgamātparamastīti bruvannapi parājitaḥ //
meaning:
दृश्यमाने विनाशे च प्रत्यक्षे लोकसाक्षिके /
आगमात्परमस्तीति ब्रुवन्नपि पराजितः //
text_mt: And when destruction is seen directly, witnessed by the world, / even one who asserts from scripture, 'The supreme exists,' is defeated.

sanskrit_iast:
anātmā hyātmano mṛtyuḥ kleśo mṛtyurjarāmayaḥ /
ātmānaṃ manyate mohāttadasamyak paraṃ matam //
meaning:
अनात्मा ह्यात्मनो मृत्युः क्लेशो मृत्युर्जरामयः /
आत्मानं मन्यते मोहात्तदसम्यक् परं मतम् //
text_mt: For death is not the Self, affliction is death, as are old age and disease; / out of delusion one considers [the body] to be the Self; that is considered an erroneous view.

sanskrit_iast:
atha cedevamapyasti yalloke nopapadyate /
ajaro 'yamamṛtyuśca rājāsau manyate yathā //
meaning:
अथ चेदेवमप्यस्ति यल्लोके नोपपद्यते /
अजरो ऽयममृत्युश्च राजासौ मन्यते यथा //
text_mt: Now, even if this is so, which does not hold true in the world, / [it is] just as this king considers, 'I am ageless and deathless.'

sanskrit_iast:
asti nāstīti cāpyetattasminnasitalakṣaṇe /
kimadhiṣṭāya tad brūyāllokayātrāviniścayam //
meaning:
अस्ति नास्तीति चाप्येतत्तस्मिन्नसितलक्षणे /
किमधिष्टाय तद् ब्रूयाल्लोकयात्राविनिश्चयम् //
text_mt: Regarding that which is characterized by unclarity as to whether 'it is' or 'it is not,' / relying on what could one declare a settled conclusion regarding the ways of the world?

sanskrit_iast:
pratyakṣaṃ hyetayormūlaṃ kṛtānta hyetayorapi /
pratyakṣo hyāgamo bhinnaḥ kṛtānto vā na kiñcana //
meaning:
प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतयोर्मूलं कृतान्त ह्येतयोरपि /
प्रत्यक्षो ह्यागमो भिन्नः कृतान्तो वा न किञ्चन //
text_mt: Perception indeed is the root of these two, and the settled conclusion also belongs to them; / for perception contradicted by scripture, or a settled doctrine [contrary to perception], is nothing at all.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra tatrānumāne 'sminkṛtaṃ bhāvayate 'pi ca /
anyojīvaḥ śarīrasya nāstikānāṃ mate sthitaḥ //
meaning:
यत्र तत्रानुमाने ऽस्मिन्कृतं भावयते ऽपि च /
अन्योजीवः शरीरस्य नास्तिकानां मते स्थितः //
text_mt: Wherever in this inference one conceives what is done, / the living soul is distinct from the body—such is the position in the doctrine of the materialists.

sanskrit_iast:
retovaṭakaṇīkāyāṃ ghṛtapākādhivāsanam /
jātismṛtirayaskāntaḥ sūryakāntoṃ'bubhakṣaṇam //
meaning:
रेतोवटकणीकायां घृतपाकाधिवासनम् /
जातिस्मृतिरयस्कान्तः सूर्यकान्तोंऽबुभक्षणम् //
text_mt: The infusion of clarified butter when cooking, in a speck of a banyan seed, / the memory of past births, the lodestone, the sunstone, the drinking of water,

sanskrit_iast:
pretabhūtapriyaścaiva devatā hyupayācanam /
mṛtakarmanivattiṃ ca pramāṇamiti niścayaḥ //
meaning:
प्रेतभूतप्रियश्चैव देवता ह्युपयाचनम् /
मृतकर्मनिवत्तिं च प्रमाणमिति निश्चयः //
text_mt: and the fondness for spirits and ghosts, the entreaty made to deities, / and the cessation of work upon death—the certainty is that [these] constitute proof.

sanskrit_iast:
nanvete hetavaḥ saṃti ye kecinmūrtisasthitāḥ /
amūtasya hi mūrtena sāmānyaṃ nopalabhyate //
meaning:
नन्वेते हेतवः संति ये केचिन्मूर्तिसस्थिताः /
अमूतस्य हि मूर्तेन सामान्यं नोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: "Indeed, these reasons exist, whatever are located in material form; / for there is no commonality perceived between the formless and that which has form."

sanskrit_iast:
avidyā karma tṛṣṇā ca kecidāhuḥ punarbhavam /
tasminnaṣṭe ca dagdhe ca citte maraṇadharmiṇi //
meaning:
अविद्या कर्म तृष्णा च केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवम् /
तस्मिन्नष्टे च दग्धे च चित्ते मरणधर्मिणि //
text_mt: "Some say that ignorance, action, and craving are rebirth; / and when that mortal mind is destroyed and burned,

sanskrit_iast:
anyo 'smājjāyate mohastamāhuḥ sattvasaṃkṣayam /
yadā sarūpataścānyo jātitaḥ śrutator'thataḥ //
meaning:
अन्यो ऽस्माज्जायते मोहस्तमाहुः सत्त्वसंक्षयम् /
यदा सरूपतश्चान्यो जातितः श्रुततोर्ऽथतः //
text_mt: another delusion is born from this, which they call the destruction of the living being. / When it is different in form, birth, learning, and meaning,

sanskrit_iast:
kathamasminsa ityeva saṃbandhaḥ syādasaṃhitaḥ /
evaṃ sati ca kā prīhirjñānavidyātapobalaiḥ //
meaning:
कथमस्मिन्स इत्येव संबन्धः स्यादसंहितः /
एवं सति च का प्रीहिर्ज्ञानविद्यातपोबलैः //
text_mt: how could an unconnected relation exist in this [case], such as 'this is he'? / If this be so, what joy is there in the powers of knowledge, learning, and austerities,

sanskrit_iast:
yadasyācaritaṃ karma sāmānyātpratipadyate /
api tvayamihaivānyaiḥ prākṛtairduḥkhito bhavet //
meaning:
यदस्याचरितं कर्म सामान्यात्प्रतिपद्यते /
अपि त्वयमिहैवान्यैः प्राकृतैर्दुःखितो भवेत् //
text_mt: since he incurs the action performed by this [other] on account of commonality? / Rather, he would become distressed right here by other ordinary [factors].

sanskrit_iast:
sukhito duḥkhito vāpi dṛśyādṛśyavinirṇayaḥ /
yathā hi muśalairhanyuḥ śarīraṃ tatpunarbhavet //
meaning:
सुखितो दुःखितो वापि दृश्यादृश्यविनिर्णयः /
यथा हि मुशलैर्हन्युः शरीरं तत्पुनर्भवेत् //
text_mt: Whether happy or distressed, there is the ascertainment of the visible and invisible; / just as if they beat a body with clubs, that would exist again.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛthā jñānaṃ yadanyañca yenaitannopalabhyate /
ṛmasaṃvatsarau tiṣyaḥ śītoṣṇo 'tha priyāpriye //
meaning:
वृथा ज्ञानं यदन्यञ्च येनैतन्नोपलभ्यते /
ऋमसंवत्सरौ तिष्यः शीतोष्णो ऽथ प्रियाप्रिये //
text_mt: Futile is the knowledge that is different, by which this is not perceived: / seasons, years, the constellation Tiṣya, cold and heat, pleasant and unpleasant.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā tātāni paśyati tādṛśaḥ sattvasaṃkṣayaḥ /
jarayābhiparītasya mṛtyunā ca vināśitam //
meaning:
यथा तातानि पश्यति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः /
जरयाभिपरीतस्य मृत्युना च विनाशितम् //
text_mt: As one sees these, such is the destruction of the living being; / destroyed by death when overcome by old age,

sanskrit_iast:
durbalaṃ durbalaṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhasyeva vinaśyati /
indriyāṇi mano vāyuḥ śoṇitaṃ māṃsamasthi ca //
meaning:
दुर्बलं दुर्बलं पूर्वं गृहस्येव विनश्यति /
इन्द्रियाणि मनो वायुः शोणितं मांसमस्थि च //
text_mt: the weak [part] perishes first, like that of a house: / the senses, mind, breath, blood, flesh, and bone

sanskrit_iast:
ānupūrvyā vinaśyanti svaṃ dhātumupayāti ca /
lokayātrāvidhātaśca dānadharmaphalāgame //
meaning:
आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति स्वं धातुमुपयाति च /
लोकयात्राविधातश्च दानधर्मफलागमे //
text_mt: perish in sequence and go to their own element. / And by the ordinance of worldly life, upon the arrival of the fruit of charity and righteousness,

sanskrit_iast:
tadarthaṃ vedaṃśabdāśca vyavahārāśca laukikāḥ /
iti samyaṅ manasyete bahavaḥ saṃti hetavaḥ //
meaning:
तदर्थं वेदंशब्दाश्च व्यवहाराश्च लौकिकाः /
इति सम्यङ् मनस्येते बहवः संति हेतवः //
text_mt: there are the words of the Veda for that purpose, and worldly conventions. / Thus in the mind, there are indeed many reasons for this.

sanskrit_iast:
aita dastīti nāstīti na kaścitpratidṛśyate /
teṣāṃ vimṛśatāmeva tatsamyagabhidhāvatām //
meaning:
ऐत दस्तीति नास्तीति न कश्चित्प्रतिदृश्यते /
तेषां विमृशतामेव तत्सम्यगभिधावताम् //
text_mt: No one is seen to clearly distinguish, 'This exists,' or 'This does not exist.' / While they are thus deliberating, running fully toward it,

sanskrit_iast:
kvacinnivasate buddhistatra jīryati vṛkṣavat /
evantur thairanarthaiśca duḥkhitāḥ sarvajantavaḥ //
meaning:
क्वचिन्निवसते बुद्धिस्तत्र जीर्यति वृक्षवत् /
एवन्तुर् थैरनर्थैश्च दुःखिताः सर्वजन्तवः //
text_mt: the intellect settles somewhere, and there it withers like a tree. / Thus, distressed by purposeful and unpurposed things, all creatures

sanskrit_iast: āgamairapakṛṣyante hastipairhastino yathā //
meaning: आगमैरपकृष्यन्ते हस्तिपैर्हस्तिनो यथा //
text_mt: are dragged away by scriptures, as elephants are by elephant-drivers."

sanskrit_iast:
arthāstathā hṝnti sukhāvahāṃśca lihata ete bahavopaśuṣkāḥ /
mahattaraṃ duḥkhamabhiprapannā hitvāmiṣaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ prayānti //
meaning:
अर्थास्तथा हॄन्ति सुखावहांश्च लिहत एते बहवोपशुष्काः /
महत्तरं दुःखमभिप्रपन्ना हित्वामिषं मृत्युवशं प्रयान्ति //
text_mt: "Objects of sense likewise carry off agreeable things; licking these, many wither away; / falling into greater sorrow, abandoning the bait, they pass into the power of death.

sanskrit_iast:
vināśino hyadhruvajīvinaḥ kiṃ kiṃ bandhubhirmatraparigrahaiśca /
vihāya yo gacchati sarvameva kṣaṇena gatvā na nivartate ca //
meaning:
विनाशिनो ह्यध्रुवजीविनः किं किं बन्धुभिर्मत्रपरिग्रहैश्च /
विहाय यो गच्छति सर्वमेव क्षणेन गत्वा न निवर्तते च //
text_mt: What is the use of relatives, mantras, and possessions for those who perish, who live impermanently? / He who leaves everything and departs, having gone in an instant, does not return.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūvyomatoyānalavāyavo 'pi sadā śarīraṃ pratipālayanti /
itīdamālakṣya ratiḥ kuto bhavedvināśināpyasya na śama vidyate //
meaning:
भूव्योमतोयानलवायवो ऽपि सदा शरीरं प्रतिपालयन्ति /
इतीदमालक्ष्य रतिः कुतो भवेद्विनाशिनाप्यस्य न शम विद्यते //
text_mt: Earth, space, water, fire, and wind also constantly sustain the body; / having perceived this, whence could pleasure arise? Even though it perishes, there is no peace for it."

sanskrit_iast:
idamanupadhivākyamacchalaṃ paramanirāmayamātmasākṣikam /
narapatirabhivīkṣya vismitaḥ punaranuyoktumidaṃ pracakrame //
meaning:
इदमनुपधिवाक्यमच्छलं परमनिरामयमात्मसाक्षिकम् /
नरपतिरभिवीक्ष्य विस्मितः पुनरनुयोक्तुमिदं प्रचक्रमे //
text_mt: Seeing this speech—free from deceit, without guile, supremely wholesome, and witnessed by the Self— / the king of men was astonished, and proceeded to question him again:

sanskrit_iast:
janaka uvāca
bhagavanyadi na pretya saṃjñā bhavati kasyacit /
evaṃ sati kimajñānaṃ jñānaṃ vā kiṃ kariṣyati //
meaning:
जनक उवाच
भगवन्यदि न प्रेत्य संज्ञा भवति कस्यचित् /
एवं सति किमज्ञानं ज्ञानं वा किं करिष्यति //
text_mt: Janaka said: / "O venerable one, if there is no consciousness for anyone after death, / this being so, what will ignorance do, or what will knowledge do?

sanskrit_iast:
sarvamucchedaniṣṭasyātpaśya caitaddvijottama /
apramattaḥ pramatto vā kiṃ viśeṣaṃ kariṣyati //
meaning:
सर्वमुच्छेदनिष्टस्यात्पश्य चैतद्द्विजोत्तम /
अप्रमत्तः प्रमत्तो वा किं विशेषं करिष्यति //
text_mt: All would result in annihilation; see this, O best of the twice-born! / What distinction will the vigilant or the negligent make?

sanskrit_iast:
asaṃsargo hi bhūteṣu saṃsargo vā vināśiṣu /
kasmai kriyata kalpeta niścayaḥ ko 'tra tattvataḥ //
meaning:
असंसर्गो हि भूतेषु संसर्गो वा विनाशिषु /
कस्मै क्रियत कल्पेत निश्चयः को ऽत्र तत्त्वतः //
text_mt: Non-contact with beings, or contact with perishable things: / for what purpose would an action be performed? What is the ascertainment in truth here?"

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
tamasā hi maticchatraṃ vibhrāntamiva cāturam /
punaḥ praśamayanvākyaiḥ kaviḥ pañcaśikho 'bravīt //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
तमसा हि मतिच्छत्रं विभ्रान्तमिव चातुरम् /
पुनः प्रशमयन्वाक्यैः कविः पञ्चशिखो ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / As the umbrella of the intellect was bewildered and afflicted, as it were, by darkness, / the wise sage Pañcaśikha, calming him again with words, spoke:

sanskrit_iast:
pañcaśikha uvāca
ucchedaniṣṭā nehāsti bhāvaniṣṭā na vidyate /
ayaṃ hyapi samāhāraḥ śarīredriyacetasām //
meaning:
पञ्चशिख उवाच
उच्छेदनिष्टा नेहास्ति भावनिष्टा न विद्यते /
अयं ह्यपि समाहारः शरीरेद्रियचेतसाम् //
text_mt: Pañcaśikha said: / "There is no annihilationism here, nor does eternalism exist. / For this is an aggregation of the body, the senses, and consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
vartate pṛthaganyonyamapyupāśritya karmasu /
dhātavaḥ pañcadhā toyaṃ khe vāyurjyotiṣo dharā //
meaning:
वर्तते पृथगन्योन्यमप्युपाश्रित्य कर्मसु /
धातवः पञ्चधा तोयं खे वायुर्ज्योतिषो धरा //
text_mt: It operates distinctly, having recourse also to one another in actions. / The elements are fivefold: water, wind in space, light, and earth.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu bhāvena tiṣṭanti viyujyante svabhāvataḥ /
ākāśaṃ vāyurūṣmā ca sneho yaścāpi pārthivaḥ //
meaning:
तेषु भावेन तिष्टन्ति वियुज्यन्ते स्वभावतः /
