तापत्रयचिकित्सार्थं किमन्यत्कथयामि ते //
इति श्रूबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे सप्तचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
All this has been told to you that you asked me about / for the cure of the threefold suffering; what else shall I tell you?

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter in the second quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
śrutaṃ mayā mahāmāga tāpatrayacikitsitam /
tathāpi me mano bhrāntaṃ na sthitiṃ labhateṃ'jasā //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
श्रुतं मया महामाग तापत्रयचिकित्सितम् /
तथापि मे मनो भ्रान्तं न स्थितिं लभतेंऽजसा //
text_mt: Nārada said: / "I have heard the cure for the threefold suffering, O highly fortunate one; / nonetheless, my wandering mind does not readily attain stability.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmavyatikramaṃ brahmandurjanācaritaṃ katham /
soḍhuṃ śakyeta manujaistanmamākhyāhi mānada //
meaning:
आत्मव्यतिक्रमं ब्रह्मन्दुर्जनाचरितं कथम् /
सोढुं शक्येत मनुजैस्तन्ममाख्याहि मानद //
text_mt: How can the violation of one's own self committed by wicked people / be endured by human beings? Tell me that, O giver of honor."

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
tacchrṛtvā nāradenoktaṃ brahmaputraḥ sanandanaḥ /
uvāca harṣasaṃyuktaḥ smaranbhagharataceṣṭitam //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
तच्छ्रृत्वा नारदेनोक्तं ब्रह्मपुत्रः सनन्दनः /
उवाच हर्षसंयुक्तः स्मरन्भघरतचेष्टितम् //
text_mt: Sūta said: / Having heard that spoken by Nārada, Sanandana, son of Brahmā, / filled with joy, said, remembering the deeds of Bharata:

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
atra te kathayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam /
yaṃ śrutvā tvanmano bhrāntamāsthānaṃ labhate bhūśam //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् /
यं श्रुत्वा त्वन्मनो भ्रान्तमास्थानं लभते भूशम् //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / "Here I shall narrate to you an ancient story, / hearing which your wandering mind will greatly attain stability.

sanskrit_iast:
āsītpurā muniśreṣṭha bharato nāma bhūpatiḥ /
ārṣabho yasya nāmnedaṃ bhārataṃ khaṇḍamucyate //
meaning:
आसीत्पुरा मुनिश्रेष्ठ भरतो नाम भूपतिः /
आर्षभो यस्य नाम्नेदं भारतं खण्डमुच्यते //
text_mt: Formerly there was a king named Bharata, O best of sages, / the son of Ṛṣabha, by whose name this land is called Bhārata.

sanskrit_iast:
sa rājā prāptarājyastu pitṛpaitāmahaṃ kramāt /
pālayāmāsa dharmeṇa pitṛbadrañjayan prajāḥ //
meaning:
स राजा प्राप्तराज्यस्तु पितृपैतामहं क्रमात् /
पालयामास धर्मेण पितृबद्रञ्जयन् प्रजाः //
text_mt: Having obtained the kingdom inherited from his father and grandfather in due succession, / that king protected the subjects with righteousness, gladdening them like a father.

sanskrit_iast:
rddaje ca vividhairyajñairbhagavantamadhokṣajam /
sarvadevātmakaṃ dhyāyannānākarmasu tanmatiḥ //
meaning:
र्द्दजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्भगवन्तमधोक्षजम् /
सर्वदेवात्मकं ध्यायन्नानाकर्मसु तन्मतिः //
text_mt: He worshiped the Lord, Adhokṣaja, with various sacrifices, / meditating on him as the self of all deities, his mind intent on various rites.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ samutpādya sutānvirakto viṣayeṣu saḥ /
muktvā rājyaṃ yayau vidvānpulastyapuhāśramam //
meaning:
ततः समुत्पाद्य सुतान्विरक्तो विषयेषु सः /
मुक्त्वा राज्यं ययौ विद्वान्पुलस्त्यपुहाश्रमम् //
text_mt: Then, having fathered sons, detached from sense-objects, / giving up the kingdom, the wise king went to the hermitage of Pulastya and Pulaha,

sanskrit_iast:
śālagrāmaṃ mahākṣetraṃ mumukṣujanasevitam /
tatrāsau tāpaso tāpaso bhūtvā viṣṇorārādhanaṃ mune //
meaning:
शालग्रामं महाक्षेत्रं मुमुक्षुजनसेवितम् /
तत्रासौ तापसो तापसो भूत्वा विष्णोराराधनं मुने //
text_mt: to the great sacred field Śālagrāma, frequented by seekers of liberation. / Becoming an ascetic there, O sage, he performed the worship of Viṣṇu

sanskrit_iast:
cakāra bhaktibhāvena yathālabdhasaparyayā /
nityaṃ prātaḥ samāplutya nirmale 'bhali nārada //
meaning:
चकार भक्तिभावेन यथालब्धसपर्यया /
नित्यं प्रातः समाप्लुत्य निर्मले ऽभलि नारद //
text_mt: with devotion, through offerings procured as available. / Constantly bathing in the morning in the pure water, O Nārada,

sanskrit_iast:
upatiṣṭedraviṃ bhaktyā gṛṇanbrahmākṣaraṃ param /
athāśrame samāgatya vāsudevaṃ jagatpatim //
meaning:
उपतिष्टेद्रविं भक्त्या गृणन्ब्रह्माक्षरं परम् /
अथाश्रमे समागत्य वासुदेवं जगत्पतिम् //
text_mt: he would worship the sun with devotion, chanting the supreme imperishable Brahman. / Then, returning to the hermitage, [he worshiped] Vāsudeva, the Lord of the universe,

sanskrit_iast:
samāhṛtaiḥ svayaṃ dravyaiḥ samitkuśamṛdādibhiḥ /
phalaiḥ puṣpaiṃstathā patraistulasyāḥ svacchavāribhiḥ //
meaning:
समाहृतैः स्वयं द्रव्यैः समित्कुशमृदादिभिः /
फलैः पुष्पैंस्तथा पत्रैस्तुलस्याः स्वच्छवारिभिः //
text_mt: with materials gathered by himself: sacrificial sticks, kuśa grass, earth, and so forth, / with fruits, flowers, and leaves of tulasī, and with clear water,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjayanprayato bhūtvā bhaktiprasarasaṃplutaḥ /
sacaikadā mahābhāgaḥ snātvā prātaḥ samāhitaḥ //
meaning:
पूजयन्प्रयतो भूत्वा भक्तिप्रसरसंप्लुतः /
सचैकदा महाभागः स्नात्वा प्रातः समाहितः //
text_mt: worshiping with self-restraint, flooded by an outflow of devotion. / And once that illustrious king, having bathed in the morning, composed in mind,

sanskrit_iast:
cakranadyāṃ japaṃstasthau muhurtatrayamaṃbuni /
athājagāma tattīraṃ jalaṃ pātuṃ pipāsitā //
meaning:
चक्रनद्यां जपंस्तस्थौ मुहुर्तत्रयमंबुनि /
अथाजगाम तत्तीरं जलं पातुं पिपासिता //
text_mt: stood in the water of the Cakranadī for three muhūrtas, reciting prayers. / Then a thirsty doe came to that riverbank to drink water,

sanskrit_iast:
āsannapsavā brahmannaikaiva hiṇī vanāt /
tataḥ samabhavattatra pītaprāye jale tayā //
meaning:
आसन्नप्सवा ब्रह्मन्नैकैव हिणी वनात् /
ततः समभवत्तत्र पीतप्राये जले तया //
text_mt: about to give birth, O brāhmaṇa, all alone from the forest. / Then, when the water was almost drunk by her there,

sanskrit_iast:
siṃhasya nādaḥ sumahān sarvaprāṇibhayaṅkaraḥ /
tataḥ sā siṃhasannādādutplutā nimnagātaṭam //
meaning:
सिंहस्य नादः सुमहान् सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करः /
ततः सा सिंहसन्नादादुत्प्लुता निम्नगातटम् //
text_mt: there arose a very great roar of a lion, terrifying to all living beings. / Then she, springing up from the roar of the lion toward the riverbank,

sanskrit_iast:
atyuñcārohaṇenāsyā nadyāṃ garbhaḥ papāta ha /
tamuhyamānaṃ vegena vīcimālāpariplutam //
meaning:
अत्युञ्चारोहणेनास्या नद्यां गर्भः पपात ह /
तमुह्यमानं वेगेन वीचिमालापरिप्लुतम् //
text_mt: due to leaping extremely high, her fetus fell into the river. / Carried away by the current, tossed by a series of waves,

sanskrit_iast:
jagrāha bharato garbhātpatitaṃ mṛgapotakam /
garbhapracyutiduḥkhena prottuṅgākraṇena ca //
meaning:
जग्राह भरतो गर्भात्पतितं मृगपोतकम् /
गर्भप्रच्युतिदुःखेन प्रोत्तुङ्गाक्रणेन च //
text_mt: Bharata caught the fawn that had fallen from the womb. / From the pain of miscarriage and from the high leap,

sanskrit_iast:
munīndra sā tu hariṇī nipapāta mamāra ca /
hariṇīṃ tāṃ vilokyātha vipannāṃ nṛpatāpasaḥ //
meaning:
मुनीन्द्र सा तु हरिणी निपपात ममार च /
हरिणीं तां विलोक्याथ विपन्नां नृपतापसः //
text_mt: that doe fell down and died, O lord of sages. / Then, seeing that doe dead, the royal ascetic,

sanskrit_iast:
mṛgapotaṃ samāgṛhya svamāśramamupāgataḥ /
cakārānudinaṃ cāsau mṛgapotasya vai nṛpaḥ //
meaning:
मृगपोतं समागृह्य स्वमाश्रममुपागतः /
चकारानुदिनं चासौ मृगपोतस्य वै नृपः //
text_mt: taking the young fawn, returned to his hermitage. / And day after day, that king indeed took care of

sanskrit_iast:
poṣaṇaṃ puṣyamāṇaśca sa tena vavṛdhe mune /
cacārāśramaparyantaṃ tṛṇāni gahaneṣu saḥ //
meaning:
पोषणं पुष्यमाणश्च स तेन ववृधे मुने /
चचाराश्रमपर्यन्तं तृणानि गहनेषु सः //
text_mt: the fawn's nourishment, and nourished by him, it grew, O sage. / It grazed on the grasses in the thickets around the hermitage;

sanskrit_iast:
dūraṃ gatvā ca śārdūlatrāsādabhyāyayau punaḥ /
prātargatvādidūraṃ ca sāyamāyātyathāśramam //
meaning:
दूरं गत्वा च शार्दूलत्रासादभ्याययौ पुनः /
प्रातर्गत्वादिदूरं च सायमायात्यथाश्रमम् //
text_mt: having gone far, it returned again out of fear of a tiger; / going far in the morning, it came back to the hermitage in the evening.

sanskrit_iast:
punaśca bharatasyābhūdāśramasyoṭajāntare /
tasyatasminmṛge dūrasamīpaparivartini //
meaning:
पुनश्च भरतस्याभूदाश्रमस्योटजान्तरे /
तस्यतस्मिन्मृगे दूरसमीपपरिवर्तिनि //
text_mt: And again it remained within the hut of Bharata's hermitage. / While that deer wandered far and near,

sanskrit_iast:
āsīñcetaḥ samāsaktaṃ na tathā hyacyute mune /
vimuktarājyatanayaḥ projjhitāśeṣabāndhavaḥ //
meaning:
आसीञ्चेतः समासक्तं न तथा ह्यच्युते मुने /
विमुक्तराज्यतनयः प्रोज्झिताशेषबान्धवः //
text_mt: his mind became attached to it, but not so toward Acyuta, O sage. / Though he had abandoned his kingdom and sons, and cast aside all relatives,

sanskrit_iast:
mamatva sa cakāroñcaistasminhariṇapotake /
kiṃ vṛkaibhakṣito vyāghnaiḥ kiṃ siṃhena nipātitaḥ //
meaning:
ममत्व स चकारोञ्चैस्तस्मिन्हरिणपोतके /
किं वृकैभक्षितो व्याघ्नैः किं सिंहेन निपातितः //
text_mt: he felt intense possessiveness toward that young fawn. / 'Has it been eaten by wolves, by tigers, or struck down by a lion?'

sanskrit_iast:
cirāyamāṇe niṣkānte tasyāsīditi mānasam /
prītiprasannavadanaḥ pārśvasthe cābhavanmṛge //
meaning:
चिरायमाणे निष्कान्ते तस्यासीदिति मानसम् /
प्रीतिप्रसन्नवदनः पार्श्वस्थे चाभवन्मृगे //
text_mt: Such was his thought when it was late in returning after wandering out; / and his face became bright with affection when the deer was at his side.

sanskrit_iast:
samādhibhaṅgastasyāsīnmamatvākṛṣṭamānasaḥ /
kālena gacchatā so 'tha kālaṃ cakre mahīpatiḥ //
meaning:
समाधिभङ्गस्तस्यासीन्ममत्वाकृष्टमानसः /
कालेन गच्छता सो ऽथ कालं चक्रे महीपतिः //
text_mt: There was an interruption of his samādhi, his mind drawn away by possessiveness. / With the passing of time, the king met his death.

sanskrit_iast:
piteva sāstraṃ putreṇa mṛgapotena vīkṣitaḥ /
mṛgameva tadādrākṣīttyajanprāṇānasāvapi //
meaning:
पितेव सास्त्रं पुत्रेण मृगपोतेन वीक्षितः /
मृगमेव तदाद्राक्षीत्त्यजन्प्राणानसावपि //
text_mt: Looked upon by the young deer like a father by a son with tears, / he too looked only upon that deer as he gave up his life-breaths.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛgo babhūva sa mune tādṛśīṃ bhāvanāṃ gataḥ /
jāti smaratvādudvignaḥ saṃsārasya dvijottama //
meaning:
मृगो बभूव स मुने तादृशीं भावनां गतः /
जाति स्मरत्वादुद्विग्नः संसारस्य द्विजोत्तम //
text_mt: He became a deer, O sage, having reached such a state of consciousness. / Distressed by the cycle of rebirth because he remembered his previous birth, O best of brāhmaṇas,

sanskrit_iast:
vihāya mātaraṃ bhūyaḥ śālagrāmamupāyayau /
śuṣkaistṛṇaistathā parṇaiḥ sa kurvannātmapoṣaṇam //
meaning:
विहाय मातरं भूयः शालग्राममुपाययौ /
शुष्कैस्तृणैस्तथा पर्णैः स कुर्वन्नात्मपोषणम् //
text_mt: leaving his mother, he went again to Śālagrāma. / Sustaining himself with dry grass and leaves,

sanskrit_iast:
mṛgatvahetubhūtasya karmaṇo niṣkṛtiṃ yayau /
tatra cotsṛṣṭadeho 'sau jajñe jātismaro dvijaḥ //
meaning:
मृगत्वहेतुभूतस्य कर्मणो निष्कृतिं ययौ /
तत्र चोत्सृष्टदेहो ऽसौ जज्ञे जातिस्मरो द्विजः //
text_mt: he attained expiation of the karma that had caused his state as a deer. / Leaving his body there, he was born as a brāhmaṇa remembering his previous lives,

sanskrit_iast:
sadācāravatāṃ śuddhe yāgināṃ pravare kule /
sarvavijñāna saṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstrārthatattvavit //
meaning:
सदाचारवतां शुद्धे यागिनां प्रवरे कुले /
सर्वविज्ञान संपन्नः सर्वशास्त्रार्थतत्त्ववित् //
text_mt: in a pure, noble family of sacrificers endowed with good conduct, / endowed with all knowledge, knowing the essential truth of all scriptures.

sanskrit_iast:
apaśyatsa muniśreṣṭhaḥ svātmānaṃ prakṛteḥ param /
ātmanodhigatajñānāddvevādīni mahāmune //
meaning:
अपश्यत्स मुनिश्रेष्ठः स्वात्मानं प्रकृतेः परम् /
आत्मनोधिगतज्ञानाद्द्वेवादीनि महामुने //
text_mt: That best of sages saw his own Self as beyond Prakṛti. / Through the knowledge realized by the Self, O great sage,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtānyabhe dena dadarśa sa mahāmatiḥ /
na papāṭha guruproktaṃ kṛtopanayanaḥ śrutam //
meaning:
सर्वभूतान्यभे देन ददर्श स महामतिः /
न पपाठ गुरुप्रोक्तं कृतोपनयनः श्रुतम् //
text_mt: that noble-minded one beheld all beings, beginning with the gods, without difference. / Having had the upanayana performed, he did not recite what was taught by the guru from scripture;

sanskrit_iast:
na dadarśa ca karmāṇi śāstrāṇi jagṛhe na ca /
ukto 'pi bahuśaḥ kiñcijjaṇḍa vākyamabhāṣata //
meaning:
न ददर्श च कर्माणि शास्त्राणि जगृहे न च /
उक्तो ऽपि बहुशः किञ्चिज्जण्ड वाक्यमभाषत //
text_mt: he did not perform rituals, nor did he study the scriptures; / and even though addressed many times, he spoke only a few dull words.

sanskrit_iast:
tadapyasaṃskāraguṇaṃ grāmabhāṣoktisaṃyutam /
apaddhastavapuḥ so 'pi malināṃbaradhṛṅ mune //
meaning:
तदप्यसंस्कारगुणं ग्रामभाषोक्तिसंयुतम् /
अपद्धस्तवपुः सो ऽपि मलिनांबरधृङ् मुने //
text_mt: Even so, lacking refinements, speaking the vulgar dialect, / with distorted body, he wore filthy garments, O sage;

sanskrit_iast:
klinnadantāntaraḥ sarvaiḥ paribhūtaḥ sa nāgaraiḥ /
saṃmānena parāṃ hāniṃ yogarddheḥ kurute yataḥ //
meaning:
क्लिन्नदन्तान्तरः सर्वैः परिभूतः स नागरैः /
संमानेन परां हानिं योगर्द्धेः कुरुते यतः //
text_mt: with dirt between his teeth, he was despised by all the townsfolk; / for honor causes the greatest ruin to the prosperity of yoga.

sanskrit_iast:
janenāvamato yogī yogasiddhiṃ ca vindati /
tasmāñcareta vai yogī satāṃ dharmamadūṣayan //
meaning:
जनेनावमतो योगी योगसिद्धिं च विन्दति /
तस्माञ्चरेत वै योगी सतां धर्ममदूषयन् //
text_mt: Disdained by the people, the yogin attains perfection in yoga; / therefore the yogin should wander without corrupting the dharma of the virtuous,

sanskrit_iast:
janā yathāvamanyeyurgaccheyurnaiva saṃgatim /
hiraṇyagarbhavacanaṃ vicintyetthaṃ mahāmatiḥ //
meaning:
जना यथावमन्येयुर्गच्छेयुर्नैव संगतिम् /
हिरण्यगर्भवचनं विचिन्त्येत्थं महामतिः //
text_mt: so that people might despise him and never associate with him. / Reflecting thus on the words of Hiraṇyagarbha, the great-minded one

sanskrit_iast:
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa jaḍonmattākṛtiṃ jane /
bhuṅkte kulmāṣavaṭakān śākaṃ tranyaphalaṃ kaṇān //
meaning:
आत्मानं दर्शयामास जडोन्मत्ताकृतिं जने /
भुङ्क्ते कुल्माषवटकान् शाकं त्रन्यफलं कणान् //
text_mt: showed himself to the people in the form of a dull-witted madman. / He ate boiled pulse cakes, vegetables, wild fruits, and grains;

sanskrit_iast:
yadyadāpnoti sa bahūnatti vai kālasaṃbhavam /
pitaryuparate so 'tha bhrātṛbhrātṛvyabāndhavaiḥ //
meaning:
यद्यदाप्नोति स बहूनत्ति वै कालसंभवम् /
पितर्युपरते सो ऽथ भ्रातृभ्रातृव्यबान्धवैः //
text_mt: whatever abundant [food] came in season, he indeed consumed. / Then, when his father passed away, he was made by his brothers, nephews, and kinsmen

sanskrit_iast:
kāritaḥ kṣetrakarmādi kadannāhārapoṣitaḥ /
sarūkṣapīnāvayavo jaḍakārī ca karmaṇi //
meaning:
कारितः क्षेत्रकर्मादि कदन्नाहारपोषितः /
सरूक्षपीनावयवो जडकारी च कर्मणि //
text_mt: to do farm-work and the like, nourished on coarse food. / With rough, stout limbs, he acted like an idiot in [every] task.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvalokopakaraṇaṃ babhūvāhāravetanaḥ /
taṃ tādṛśamasaṃskāraṃ viprākṛtiviceṣṭitam //
meaning:
सर्वलोकोपकरणं बभूवाहारवेतनः /
तं तादृशमसंस्कारं विप्राकृतिविचेष्टितम् //
text_mt: He became the servant of all people, receiving food as his wage. / Seeing him thus devoid of refinements, acting contrary to the nature of a brāhmaṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣattā sauvīrarājyasya viṣṭiyogyamamanyata /
sa rājā śibikārūḍho gantuṃ kṛtamatirdvija //
meaning:
क्षत्ता सौवीरराज्यस्य विष्टियोग्यममन्यत /
स राजा शिबिकारूढो गन्तुं कृतमतिर्द्विज //
text_mt: the chamberlain of the Sauvīra king considered him fit for forced labor. / That king, mounted on a palanquin, resolved to go, O twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
babhūvekṣumatītīre kapilarṣervarāśramam /
śreyaḥ kimatra saṃsāre duḥkhaprāye nṛṇāmiti //
meaning:
बभूवेक्षुमतीतीरे कपिलर्षेर्वराश्रमम् /
श्रेयः किमत्र संसारे दुःखप्राये नृणामिति //
text_mt: to the excellent hermitage of the sage Kapila on the bank of the Ikṣumatī, / thinking: 'What is the highest good for men in this worldly existence, which is mostly suffering?'

sanskrit_iast:
praṣṭuṃ taṃ mokṣadharmajñaṃ kapilākhyaṃ mahāmunim /
uvāha śibikāmasya kṣatturvacanacoditaḥ //
meaning:
प्रष्टुं तं मोक्षधर्मज्ञं कपिलाख्यं महामुनिम् /
उवाह शिबिकामस्य क्षत्तुर्वचनचोदितः //
text_mt: In order to question that great sage named Kapila, who knew the path to liberation, / he was carried in a palanquin; and urged by the chamberlain's command,

sanskrit_iast:
nṛṇāṃ viṣṭigṛhītānāmanyeṣāṃ so 'pi madhyagaḥ /
gṛhīto viṣṭinā vipra sarvajñānaikabhājanam //
meaning:
नृणां विष्टिगृहीतानामन्येषां सो ऽपि मध्यगः /
गृहीतो विष्टिना विप्र सर्वज्ञानैकभाजनम् //
text_mt: he too went in the midst of other men seized for forced labor. / Seized for forced labor, O twice-born, though the sole receptacle of all knowledge,

sanskrit_iast:
jātismaro 'sau pāpasya kṣayakāma uvāha tām /
yayau jaḍagatistatra yugamātrāvalokanam //
meaning:
जातिस्मरो ऽसौ पापस्य क्षयकाम उवाह ताम् /
ययौ जडगतिस्तत्र युगमात्रावलोकनम् //
text_mt: remembering his past births and desiring the destruction of sin, he carried it. / He walked with the slow gait of an idiot, looking ahead only the distance of a yoke.

sanskrit_iast:
kurvanmatimatāṃ śreṣṭhaste tvanye tvaritaṃ yayuḥ /
vilokya nṛpatiḥ so 'tha viṣamaṃ śibikāgatam //
meaning:
कुर्वन्मतिमतां श्रेष्ठस्ते त्वन्ये त्वरितं ययुः /
विलोक्य नृपतिः सो ऽथ विषमं शिबिकागतम् //
text_mt: While he, best among the wise, moved thus, the others walked swiftly. / Then the king, noticing that the palanquin was moving unevenly,

sanskrit_iast:
kimetadityāha samaṃ gamyatāṃ śibikāvahāḥ /
punastathaiva śibikāṃ vilokya viṣamāṃ hasan //
meaning:
किमेतदित्याह समं गम्यतां शिबिकावहाः /
पुनस्तथैव शिबिकां विलोक्य विषमां हसन् //
text_mt: said: 'What is this? Walk evenly, palanquin-bearers!' / Again seeing the palanquin moving unevenly, smiling,

sanskrit_iast:
nṛpaḥ kime 'tadityāha bhavadbhirgamyate 'nyathā /
bhūpatervadatastasya śrutvetthaṃ bahuśo vacaḥ /
śibikāvāhakāḥ procurayaṃ yātītyasatvaram //
meaning:
नृपः किमे ऽतदित्याह भवद्भिर्गम्यते ऽन्यथा /
भूपतेर्वदतस्तस्य श्रुत्वेत्थं बहुशो वचः /
शिबिकावाहकाः प्रोचुरयं यातीत्यसत्वरम् //
text_mt: the king said: 'What is this? You are walking improperly!' / Hearing this utterance spoken repeatedly by the lord of the earth, / the palanquin-bearers said: 'This one is walking slowly.'

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
kiṃ śrānto 'syalpamadhvānaṃ tvayoḍhā śibikā mama /
kimāyāsasaho na tvaṃ pīvā nāsi nirīkṣyase //
meaning:
राजोवाच
किं श्रान्तो ऽस्यल्पमध्वानं त्वयोढा शिबिका मम /
किमायाससहो न त्वं पीवा नासि निरीक्ष्यसे //
text_mt: The king said: / 'Are you fatigued? My palanquin has been carried by you for only a short distance. / Can you not bear exertion? Are you not robust? You are seen [to be so].'

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
nāhaṃ pīvā na caivoḍhā śibikā bhavato mayā /
na śrānto 'smi na cāyāso voḍhānyo 'sti mahīpate //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
नाहं पीवा न चैवोढा शिबिका भवतो मया /
न श्रान्तो ऽस्मि न चायासो वोढान्यो ऽस्ति महीपते //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'I am not robust, nor has your palanquin been carried by me; / I am not fatigued, nor is there exertion. There is another bearer, O ruler of the earth.'

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
pratyakṣaṃ dṛśyate pīvātvadyāpi śibikā tvayi /
śramaśca bhāro dvahane bhavatyeva hi dehinām //
meaning:
राजोवाच
प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते पीवात्वद्यापि शिबिका त्वयि /
श्रमश्च भारो द्वहने भवत्येव हि देहिनाम् //
text_mt: The king said: / 'Directly visible is your stoutness, and the palanquin is upon you even now; / and fatigue certainly arises for embodied beings from carrying a burden.'

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
pratyakṣaṃ bhavatā bhūpa yaddṛṣṭaṃ mama tadvada /
balavānabalaśceti vācyaṃ paścādviśeṣaṇam //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
प्रत्यक्षं भवता भूप यद्दृष्टं मम तद्वद /
बलवानबलश्चेति वाच्यं पश्चाद्विशेषणम् //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'Tell me what was directly seen by you, O king, regarding me. / The qualification "strong" or "weak" is to be spoken only afterwards.

sanskrit_iast:
tvayoḍhā śibikā ceti tvayyadyāpi ca saṃsthitā /
mithyā tadapyatra bhavān śṛṇotu vacanaṃ mama //
meaning:
त्वयोढा शिबिका चेति त्वय्यद्यापि च संस्थिता /
मिथ्या तदप्यत्र भवान् शृणोतु वचनं मम //
text_mt: "The palanquin was carried by you, and even now it rests upon you"— / that too is false; listen to my word in this matter.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmau pādayugaṃ cātha jaṅghe pādadvaye sthite /
ūru jaṅghādvayāvasthau tadādhāraṃ tathodaram //
meaning:
भूमौ पादयुगं चाथ जङ्घे पादद्वये स्थिते /
ऊरु जङ्घाद्वयावस्थौ तदाधारं तथोदरम् //
text_mt: The two feet rest on the earth, and the shanks are situated upon the two feet; / the thighs rest on the two shanks, and the belly is supported by them.

sanskrit_iast:
vakṣasthalaṃ tathā bāhū skandhau codarasaṃsthitau /
skandhāśritayeṃ śibikā mamādhāro 'tra kiṅkṛtaḥ //
meaning:
वक्षस्थलं तथा बाहू स्कन्धौ चोदरसंस्थितौ /
स्कन्धाश्रितयें शिबिका ममाधारो ऽत्र किङ्कृतः //
text_mt: Likewise the chest, arms, and shoulders are situated upon the belly; / this palanquin is resting upon the shoulders. How is it made into my burden?

sanskrit_iast:
śibikāyāṃ sthitaṃ cedaṃ dehaṃ tvadupalakṣitam /
tatra tvamahamapyatretyucyate cedamanyathā //
meaning:
शिबिकायां स्थितं चेदं देहं त्वदुपलक्षितम् /
तत्र त्वमहमप्यत्रेत्युच्यते चेदमन्यथा //
text_mt: And this body, designated as "you", rests upon the palanquin. / That "you are there" and "I am here" is said improperly.

sanskrit_iast:
ahaṃ tvaṃ ca tathānye ca bhūtairuhyāśca pārthiva /
guṇapravāhapatito bhūtavargo 'pi yātyayam //
meaning:
अहं त्वं च तथान्ये च भूतैरुह्याश्च पार्थिव /
गुणप्रवाहपतितो भूतवर्गो ऽपि यात्ययम् //
text_mt: I, you, and others are carried by the material elements, O king; / and this collection of elements, fallen into the stream of the guṇas, moves along.

sanskrit_iast:
karmavaśyā guṇaścaite sattvādyāḥ pṛthivīpate /
avidyāsaṃcitaṃ karmataścāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu //
meaning:
कर्मवश्या गुणश्चैते सत्त्वाद्याः पृथिवीपते /
अविद्यासंचितं कर्मतश्चाशेषेषु जन्तुषु //
text_mt: And these guṇas, sattva and the rest, are subject to karma, O protector of the earth; / and karma, accumulated by ignorance, exists in all living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraḥ śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛte paraḥ /
pravṛddhyapacayau na sta ekasyākhilajantuṣu //
meaning:
आत्मा शुद्धो ऽक्षरः शान्तो निर्गुणः प्रकृते परः /
प्रवृद्ध्यपचयौ न स्त एकस्याखिलजन्तुषु //
text_mt: The self is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of qualities, beyond primordial nature; / there is no growth or decay for the One residing in all living beings.

sanskrit_iast:
yadā nopacayastasya nacaivāpacayo nṛpa /
tadāpi bāliśo 'si tvaṃ kayā yuktyā tvayeritam //
meaning:
यदा नोपचयस्तस्य नचैवापचयो नृप /
तदापि बालिशो ऽसि त्वं कया युक्त्या त्वयेरितम् //
text_mt: When there is no growth for it, and no decay either, O king, / even then [you ask]: "Are you robust?" By what reasoning was that spoken by you?

sanskrit_iast:
/
bhūpādajaṅghākaṭyūrujaṭharādiṣu saṃsthitā /
śibikeyaṃ yadā skandhe tadā bhāraḥ samastvayā //
meaning:
/
भूपादजङ्घाकट्यूरुजठरादिषु संस्थिता /
शिबिकेयं यदा स्कन्धे तदा भारः समस्त्वया //
text_mt: When this palanquin, resting upon the feet, shanks, hips, thighs, belly, and so forth [of the body] / which is upon the earth, is upon the shoulder, then the burden is the same for you

sanskrit_iast:
tathānyajantubhirbhūpa śibikoḍhāna kevalam /
śailadrumagṛhottho 'pi pṛthivīsaṃbhavo 'pi ca //
meaning:
तथान्यजन्तुभिर्भूप शिबिकोढान केवलम् /
शैलद्रुमगृहोत्थो ऽपि पृथिवीसंभवो ऽपि च //
text_mt: as well as for other living beings, O king. Not only the palanquin is carried, / but also whatever arises from mountains, trees, and houses, or whatever originates from the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā puṃsaḥ pṛthagbhāvaḥ prākṛtaiḥ karaṇairnṛpa /
soḍhavyaḥ sumahānbhāraḥ katamo nṛpa te mayā //
meaning:
यथा पुंसः पृथग्भावः प्राकृतैः करणैर्नृप /
सोढव्यः सुमहान्भारः कतमो नृप ते मया //
text_mt: Since the self is distinct from the material instruments, O king, / what exceedingly great burden of yours is to be borne by me, O king?

sanskrit_iast:
yaddravyo śibikā ceyaṃ taddravyo bhūtasaṃgrahaḥ /
bhavato me 'khilasyāsya samatvenopabṛṃhitaḥ //
meaning:
यद्द्रव्यो शिबिका चेयं तद्द्रव्यो भूतसंग्रहः /
भवतो मे ऽखिलस्यास्य समत्वेनोपबृंहितः //
text_mt: The substance of which this palanquin is made is the same substance as the collection of elements / of you and of me and of all this [world], magnified through sameness.'

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
evamuktvābhavaṃnmaunī sa vahañśibikāṃ dvijaḥ /
so 'pi rājāvatīryorvyāṃ tatpādau jagṛhe tvaran //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
एवमुक्त्वाभवंन्मौनी स वहञ्शिबिकां द्विजः /
सो ऽपि राजावतीर्योर्व्यां तत्पादौ जगृहे त्वरन् //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / Having spoken thus, the twice-born remained silent as he carried the palanquin. / That king too, having quickly descended to the ground, clasped his feet.

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
bho bho visṛjya śibikāṃ prasādaṃ kuru me dvija /
kathyatāṃ ko bhavānatra jālmarupadharaḥ sthitaḥ //
meaning:
राजोवाच
भो भो विसृज्य शिबिकां प्रसादं कुरु मे द्विज /
कथ्यतां को भवानत्र जाल्मरुपधरः स्थितः //
text_mt: The king said: / 'O sir, setting down the palanquin, grant me your favor, O twice-born! / Tell me, who are you who stand here in the guise of a fool?

sanskrit_iast:
yo bhavānyadapatyaṃ vā yadāgamanakāraṇam /
tatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vidvanmahyaṃ śuśrūṣave tvayā //
meaning:
यो भवान्यदपत्यं वा यदागमनकारणम् /
तत्सर्वं कथ्यतां विद्वन्मह्यं शुश्रूषवे त्वया //
text_mt: Who you are, whose son, or what the reason for your coming is— / let all that be told by you, O wise one, to me who wish to listen!'

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śrūyatāṃ ko 'hamityetadvaktuṃ bhūpa na śakyate /
upayoganimittaṃ ca sarvatrāgamanakriyā //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
श्रूयतां को ऽहमित्येतद्वक्तुं भूप न शक्यते /
उपयोगनिमित्तं च सर्वत्रागमनक्रिया //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / 'Listen: to state "who I am" is not possible, O king; / and the action of coming everywhere is for the sake of functional purpose.'

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaduḥkhopabhogau tu tau dehādyupapādakau /
dharmādharmodbhavau bhoktuṃ janturdehādimṛcchati //
meaning:
सुखदुःखोपभोगौ तु तौ देहाद्युपपादकौ /
धर्माधर्मोद्भवौ भोक्तुं जन्तुर्देहादिमृच्छति //
text_mt: The experience of pleasure and pain produces the body and the rest; / born of merit and demerit, a creature obtains a body and other [instruments] in order to experience them.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvasyaiva hi bhūpāla jantoḥ sarvatra kāraṇam /
dharmādharmauṃ yatastasmātkāraṇaṃ pṛcchyate kutaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वस्यैव हि भूपाल जन्तोः सर्वत्र कारणम् /
धर्माधर्मौं यतस्तस्मात्कारणं पृच्छ्यते कुतः //
text_mt: For in every creature, O king, merit and demerit / are indeed the cause everywhere; therefore, why is a cause asked about?

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
dharmādharmauṃ na saṃdehaḥ sarvakāryeṣu kāraṇam /
upabhoganimittaṃ ca dehāddehāntarāgamaḥ //
meaning:
राजोवाच
धर्माधर्मौं न संदेहः सर्वकार्येषु कारणम् /
उपभोगनिमित्तं च देहाद्देहान्तरागमः //
text_mt:
The king said:
Merit and demerit, without doubt, are the cause in all effects, / and the passage from one body to another body is for the sake of experience.

sanskrit_iast:
yattvetadbhavatā proktaṃ ko 'hamityetadātmanaḥ /
vaktuṃ na śakyate śrotuṃ tanmameccā pravartate //
meaning:
यत्त्वेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं को ऽहमित्येतदात्मनः /
वक्तुं न शक्यते श्रोतुं तन्ममेच्चा प्रवर्तते //
text_mt: However, as to what you said, that one cannot say of the self / “Who am I?”, my desire arises to hear about that.

sanskrit_iast:
yo 'sti yo 'hamiti brahmankathaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate /
ātmanyeva na doṣāya śabdo 'hamiti yo dvijā //
meaning:
यो ऽस्ति यो ऽहमिति ब्रह्मन्कथं वक्तुं न शक्यते /
आत्मन्येव न दोषाय शब्दो ऽहमिति यो द्विजा //
text_mt: How can it not be possible to say who one is, [stating] “I am [so-and-so]”, O Brahmin? / The word “I” with reference to the self itself cannot be faulty, O twice-born!

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śabdo 'hamiti doṣāya nātmanyevaṃ tathaiva tat /
anātmanyātmavijñānaṃ śabdo vā śrutilakṣaṇaḥ //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
शब्दो ऽहमिति दोषाय नात्मन्येवं तथैव तत् /
अनात्मन्यात्मविज्ञानं शब्दो वा श्रुतिलक्षणः //
text_mt:
The Brahmin said:
The word “I” is indeed not faulty with reference to the self, that is so; / [it is faulty when there is] the notion of self in what is not the self, or [when] a word has the character of [mere] sounds.

sanskrit_iast:
jihvā bravītyahamiti dantauṣṭatāluka nṛpa /
etenāhaṃ yataḥ sarve vāṅniṣpādanahetavaḥ //
meaning:
जिह्वा ब्रवीत्यहमिति दन्तौष्टतालुक नृप /
एतेनाहं यतः सर्वे वाङ्निष्पादनहेतवः //
text_mt: The tongue says “I”, [as do] the teeth, the lips, and the palate, O king; / [yet can one say] “I am these”, since all of them are merely causes for producing speech?

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ hetubhirvadūtyeṣā vāgevāhamiti svayam /
tathāpi vāgahamedvaktumitthaṃ na yujyate //
meaning:
किं हेतुभिर्वदूत्येषा वागेवाहमिति स्वयम् /
तथापि वागहमेद्वक्तुमित्थं न युज्यते //
text_mt: Does speech itself say “I am” through these causes? / Even so, it is not fitting to say in this manner: “I am speech.”

sanskrit_iast:
piṇḍaḥ pṛthagyataḥ puṃsaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādilakṣaṇaḥ /
tato 'hamiti kutraināṃ saṃjñāṃ rājankaromyaham //
meaning:
पिण्डः पृथग्यतः पुंसः शिरःपाण्यादिलक्षणः /
ततो ऽहमिति कुत्रैनां संज्ञां राजन्करोम्यहम् //
text_mt: Since the physical body, characterized by the head, hands, and other [limbs], is separate from the person, / where, then, O king, do I apply this designation “I”?

sanskrit_iast:
yadyanyo 'sti paraḥ ko 'pi mattaḥ pārthivasattam /
na deho 'hamayaṃ cānye vaktumevamapīṣyate //
meaning:
यद्यन्यो ऽस्ति परः को ऽपि मत्तः पार्थिवसत्तम् /
न देहो ऽहमयं चान्ये वक्तुमेवमपीष्यते //
text_mt: If there is any other supreme [entity] different from me, O best of kings, / then one may wish to say: “I am not this body, and they are others.”

sanskrit_iast:
yadā samastadeheṣu pumāneko vyavasthitaḥ /
tadadā hi ko bhavānko 'hamityetadviphalaṃ vacaḥ //
meaning:
यदा समस्तदेहेषु पुमानेको व्यवस्थितः /
तददा हि को भवान्को ऽहमित्येतद्विफलं वचः //
text_mt: en: When one single person resides in all bodies, / then indeed words like "Who are you?" or "Who am I?" are meaningless.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ rājā śibikā ceyaṃ vayaṃ vāhāḥ puraḥ sarāḥ /
ayaṃ ca bhavato loko na sadetannṛpocyate //
meaning:
त्वं राजा शिबिका चेयं वयं वाहाः पुरः सराः /
अयं च भवतो लोको न सदेतन्नृपोच्यते //
text_mt: en: "You are the king, this is the palanquin, we are the bearers walking ahead, / and this is your folk"—king, this is not said of what is real.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛkṣāddāru tataśceyaṃ śibikā tvadadhiṣṭitā /
kva vṛkṣasaṃjñā vai tasyā dārusaṃjñāthavā nṛpa //
meaning:
वृक्षाद्दारु ततश्चेयं शिबिका त्वदधिष्टिता /
क्व वृक्षसंज्ञा वै तस्या दारुसंज्ञाथवा नृप //
text_mt: en: From a tree comes wood, and from that comes this palanquin upon which you sit; / where indeed is the designation "tree" for it, or the designation "wood", O king?

sanskrit_iast:
vṛkṣārūḍho mahārājo nāyaṃ vadati te janaḥ /
na ca dāruṇi sarvastvāṃ bravīti śibikāgatam //
meaning:
वृक्षारूढो महाराजो नायं वदति ते जनः /
न च दारुणि सर्वस्त्वां ब्रवीति शिबिकागतम् //
text_mt: en: This folk of yours does not say, "The great king is mounted on a tree"; / nor does anyone say of you, seated in the palanquin, "He is on wood."

sanskrit_iast:
śibikādārusaṃghāto svanāmasthitisaṃsthitaḥ /
anviṣyatāṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhānandadāśibikā tvayā //
meaning:
शिबिकादारुसंघातो स्वनामस्थितिसंस्थितः /
अन्विष्यतां नृपश्रेष्ठानन्ददाशिबिका त्वया //
text_mt: en: The palanquin is an aggregate of pieces of wood, abiding under the status of its own name; / let the palanquin be sought by you, O best of kings, [which is] a giver of bliss.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ chatraṃ śalākābhyaḥ pṛthagbhāvo vimṛśyatām /
kva jātaṃ chatramityeṣa nyāyastvayi tathā mayi //
meaning:
एवं छत्रं शलाकाभ्यः पृथग्भावो विमृश्यताम् /
क्व जातं छत्रमित्येष न्यायस्त्वयि तथा मयि //
text_mt: en: In this way, let the parasol be considered distinct from its ribs: / where has the parasol arisen? This reasoning applies to you and likewise to me.

sanskrit_iast:
pumānstrī gaurajā bājī kuñjaro vihagastaruḥ /
deheṣu lokasaṃjñeyaṃ vijñeyā karmahetuṣu //
meaning:
पुमान्स्त्री गौरजा बाजी कुञ्जरो विहगस्तरुः /
देहेषु लोकसंज्ञेयं विज्ञेया कर्महेतुषु //
text_mt: en: Man, woman, cow, goat, horse, elephant, bird, tree— / this worldly designation is to be understood regarding bodies caused by past karma.

sanskrit_iast:
pumānna devo na naro na paśurna ca pādapaḥ /
śarīrākṛtibhedāstu bhūpaite karmayonayaḥ //
meaning:
पुमान्न देवो न नरो न पशुर्न च पादपः /
शरीराकृतिभेदास्तु भूपैते कर्मयोनयः //
text_mt: en: The person is neither a god nor a man, nor a beast, nor a tree; / these bodily forms, O king, are born of karma.

sanskrit_iast:
vastu rājeti yalleke yañca rājabhaṭātmakam /
tathānyaśca nṛpetthaṃ tanna satyaṃ kalpanāmayam //
meaning:
वस्तु राजेति यल्लेके यञ्च राजभटात्मकम् /
तथान्यश्च नृपेत्थं तन्न सत्यं कल्पनामयम् //
text_mt: en: That entity which is in the world as "king", and that which consists of royal soldiers, / and likewise another, O king: in this manner, that is not real; it is made of imagination.

sanskrit_iast:
yastu kālāntareṇāpi nāśasaṃjñāmupaiti vai /
pariṇāmādisaṃbhūtaṃ tadvastu nṛpa tañca kim //
meaning:
यस्तु कालान्तरेणापि नाशसंज्ञामुपैति वै /
परिणामादिसंभूतं तद्वस्तु नृप तञ्च किम् //
text_mt: en: But that which, even in the course of time, attains the designation of destruction, / arisen from transformation and the like—what entity is that, O king?

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ rājā sarvasokasya pituḥ putro ripo ripuḥ /
patnyāḥ patiḥ pitā sūnoḥ kastvaṃ bhūpa vadāmyaham //
meaning:
त्वं राजा सर्वसोकस्य पितुः पुत्रो रिपो रिपुः /
पत्न्याः पतिः पिता सूनोः कस्त्वं भूप वदाम्यहम् //
text_mt: en: You are the king of all the world, the son of a father, the enemy of an enemy, / the husband of a wife, the father of a son: which of these are you, O king? Tell [me].

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ kimetacciraḥ kiṃ tu śirastava tatho daram /
kimu pādādikaṃ tvetannaiva kiṃ te mahīpate //
meaning:
त्वं किमेतच्चिरः किं तु शिरस्तव तथो दरम् /
किमु पादादिकं त्वेतन्नैव किं ते महीपते //
text_mt: en: Are you this head? Or is the head yours, and likewise the belly? / Or are the feet and so forth you, or are they not yours, O lord of the earth?

sanskrit_iast:
samastāvayavebhyastvaṃ pṛthagbhūto vyavasthitaḥ /
ko 'hamityatra nipuṇaṃ bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva //
meaning:
समस्तावयवेभ्यस्त्वं पृथग्भूतो व्यवस्थितः /
को ऽहमित्यत्र निपुणं भूत्वा चिन्तय पार्थिव //
text_mt: en: You exist standing apart from all the limbs; / having become discerning, reflect on this, O ruler: "Who am I?"

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ vyavasthite tattve mayāhamiti bhāvitum /
pṛthakūcaraṇaniṣpādyaṃ śakyaṃ tu nṛpate katham //
iti śṛbṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvi.pā.ṣṭacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एवं व्यवस्थिते तत्त्वे मयाहमिति भावितुम् /
पृथकूचरणनिष्पाद्यं शक्यं तु नृपते कथम् //
इति शृबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वि.पा.ष्टचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
en: When the truth is established thus, how can it be possible, O king, / for me to imagine "I", which is brought about by separate limbs?

en: Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter in the Second Part of the Great Narrative in the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
niśamya tasyeti vacaḥ paramārthasamanvitam /
praśrayāvanato bhūtvā tamāha nṛpatirdvijam //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
निशम्य तस्येति वचः परमार्थसमन्वितम् /
प्रश्रयावनतो भूत्वा तमाह नृपतिर्द्विजम् //
text_mt: en: Sanandana said: / Having heard his words endowed with ultimate truth, / the king, bowing down with humility, said to that twice-born:

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
bhagavanyattvayā prokta paramārthamayaṃ vacaḥ /
śrute tasminbhramantīva manaso mama vṛttayaḥ //
meaning:
राजोवाच
भगवन्यत्त्वया प्रोक्त परमार्थमयं वचः /
श्रुते तस्मिन्भ्रमन्तीव मनसो मम वृत्तयः //
text_mt: en: The king said: / Holy one, as for this word full of ultimate truth that you have spoken, / when it was heard, the movements of my mind seem to wander.

sanskrit_iast:
etadvivekavijñānaṃ yadi śeṣeṣu jantuṣu /
bhavatā darśitaṃ vipra tatparaṃ prakṛtermahat //
meaning:
एतद्विवेकविज्ञानं यदि शेषेषु जन्तुषु /
भवता दर्शितं विप्र तत्परं प्रकृतेर्महत् //
text_mt: en: If this discriminative knowledge regarding all remaining creatures / has been shown by you, O twice-born, it is beyond Prakṛti, supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
nāhaṃ vahāmi śibikāṃ śibikā mayi na sthitā /
śarīramanyadasmatto yeneyaṃ śibikā dhṛtā //
meaning:
नाहं वहामि शिबिकां शिबिका मयि न स्थिता /
शरीरमन्यदस्मत्तो येनेयं शिबिका धृता //
text_mt: en: "I do not carry the palanquin; the palanquin does not rest on me; / the body by which this palanquin is borne is different from us;

sanskrit_iast:
guṇa pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ pravṛttiḥ karmacoditā /
pravartante guṇāścaite kiṃ mameti tvayoditam //
meaning:
गुण प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां प्रवृत्तिः कर्मचोदिता /
प्रवर्तन्ते गुणाश्चैते किं ममेति त्वयोदितम् //
text_mt: en: the activity of beings is the activity of the guṇas impelled by karma, / and these guṇas are active—what is it to me?"—so you have said.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminparamārthajña mama śrotrapathaṃ gate /
mano vihvalatāmeti paramārthārthatāṃ gatam //
meaning:
एतस्मिन्परमार्थज्ञ मम श्रोत्रपथं गते /
मनो विह्वलतामेति परमार्थार्थतां गतम् //
text_mt: en: When this has entered the path of my hearing, O knower of the ultimate truth, / my mind, seeking the purpose of the ultimate truth, becomes bewildered.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvameva mahābhāga kapilarṣimahaṃ dvija /
praṣṭumabhyudyato gatvā śreyaḥ kintvatra saṃśaye //
meaning:
पूर्वमेव महाभाग कपिलर्षिमहं द्विज /
प्रष्टुमभ्युद्यतो गत्वा श्रेयः किन्त्वत्र संशये //
text_mt: en: Previously indeed, O fortunate one, I set out, having gone to the sage Kapila, / to ask, O twice-born, what is the ultimate good; but here I am in doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
tadantare ca bhavatā yadidaṃ vākyamīritam /
tenaiva paramārthārthaṃ tvayi cetaḥ pradhāvati //
meaning:
तदन्तरे च भवता यदिदं वाक्यमीरितम् /
तेनैव परमार्थार्थं त्वयि चेतः प्रधावति //
text_mt: en: And meanwhile, this speech has been uttered by you; / by that very [speech], my mind runs towards you for the sake of the ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
kapilarṣirbhagavataḥ sarvabhūtasya vai kila /
viṣṇoraṃśo jaganmohanāśāya samupāgataḥ //
meaning:
कपिलर्षिर्भगवतः सर्वभूतस्य वै किल /
विष्णोरंशो जगन्मोहनाशाय समुपागतः //
text_mt: en: The sage Kapila, surely, is a portion of the blessed Viṣṇu, who is all beings, / come to destroy the delusion of the world.

sanskrit_iast:
sa eva bhagavānnūnamasmākaṃ hitakāmyayā /
pratyakṣatāmanugatastathaitadbhavatocyate //
meaning:
स एव भगवान्नूनमस्माकं हितकाम्यया /
प्रत्यक्षतामनुगतस्तथैतद्भवतोच्यते //
text_mt: en: That very Blessed One, indeed, wishing our welfare, / has come into view, and thus it is spoken by you.

sanskrit_iast:
tanmahyaṃ mohanāśāya yacchreyaḥ paramaṃ dvija /
tadvadākhila vijñānajalavīcyujadhirbhavān //
meaning:
तन्मह्यं मोहनाशाय यच्छ्रेयः परमं द्विज /
तद्वदाखिल विज्ञानजलवीच्युजधिर्भवान् //
text_mt: en: Therefore, for the destruction of my delusion, O twice-born, tell me what is the highest good; / you are an ocean of the waters and waves of all knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
bhūyaḥ pṛcchasi kiṃ śreyaḥ paramārthena pṛcchasi /
śreyāṃsi paramārthāni hyaśeṣāṇyena bhūpate //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
भूयः पृच्छसि किं श्रेयः परमार्थेन पृच्छसि /
श्रेयांसि परमार्थानि ह्यशेषाण्येन भूपते //
text_mt: en: The brāhmaṇa said: / Again you ask: "What is the highest good?" Do you ask from the viewpoint of ultimate truth? / For all goods are ultimate truths, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
devatārādhanaṃ kṛtvā dhanasaṃpadamicchati /
putrānicchati rājyaṃ ca śreyastasyaiva tannṛpa //
meaning:
देवताराधनं कृत्वा धनसंपदमिच्छति /
पुत्रानिच्छति राज्यं च श्रेयस्तस्यैव तन्नृप //
text_mt: en: Having performed the worship of deities, one desires wealth and abundance, / one desires sons and kingship; that indeed is the good for him, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
vivakinastu saṃyogaḥ śreyo 'sau paramātmanā /
karmayajñādikaṃ śreyaḥ svarlokapaladāyi yat //
meaning:
विवकिनस्तु संयोगः श्रेयो ऽसौ परमात्मना /
कर्मयज्ञादिकं श्रेयः स्वर्लोकपलदायि यत् //
text_mt: en: But for the discerning, union with the Supreme Self is the good; / the rites of sacrifice and the like, which bestow the fruit of heaven, are [also] a good.

sanskrit_iast:
śreyaḥ pradhānaṃ ca phale tadevānabhisaṃhite /
ātmā dhyeyaḥ sadā bhūpa yogayuktaistathā paraiḥ //
meaning:
श्रेयः प्रधानं च फले तदेवानभिसंहिते /
आत्मा ध्येयः सदा भूप योगयुक्तैस्तथा परैः //
text_mt: en: And that very [action] is the foremost good when its fruit is not aimed at; / the Self is always to be meditated upon by those joined in yoga, O king, as well as by others.

sanskrit_iast:
śreya stasyaiva saṃyogaḥ śreyo yaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
śreyāṃsyevamanekāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
meaning:
श्रेय स्तस्यैव संयोगः श्रेयो यः परमात्मनः /
श्रेयांस्येवमनेकानि शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः //
text_mt: en: His good is union with that very Supreme Self; / thus there are many goods, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃtyatra paramārthāstu na tvete śrūyatāṃ ca me /
dharmo 'yaṃ tyajate kiṃ tu paramārtho dhanaṃ yadi //
meaning:
संत्यत्र परमार्थास्तु न त्वेते श्रूयतां च मे /
धर्मो ऽयं त्यजते किं तु परमार्थो धनं यदि //
text_mt: en: But these are not the ultimate truth here; listen to me: / if wealth is the ultimate truth, why is this dharma abandoned?

sanskrit_iast:
vyayaścakriyata kasmātkāmaprāptyupalakṣaṇaḥ /
mutraścetparamārthākhyaḥ so 'pyanyasya nareśvara //
meaning:
व्ययश्चक्रियत कस्मात्कामप्राप्त्युपलक्षणः /
मुत्रश्चेत्परमार्थाख्यः सो ऽप्यन्यस्य नरेश्वर //
text_mt: en: And why is expenditure incurred, characterized by the attainment of desire? / If a son is called the ultimate truth, he too [belongs] to another, O ruler of men.

sanskrit_iast:
paramārthabhūtaḥ so 'nyasya paramārtho hi naḥ pitā /
evaṃ na paramārtho 'sti jagatyatra carācare //
meaning:
परमार्थभूतः सो ऽन्यस्य परमार्थो हि नः पिता /
एवं न परमार्थो ऽस्ति जगत्यत्र चराचरे //
text_mt: en: He is an ultimate truth to another; indeed, our father is an ultimate truth [to us]; / thus there is no ultimate truth in this moving and unmoving world.

sanskrit_iast:
paramārtho hi kāryāṇi karaṇānāmaśeṣataḥ /
rājyādiprāptiratroktā paramārthatayā yadi //
meaning:
परमार्थो हि कार्याणि करणानामशेषतः /
राज्यादिप्राप्तिरत्रोक्ता परमार्थतया यदि //
text_mt: en: For the ultimate truth [would be] the actions of the sense organs without remainder; / if the attainment of kingship and the like here is spoken of as the ultimate truth,

sanskrit_iast:
paramārthā bhavantyatra na bhavanti ca vai tataḥ /
ṛgyajuḥsāmaniṣpādyaṃ yajñakarma mataṃ tava //
meaning:
परमार्था भवन्त्यत्र न भवन्ति च वै ततः /
ऋग्यजुःसामनिष्पाद्यं यज्ञकर्म मतं तव //
text_mt: en: then ultimate truths exist and do not exist here on that account. / Sacrificial rite accomplished by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma [Vedas] is held by you

sanskrit_iast:
paramārthabhūtaṃ tatrāpi śrūyatāṃ gadato mama /
yattu niṣpādyate kāryaṃ mṛdā kāraṇabhūtayā //
meaning:
परमार्थभूतं तत्रापि श्रूयतां गदतो मम /
यत्तु निष्पाद्यते कार्यं मृदा कारणभूतया //
text_mt: en: to be the ultimate truth; hear from me speaking on that too: / that effect which is produced by clay as the material cause,

sanskrit_iast:
tatkāraṇānugamanājjāyate nṛpa mṛnmayam /
evaṃ vināśibhirdravyaiḥ samidājyakuśādibhiḥ //
meaning:
तत्कारणानुगमनाज्जायते नृप मृन्मयम् /
एवं विनाशिभिर्द्रव्यैः समिदाज्यकुशादिभिः //
text_mt: en: that, by following its cause, O king, becomes made of clay; / so too, by perishable substances such as fuel, ghee, and kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
niṣpādyate kriyā yā tu sā bhavitrī vināśinī /
anāśī paramārthastu prājñairabhyupagamyate //
meaning:
निष्पाद्यते क्रिया या तु सा भवित्री विनाशिनी /
अनाशी परमार्थस्तु प्राज्ञैरभ्युपगम्यते //
text_mt: en: that rite which is performed is bound to be perishable; / but the imperishable is accepted as the ultimate truth by the wise.

sanskrit_iast:
yattuṃ nāśi na saṃdeho nāśidravyopapāditam /
tadevāpaladaṃ karma paramārtho mato mama //
meaning:
यत्तुं नाशि न संदेहो नाशिद्रव्योपपादितम् /
तदेवापलदं कर्म परमार्थो मतो मम //
text_mt: en: What is produced by perishable substances is perishable—there is no doubt; / that very action which is without [desire for] fruit is held by me to be the ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
muktisādhanabhūtatvātparamārtho na sādhanam /
dhyānamevātmano bhūpaparamārthārthaśabditam //
meaning:
मुक्तिसाधनभूतत्वात्परमार्थो न साधनम् /
ध्यानमेवात्मनो भूपपरमार्थार्थशब्दितम् //
text_mt: en: Because it is a means to liberation, the ultimate truth is not a [mere] means; / meditation on the Self alone, O king, is designated as the ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
bhedakāri parebhyastu paramārtho na bhedavān /
paramārthātmanoryogaḥ paramārtha itīṣyate //
meaning:
भेदकारि परेभ्यस्तु परमार्थो न भेदवान् /
परमार्थात्मनोर्योगः परमार्थ इतीष्यते //
text_mt: en: But what creates division [belongs] to other things; the ultimate truth is without division; / the union of the ultimate truth and the Self is acknowledged as the ultimate truth.

sanskrit_iast:
mithyaitadanyaddravyaṃ hi naitaddravyamayaṃ yataḥ /
tasmācchreyāṃsyaśeṣāṇi nṛpaitāni na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
मिथ्यैतदन्यद्द्रव्यं हि नैतद्द्रव्यमयं यतः /
तस्माच्छ्रेयांस्यशेषाणि नृपैतानि न संशयः //
text_mt: en: For this other substance is false, because it does not consist of [that real] substance; / therefore all these are goods, O king, there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
paramārthastu bhūpāla saṃkṣepācchrūyatāṃ mama /
eko vyāpī samaḥ śuddho nirguṇa prakṛteḥ paraḥ //
meaning:
परमार्थस्तु भूपाल संक्षेपाच्छ्रूयतां मम /
एको व्यापी समः शुद्धो निर्गुण प्रकृतेः परः //
text_mt: en: But hear the ultimate truth briefly from me, O king: / one, all-pervading, equal, pure, free from the guṇas, beyond Prakṛti,

sanskrit_iast:
janmavṛddhyādirahita ātmā sarvagato nṛpa /
parijñānamayo sadbhirnāmajātyādibhivibhuḥ //
meaning:
जन्मवृद्ध्यादिरहित आत्मा सर्वगतो नृप /
परिज्ञानमयो सद्भिर्नामजात्यादिभिविभुः //
text_mt: en: devoid of birth, growth, and the like, the Self is all-pervading, O king, / consisting of full consciousness, [perceived] by the wise, all-pervasive through names, species, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
na yogavānna yukto 'bhūnnaiva pārthivaḥ yokṣyati /
tasyātmaparadeheṣu sato 'pyekamayaṃ hi tat //
meaning:
न योगवान्न युक्तो ऽभून्नैव पार्थिवः योक्ष्यति /
तस्यात्मपरदेहेषु सतो ऽप्येकमयं हि तत् //
text_mt: en: It has no contact, nor was it united, nor will it be united, O king; / though existing in one's own and others' bodies, it is indeed of one nature.

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānaṃ paramārtho 'sau vetti no 'tathyadarśanaḥ /
veṇuraṅghravibhedena bhedaḥ ṣaṅjādisaṃjñitaḥ //
meaning:
विज्ञानं परमार्थो ऽसौ वेत्ति नो ऽतथ्यदर्शनः /
वेणुरङ्घ्रविभेदेन भेदः षङ्जादिसंज्ञितः //
text_mt: en: That consciousness is the ultimate truth; one who perceives untruth does not know it. / By the difference of holes in a flute, there is a difference known as the notes ṣaḍja and the rest;

sanskrit_iast:
abhedo vyāpino vāyostathā tasya mahātmanaḥ /
ekatvaṃ rūpabhedaśca vāhyakarmapravṛttijaḥ //
meaning:
अभेदो व्यापिनो वायोस्तथा तस्य महात्मनः /
एकत्वं रूपभेदश्च वाह्यकर्मप्रवृत्तिजः //
text_mt: en: there is no difference in the all-pervading air; likewise is it for that Great Self: / unity [is its nature], and diversity of form arises from the operation of external karma.

sanskrit_iast:
devādibhedamadhyāste nāstyevācaraṇo hi saḥ /
śṛṇvatra bhūpa prāgvṛttaṃ yadgītamṛbhuṇā bhavet //
meaning:
देवादिभेदमध्यास्ते नास्त्येवाचरणो हि सः /
शृण्वत्र भूप प्राग्वृत्तं यद्गीतमृभुणा भवेत् //
text_mt: He who resides within differences such as gods and the rest is indeed without bodily action. / Hear regarding this, O king, an ancient event that was sung by Ṛbhu,

sanskrit_iast:
avabodhaṃ janayato nidādhasya dvijanmanaḥ /
ṛbhurnāmābavatputro brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭinaḥ //
meaning:
अवबोधं जनयतो निदाधस्य द्विजन्मनः /
ऋभुर्नामाबवत्पुत्रो ब्रह्मणः परमेष्टिनः //
text_mt: imparting awakening to the twice-born Nidāgha. / There was a son of the supreme lord Brahmā named Ṛbhu,

sanskrit_iast:
vijñāta tattvasadbhāvo nisargādeva bhūpate /
tasya śiṣyo nidāgho 'bhūtpulastyatanayaḥ purā //
meaning:
विज्ञात तत्त्वसद्भावो निसर्गादेव भूपते /
तस्य शिष्यो निदाघो ऽभूत्पुलस्त्यतनयः पुरा //
text_mt: who had understood the reality of truth by his very nature, O ruler of the earth. / Formerly, his disciple was Nidāgha, the son of Pulastya.

sanskrit_iast:
prādādaśeṣavijñānaṃ sa tasmai parayā mudā /
avāptajñāna tattvasya na tasyādvaitavāsanā //
meaning:
प्रादादशेषविज्ञानं स तस्मै परया मुदा /
अवाप्तज्ञान तत्त्वस्य न तस्याद्वैतवासना //
text_mt: With great joy, he gave him complete knowledge; / yet though he had attained knowledge of truth, he lacked the latent impression of non-duality.

sanskrit_iast:
sa ṛbhustarkayāmāsa nidāghasya nareśvara /
devikāyāstaṭe vīra nāgaraṃ nāma vai puram //
meaning:
स ऋभुस्तर्कयामास निदाघस्य नरेश्वर /
देविकायास्तटे वीर नागरं नाम वै पुरम् //
text_mt: That Ṛbhu reflected upon Nidāgha, O ruler of men. / On the bank of the Devikā, O hero, there was a city named Nāgara,

sanskrit_iast:
samṛddhamatiramyaṃ ca pulastyena niveśitam /
ramyopavanaparyantaṃ sa tasminpārthavottama //
meaning:
समृद्धमतिरम्यं च पुलस्त्येन निवेशितम् /
रम्योपवनपर्यन्तं स तस्मिन्पार्थवोत्तम //
text_mt: prosperous and very charming, founded by Pulastya, / surrounded by delightful groves; in it, O best of kings,

sanskrit_iast:
nidādhanāmāyogajñastasya śiṣyo 'bhavatpurā /
divye varṣasahasre tu samatīte 'sya tatpuram //
meaning:
निदाधनामायोगज्ञस्तस्य शिष्यो ऽभवत्पुरा /
दिव्ये वर्षसहस्रे तु समतीते ऽस्य तत्पुरम् //
text_mt: his disciple formerly lived, Nidāgha by name, who knew yoga. / When a thousand divine years had elapsed, to his city

sanskrit_iast:
jagāma sa ṛbhuḥ śiṣyaṃ nidāghamavalokitum /
sa tasya vaiśvadevanti dvārālokanagocaraḥ //
meaning:
जगाम स ऋभुः शिष्यं निदाघमवलोकितुम् /
स तस्य वैश्वदेवन्ति द्वारालोकनगोचरः //
text_mt: that Ṛbhu went, to see his disciple Nidāgha. / At the end of his Vaiśvadeva rite, [Ṛbhu] came into the range of his sight at the doorway.

sanskrit_iast:
sthita stena gṛhītārtho nijaveśma praveśitaḥ /
prakṣālitāṅghripāṇiṃ ca kṛtāsanaparigraham //
meaning:
स्थित स्तेन गृहीतार्थो निजवेश्म प्रवेशितः /
प्रक्षालिताङ्घ्रिपाणिं च कृतासनपरिग्रहम् //
text_mt: Standing there, his hospitality was accepted by him and he was led into his house; / and when his feet and hands had been washed and he had taken a seat,

sanskrit_iast:
uvāca sa dvijaśreṣṭho bhujyatāmiti sādaram /
ṛbhuruvāca
bho vipravarya bhoktavyaṃ yadatra bhavato gṛhe //
meaning:
उवाच स द्विजश्रेष्ठो भुज्यतामिति सादरम् /
ऋभुरुवाच
भो विप्रवर्य भोक्तव्यं यदत्र भवतो गृहे //
text_mt:
that best of the twice-born said respectfully: “Please eat.” / Ṛbhu said:
“O best of Brahmins, whatever food is here in your house,

sanskrit_iast:
tatkathyatāṃ kadanneṣu na prītiḥ satataṃ mama /
nidāgha uvāca
saktuyāvakavrīhīnāmapūpānāṃ ca me gṛhe //
meaning:
तत्कथ्यतां कदन्नेषु न प्रीतिः सततं मम /
निदाघ उवाच
सक्तुयावकव्रीहीनामपूपानां च मे गृहे //
text_mt:
let that be told; I never have pleasure in bad food.” / Nidāgha said:
“In my house there are roasted grain flours, barley dishes, rice, and cakes;

sanskrit_iast:
yadrocate dvijaśreṣṭha tāvadbhuṅkṣva yathecchayā /
ṛbhuruvāca
kadannāni dijaitāni miṣṭamannaṃ prayaccha me //
meaning:
यद्रोचते द्विजश्रेष्ठ तावद्भुङ्क्ष्व यथेच्छया /
ऋभुरुवाच
कदन्नानि दिजैतानि मिष्टमन्नं प्रयच्छ मे //
text_mt:
whatever pleases you, O best of the twice-born, eat that much as you wish.” / Ṛbhu said:
“These are bad foods, O twice-born; give me sweet food,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃyāvapāyasādīni cekṣukā rasavanti ca /
nidāgha uvāca
gṛhe śālini madgehe yatkiñcidati śobhanam //
meaning:
संयावपायसादीनि चेक्षुका रसवन्ति च /
निदाघ उवाच
गृहे शालिनि मद्गेहे यत्किञ्चिदति शोभनम् //
text_mt:
such as saṃyāva sweets, milk rice, and sweet dishes prepared with sugarcane juice.” / Nidāgha said:
“O lady of the house, whatever is exceedingly fine in my home,

sanskrit_iast:
bhojyeṣu sādhanaṃ miṣṭaṃ tenāsyānnaṃ prasādhaya /
ityuktā tena sā patnī miṣṭamannaṃ dvijasya tat //
meaning:
भोज्येषु साधनं मिष्टं तेनास्यान्नं प्रसाधय /
इत्युक्ता तेन सा पत्नी मिष्टमन्नं द्विजस्य तत् //
text_mt: the sweet ingredients among foods, prepare his meal with that.” / Addressed in this way by him, his wife prepared that sweet food

sanskrit_iast:
prasādhitavatī tadvai bharturvacanagauravāt /
na bhuktavantamicchāto miṣṭamannaṃ mahāmunim //
meaning:
प्रसाधितवती तद्वै भर्तुर्वचनगौरवात् /
न भुक्तवन्तमिच्छातो मिष्टमन्नं महामुनिम् //
text_mt: for the twice-born, out of respect for her husband's word. / When the great sage had eaten the sweet food to his satisfaction,

sanskrit_iast:
nidāghaḥ prāhabhūpāla praśrayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ /
nidāgha uvāca
api te paramā tṛptirutpannā puṣṭireva //
meaning:
निदाघः प्राहभूपाल प्रश्रयावनतः स्थितः /
निदाघ उवाच
अपि ते परमा तृप्तिरुत्पन्ना पुष्टिरेव //
text_mt:
Nidāgha, standing bowed with deference, said, O king: / Nidāgha said:
“Has supreme satisfaction arisen in you, and nourishment as well?

sanskrit_iast:
api te mānasaṃ svasthamāhāreṇa kṛtaṃ dvija /
kva nivāsī bhavānvipra kva vā gantuṃ samudyataḥ //
meaning:
अपि ते मानसं स्वस्थमाहारेण कृतं द्विज /
क्व निवासी भवान्विप्र क्व वा गन्तुं समुद्यतः //
text_mt: Has your mind been made comfortable by the meal, O twice-born? / Where is your dwelling, O Brahmin, and where are you preparing to go?

sanskrit_iast:
āgamyate ca bhavatā yatastaśca nivedyatām /
ṛmuruvāca
kṣudhitasya ca bhukte 'nne tṛptirbrahmanvijāyate //
meaning:
आगम्यते च भवता यतस्तश्च निवेद्यताम् /
ऋमुरुवाच
क्षुधितस्य च भुक्ते ऽन्ने तृप्तिर्ब्रह्मन्विजायते //
text_mt:
And from where have you arrived? Please tell that.” / Ṛbhu said:
“When food is eaten by a hungry man, O Brahmin, satisfaction arises.

sanskrit_iast:
na me kṣudhā bhavettṝptiḥ kasmānmāṃ dvija pṛcchati /
vahninā pārthivenādau dagdhe vai kṣurāpīśvaḥ //
meaning:
न मे क्षुधा भवेत्तॄप्तिः कस्मान्मां द्विज पृच्छति /
वह्निना पार्थिवेनादौ दग्धे वै क्षुरापीश्वः //
text_mt: I have no hunger; why does the twice-born ask me about satisfaction? / When the bodily essence is consumed by the gastric fire, hunger arises;

sanskrit_iast:
bhavatyaṃbhasi ca kṣīṇe nṛṇāṃ tṛṣṇāsamudbhavaḥ /
kṣuttṛṣṇe dehadharmākhye na mamaite yato dvija //
meaning:
भवत्यंभसि च क्षीणे नृणां तृष्णासमुद्भवः /
क्षुत्तृष्णे देहधर्माख्ये न ममैते यतो द्विज //
text_mt: and when water is diminished, thirst arises in men. / Hunger and thirst are properties of the body; because these are not mine, O twice-born,

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ kṣutsaṃbhavābhāvāttṛptirastyeva me sadā /
manasaḥ svasthatā tuṣṭiścittadharmāvimau dvija //
meaning:
ततः क्षुत्संभवाभावात्तृप्तिरस्त्येव मे सदा /
मनसः स्वस्थता तुष्टिश्चित्तधर्माविमौ द्विज //
text_mt: therefore, in the absence of the occurrence of hunger, there is ever satisfaction for me. / Composure of mind and contentment are properties of thought, O twice-born.

sanskrit_iast:
cetaso yasya yatpṛṣṭaṃ pumānebhirna yujyate /
kva nivāsastavetyuktaṃ kva gantāsi ca yattvayā //
meaning:
चेतसो यस्य यत्पृष्टं पुमानेभिर्न युज्यते /
क्व निवासस्तवेत्युक्तं क्व गन्तासि च यत्त्वया //
text_mt: What was asked belongs to the mind; the person is not connected with these. / As to what was said by you: ‘Where is your dwelling, and where will you go,’

sanskrit_iast:
kutaścāgamyate tvetātrritaye 'pi nibodha me /
pumānsavargato vyāpītyākāśavadayaṃ yataḥ //
meaning:
कुतश्चागम्यते त्वेतात्र्रितये ऽपि निबोध मे /
पुमान्सवर्गतो व्यापीत्याकाशवदयं यतः //
text_mt: ‘and whence do you come?’—listen to me regarding all three of these: / since the person is all-pervading and omnipresent like space,

sanskrit_iast:
kutaḥ kutra kva gantāsītyetadapyarthavatkatham /
so 'haṃ gantā na cāgantā naikadeśaniketanaḥ //
meaning:
कुतः कुत्र क्व गन्तासीत्येतदप्यर्थवत्कथम् /
सो ऽहं गन्ता न चागन्ता नैकदेशनिकेतनः //
text_mt: how is this meaningful: ‘Whence, whither, and where will you go?’ / As such, I am neither a goer nor a comer, nor do I have a home in any single place.

sanskrit_iast:
tvaṃ cānye ca na ca tvaṃ tvaṃ nānye naivāhamapyaham /
miṣṭanne miṣṭamityeṣā jihvā sā me kṛtā tava //
meaning:
त्वं चान्ये च न च त्वं त्वं नान्ये नैवाहमप्यहम् /
मिष्टन्ने मिष्टमित्येषा जिह्वा सा मे कृता तव //
text_mt: You and others [are one]; you are not you, others are not others, nor am I indeed I. / As for sweet food, this tongue of mine was made by you [to ask]: ‘What is sweet?’

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ vakṣyatīti tatrāpi śrūyatāṃ dvijasattamā /
miṣṭameva yadāmiṣṭaṃ tadevodvegakāraṇam //
meaning:
किं वक्ष्यतीति तत्रापि श्रूयतां द्विजसत्तमा /
मिष्टमेव यदामिष्टं तदेवोद्वेगकारणम् //
text_mt: Regarding what it would say, hear that too, O best of the twice-born: / when sweet food itself becomes non-sweet, it becomes a cause of distress.

sanskrit_iast:
amiṣṭaṃ jāyate miṣṭaṃ miṣṭādudvijate janaḥ /
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu kimannaṃ rucikāraṇam //
meaning:
अमिष्टं जायते मिष्टं मिष्टादुद्विजते जनः /
आदिमध्यावसानेषु किमन्नं रुचिकारणम् //
text_mt: The non-sweet becomes sweet, and a person grows disgusted with the sweet; / at the beginning, middle, and end, what food is [inherently] the cause of delight?

sanskrit_iast:
mṛṇmayaṃ hi mṛdā yadvadgṛhaṃ liptaṃ sthirībhavet /
pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā dehaḥ pārthivaiḥ paramāṇubhiḥ //
meaning:
मृण्मयं हि मृदा यद्वद्गृहं लिप्तं स्थिरीभवेत् /
पार्थिवो ऽयं तथा देहः पार्थिवैः परमाणुभिः //
text_mt: Just as an earthen house plastered with earth becomes firm, / so this earthy body is maintained by earthy particles.

sanskrit_iast:
yavagodhūmamudgādir ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ payo dadhi /
guḍaḥ phalānīti tathā pārthivāḥ paramāṇavaḥ //
meaning:
यवगोधूममुद्गादिर् घृतं तैलं पयो दधि /
गुडः फलानीति तथा पार्थिवाः परमाणवः //
text_mt: Barley, wheat, mung beans, and the like, ghee, oil, milk, curd, / molasses, and fruits are likewise earthy particles.

sanskrit_iast:
tadetadbhavatā jñātvā miṣṭāmiṣṭavicāri yat /
tanmanaḥ śamanālabi kāryaṃ prāpyaṃ hi muktaye //
meaning:
तदेतद्भवता ज्ञात्वा मिष्टामिष्टविचारि यत् /
तन्मनः शमनालबि कार्यं प्राप्यं हि मुक्तये //
text_mt: Knowing all this, one should bring peace to that mind / which deliberates upon the sweet and the non-sweet, for liberation is to be attained.”

sanskrit_iast:
ityākarṇya vacastasya paramārthāśritaṃ nṛpa /
praṇipatya mahābhāgo nidāgho vākyamabravīt //
meaning:
इत्याकर्ण्य वचस्तस्य परमार्थाश्रितं नृप /
प्रणिपत्य महाभागो निदाघो वाक्यमब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Hearing his speech based upon the supreme truth, O king, / the illustrious Nidāgha prostrated and spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
prasīda maddhitārthāya kathyatāṃ yastvamāgataḥ /
naṣṭo mohastavākarṇya vacāṃsyetāni me dvija //
meaning:
प्रसीद मद्धितार्थाय कथ्यतां यस्त्वमागतः /
नष्टो मोहस्तवाकर्ण्य वचांस्येतानि मे द्विज //
text_mt: “Be gracious; for my benefit, tell who you are that have come. / Hearing these words of yours, my delusion has been destroyed, O twice-born.”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
ṛbhurasmi tavācāryaḥ prajñādānāya te dvija /
ihāgato 'haṃ dāsyāmi paramārthaṃ subodhitam //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
ऋभुरस्मि तवाचार्यः प्रज्ञादानाय ते द्विज /
इहागतो ऽहं दास्यामि परमार्थं सुबोधितम् //
text_mt:
Ṛbhu said:
“I am Ṛbhu, your teacher, [come] to bestow wisdom upon you, O twice-born. / Having come here, I will impart the well-understood supreme truth.

sanskrit_iast:
eka evamidaṃ viddhi na bhedi sakalaṃ jagat /
vāsudevābhidheyasya svarupaṃ parātmanaḥ //
meaning:
एक एवमिदं विद्धि न भेदि सकलं जगत् /
वासुदेवाभिधेयस्य स्वरुपं परात्मनः //
text_mt: Know this entire universe to be one only, without differentiation: / the essential form of the supreme self, designated as Vāsudeva.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmaṇa uvāca
tathetyuktvā nidādhena praṇipātapuraḥ saram /
pūjitaḥ parayā bhaktyānicchitaḥ prayayau vibhuḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मण उवाच
तथेत्युक्त्वा निदाधेन प्रणिपातपुरः सरम् /
पूजितः परया भक्त्यानिच्छितः प्रययौ विभुः //
text_mt:
The Brahmin said:
Having said “So be it”, Nidāgha prostrated before him / and worshipped him with supreme devotion; and the powerful lord departed without any desire.

sanskrit_iast:
punavaṣasahasrante samāyāto nareśvara /
nidāghajñānadānāya tadeva nagaraṃ guruḥ //
meaning:
पुनवषसहस्रन्ते समायातो नरेश्वर /
निदाघज्ञानदानाय तदेव नगरं गुरुः //
text_mt: At the end of another thousand years, O ruler of men, / the teacher came again to that very city to bestow knowledge upon Nidāgha.

sanskrit_iast:
nagarasya bahiḥ so 'tha nidāghaṃ dṛṣṭavān munim /
mahābalaparīvāre puraṃ viśati pārthive //
meaning:
नगरस्य बहिः सो ऽथ निदाघं दृष्टवान् मुनिम् /
महाबलपरीवारे पुरं विशति पार्थिवे //
text_mt: Then, outside the city, he saw the sage Nidāgha / while the king, surrounded by a large army, was entering the city.

sanskrit_iast:
dūrasthitaṃ mahābhāge janasaṃmardavarjakam /
kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhamāyāntamaraṇyātsasamitkuśam //
meaning:
दूरस्थितं महाभागे जनसंमर्दवर्जकम् /
क्षुत्क्षामकण्ठमायान्तमरण्यात्ससमित्कुशम् //
text_mt: Standing far away, O fortunate one, avoiding the crowd of people, / his throat parched with hunger, coming from the forest with sacrificial fuel and kuśa grass,

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvā nidāghaṃ sa ṛbhurupāgatyābhivādya ca /
uvāca kasmādekāntaṃ sthīyata bhavatā dvija //
meaning:
दृष्ट्वा निदाघं स ऋभुरुपागत्याभिवाद्य च /
उवाच कस्मादेकान्तं स्थीयत भवता द्विज //
text_mt: seeing Nidāgha, Ṛbhu approached, saluted him, / and said: “Why are you staying apart in solitude, O twice-born one?”
Nidāgha said: / “O brāhmaṇa, great is this crowd of people as the lord of men / is wishing to enter this delightful city; therefore do I stay here.”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
narādhipo 'tra katamaḥ katamaścetaro janaḥ /
kathyatāṃ me dvijaśreṣṭha tvamabhijño mato mama //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
नराधिपो ऽत्र कतमः कतमश्चेतरो जनः /
कथ्यतां मे द्विजश्रेष्ठ त्वमभिज्ञो मतो मम //
text_mt: Ṛbhu said: / “Which one here is the king, and which one is the other person? / Tell me, O best of the twice-born; in my view, you are knowledgeable.”

sanskrit_iast:
nidāgha uvāca
yo 'yaṃ gajendramunmattamadriśṛṅgasamucchrayam /
adhiruḍho narendro 'yaṃ parito yastathetaraḥ //
meaning:
निदाघ उवाच
यो ऽयं गजेन्द्रमुन्मत्तमद्रिशृङ्गसमुच्छ्रयम् /
अधिरुढो नरेन्द्रो ऽयं परितो यस्तथेतरः //
text_mt: Nidāgha said: / “He who is mounted upon that lordly elephant, furious and lofty like a mountain peak, / is the king; those who are around him are the others.”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
etau hi gajarājānau dṛṣṭau hi yugapanmayā /
bhavatā nirviśeṣeṇa pṛthagvedopalakṣitau //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
एतौ हि गजराजानौ दृष्टौ हि युगपन्मया /
भवता निर्विशेषेण पृथग्वेदोपलक्षितौ //
text_mt: Ṛbhu said: / “Indeed, both of these—the elephant and the king—are seen at once by me; / but by you, without distinction, they are characterized as distinct.

sanskrit_iast:
tatkathyatāṃ mahābhāga viśeṣo bhavatānayoḥ /
jñātumicchāmyahaṃ ko 'tra gajaḥ ko vā narādhipaḥ //
meaning:
तत्कथ्यतां महाभाग विशेषो भवतानयोः /
ज्ञातुमिच्छाम्यहं को ऽत्र गजः को वा नराधिपः //
text_mt: Therefore tell me, O fortunate one, the distinction between the two of them; / I wish to know who here is the elephant, and who is the king.”

sanskrit_iast:
nidādha uvāca
gajoyo 'yamadho brahmannuparyasyaiṣa bhūpatiḥ /
vāhyavāhakasaṃbandhaṃ ko na jānāti vai dvija //
meaning:
निदाध उवाच
गजोयो ऽयमधो ब्रह्मन्नुपर्यस्यैष भूपतिः /
वाह्यवाहकसंबन्धं को न जानाति वै द्विज //
text_mt: Nidāgha said: / “This one below, O brāhmaṇa, is the elephant; above him is the king. / Who indeed does not know the relation between the bearer and the borne, O twice-born one?”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
brahmanyathāhaṃ jānīyāṃ tathā māmavabodhaya /
adhaḥ sattvavibhāgaṃ kiṃ kiṃ corddhamabhidhīyate //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
ब्रह्मन्यथाहं जानीयां तथा मामवबोधय /
अधः सत्त्वविभागं किं किं चोर्द्धमभिधीयते //
text_mt: Ṛbhu said: / “O brāhmaṇa, instruct me so that I may understand: / what is designated as the lower entity, and what as the upper?”

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
ityuktvā sahasāruhya nidāghaḥ prāha taṃ ṛbhum /
śrayatāṃ kathayāmyeṣa yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा सहसारुह्य निदाघः प्राह तं ऋभुम् /
श्रयतां कथयाम्येष यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / Having spoken thus, suddenly mounting upon him, Nidāgha said to Ṛbhu: / “Listen, I shall explain that about which you question me:

sanskrit_iast:
uparyahaṃ yathā rājā tvamadhaḥkuñjaro yathā /
avabodhāya te brahmandṛṣṭānto darśito mayā //
meaning:
उपर्यहं यथा राजा त्वमधःकुञ्जरो यथा /
अवबोधाय ते ब्रह्मन्दृष्टान्तो दर्शितो मया //
text_mt: I am above, like the king; you are below, like the elephant. / For your understanding, O brāhmaṇa, this example has been shown by me.”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
tvaṃ rājeva dvijaśreṣṭha sthito 'haṃ gajavadyadi /
tadevaṃ tvaṃ samācakṣva katamastvamahaṃ tathā //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
त्वं राजेव द्विजश्रेष्ठ स्थितो ऽहं गजवद्यदि /
तदेवं त्वं समाचक्ष्व कतमस्त्वमहं तथा //
text_mt: Ṛbhu said: / “If you are like the king, O best of the twice-born, and I stand like the elephant, / then explain this: which one are you, and which one am I?”

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
ityuktaḥ satvarastasya caraṇāvabhivandya saḥ /
nidādhaḥ prāha bhagavannācāryastvamṛbhurmam //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
इत्युक्तः सत्वरस्तस्य चरणावभिवन्द्य सः /
निदाधः प्राह भगवन्नाचार्यस्त्वमृभुर्मम् //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / Addressed thus, quickly bowing to his feet, / Nidāgha said: “O venerable one, you are my teacher, Ṛbhu!

sanskrit_iast:
nānyasyādvai vasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaṃ mānasaṃ tathā /
yathācāryasya tena tvāṃ manye prāptamahaṃ gurum //
meaning:
नान्यस्याद्वै वसंस्कारसंस्कृतं मानसं तथा /
यथाचार्यस्य तेन त्वां मन्ये प्राप्तमहं गुरुम् //
text_mt: No one else’s mind is thus refined by the impression of non-duality / as that of my teacher; by that I recognize that you, my guru, have arrived.”

sanskrit_iast:
ṛbhuruvāca
tavopadeśadānāya pūrvaśuśrūṣaṇāttava /
gurusnehādṛbhurnāmanidāghaṃ samupāgataḥ //
meaning:
ऋभुरुवाच
तवोपदेशदानाय पूर्वशुश्रूषणात्तव /
गुरुस्नेहादृभुर्नामनिदाघं समुपागतः //
text_mt: Ṛbhu said: / “To bestow instruction upon you, because of your past service / and out of affection for a disciple, I, named Ṛbhu, have come to Nidāgha.

sanskrit_iast:
tadetadupadiṣṭaṃ te saṃkṣepeṇa mahāmate /
paramārthasārabhūtaṃ yattadadvaitamaśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
तदेतदुपदिष्टं ते संक्षेपेण महामते /
परमार्थसारभूतं यत्तदद्वैतमशेषतः //
text_mt: Thus has this been taught to you in brief, O great-minded one: / that which is the essence of the ultimate truth, non-duality, completely.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
evamuktvā dadau vidyāṃ nidāghaṃ sa ṛbhurguruḥ /
nidāgho 'pyupadeśena tenādvaitaparo 'bhavat //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
एवमुक्त्वा ददौ विद्यां निदाघं स ऋभुर्गुरुः /
निदाघो ऽप्युपदेशेन तेनाद्वैतपरो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: The brāhmaṇa said: / Having spoken thus, the guru Ṛbhu imparted knowledge to Nidāgha; / and Nidāgha too, through that instruction, became devoted to non-duality.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvabhūtānyabhedena dadṛśe sa tadātmanaḥ /
tathā brahmatanau muktimavāca paramādvijaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वभूतान्यभेदेन ददृशे स तदात्मनः /
तथा ब्रह्मतनौ मुक्तिमवाच परमाद्विजः //
text_mt: He beheld all beings without distinction from his own Self; / and thus the twice-born one attained supreme liberation in the body of Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā tvamapi dharmajña tulyātmaripubāndhavaḥ /
bhava sarvagataṃ jñānamātmānamavanīpate //
meaning:
तथा त्वमपि धर्मज्ञ तुल्यात्मरिपुबान्धवः /
भव सर्वगतं ज्ञानमात्मानमवनीपते //
text_mt: So you too, O knower of dharma, seeing yourself, your enemy, and your relative as equal, / become the Self, which is omnipresent knowledge, O lord of the earth!

sanskrit_iast:
sitanīlādibhedena yathaikaṃ dṛśyate nabhaḥ /
bhrāntadṛṣṭibhirātmāpi tathaikaḥ sanpṛthak pṛthak //
meaning:
सितनीलादिभेदेन यथैकं दृश्यते नभः /
भ्रान्तदृष्टिभिरात्मापि तथैकः सन्पृथक् पृथक् //
text_mt: Just as the single sky appears different through designations such as white or blue, / so too the Self, though single, appears manifold to those whose vision is confused.

sanskrit_iast:
ekaḥ samastaṃ yadihāsti kiñcittadacyuto nāsti paraṃ tato 'nyat /
so 'haṃ sa ca tvaṃ sa ca sarvametadātmāṃsvayaṃ bhātyapabhedamohaḥ //
meaning:
एकः समस्तं यदिहास्ति किञ्चित्तदच्युतो नास्ति परं ततो ऽन्यत् /
सो ऽहं स च त्वं स च सर्वमेतदात्मांस्वयं भात्यपभेदमोहः //
text_mt: All that is anything whatever here is one, and that is Acyuta; there is nothing else beyond Him. / ‘He is I,’ and ‘He is you,’ and ‘He is all this’: the Self shines of Itself when the delusion of difference is removed.”

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
itīritastena sa rājavaryastatyāja bhedaṃ paramārthadṛṣṭiḥ /
sa cāpi jātismaraṇāvabodastatraiva janmanyapavargamāpa //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
इतीरितस्तेन स राजवर्यस्तत्याज भेदं परमार्थदृष्टिः /
स चापि जातिस्मरणावबोदस्तत्रैव जन्मन्यपवर्गमाप //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / Addressed thus by him, that best of kings, endowed with insight into the ultimate truth, abandoned difference; / and he too, awakening to the memory of previous births, attained final emancipation in that very life.

sanskrit_iast:
paramārthādhyātmametattubhyamuktaṃ munīśvara /
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śrortṛāṇāṃ cāpi muktidam //
meaning:
परमार्थाध्यात्ममेतत्तुभ्यमुक्तं मुनीश्वर /
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां श्रोर्तृआणां चापि मुक्तिदम् //
text_mt: This spiritual discourse on the ultimate truth has been spoken to you, O lord of sages; / it grants liberation to brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and listeners as well.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā brahmaṃstathā te gaditaṃ mayā /
brahmajñānamidaṃ śuddhaṃ kimanyatkathayāmi vai //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvi.pā.ekonapañcāśattamodhyāyaḥ
meaning:
यथा पृष्टं त्वया ब्रह्मंस्तथा ते गदितं मया /
ब्रह्मज्ञानमिदं शुद्धं किमन्यत्कथयामि वै //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वि.पा.एकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोध्यायः
text_mt:
As was asked by you, O brāhmaṇa, so has it been declared to you by me: / this pure knowledge of Brahman. What else indeed shall I tell you?”

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter in the second quarter of the Bṛhadupākhyāna in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
śrutvā sanandanasyetthaṃ vacanaṃ nārado muniḥ /
asaṃtuṣṭa iva prāha bhrātaraṃ taṃ sanandanam //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
श्रुत्वा सनन्दनस्येत्थं वचनं नारदो मुनिः /
असंतुष्ट इव प्राह भ्रातरं तं सनन्दनम् //
text_mt: Sūta said: / Having heard these words of Sanandana, the sage Nārada, / as if unsatisfied, said to his brother Sanandana:

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭaṃ bhavato mayā /
tathāpi nātmā prīyeta śṛṇvanharikathāṃ muhuḥ //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टं भवतो मया /
तथापि नात्मा प्रीयेत शृण्वन्हरिकथां मुहुः //
text_mt: Nārada said: / “O venerable one, everything about which I asked you has been told; / nonetheless, my soul is not satiated by repeatedly hearing discourse on Hari.

sanskrit_iast:
śrūyate vyāsaputrastu śukaḥ paramadharmavit /
siddhiṃ sumahatīṃ prāpto nirviṇṇo 'vāntaraṃ bahiḥ //
meaning:
श्रूयते व्यासपुत्रस्तु शुकः परमधर्मवित् /
सिद्धिं सुमहतीं प्राप्तो निर्विण्णो ऽवान्तरं बहिः //
text_mt: It is heard that Vyāsa’s son, Śuka, knowing the highest dharma, / attained exceedingly great perfection, being detached within and without.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmanpuṃsastu vijñānaṃ mahatāṃ sevanaṃ vinā /
na jāyate kathaṃ prāpto jñānaṃ vyāsātmajaḥ śiśuḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मन्पुंसस्तु विज्ञानं महतां सेवनं विना /
न जायते कथं प्राप्तो ज्ञानं व्यासात्मजः शिशुः //
text_mt: O brāhmaṇa, discernment does not arise in a person without serving the great; / how did Vyāsa’s son, as a child, attain knowledge?

sanskrit_iast:
tasya janmarahasyaṃ me kamacāpyasya śṛṇvate /
samākhyāhi mahābhāga mo7śāstrārthavidbhavān //
meaning:
तस्य जन्मरहस्यं मे कमचाप्यस्य शृण्वते /
समाख्याहि महाभाग मो7शास्त्रार्थविद्भवान् //
text_mt: Tell me, who am listening, the secret of his birth and of his deeds, / O fortunate one, for you know the meaning of the scriptures on liberation.”

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu viprapravakṣyāmi śukotpattiṃ samāsataḥ /
yāṃ śrutvā brahmatattvajño jāyate mānavo mune //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु विप्रप्रवक्ष्यामि शुकोत्पत्तिं समासतः /
यां श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मतत्त्वज्ञो जायते मानवो मुने //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / “Listen, O brāhmaṇa; I shall relate the origin of Śuka in brief, / hearing which a man becomes a knower of the truth of Brahman, O sage.

sanskrit_iast:
na hāyanairna palitairna vittena na bandhubhiḥ /
ṛṣayaścakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān //
meaning:
न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः /
ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्मं यो ऽनूचानः स नो महान् //
text_mt: Not by years, nor by grey hair, nor by wealth, nor by kinsmen / did the ṛṣis establish dharma: ‘He who has studied the Veda is great among us.’

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
anūcānaḥ kathaṃbrahmanpumānbhavati mānada /
tanme karma samācakṣva śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ mama //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
अनूचानः कथंब्रह्मन्पुमान्भवति मानद /
तन्मे कर्म समाचक्ष्व श्रोतुं कौतूहलं मम //
text_mt: Nārada said: / “How does a man become an anūcāna, O brāhmaṇa, O giver of honor? / Explain that practice to me; I have curiosity to hear.”

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi hyanūcānasya lakṣaṇam /
yajjñātvā sāṅgavedānāmabhijño jāyate naraḥ //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि ह्यनूचानस्य लक्षणम् /
यज्ज्ञात्वा साङ्गवेदानामभिज्ञो जायते नरः //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / “Listen, O Nārada, I shall declare the characteristics of an anūcāna, / knowing which a man becomes proficient in the Vedas along with their auxiliary limbs.

sanskrit_iast:
śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣaṃ tathā /
chandaḥśāstraṃ ṣaḍetāni vādāṅgāni vidurbudhāḥ //
meaning:
शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं ज्योतिषं तथा /
छन्दःशास्त्रं षडेतानि वादाङ्गानि विदुर्बुधाः //
text_mt: Phonetics, ritual treatises, grammar, etymology, astronomy, / and the science of metrics—the wise know these six as the limbs of the Vedas.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgvedro 'tha yadurvedaḥ sāmavedo hyatharvaṇaḥ /
vedāścatvāra evaite proktā dharmanirūpaṇe //
meaning:
ऋग्वेद्रो ऽथ यदुर्वेदः सामवेदो ह्यथर्वणः /
वेदाश्चत्वार एवैते प्रोक्ता धर्मनिरूपणे //
text_mt: The Ṛgveda, then the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda: / these four alone are declared as the Vedas for determining dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃgānvedānguroryastu samadhīte dvijottamaḥ /
so 'nūcānaḥ prabhavati nānyathā granthakoṭibhiḥ //
meaning:
सांगान्वेदान्गुरोर्यस्तु समधीते द्विजोत्तमः /
सो ऽनूचानः प्रभवति नान्यथा ग्रन्थकोटिभिः //
text_mt: That best of the twice-born who properly studies the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs from a teacher / becomes an anūcāna, not otherwise through crores of texts.”

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
aṅgānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi vedānāṃ cāpi vistarāt /
tvaṃmasmāsu mahāvijñaḥ sāṃgeṣveteṣu mānada //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
अङ्गानां लक्षणं ब्रूहि वेदानां चापि विस्तरात् /
त्वंमस्मासु महाविज्ञः सांगेष्वेतेषु मानद //
text_mt: Nārada said: / “Tell the characteristics of the auxiliary limbs and of the Vedas in detail; / among us you are exceedingly wise concerning these [Vedas] with their auxiliary limbs, O giver of honor.”

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
praśnabhāro 'yamatulastvayā mama kṛto dvija /
saṃkṣepātkathayiṣyāmi sārameṣāṃ suniścitam //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
प्रश्नभारो ऽयमतुलस्त्वया मम कृतो द्विज /
संक्षेपात्कथयिष्यामि सारमेषां सुनिश्चितम् //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / “An unequaled burden of questions has been laid upon me by you, O twice-born one; / I shall relate their well-ascertained essence in brief.

sanskrit_iast:
svaraḥ pradhānaḥ śikṣāyāṃ kīrttito munibhirdijaiḥ /
vedānāṃ vedavidbhistu tacchṛṇuṣva vadāmi te //
meaning:
स्वरः प्रधानः शिक्षायां कीर्त्तितो मुनिभिर्दिजैः /
वेदानां वेदविद्भिस्तु तच्छृणुष्व वदामि ते //
text_mt: Pitch is proclaimed by twice-born sages to be the chief [element] in phonetics / for the Vedas, by the knowers of the Veda; listen to that, I shall tell you.

sanskrit_iast:
ārcikaṃ gāthikaṃ caiva sāmikaṃ ca svarāntaram /
kṛtānte svaraśāstrāṇāṃ prayoktavya viśeṣataḥ //
meaning:
आर्चिकं गाथिकं चैव सामिकं च स्वरान्तरम् /
कृतान्ते स्वरशास्त्राणां प्रयोक्तव्य विशेषतः //
text_mt: Belonging to the Ṛc, to the Gāthā, and to the Sāman, and another pitch; / according to the conclusion of the texts on pitch, they are to be employed distinctively.

sanskrit_iast:
ekāntaraḥ svaro hyapsu gāthāsudvyantaraḥ svaraḥ /
sāmasu tryantaraṃ vidyādetāvatsvarato 'ntaram //
meaning:
एकान्तरः स्वरो ह्यप्सु गाथासुद्व्यन्तरः स्वरः /
सामसु त्र्यन्तरं विद्यादेतावत्स्वरतो ऽन्तरम् //
text_mt: Pitch is separated by one interval in the verses, by two intervals in the gāthās, / and one should know it as having three intervals in the sāmans: such is the interval of pitch.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛksāmayajuraṅgāni ye yajñeṣu prayuñjate /
avijñānāddhi śikṣāyāsteṣāṃ bhavati visvaraḥ //
meaning:
ऋक्सामयजुरङ्गानि ये यज्ञेषु प्रयुञ्जते /
अविज्ञानाद्धि शिक्षायास्तेषां भवति विस्वरः //
text_mt: Those who employ the limbs of the Ṛc, Sāman, and Yajus in sacrifices / without knowledge of phonetics—their chant becomes discordant.

sanskrit_iast:
mantro hīnaḥ svarato varṇato vā mithyāprayukto na tamarthamāha /
sa vāgvajro yajamānaṃ hirnāsti yathendraśatruḥ svarato 'parādhāt //
meaning:
मन्त्रो हीनः स्वरतो वर्णतो वा मिथ्याप्रयुक्तो न तमर्थमाह /
स वाग्वज्रो यजमानं हिर्नास्ति यथेन्द्रशत्रुः स्वरतो ऽपराधात् //
text_mt: A mantra deficient in pitch or accent, or falsely employed, does not convey that intended meaning; / that verbal thunderbolt destroys the sacrificer, as did the word ‘indraśatru’ due to an error in pitch.”

sanskrit_iast:
uraḥ kaṇṭhaḥ śiraścaiva sthānāni trīṇi vāṅkye /
savanānyāhuretāni sāma vāpyarddhatoṃ'taram //
meaning:
उरः कण्ठः शिरश्चैव स्थानानि त्रीणि वाङ्क्ये /
सवनान्याहुरेतानि साम वाप्यर्द्धतोंऽतरम् //
text_mt: The chest, the throat, and the head: these are the three places in speech. / They call these the pressings, or [in] the Sāma, intermediate in half.

sanskrit_iast:
uraḥ saptavivāraṃ syāttathā kaṇṭhastathā śiraḥ /
na ca śakto 'si vyaktastu tathā prāvacanā vidhiḥ //
meaning:
उरः सप्तविवारं स्यात्तथा कण्ठस्तथा शिरः /
न च शक्तो ऽसि व्यक्तस्तु तथा प्रावचना विधिः //
text_mt: The chest has seven apertures, as does the throat, and likewise the head; / but you are not capable [to produce it] distinctly, such is the rule of recitation.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṭhakālāpavṛtteṣu taittirāhvarakeṣu ca /
ṛgvede sāmavede ca vaktavyaḥ prathamaḥ svaraḥ //
meaning:
कठकालापवृत्तेषु तैत्तिराह्वरकेषु च /
ऋग्वेदे सामवेदे च वक्तव्यः प्रथमः स्वरः //
text_mt: In the meters of the Kaṭhas and the Kalāpas, and among the Taittirīyas and Āhvarakas, / in the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda, the first note should be uttered.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgvedastu dvitīyena tṛtīyena ca vartate /
uccamadhyamasaṃghātaḥ svaro bhavati pārthivaḥ //
meaning:
ऋग्वेदस्तु द्वितीयेन तृतीयेन च वर्तते /
उच्चमध्यमसंघातः स्वरो भवति पार्थिवः //
text_mt: The Ṛgveda proceeds with the second and third [notes]; / a combination of high and middle becomes the terrestrial note, O king.

sanskrit_iast:
tṛtīya prathamakruṣṭā kurvantyāhvarakān svarān /
dvitīyādyāstu madrāntāstaittirīyāścatuḥsvarān //
meaning:
तृतीय प्रथमक्रुष्टा कुर्वन्त्याह्वरकान् स्वरान् /
द्वितीयाद्यास्तु मद्रान्तास्तैत्तिरीयाश्चतुःस्वरान् //
text_mt: The Āhvarakas make their notes using the third, the first, and the kruṣṭa; / but the Taittirīyas use four notes, beginning with the second and ending with the mandra.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamaśca dvitīyaśca tṛtīyo 'tha caturthakaḥ /
mandraḥ kruṣṭo munīśvara etānkurvanti sāmagāḥ //
meaning:
प्रथमश्च द्वितीयश्च तृतीयो ऽथ चतुर्थकः /
मन्द्रः क्रुष्टो मुनीश्वर एतान्कुर्वन्ति सामगाः //
text_mt: The first, the second, the third, then the fourth, / the mandra, and the kruṣṭa, O lord of sages—these the Sāma-singers produce.

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyaprathamāvetau nāṇḍibhāllavinau svarau /
tathā śātapathāvetau svarau vājasaneyinām //
meaning:
द्वितीयप्रथमावेतौ नाण्डिभाल्लविनौ स्वरौ /
तथा शातपथावेतौ स्वरौ वाजसनेयिनाम् //
text_mt: These two notes, the second and the first, belong to the Nāṇḍis and Bhāllavins; / likewise these two belong to the Śatapatha [tradition] of the Vājasaneyins.

sanskrit_iast:
ete viśeṣataḥ proktāḥ svarā vai sārvavaidikāḥ /
ityetañcaritaṃ sarvaṃ svarāṇāṃ sārvavaidikam //
meaning:
एते विशेषतः प्रोक्ताः स्वरा वै सार्ववैदिकाः /
इत्येतञ्चरितं सर्वं स्वराणां सार्ववैदिकम् //
text_mt: These have been proclaimed specifically as the universal Vedic notes; / thus has been described this entire course of the universal Vedic notes.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmavede tu vakṣyāmi svarāṇāṃ caritaṃ yathā /
alpagranthaṃ prabhūtārthaṃ sāmavedāṅgamuttamam //
meaning:
सामवेदे तु वक्ष्यामि स्वराणां चरितं यथा /
