अल्पग्रन्थं प्रभूतार्थं सामवेदाङ्गमुत्तमम् //
text_mt: Now I shall explain the course of notes according to the Sāmaveda— / concise in text, abundant in meaning, the supreme subsidiary limb of the Sāmaveda—

sanskrit_iast:
tānarāgasvaragrāmamūrcchanānāṃ tu lakṣaṇam /
pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ yathā tubhyaṃ prakīrtitam //
meaning:
तानरागस्वरग्राममूर्च्छनानां तु लक्षणम् /
पवित्रं पावनं पुण्यं यथा तुभ्यं प्रकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: namely, the characteristics of the tānas, rāgas, svaras, grāmas, and mūrcchanās, / pure, purifying, and meritorious, just as it has been related to you.

sanskrit_iast:
śikṣāmāhurdvijātīnāmṛgyajuḥ sāmalakṣaṇam /
sapta svarāsrayo grāmā mṛrchanāstvekaviṃśatiḥ //
meaning:
शिक्षामाहुर्द्विजातीनामृग्यजुः सामलक्षणम् /
सप्त स्वरास्रयो ग्रामा मृर्छनास्त्वेकविंशतिः //
text_mt: They declare phonetics (śikṣā) to be the characteristic sign of the twice-born for the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma. / There are seven notes, three grāmas, and twenty-one mūrcchanās,

sanskrit_iast:
tānā ekonapañcāśadityetaḥsvaramaṇḍalam /
ṣaṅjaśca ṛṣabhaścaiva gāndhāro madhyamastathā //
meaning:
ताना एकोनपञ्चाशदित्येतःस्वरमण्डलम् /
षङ्जश्च ऋषभश्चैव गान्धारो मध्यमस्तथा //
text_mt: and forty-nine tānas—such is the circle of musical notes: / ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, and madhyama,

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamo dhaivataścaivaṃ niṣādaḥ saptamaḥ svaraḥ /
ṣaṅjamadhyamagāndhārāsrarayo grāmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चमो धैवतश्चैवं निषादः सप्तमः स्वरः /
षङ्जमध्यमगान्धारास्ररयो ग्रामाः प्रकीर्तिताः //
text_mt: pañcama, dhaivata, and niṣāda as the seventh note. / Ṣaḍja, madhyama, and gāndhāra are proclaimed as the three grāmas.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūrllokājjāyate ṣaṅjo bhuvarlokāñca madhyamaḥ /
svargābhrāñcaiva gāndhāro grāmasthānāni trīṇi hi //
meaning:
भूर्ल्लोकाज्जायते षङ्जो भुवर्लोकाञ्च मध्यमः /
स्वर्गाभ्राञ्चैव गान्धारो ग्रामस्थानानि त्रीणि हि //
text_mt: Ṣaḍja is born from the earth world (bhūrloka), and madhyama from the mid-region (bhuvarloka), / and gāndhāra from the heavens (svarga); for there are three seats of the grāmas.

sanskrit_iast:
svarāṇāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa grāmarāgā iti smṛtāḥ /
viṃśatirmadhyamagrāme ṣaṅjagrāme caturdaśa //
meaning:
स्वराणां च विशेषेण ग्रामरागा इति स्मृताः /
विंशतिर्मध्यमग्रामे षङ्जग्रामे चतुर्दश //
text_mt: And in particular, they are known as the grāmarāgas of the notes: / twenty in the madhyama-grāma, and fourteen in the ṣaḍja-grāma.

sanskrit_iast:
tānānpaṃ cadaśecchanti gāndhāre sāmagāyinām /
nadī viśālā sumukhī citrā citravatī mukhā //
meaning:
तानान्पं चदशेच्छन्ति गान्धारे सामगायिनाम् /
नदी विशाला सुमुखी चित्रा चित्रवती मुखा //
text_mt: They desire fifteen tānas in the gāndhāra[-grāma] for the singers of the Sāma. / Nadī, Viśālā, Sumukhī, Citrā, Citravatī, Mukhā,

sanskrit_iast:
balā cāpyatha vijñeyā devānāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
āpyāyinī viśvabhṛtā candrā hemā kapardinī //
meaning:
बला चाप्यथ विज्ञेया देवानां सप्त मूर्छनाः /
आप्यायिनी विश्वभृता चन्द्रा हेमा कपर्दिनी //
text_mt: and Balā should be known as the seven mūrcchanās of the gods. / Āpyāyinī, Viśvabhṛtā, Candrā, Hemā, Kapardinī,

sanskrit_iast:
maitrī ca bārhatī caiva pitṝṇāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
ṣaṅje tūttaramandrā syādṛṣabhe cābhirūhatā //
meaning:
मैत्री च बार्हती चैव पितॄणां सप्त मूर्छनाः /
षङ्जे तूत्तरमन्द्रा स्यादृषभे चाभिरूहता //
text_mt: Maitrī, and Bārhatī are the seven mūrcchanās of the ancestors. / In ṣaḍja there is Uttaramandrā, and in ṛṣabha, Abhirūhatā;

sanskrit_iast:
aśvakrāntā tu gāndhāre tṛtīyā mūrcchanā smṛtā /
madhyame khalu sauvīrā hṛṣikā pañcame svare //
meaning:
अश्वक्रान्ता तु गान्धारे तृतीया मूर्च्छना स्मृता /
मध्यमे खलु सौवीरा हृषिका पञ्चमे स्वरे //
text_mt: Aśvakrāntā in gāndhāra is considered the third mūrcchanā; / Sauvīrā indeed in madhyama, and Hṛṣīkā on the note pañcama;

sanskrit_iast:
dhaivate cāpi vijñeyā mūrchanā tūttarā matā /
niṣāde rajanīṃ vidyādṛṣīṇāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ //
meaning:
धैवते चापि विज्ञेया मूर्छना तूत्तरा मता /
निषादे रजनीं विद्यादृषीणां सप्त मूर्छनाः //
text_mt: on dhaivata, the mūrcchanā known as Uttarā is recognized; / on niṣāda, one should know Rajanī: [these are] the seven mūrcchanās of the sages.

sanskrit_iast:
upajīvanti gandharvā devānāṃ sapta mūrchanāḥ /
pitṝṇāṃ mūrcchānāḥ sapta tathā yakṣā na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
उपजीवन्ति गन्धर्वा देवानां सप्त मूर्छनाः /
पितॄणां मूर्च्छानाः सप्त तथा यक्षा न संशयः //
text_mt: The Gandharvas depend upon the seven mūrcchanās of the gods; / likewise the Yakṣas without doubt [depend upon] the seven mūrcchanās of the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣīṇāṃ mūrchanāḥ sapta yāstvimā laukikāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ṣaṅjaḥ prīṇāti vai devānṛṣīnprīṇāti carṣabhaḥ //
meaning:
ऋषीणां मूर्छनाः सप्त यास्त्विमा लौकिकाः स्मृताः /
षङ्जः प्रीणाति वै देवानृषीन्प्रीणाति चर्षभः //
text_mt: These seven mūrcchanās of the sages are considered mundane (laukika). / Ṣaḍja pleases the gods, and ṛṣabha pleases the sages;

sanskrit_iast:
pitṝn prīṇāti gāndhāro gandharvānmadhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
devānpitṝnṛṣīṃścaiva svaraḥ prīṇāti pañcamaḥ //
meaning:
पितॄन् प्रीणाति गान्धारो गन्धर्वान्मध्यमः स्वरः /
देवान्पितॄनृषींश्चैव स्वरः प्रीणाति पञ्चमः //
text_mt: gāndhāra pleases the ancestors, and the note madhyama pleases the Gandharvas; / the note pañcama pleases the gods, the ancestors, and the sages;

sanskrit_iast:
yakṣānniṣādaḥ prīṇāti bhūtagrāmaṃ ca dhaivataḥ /
gānasya tu daśavidhā guṇavṛttistu tadyathā //
meaning:
यक्षान्निषादः प्रीणाति भूतग्रामं च धैवतः /
गानस्य तु दशविधा गुणवृत्तिस्तु तद्यथा //
text_mt: niṣāda pleases the Yakṣas, and dhaivata pleases the host of living beings. / Now, the tenfold execution of qualities in singing is as follows:

sanskrit_iast: raktaṃ pūrṇamalaṅkṛtaṃ prasannaṃ vyaktaṃ vikruṣṭaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ samaṃ sukumāraṃ madhuramiti guṇāstatra raktaṃ nāma veṇuvīṇāsvarāṇāmekībhāvaṃ raktamityucyate pūrṇaṃ nāma svaraśrutipūraṇācchandaḥ pādākṣaraṃ saṃyogātpūrṇamityucyate alaṅkṛtaṃ nāmorasi śirasi kaṇṭhayuktamityalaṅkṛtaṃ prasannaṃ nāmāpagatāgadgadanirviśaṅkaṃ prasannamityucyate vyaktaṃ nāma padapadārthaprakṛtivikārāgamanopakṛttaddhitasamāsadhātunipātopasargasvaraliṅgaṃ vṛttivārttikavibhaktyarthavacanānāṃ samyagupapādanaṃ vyaktamityucyate vikruṣṭaṃ nāmoñcairuñcāritaṃ vyaktapadākṣaraṃ vikruṣṭamityucyate ślekṣṇaṃ nāma drutamavilaṃbitamuccanīcaplutasamāhārahelatālopanayādibhirupapādanābhiḥ ślakṣṇamityucyate samaṃ nāmāvāpanirvāpapradeśe pratyantarasthānānāṃ samāsaḥ samamityucyate sukumāraṃ nāma mṛdupadavarṇasvarakuhagaraṇayuktaṃ sukumāramityucyate madhuraṃ nāma svabhāvopanītalalitapadākṣaraguṇasamṛddhaṃ madhuramityucyate evametairdaśabhirguṇairyuktaṃ gānaṃ bhavati // 1//
meaning: रक्तं पूर्णमलङ्कृतं प्रसन्नं व्यक्तं विक्रुष्टं श्लक्ष्णं समं सुकुमारं मधुरमिति गुणास्तत्र रक्तं नाम वेणुवीणास्वराणामेकीभावं रक्तमित्युच्यते पूर्णं नाम स्वरश्रुतिपूरणाच्छन्दः पादाक्षरं संयोगात्पूर्णमित्युच्यते अलङ्कृतं नामोरसि शिरसि कण्ठयुक्तमित्यलङ्कृतं प्रसन्नं नामापगतागद्गदनिर्विशङ्कं प्रसन्नमित्युच्यते व्यक्तं नाम पदपदार्थप्रकृतिविकारागमनोपकृत्तद्धितसमासधातुनिपातोपसर्गस्वरलिङ्गं वृत्तिवार्त्तिकविभक्त्यर्थवचनानां सम्यगुपपादनं व्यक्तमित्युच्यते विक्रुष्टं नामोञ्चैरुञ्चारितं व्यक्तपदाक्षरं विक्रुष्टमित्युच्यते श्लेक्ष्णं नाम द्रुतमविलंबितमुच्चनीचप्लुतसमाहारहेलतालोपनयादिभिरुपपादनाभिः श्लक्ष्णमित्युच्यते समं नामावापनिर्वापप्रदेशे प्रत्यन्तरस्थानानां समासः सममित्युच्यते सुकुमारं नाम मृदुपदवर्णस्वरकुहगरणयुक्तं सुकुमारमित्युच्यते मधुरं नाम स्वभावोपनीतललितपदाक्षरगुणसमृद्धं मधुरमित्युच्यते एवमेतैर्दशभिर्गुणैर्युक्तं गानं भवति // 1//
text_mt: Harmonious (rakta), full (pūrṇa), ornamented (alaṅkṛta), lucid (prasanna), distinct (vyakta), raised (vikruṣṭa), smooth (ślakṣṇa), even (sama), delicate (sukumāra), and sweet (madhura)—these are the qualities. Among them, 'harmonious' means that the unison of the notes of the flute and the lute is called harmonious. 'Full' means that by filling out notes and microtones (śrutis), the syllables of the metrical quarters are brought into alignment; this is called full. 'Ornamented' means performed appropriately in the chest, the head, and the throat; this is called ornamented. 'Lucid' means free from stammering and hesitation; this is called lucid. 'Distinct' means that words, word-meanings, base forms, phonetic modifications, augmentations, prefixes, secondary suffixes, compounds, roots, particles, preverbs, pitch accents, grammatical gender, grammatical functions, vārttika rules, nominal case meanings, and numbers are correctly produced; this is called distinct. 'Raised' means uttered loudly with distinct words and syllables; this is called raised. 'Smooth' means produced gracefully, neither too hurried nor delayed, with proper management of high, low, and prolonged accents, easy cadence, and elision; this is called smooth. 'Even' means that in insertions and omissions the mutual pauses between adjacent positions are harmonized; this is called even. 'Delicate' means furnished with soft words, phonemes, and notes in gentle sequences; this is called delicate. 'Sweet' means rich in the naturally charming qualities of graceful words and syllables; this is called sweet. Thus singing is endowed with these ten qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
bavanti cātra ślokāḥ
śaṅkitaṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ bhītamuddhuṣṭamanunāsikam /
kākasvaraṃ mūrddhagataṃ tathā sthānavivarjitam //
meaning:
बवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाः
शङ्कितं भीषणं भीतमुद्धुष्टमनुनासिकम् /
काकस्वरं मूर्द्धगतं तथा स्थानविवर्जितम् //
text_mt: There are also verses on this topic: / Hesitant, terrifying, frightened, shouted, nasal, / crow-voiced, off-pitch in the head, devoid of proper place of articulation,

sanskrit_iast:
vistaraṃ virasaṃ caiva viśliṣṭaṃ viṣamāhatam /
vyākulaṃ tālahīnaṃ ca gītidoṣāścaturdaśa //
meaning:
विस्तरं विरसं चैव विश्लिष्टं विषमाहतम् /
व्याकुलं तालहीनं च गीतिदोषाश्चतुर्दश //
text_mt: diffuse, tasteless, disjointed, unevenly struck, / confused, and devoid of rhythm (tāla)—these are the fourteen defects of singing.

sanskrit_iast:
ācāryāḥ samamicchanti padacchedaṃ tu paṇḍitāḥ /
sriyo madhuramicchanti vikruṣṭamitare janāḥ //
meaning:
आचार्याः सममिच्छन्ति पदच्छेदं तु पण्डिताः /
स्रियो मधुरमिच्छन्ति विक्रुष्टमितरे जनाः //
text_mt: The teachers desire evenness, while scholars desire proper division of words; / women desire sweetness, and other people desire loud volume.

sanskrit_iast:
padmapatraprabhaḥ ṣaṅja ṛṣabhaḥ śukapiñjaraḥ /
kanakābhastu gāndhāro madhyamaḥ kundasannibhaḥ //
meaning:
पद्मपत्रप्रभः षङ्ज ऋषभः शुकपिञ्जरः /
कनकाभस्तु गान्धारो मध्यमः कुन्दसन्निभः //
text_mt: Ṣaḍja has the radiance of a lotus petal; ṛṣabha is reddish-yellow like a parrot; / gāndhāra has the hue of gold; madhyama resembles a kunda flower;

sanskrit_iast:
pañcamastu bhavetkṛṣṇaḥ pītakaṃ dhaivataṃ viduḥ /
niṣādaḥ sarvavarṇaḥ syādityetāḥ svaravarṇatāḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चमस्तु भवेत्कृष्णः पीतकं धैवतं विदुः /
निषादः सर्ववर्णः स्यादित्येताः स्वरवर्णताः //
text_mt: pañcama should be dark; they know dhaivata to be yellow; / niṣāda is multicolored: such are the colors of the notes.

sanskrit_iast:
pacamo madhyamaḥ ṣaṅja ityete brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ṛṣabho dhaivataścāpītyetau vai kṣatriyāvubhau //
meaning:
पचमो मध्यमः षङ्ज इत्येते ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः /
ऋषभो धैवतश्चापीत्येतौ वै क्षत्रियावुभौ //
text_mt: Pañcama, madhyama, and ṣaḍja are remembered as brāhmaṇas; / ṛṣabha and dhaivata are both kṣatriyas;

sanskrit_iast:
gāndhāraśca niṣādaśca vaiśyāvarddhena vai smṛto /
śūdratvaṃ vidhinārddhena patitatvānna saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
गान्धारश्च निषादश्च वैश्यावर्द्धेन वै स्मृतो /
शूद्रत्वं विधिनार्द्धेन पतितत्वान्न संशयः //
text_mt: gāndhāra and niṣāda are recognized as half vaiśya; / by rule, they are half śūdra, because they are fallen, without doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣabho mūrchitavarjito dhaivatasahitaśca pañcamo yatra /
nipatati madhyamarāge sa niṣādaṃ ṣāṅjavaṃ vidyāt //
meaning:
ऋषभो मूर्छितवर्जितो धैवतसहितश्च पञ्चमो यत्र /
निपतति मध्यमरागे स निषादं षाङ्जवं विद्यात् //
text_mt: Where ṛṣabha is free of mūrcchanā and pañcama is combined with dhaivata / and falls in the madhyamarāga, one should know that to be a ṣāḍava [scale] with niṣāda.

sanskrit_iast:
yadi pañcamo viramate gāndhāraścāntarasvaro bhavati /
ṛṣabho niṣādasahitastaṃ pañcamamīdṛśaṃ vidyāt //
meaning:
यदि पञ्चमो विरमते गान्धारश्चान्तरस्वरो भवति /
ऋषभो निषादसहितस्तं पञ्चममीदृशं विद्यात् //
text_mt: If pañcama comes to rest and gāndhāra becomes an intermediate note, / and ṛṣabha is joined with niṣāda, one should know such to be pañcama.

sanskrit_iast:
gāndhārasyādhipatyena niṣādasya gatāgataiḥ /
dhaivatasya ca daurbalyānmadhyamagrāma ucyate //
meaning:
गान्धारस्याधिपत्येन निषादस्य गतागतैः /
धैवतस्य च दौर्बल्यान्मध्यमग्राम उच्यते //
text_mt: Through the dominance of gāndhāra, the movements of niṣāda, / and the weakness of dhaivata, the madhyama-grāma is proclaimed.

sanskrit_iast:
īṣatpṛṣṭo niṣādastu gāndhāraścādhiko bhavet /
dhaivataḥ kaṃpito yatra sa ṣaṅgayāma īritaḥ //
meaning:
ईषत्पृष्टो निषादस्तु गान्धारश्चाधिको भवेत् /
धैवतः कंपितो यत्र स षङ्गयाम ईरितः //
text_mt: Where niṣāda is slightly touched, gāndhāra is heightened, / and dhaivata is shaken, that is said to be the ṣaḍja-grāma.

sanskrit_iast:
antarasvarasaṃyuktaḥ kākaliryatra dṛśyate /
taṃ tu sādhāritaṃ vidyātpañcamasthaṃ tu kaiśikam //
meaning:
अन्तरस्वरसंयुक्तः काकलिर्यत्र दृश्यते /
तं तु साधारितं विद्यात्पञ्चमस्थं तु कैशिकम् //
text_mt: Where the kākalī [note] is seen joined with an intermediate note, / one should know that as sādhārita; but that which resides in pañcama is kaiśika.

sanskrit_iast:
kaiśikaṃ bhāvayitvā tu svaraiḥ sarvaiḥ samantataḥ /
yasmā ttu madhyame nyāsastasmātkaiśikamadhyamaḥ //
meaning:
कैशिकं भावयित्वा तु स्वरैः सर्वैः समन्ततः /
यस्मा त्तु मध्यमे न्यासस्तस्मात्कैशिकमध्यमः //
text_mt: Having produced kaiśika on all sides through all the notes, / because the resting note (nyāsa) is in madhyama, it is therefore called kaiśikamadhyama.

sanskrit_iast:
kākalirdṛśyate yatra prādhānyaṃ pañcamasya tu /
kaśyapaḥ kaiśikaṃ prāha madhyamagrāmasaṃbhavam //
meaning:
काकलिर्दृश्यते यत्र प्राधान्यं पञ्चमस्य तु /
कश्यपः कैशिकं प्राह मध्यमग्रामसंभवम् //
text_mt: Where the kākalī is observed and the pañcama is predominant, / Kaśyapa declared that [mode] to be the kaiśika, arising from the madhyamagrāma.

sanskrit_iast:
geti geyaṃ viduḥ prājñā dheti kārupravādanam /
veti vādyasya saṃjñeyaṃ gandharvasya prarocanam //
meaning:
गेति गेयं विदुः प्राज्ञा धेति कारुप्रवादनम् /
वेति वाद्यस्य संज्ञेयं गन्धर्वस्य प्ररोचनम् //
text_mt: The wise know that 'ga' means singing, 'dha' means the instrument's sounding, / and 'va' is the designation of an instrument; this is the explanation of 'gandharva'.

sanskrit_iast:
yaḥ sāmagānāṃ prathamaḥ sa veṇormadhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
yo dvitīyaḥ sa gāndhārastṛtīyastvṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
यः सामगानां प्रथमः स वेणोर्मध्यमः स्वरः /
यो द्वितीयः स गान्धारस्तृतीयस्त्वृषभः स्मृतः //
text_mt: The note which is the first among the Sāman-singers is the madhyama note of the flute; / that which is the second is the gāndhāra, and the third is remembered as the ṛṣabha;

sanskrit_iast:
caturthaḥ ṣaṅja ityāhuḥ pañcamo dhaivato bhavet /
ṣaṣṭho niṣādo vijñeyaḥ saptamaḥ pañcamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
चतुर्थः षङ्ज इत्याहुः पञ्चमो धैवतो भवेत् /
षष्ठो निषादो विज्ञेयः सप्तमः पञ्चमः स्मृतः //
text_mt: The fourth, they say, is the ṣaḍja; the fifth is the dhaivata; / the sixth is known as the niṣāda; and the seventh is remembered as the pañcama.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṅjaṃ mayūro vadati gāvo raṃbhanti carṣabham /
ajāvike tu gāndhāraṃ kraiñco vadati madhyamam //
meaning:
षङ्जं मयूरो वदति गावो रंभन्ति चर्षभम् /
अजाविके तु गान्धारं क्रैञ्चो वदति मध्यमम् //
text_mt: The peacock cries the ṣaḍja, and cows low the ṛṣabha; / goats and sheep bleat the gāndhāra, and the krauñca utters the madhyama;

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpasādhāraṇe kāle kokilā vakti pañcamam /
aśvastu dhaivataṃ vakti niṣaādaṃ vakti kuñjaraḥ //
meaning:
पुष्पसाधारणे काले कोकिला वक्ति पञ्चमम् /
अश्वस्तु धैवतं वक्ति निषआदं वक्ति कुञ्जरः //
text_mt: In the season of flowers, the cuckoo sings the pañcama; / the horse utters the dhaivata, and the elephant trumpets the niṣāda.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṇṭhāduttiṣṭate ṣaṅjaḥ śirasastvṛṣabhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
gāndhārastvanunāsikya uraso madhyamaḥ svaraḥ //
meaning:
कण्ठादुत्तिष्टते षङ्जः शिरसस्त्वृषभः स्मृतः /
गान्धारस्त्वनुनासिक्य उरसो मध्यमः स्वरः //
text_mt: The ṣaḍja arises from the throat, and the ṛṣabha is remembered to come from the head; / the gāndhāra is nasal, and the madhyama note comes from the chest.

sanskrit_iast:
urasaḥ śirasaḥ kaṇṭhādutthitaḥ pañcamaḥ svaraḥ /
lalāṭāddhaivataṃ vidyānniṣādaṃ sarvasandhijam //
meaning:
उरसः शिरसः कण्ठादुत्थितः पञ्चमः स्वरः /
ललाटाद्धैवतं विद्यान्निषादं सर्वसन्धिजम् //
text_mt: the note pañcama arises from the chest, head, and throat; / one should know dhaivata from the forehead, and niṣāda born from all the joints.

sanskrit_iast:
nāsā kaṇṭhamurastālujihvādatāṃśca saṃśritaḥ /
ṣaṅbhiḥ saṃ jāyate yasmāttasmātṣaṅja iti smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
नासा कण्ठमुरस्तालुजिह्वादतांश्च संश्रितः /
षङ्भिः सं जायते यस्मात्तस्मात्षङ्ज इति स्मृतः //
text_mt: Relying on the nose, the throat, the chest, the palate, the tongue, and the teeth, / it is born from these six, and therefore it is remembered as the ṣaḍja.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābheḥ kaṇṭhaśīrṣasamāhataḥ /
nardatyṛṣabhavadyasmāttasmādṛṣerbha ucyate //
meaning:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेः कण्ठशीर्षसमाहतः /
नर्दत्यृषभवद्यस्मात्तस्मादृषेर्भ उच्यते //
text_mt: The wind arising from the navel, striking the throat and the head, / roars like a bull; therefore it is called the ṛṣabha.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābheḥ kaṇṭhaśīrṣasamāhataḥ /
vāti gandhavahaḥ puṇyo gāndhārastena hetunā //
meaning:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेः कण्ठशीर्षसमाहतः /
वाति गन्धवहः पुण्यो गान्धारस्तेन हेतुना //
text_mt: The wind arising from the navel, striking the throat and the head, / blows as a pure carrier of fragrance; for that reason it is the gāndhāra.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābherurau hṛdi samāhataḥ /
nābhiprāpto madhyavartī madhyamatvaṃ samarśnute //
meaning:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेरुरौ हृदि समाहतः /
नाभिप्राप्तो मध्यवर्ती मध्यमत्वं समर्श्नुते //
text_mt: The wind arising from the navel, striking the chest and the heart, / reaches the navel and, dwelling in the middle, attains the quality of madhyama.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuḥ samutthito nābherurohṛtkaṇṭhakāhṛtaḥ /
pañcasthānotthitasyāsya pañcamatvaṃ vidhīyate //
meaning:
वायुः समुत्थितो नाभेरुरोहृत्कण्ठकाहृतः /
पञ्चस्थानोत्थितस्यास्य पञ्चमत्वं विधीयते //
text_mt: The wind arising from the navel, drawn through the chest, heart, and throat, / coming forth from five places, is designated as the pañcama.

sanskrit_iast:
dhaivataṃ ca niṣādaṃ ca varjayitvā tu tāvubhau /
śeṣānpañca svarāṃstvanye pañcasthānotthitānviduḥ //
meaning:
धैवतं च निषादं च वर्जयित्वा तु तावुभौ /
शेषान्पञ्च स्वरांस्त्वन्ये पञ्चस्थानोत्थितान्विदुः //
text_mt: Excepting both the dhaivata and the niṣāda, / others consider the remaining five notes as arising from five places.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcasthānasthitatvena sarvasthānāni dhāryate /
agnigītasvaraḥ ṣaṅja ṛṣabho brahmaṇocyate //
meaning:
पञ्चस्थानस्थितत्वेन सर्वस्थानानि धार्यते /
अग्निगीतस्वरः षङ्ज ऋषभो ब्रह्मणोच्यते //
text_mt: By abiding in five places, it maintains all places. / The ṣaḍja note is sung by Agni, and the ṛṣabha is spoken by Brahmā;

sanskrit_iast:
somena gīto gāndhāro viṣṇunā madhyamaḥ svaraḥ /
pañcamastu svaro gītastvayaiveti nidhāraya //
meaning:
सोमेन गीतो गान्धारो विष्णुना मध्यमः स्वरः /
पञ्चमस्तु स्वरो गीतस्त्वयैवेति निधारय //
text_mt: The gāndhāra was sung by Soma, and the madhyama note by Viṣṇu; / and ascertain that the pañcama note was sung by you alone [Nārada].

sanskrit_iast:
dhaivataśca niṣādaśca gītau tuṃburuṇā svarau /
ādyaṃsya daivataṃ brahmā ṣaṅjasyāpyucyate budhaiḥ //
meaning:
धैवतश्च निषादश्च गीतौ तुंबुरुणा स्वरौ /
आद्यंस्य दैवतं ब्रह्मा षङ्जस्याप्युच्यते बुधैः //
text_mt: The dhaivata and niṣāda notes were sung by Tumburu. / Brahmā is also declared by the wise to be the deity of the first note, the ṣaḍja;

sanskrit_iast:
tīkṣṇadīptaprakāśatvādṛṣabhasya hutāśanaḥ /
gāvaḥ praṇīte tuṣyanti gāndhārastena hetunā //
meaning:
तीक्ष्णदीप्तप्रकाशत्वादृषभस्य हुताशनः /
गावः प्रणीते तुष्यन्ति गान्धारस्तेन हेतुना //
text_mt: Because of its sharp and blazing brilliance, Hutāśana is [the deity] of the ṛṣabha; / cows are delighted when it is performed, and for that reason it is the gāndhāra;

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā caivopatiṣṭanti saurabheyā na saṃśayaḥ /
somastu pañcamasyāpi daivataṃ brahmarādrasmṛtam //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा चैवोपतिष्टन्ति सौरभेया न संशयः /
सोमस्तु पञ्चमस्यापि दैवतं ब्रह्मराद्रस्मृतम् //
text_mt: And having heard it, the progeny of Surabhī surely approach without doubt. / Soma is remembered as the deity of the pañcama, O sage-seer [Nārada];

sanskrit_iast:
nihrāso yasya vṛddhiśca grāmamāsādya somavat /
atisaṃdhīyate yasmādetānpūrvotthitānsvarān //
meaning:
निह्रासो यस्य वृद्धिश्च ग्राममासाद्य सोमवत् /
अतिसंधीयते यस्मादेतान्पूर्वोत्थितान्स्वरान् //
text_mt: Like the moon, its decrease and increase occur depending on the grāma; / because it binds together these previously arisen notes,

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādasya svarasyāpi dhaivatatvaṃ vidhīyate /
niṣīdanti svarā yasmānniṣādastena hetunā //
meaning:
तस्मादस्य स्वरस्यापि धैवतत्वं विधीयते /
निषीदन्ति स्वरा यस्मान्निषादस्तेन हेतुना //
text_mt: Therefore the quality of dhaivata is ordained for this note. / Because the notes settle down [into it], for that reason it is the niṣāda;

sanskrit_iast: sarvāṃścābhibhavatyeṣa yadādityo 'sya daivatam //
meaning: सर्वांश्चाभिभवत्येष यदादित्यो ऽस्य दैवतम् //
text_mt: And because Āditya is its deity, it overpowers all [other notes].

sanskrit_iast: dāravī gātravīṇā ca dve vīṇe gānajātiṣu //
meaning: दारवी गात्रवीणा च द्वे वीणे गानजातिषु //
text_mt: Among the classes of song, there are two vīṇās: the wooden vīṇā and the bodily vīṇā.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmanī gātravīṇā tu tasyāstvaṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇam /
gātravīṇā tu sā proktā yasyāṃ gāyanti sāmaṅgāḥ //
meaning:
सामनी गात्रवीणा तु तस्यास्त्वं शृणु लक्षणम् /
गात्रवीणा तु सा प्रोक्ता यस्यां गायन्ति सामङ्गाः //
text_mt: The bodily vīṇā belongs to the Sāman; listen now to its characteristics. / That is declared to be the bodily vīṇā on which the Sāman-singers sing,

sanskrit_iast:
svaravyañjanasaṃyuktā aṅgulyaṅguṣṭarañjitā /
hastau tu saṃyatau dhāryauṃ jānubhyāmuparisthitau //
meaning:
स्वरव्यञ्जनसंयुक्ता अङ्गुल्यङ्गुष्टरञ्जिता /
हस्तौ तु संयतौ धार्यौं जानुभ्यामुपरिस्थितौ //
text_mt: Joined with vowels and consonants, illuminated by the fingers and thumb. / The two restrained hands should be kept resting above the knees.

sanskrit_iast:
guroranukṛtiṃ kuryādyathānyā na matirbhavet /
praṇavaṃ prākprayuñjīta vyāhṛtīstadanantaram //
meaning:
गुरोरनुकृतिं कुर्याद्यथान्या न मतिर्भवेत् /
प्रणवं प्राक्प्रयुञ्जीत व्याहृतीस्तदनन्तरम् //
text_mt: One should imitate the teacher so that no other thought occurs. / One should first utter the praṇava, and immediately after that the vyāhṛtis;

sanskrit_iast:
sāvitrīṃ cānuvacanaṃ tato vai gānamārabhet /
prasārya cāṅgulīḥ sarvā ropayetsvaramaṇḍalam //
meaning:
सावित्रीं चानुवचनं ततो वै गानमारभेत् /
प्रसार्य चाङ्गुलीः सर्वा रोपयेत्स्वरमण्डलम् //
text_mt: Then the Sāvitrī and the recitation, and after that one should indeed begin the song. / Extending all the fingers, one should establish the circle of notes.

sanskrit_iast:
na cāṅgulībhiraṅguṣṭamaṅguṣṭenāgulīḥ spṛśet /
viralā nāṅgulīḥ kuryānmūle caitāṃ na saṃspṛśet //
meaning:
न चाङ्गुलीभिरङ्गुष्टमङ्गुष्टेनागुलीः स्पृशेत् /
विरला नाङ्गुलीः कुर्यान्मूले चैतां न संस्पृशेत् //
text_mt: One should not touch the thumb with the fingers, nor the fingers with the thumb; / one should not hold the fingers wide apart, nor touch them at the base.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅguṣṭhāgreṇa tā nityaṃ madhyame parvaṇi spṛśet /
mātrādvimātravṛddhānāṃ vibhāgārthe vibhāgavit //
meaning:
अङ्गुष्ठाग्रेण ता नित्यं मध्यमे पर्वणि स्पृशेत् /
मात्राद्विमात्रवृद्धानां विभागार्थे विभागवित् //
text_mt: Knowing the divisions, one should always touch them at the middle joint with the tip of the thumb, / for the sake of dividing the single-mātrā and two-mātrā increments.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgulībhirdvimātraṃ tu pāṇeḥ savyasya darśayet /
trirekhā yasya dṛśyate siddhiṃ tatra vinirdiśet //
meaning:
अङ्गुलीभिर्द्विमात्रं तु पाणेः सव्यस्य दर्शयेत् /
त्रिरेखा यस्य दृश्यते सिद्धिं तत्र विनिर्दिशेत् //
text_mt: One should indicate a duration of two mātrās with the fingers of the left hand; / where three lines are seen, one should indicate success there.

sanskrit_iast:
sa parva iti vijñeyaḥ śeṣamantaramantaram /
parvāntaraṃ sāmasu ca ṛkṣu kuryāttilāntaram //
meaning:
स पर्व इति विज्ञेयः शेषमन्तरमन्तरम् /
पर्वान्तरं सामसु च ऋक्षु कुर्यात्तिलान्तरम् //
text_mt: That is to be known as a joint; the rest is interval after interval. / One should make an interval between joints in the Sāmans, and an interval the size of a sesame seed in the Ṛks.

sanskrit_iast:
svarānmadhyamaparvasu suniviṣṭaṃ niveśayet /
na cātra kaṃpayetkiñcidaṅgasyāvayavaṃ budhaḥ //
meaning:
स्वरान्मध्यमपर्वसु सुनिविष्टं निवेशयेत् /
न चात्र कंपयेत्किञ्चिदङ्गस्यावयवं बुधः //
text_mt: One should set the notes well positioned upon the middle joints; / and here the wise person should not shake any part of the limb.

sanskrit_iast:
adhastanaṃ mṛdaṃ nyasya hastamātre yathākramam /
abhramadhye yathā vidyudṛśyate maṇisūtravat //
meaning:
अधस्तनं मृदं न्यस्य हस्तमात्रे यथाक्रमम् /
अभ्रमध्ये यथा विद्युदृश्यते मणिसूत्रवत् //
text_mt: Placing the lower hand lightly, according to proper order in the measure of a hand, / just as lightning is seen in the midst of a cloud like a string of gems,

sanskrit_iast:
pṛṣacchedavivṛttīnāṃ yathā bāleṣukartarī /
kūrmo 'gāni ca saṃhṛtya cetodṛṣṭiṃ diśanmanaḥ //
meaning:
पृषच्छेदविवृत्तीनां यथा बालेषुकर्तरी /
कूर्मो ऽगानि च संहृत्य चेतोदृष्टिं दिशन्मनः //
text_mt: Or as scissors [moving swiftly] among hair in cutting off drops [or tufts], / drawing in one's limbs like a tortoise, directing the mind and gaze with consciousness,

sanskrit_iast:
svasthaḥ praśānto nirbhīko varṇānuñcārayedbudhaḥ /
nāsikāyāstu pūrveṇa hastaṃ gokarṇavaddharet //
meaning:
स्वस्थः प्रशान्तो निर्भीको वर्णानुञ्चारयेद्बुधः /
नासिकायास्तु पूर्वेण हस्तं गोकर्णवद्धरेत् //
text_mt: At ease, tranquil, and fearless, the wise one should utter the syllables. / One should hold the hand forward from the nose, shaped like a cow's ear.

sanskrit_iast:
niveśya dṛṣṭiṃ hastāgre śāstrārthamanucintayet /
samyakpracārayedvākyaṃ hastena ca mukhena ca //
meaning:
निवेश्य दृष्टिं हस्ताग्रे शास्त्रार्थमनुचिन्तयेत् /
सम्यक्प्रचारयेद्वाक्यं हस्तेन च मुखेन च //
text_mt: Fixing one's gaze on the tip of the hand, one should reflect on the meaning of the scripture; / one should properly project the phrase with both hand and mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
yathaivoccārayedvarṇāṃstathaivaināṃ samāpayet /
nātyāhanyānna nirhaṇyānna pragāyenna kaṃpayet //
meaning:
यथैवोच्चारयेद्वर्णांस्तथैवैनां समापयेत् /
नात्याहन्यान्न निर्हण्यान्न प्रगायेन्न कंपयेत् //
text_mt: Just as one begins the syllables, so should one bring them to an end; / one should not strike too hard, nor suppress, nor prolong improperly, nor tremble.

sanskrit_iast:
samaṃ sāmāni gāyeta vyomni svena gātiryathā /
yathā sucaratāṃ mārgo mīnānāṃ nopalabhyate //
meaning:
समं सामानि गायेत व्योम्नि स्वेन गातिर्यथा /
यथा सुचरतां मार्गो मीनानां नोपलभ्यते //
text_mt: One should sing the Sāmans evenly, just as a bird moves in the sky; / just as the path of fishes swimming smoothly cannot be perceived,

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśe vā vihṝṅgānāṃ tadvatsvaragatā śrutiḥ /
yathā dadhini sarpiḥ syātkāṣṭastho vā yathānalaḥ //
meaning:
आकाशे वा विहॄङ्गानां तद्वत्स्वरगता श्रुतिः /
यथा दधिनि सर्पिः स्यात्काष्टस्थो वा यथानलः //
text_mt: Or of birds in the sky, even so is the microtone (śruti) residing in a note. / Just as ghee is present in curd, or fire resides in wood,

sanskrit_iast:
prayatnenopalabhyeta tadvatsvaragatā śrutiḥ /
svarātsvarasya saṃkrāmaṃsvarasaṃdhimanulbaṇam //
meaning:
प्रयत्नेनोपलभ्येत तद्वत्स्वरगता श्रुतिः /
स्वरात्स्वरस्य संक्रामंस्वरसंधिमनुल्बणम् //
text_mt: And is perceived with effort, even so is the microtone residing in a note. / The transition from note to note and the junction of notes should be unobtrusive,

sanskrit_iast:
avicchinnaṃ samaṃ kuryātsūkṣmacchāyātapopamam /
anāgatamatikrāntaṃ vicchinnaṃ viṣamāhatam //
meaning:
अविच्छिन्नं समं कुर्यात्सूक्ष्मच्छायातपोपमम् /
अनागतमतिक्रान्तं विच्छिन्नं विषमाहतम् //
text_mt: Continuous, and smooth, resembling subtle light and shade. / The wise person should avoid a vocal glide (karṣaṇa) that is premature, overdue, broken, or unevenly struck,

sanskrit_iast:
tanvantamasthitāntaṃ ca varjayetkarṣaṇaṃ budhaḥ /
svaraḥ sthānāccyuto yastu svaṃ sthānamativartate //
meaning:
तन्वन्तमस्थितान्तं च वर्जयेत्कर्षणं बुधः /
स्वरः स्थानाच्च्युतो यस्तु स्वं स्थानमतिवर्तते //
text_mt: Or one that trails off into thinness or has an unstable end. / A note that falls away from its pitch and exceeds its proper position—

sanskrit_iast:
vistaraṃ sāmagā brūyurviraktamiti vīṇinaḥ /
abhyāsārthe drutāṃ vṛttiṃ prayogārthe tu madhyamām //
meaning:
विस्तरं सामगा ब्रूयुर्विरक्तमिति वीणिनः /
अभ्यासार्थे द्रुतां वृत्तिं प्रयोगार्थे तु मध्यमाम् //
text_mt: The Sāman-singers call that vistara, and the vīṇā-players call it virakta. / For practice, [use] the fast tempo; for performance, the medium [tempo];

sanskrit_iast:
śiṣyaṇāmupadeśārthaṃ kuryādvṛttiṃ vilaṃbitām /
gṛhītagrantha evaṃ tu granthoñcāraṇaśaikṣakān //
meaning:
शिष्यणामुपदेशार्थं कुर्याद्वृत्तिं विलंबिताम् /
गृहीतग्रन्थ एवं तु ग्रन्थोञ्चारणशैक्षकान् //
text_mt: For instructing pupils, one should use the slow tempo. / Having thus mastered the text, [when instructing] students in reciting the text,

sanskrit_iast:
haste nādhyāpayecchiṣyān śaikṣeṇa vidhinā dvijaḥ /
kruṣṭasya mūrddhani sthānaṃ lalāṭe prathamasya tu //
meaning:
हस्ते नाध्यापयेच्छिष्यान् शैक्षेण विधिना द्विजः /
क्रुष्टस्य मूर्द्धनि स्थानं ललाटे प्रथमस्य तु //
text_mt: A twice-born should teach the pupils by hand according to the pedagogical rule. / The position of the kruṣṭa is in the head, and of the prathama in the forehead;

sanskrit_iast:
bhruvormadhya dvitīyasya tṛtīyasya tu karṇayoḥ /
kaṇṭhasthānaṃ caturthasya mandrasya rasanocyate //
meaning:
भ्रुवोर्मध्य द्वितीयस्य तृतीयस्य तु कर्णयोः /
कण्ठस्थानं चतुर्थस्य मन्द्रस्य रसनोच्यते //
text_mt: Of the dvitīya, between the eyebrows; and of the tṛtīya, in the ears; / the position of the caturtha is the throat; the tongue is said to be [the place] of the mandra;

sanskrit_iast:
atisvarasya nīcasya hṛdi sthānaṃ vidhīyate /
aṅguṣṭasyottame vruṣṭo hyaṅguṣṭaṃ prathamaḥ svaraḥ //
meaning:
अतिस्वरस्य नीचस्य हृदि स्थानं विधीयते /
अङ्गुष्टस्योत्तमे व्रुष्टो ह्यङ्गुष्टं प्रथमः स्वरः //
text_mt: The position of the low atisvārya is prescribed in the heart. / The kruṣṭa is on the top of the thumb, and the prathama note is on the thumb;

sanskrit_iast:
pradeśinyāṃ tu gāndhāra ṛṣabhastadanantaram /
anāmikāyāṃ ṣaṅgastu kaniṣṭāyāṃ tu dhaivataḥ //
meaning:
प्रदेशिन्यां तु गान्धार ऋषभस्तदनन्तरम् /
अनामिकायां षङ्गस्तु कनिष्टायां तु धैवतः //
text_mt: The gāndhāra is on the forefinger, and the ṛṣabha immediately after it; / the ṣaḍja is on the ring finger, and the dhaivata on the little finger;

sanskrit_iast:
tasyādhastāñca yonyāstu niṣādaṃ tatra nirdiśet /
aparvatvādamadhyatvā davyayatvāñca nityaśaḥ //
meaning:
तस्याधस्ताञ्च योन्यास्तु निषादं तत्र निर्दिशेत् /
अपर्वत्वादमध्यत्वा दव्ययत्वाञ्च नित्यशः //
text_mt: And below it, at its base, one should indicate the niṣāda, / because it has no joint, is not in the middle, and is perpetually unchanging.

sanskrit_iast:
mandro hi mandībhūtastu parisvāra iti smṛtaḥ /
kruṣṭena devā jīvanti prathamena tu mānuṣāḥ //
meaning:
मन्द्रो हि मन्दीभूतस्तु परिस्वार इति स्मृतः /
क्रुष्टेन देवा जीवन्ति प्रथमेन तु मानुषाः //
text_mt: The mandra, when subdued, is traditionally remembered as parisvāra. / By the kruṣṭa the gods live, but human beings by the prathama;

sanskrit_iast:
paśavastu dvitīyena gandharvāpsarasastvanu /
andhajāḥ pitaraścaiva caturthasvarajīvinaḥ //
meaning:
पशवस्तु द्वितीयेन गन्धर्वाप्सरसस्त्वनु /
अन्धजाः पितरश्चैव चतुर्थस्वरजीविनः //
text_mt: cattle live by the dvitīya, and gandharvas and apsarases next; / birds and the ancestors indeed live by the caturtha tone.

sanskrit_iast:
mandratvenopajīvanti piśācāsurarākṣasāḥ /
atisvareṇa nīcena jagatsthāvarajaṅgamāḥ //
meaning:
मन्द्रत्वेनोपजीवन्ति पिशाचासुरराक्षसाः /
अतिस्वरेण नीचेन जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमाः //
text_mt: Piśācas, asuras, and rākṣasas live by means of the mandra; / the mobile and immobile world lives by the low atisvara.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvāṇi khalu bhūtāni dhāryante sāmikaiḥ svaraiḥ /
dīptāyatākaruṇānāṃ mṛdumadhyamayostathā //
meaning:
सर्वाणि खलु भूतानि धार्यन्ते सामिकैः स्वरैः /
दीप्तायताकरुणानां मृदुमध्यमयोस्तथा //
text_mt: All living beings are indeed sustained by the Sāmic tones. / Of the dīptā, āyatā, and karuṇā, and likewise of the mṛdu and madhyamā,

sanskrit_iast:
śrutīnāṃ yo viśeṣajño na sa ācārya ucyate /
dīptā mandre dvitīya ca pracaturthe tathaiva ca //
meaning:
श्रुतीनां यो विशेषज्ञो न स आचार्य उच्यते /
दीप्ता मन्द्रे द्वितीय च प्रचतुर्थे तथैव च //
text_mt: he who does not know the distinction between the microtones is not called a teacher. / Dīptā is in the mandra, and in the dvitīya, and likewise in the caturtha;

sanskrit_iast:
atisvare tṛtīye ca kruṣṭe tu karuṇā śrutiḥ /
śrutayo yā dvitīyasya mṛdumadhyāyatāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
अतिस्वरे तृतीये च क्रुष्टे तु करुणा श्रुतिः /
श्रुतयो या द्वितीयस्य मृदुमध्यायताः स्मृताः //
text_mt: and in the atisvara and the tṛtīya, while in the kruṣṭa the karuṇā microtone is found. / Those which are the microtones of the dvitīya are recalled as mṛdu, madhyā, and āyatā.

sanskrit_iast:
tāsāmapi tu vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇāni pṛthak pṛthak /
āyatātvaṃ bhavennīce mṛdutā tu viparyaye //
meaning:
तासामपि तु वक्ष्यामि लक्षणानि पृथक् पृथक् /
आयतात्वं भवेन्नीचे मृदुता तु विपर्यये //
text_mt: I shall also describe their specific characteristics one by one: / āyatatva occurs in a low note, but mṛdutā occurs in the contrary;

sanskrit_iast:
sve svare madhyamātvaṃ tu tatsamīkṣya prayojayet /
dvitīye viratā yā tu kruṣṭaśca parato bhavet //
meaning:
स्वे स्वरे मध्यमात्वं तु तत्समीक्ष्य प्रयोजयेत् /
द्वितीये विरता या तु क्रुष्टश्च परतो भवेत् //
text_mt: madhyamatva occurs in its own tone; observing that, one should apply it. / That which pauses on the dvitīya and a kruṣṭa occurs beyond it,

sanskrit_iast:
dīptāṃ tāṃ tu vijānīyātprāthamyena mṛduḥ smṛtaḥ /
atraiva viratā yā tu caturthena pravartate //
meaning:
दीप्तां तां तु विजानीयात्प्राथम्येन मृदुः स्मृतः /
अत्रैव विरता या तु चतुर्थेन प्रवर्तते //
text_mt: one should know that as dīptā; because of primacy it is remembered as mṛdu. / That which pauses right here and proceeds by the caturtha,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā mandre bhaveddīptā sāmnaścaiva samāpane /
nātitāraśrutiṃ kuryātsvarayornāpi cāntare //
meaning:
तथा मन्द्रे भवेद्दीप्ता साम्नश्चैव समापने /
नातितारश्रुतिं कुर्यात्स्वरयोर्नापि चान्तरे //
text_mt: likewise in the mandra, is dīptā, and also at the conclusion of a sāman. / One should not make an excessively high pitch, nor between two tones;

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ ca hrasve ca dīrghe ca na cāpi ghuṭisajñake /
dvividhā gatiḥ padāntasthitasaṃdhiḥ sahoṣmabhiḥ //
meaning:
तं च ह्रस्वे च दीर्घे च न चापि घुटिसज्ञके /
द्विविधा गतिः पदान्तस्थितसंधिः सहोष्मभिः //
text_mt: and on a short or long [syllable], nor on what is called a ghuṭi. / Twofold is the movement: a pause standing at the end of a word together with spirants.

sanskrit_iast:
sthāneṣu pañcasveteṣu vijñeya ghuṭisaṃjñakam /
svarāntarāviratāni hrasvadīrghaghuṭāni ca //
meaning:
स्थानेषु पञ्चस्वेतेषु विज्ञेय घुटिसंज्ञकम् /
स्वरान्तराविरतानि ह्रस्वदीर्घघुटानि च //
text_mt: In these five positions it is to be known as having the designation ghuṭi: / unpaused between tones, short, long, and ghuṭa.

sanskrit_iast:
sthitisthāneṣvaśeṣāṇi śrutivatsvarato vadet /
dīptāmudātte jānīyāddīptāṃ ca svarite viduḥ //
meaning:
स्थितिस्थानेष्वशेषाणि श्रुतिवत्स्वरतो वदेत् /
दीप्तामुदात्ते जानीयाद्दीप्तां च स्वरिते विदुः //
text_mt: In all positional resting-places, one should recite in accordance with pitch as with a microtone. / One should know dīptā on an acute (udātta), and they know dīptā on a circumflex (svarita);

sanskrit_iast:
anudātte mṛdurjñeyā gandharvāḥ śrutisaṃpade /
udāttaścānudāttaśca svaritapracite tathā //
meaning:
अनुदात्ते मृदुर्ज्ञेया गन्धर्वाः श्रुतिसंपदे /
उदात्तश्चानुदात्तश्च स्वरितप्रचिते तथा //
text_mt: on a grave (anudātta) it should be known as mṛdu, [as do] the gandharvas for perfection of microtones. / Acute and grave, and circumflex and monotone (pracita),

sanskrit_iast:
nighātaśceti vijñeyaḥ svarabhedaśca pañcadhā /
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi ācikasya svaratrayam //
meaning:
निघातश्चेति विज्ञेयः स्वरभेदश्च पञ्चधा /
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि आचिकस्य स्वरत्रयम् //
text_mt: and what is known as low pitch (nighāta)—thus pitch variation is fivefold. / Beyond this I shall declare the threefold pitch of the Ācika recitation:

sanskrit_iast:
udāttaścānudāttaśca tṛtīyaḥ svaritaḥ svaraḥ /
ya evodātta ityuktaḥ sa eva svaritātparaḥ //
meaning:
उदात्तश्चानुदात्तश्च तृतीयः स्वरितः स्वरः /
य एवोदात्त इत्युक्तः स एव स्वरितात्परः //
text_mt: acute, grave, and the third pitch is the circumflex. / That which is spoken of as acute, that very pitch following a circumflex

sanskrit_iast:
pracayaḥ procyate tajjñairna cātrānyatsvarāntaram /
varṇasvaro 'tītasvaraḥ svarito dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ //
meaning:
प्रचयः प्रोच्यते तज्ज्ञैर्न चात्रान्यत्स्वरान्तरम् /
वर्णस्वरो ऽतीतस्वरः स्वरितो द्विविधः स्मृतः //
text_mt: is termed monotone by the experts, and there is no other different tone here. / A syllable pitch and an unaccented pitch: the circumflex is remembered as twofold.

sanskrit_iast:
mātriko varṇa evaṃ tu dīrghastūñcaritādanu /
sa tu saptavidho jñeyaḥ svaraḥ pratyayadarśanāt //
meaning:
मात्रिको वर्ण एवं तु दीर्घस्तूञ्चरितादनु /
स तु सप्तविधो ज्ञेयः स्वरः प्रत्ययदर्शनात् //
text_mt: A syllable consisting of one measure is thus [so pronounced], while a long one follows the uttered sound. / It is to be known as sevenfold according to the observation of its context;

sanskrit_iast:
padena tu sa vijñeyo bhavedyo yatra yādṛśaḥ /
saptasvarānprayuñjīta dakṣiṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ prati //
meaning:
पदेन तु स विज्ञेयो भवेद्यो यत्र यादृशः /
सप्तस्वरान्प्रयुञ्जीत दक्षिणं श्रवणं प्रति //
text_mt: it is to be recognized by the word, whatever and of whatever kind it may be in a given place. / One should apply the seven notes toward the right ear.

sanskrit_iast:
ācāryairvihitaṃ śāstraṃ putraśiṣyahitaiṣibhiḥ /
uccāduñcataraṃ nāsti nīcānnīcataraṃ tathā //
meaning:
आचार्यैर्विहितं शास्त्रं पुत्रशिष्यहितैषिभिः /
उच्चादुञ्चतरं नास्ति नीचान्नीचतरं तथा //
text_mt: The treatise was composed by the teachers desiring the welfare of their sons and pupils. / There is nothing higher than high, nor anything lower than low.

sanskrit_iast:
vaisvaryasvārasaṃjñāyāṃ kiṃsthānaḥ svāra ucyate /
uccanīcasya yanmadhye sādhāraṇamiti śrutiḥ //
meaning:
वैस्वर्यस्वारसंज्ञायां किंस्थानः स्वार उच्यते /
उच्चनीचस्य यन्मध्ये साधारणमिति श्रुतिः //
text_mt: With the designation 'accentual circumflex' (vaisvaryasvāra), what position is assigned to the circumflex? / That which is in between high and low is said by scripture to be common [to both].

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ svāraṃ svārasaṃjñāyāṃ pratijānanti śaikṣikāḥ /
udātte niṣādagāndhārāvanudātteṃ ṛṣabhadhaivato //
meaning:
तं स्वारं स्वारसंज्ञायां प्रतिजानन्ति शैक्षिकाः /
उदात्ते निषादगान्धारावनुदात्तें ऋषभधैवतो //
text_mt: Students of phonetics recognize that circumflex under the name svāra. / In the acute are niṣāda and gāndhāra; in the grave are ṛṣabha and dhaivata;

sanskrit_iast:
svaritaprabhavā hyete ṣaṅjamadhyamapañcamāḥ /
yatra kakhaparā ūṣmā jihvāmūlaprayojanāḥ //
meaning:
स्वरितप्रभवा ह्येते षङ्जमध्यमपञ्चमाः /
यत्र कखपरा ऊष्मा जिह्वामूलप्रयोजनाः //
text_mt: indeed, these arise from the circumflex: ṣaḍja, madhyama, and pañcama. / Where the spirants are followed by k and kh, having their point of articulation at the root of the tongue,

sanskrit_iast:
tānapyājñāpayenmātrāprakṛtyaiva tu sā kalā /
jātyaḥ kṣaipro 'bhinihita stairavyañjana eva ca //
meaning:
तानप्याज्ञापयेन्मात्राप्रकृत्यैव तु सा कला /
जात्यः क्षैप्रो ऽभिनिहित स्तैरव्यञ्जन एव च //
text_mt: one should direct them also by measure; indeed, that fraction is according to nature. / The innate (jātya), the rapid (kṣaipra), the absorbed (abhinihita), and the stairavyañjana,

sanskrit_iast:
tirovirāmaḥ praśliṣṭo 'pādavṛttaśca saptamaḥ /
svarāṇāmahameteṣāṃ pṛthagvakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam //
meaning:
तिरोविरामः प्रश्लिष्टो ऽपादवृत्तश्च सप्तमः /
स्वराणामहमेतेषां पृथग्वक्ष्यामि लक्षणम् //
text_mt: the tirovirāma, the contracted (praśliṣṭa), and the pādavṛtta is the seventh. / I shall declare the characteristic of each of these pitches separately,

sanskrit_iast:
uddiṣṭānāṃ tathā nyāyamudāharaṇameva ca /
sapakāraṃ savaṃ vāpi hyakṣaraṃ svaritaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
उद्दिष्टानां तथा न्यायमुदाहरणमेव च /
सपकारं सवं वापि ह्यक्षरं स्वरितं भवेत् //
text_mt: as well as the rule and the example for those mentioned: / A syllable containing a 'p' or an 's' that becomes circumflex,

sanskrit_iast:
na codāttaṃ puro yasya jātyaḥ svāraḥ sa ucyate /
iuvarṇo yadodāttāvāpadyete pavau kvacit //
meaning:
न चोदात्तं पुरो यस्य जात्यः स्वारः स उच्यते /
इउवर्णो यदोदात्तावापद्येते पवौ क्वचित् //
text_mt: and before which there is no acute, is called an innate circumflex. / When the vowels i and u, being acute, turn into semi-vowels y and v in some place,

sanskrit_iast:
anudāttaṃ pratyaye tu vidyātkṣaiprasya lakṣaṇam /
eo ābhyāmudāttābhyāmakāro nihitaśca yaḥ //
meaning:
अनुदात्तं प्रत्यये तु विद्यात्क्षैप्रस्य लक्षणम् /
एओ आभ्यामुदात्ताभ्यामकारो निहितश्च यः //
text_mt: and a grave vowel follows, one should recognize the characteristic of the kṣaipra. / When an a is placed after the two acute vowels e and o,

sanskrit_iast:
akāro yatra luṃpati tamabhinihitaṃ viduḥ /
udāttapūrve yatkiñcicchandasi svaritaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
अकारो यत्र लुंपति तमभिनिहितं विदुः /
उदात्तपूर्वे यत्किञ्चिच्छन्दसि स्वरितं भवेत् //
text_mt: and that a is elided, they know that as abhinihita. / Whatever is circumflex in the Veda preceded by an acute,

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa sarvabahusvārastairavyañjana ucyate /
avagrahātparaṃ yatra svaritaṃ syādanantaram //
meaning:
एष सर्वबहुस्वारस्तैरव्यञ्जन उच्यते /
अवग्रहात्परं यत्र स्वरितं स्यादनन्तरम् //
text_mt: this circumflex, which occurs most commonly of all, is called stairavyañjana. / Where a circumflex immediately follows an avagraha pause,

sanskrit_iast:
tirovirāmaṃ taṃ vidyādudātto yadyavagrahaḥ /
ikāraṃ yatra paśyeyurikāreṇaiva saṃyutam //
meaning:
तिरोविरामं तं विद्यादुदात्तो यद्यवग्रहः /
इकारं यत्र पश्येयुरिकारेणैव संयुतम् //
text_mt: one should know that as tirovirāma, if the [vowel before the] avagraha is acute. / Where one sees the letter i joined with the letter i,

sanskrit_iast:
udāttamanudāttena praśliṣṭaṃ taṃ vicāraya /
svare cetsvaritaṃ yatra vivṛtā yatra saṃhitā //
meaning:
उदात्तमनुदात्तेन प्रश्लिष्टं तं विचारय /
स्वरे चेत्स्वरितं यत्र विवृता यत्र संहिता //
text_mt: an acute with a grave, consider that to be praśliṣṭa. / If there is a circumflex on a vowel where there is an open juncture,

sanskrit_iast:
etatpādāntavṛttasya lakṣaṇaṃ śāstranoditam /
tānyaḥ svāraḥ sa jātyena śrutyagre kṣaipra ucyate //
meaning:
एतत्पादान्तवृत्तस्य लक्षणं शास्त्रनोदितम् /
तान्यः स्वारः स जात्येन श्रुत्यग्रे क्षैप्र उच्यते //
text_mt: this is the characteristic of the pādavṛtta taught in the treatise. / The innate svāra is exemplified in tānyaḥ; at the beginning of a phonetic text kṣaipra is stated,

sanskrit_iast:
te manvatābhinitastairavyañjana ūtaye /
tirovirāmo viṣkaṣite praśliṣṭo hīīgovarṇaḥ //
meaning:
ते मन्वताभिनितस्तैरव्यञ्जन ऊतये /
तिरोविरामो विष्कषिते प्रश्लिष्टो हीईगोवर्णः //
text_mt: [as in] te manvata; abhinihita in stairavyañjana ūtaye; / tirovirāma in viṣkaṣite; praśliṣṭa in hīīgovarṇaḥ;

sanskrit_iast:
pādavṛttaḥ kandavidesvarāḥ saptaivamādayaḥ /
uñcādekākṣarātpūrvātsvaraṃ yadyadihākṣaram //
meaning:
पादवृत्तः कन्दविदेस्वराः सप्तैवमादयः /
उञ्चादेकाक्षरात्पूर्वात्स्वरं यद्यदिहाक्षरम् //
text_mt: pādavṛtta in kandavide: thus are the seven pitches and so forth. / Following a high single-syllabled predecessor, whatever vowel syllable is here,

sanskrit_iast:
svārāṇāṃ jātyavarjānāmeṣā prakṛtirucyate /
catvārastvāditaḥ svārāḥ kaṃṣaṃpuṃśphutiśāstrataḥ //
meaning:
स्वाराणां जात्यवर्जानामेषा प्रकृतिरुच्यते /
चत्वारस्त्वादितः स्वाराः कंषंपुंश्फुतिशास्त्रतः //
text_mt: this is declared to be the inherent nature of the circumflexes, excepting the innate ones. / But the first four circumflexes, according to the treatise on tremolo (kampa) and bursting tones,

sanskrit_iast:
udātte caikanīce vā juhvo 'gnistannidarśanam /
ikārānte pade pūrva ukāre parataḥ sthite //
meaning:
उदात्ते चैकनीचे वा जुह्वो ऽग्निस्तन्निदर्शनम् /
इकारान्ते पदे पूर्व उकारे परतः स्थिते //
text_mt: on an acute or on a single low tone: juhvo 'gniḥ is the example of that. / When a word ending in the vowel i precedes and the vowel u stands after it,

sanskrit_iast:
hrasvaṃ kaṃpaṃ vijānīyānmedhāvī nātra saṃśayaḥ /
ikārānte pade caivokāradvayaṃ pare pade //
meaning:
ह्रस्वं कंपं विजानीयान्मेधावी नात्र संशयः /
इकारान्ते पदे चैवोकारद्वयं परे पदे //
text_mt: the wise person should know it as a short tremolo; there is no doubt here. / And when a word ends in the vowel i and two u-vowels follow in the next word,

sanskrit_iast:
dīrghaṃ kaṃpaṃ vijānīyācchāgdhūṣviti nidarśanam /
trayo dīrghāstu vijñeyā ye ca saṃdhyakṣareṣu vai //
meaning:
दीर्घं कंपं विजानीयाच्छाग्धूष्विति निदर्शनम् /
त्रयो दीर्घास्तु विज्ञेया ये च संध्यक्षरेषु वै //
text_mt: one should know it as a long tremolo; chāgdhūṣu is the example. / Three long [tremolos] are to be known, namely those in diphthongs,

sanskrit_iast:
manyā yathā na indrābhyāṃ śeṣā hrasvāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
anekānāmudāttānāmanudāttaḥ pratyayo yadi //
meaning:
मन्या यथा न इन्द्राभ्यां शेषा ह्रस्वाः प्रकीर्तिताः /
अनेकानामुदात्तानामनुदात्तः प्रत्ययो यदि //
text_mt: such as manyā na indrābhyām; the rest are declared as short. / If there is a grave following several acutes,

sanskrit_iast:
śivakaṃpaṃ vijānīyādudāttaḥ pratyayo yadi /
yatra dviprabhṛtīni syurudāttānyakṣarāṇi tu //
meaning:
शिवकंपं विजानीयादुदात्तः प्रत्ययो यदि /
यत्र द्विप्रभृतीनि स्युरुदात्तान्यक्षराणि तु //
text_mt: one should know it as a auspicious tremolo (śivakampa), if an acute is the following element. / Where, however, two or more syllables are acute,

sanskrit_iast:
nīcaṃ voñcaṃ ca paratastatrodāttaṃ vidurbudhāḥ /
na rephe vā hakāre vā dvirbhāvo jāyate kvacit //
meaning:
नीचं वोञ्चं च परतस्तत्रोदात्तं विदुर्बुधाः /
न रेफे वा हकारे वा द्विर्भावो जायते क्वचित् //
text_mt: and a low or a high note follows, the wise know the acute to be there. / Doubling never occurs in the letter r or the letter h,

sanskrit_iast:
na ca vargadvitīyeṣu na caturthe kadācana /
caturthaṃ tu tṛtīyena dvitīyaḥ prathamena tu //
meaning:
न च वर्गद्वितीयेषु न चतुर्थे कदाचन /
चतुर्थं तु तृतीयेन द्वितीयः प्रथमेन तु //
text_mt: nor ever in the second consonants of a class, nor in the fourth. / A fourth [is doubled] by a third, but a second by a first;

sanskrit_iast:
ādyamantyaṃ ca madhyaṃ ca svārākṣareṇa pīḍayet /
anantyaśca bhavetpūrvo hyantaśca parato yadi //
meaning:
आद्यमन्त्यं च मध्यं च स्वाराक्षरेण पीडयेत् /
अनन्त्यश्च भवेत्पूर्वो ह्यन्तश्च परतो यदि //
text_mt: one should compress the initial, the final, and the medial by an accented syllable. / If a non-final [stop] is initial, and a final [nasal] follows,

sanskrit_iast:
tatra madhye yamastiṣṭhetsvavarṇaḥ pūrvavaṇayoḥ /
vargāntyān śaṣasaiḥ sārddhamantasthairvāpi saṃyutān //
meaning:
तत्र मध्ये यमस्तिष्ठेत्स्ववर्णः पूर्ववणयोः /
वर्गान्त्यान् शषसैः सार्द्धमन्तस्थैर्वापि संयुतान् //
text_mt: there in the middle a yama should stand, possessing its own color of the two preceding sounds. / Seeing class-finals joined with ś, ṣ, and s, or with semivowels,

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭvā yamā nivartante adeśikamivādhvagāḥ /
tṛtīyaśca caturthaśca caturthādiparaṃ padam //
meaning:
दृष्ट्वा यमा निवर्तन्ते अदेशिकमिवाध्वगाः /
तृतीयश्च चतुर्थश्च चतुर्थादिपरं पदम् //
text_mt: the yamas turn back, like travelers lacking a guide. / A third and a fourth, followed by a word beginning with a fourth;

sanskrit_iast:
dvau tṛtīyau hakāraśca hakārādiparaṃ padam /
anusvāropadhāmūlā tān kvacitkramataḥ param //
meaning:
द्वौ तृतीयौ हकारश्च हकारादिपरं पदम् /
अनुस्वारोपधामूला तान् क्वचित्क्रमतः परम् //
text_mt: two thirds and the letter h, followed by a word beginning with h; / anusvāra and upadhmānīya: sometimes one duplicates beyond them.

sanskrit_iast:
rahapūrvasaṃyute cāpyuttaraṃ kramate 'kṣaram /
saṃyogo yatra dṛśyeta rvyañjanaṃ virate pade //
meaning:
रहपूर्वसंयुते चाप्युत्तरं क्रमते ऽक्षरम् /
संयोगो यत्र दृश्येत र्व्यञ्जनं विरते पदे //
text_mt: Also when conjunct with r and h preceding, the subsequent syllable duplicates; / where a conjunct is seen, a consonant with r in a paused word [likewise].

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvāṅgamāditaḥ kṛtvā parāṅgādau niveśayet /
saṃyoge svaritaṃ yatra udvātaḥ pratanaṃ tathā //
meaning:
पूर्वाङ्गमादितः कृत्वा पराङ्गादौ निवेशयेत् /
संयोगे स्वरितं यत्र उद्वातः प्रतनं तथा //
text_mt: Having placed the initial limb first, one should set it before the posterior limb. / Where there is a circumflex [accent] in a conjunct, [it is] elevated and likewise extended.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvāṅgaṃ tadvijānīyādyenāraṃbhaḥ paraṃ hi tat /
saṃyogāttu vijānīyātparaṃ saṃyoganāyakam //
meaning:
पूर्वाङ्गं तद्विजानीयाद्येनारंभः परं हि तत् /
संयोगात्तु विजानीयात्परं संयोगनायकम् //
text_mt: One should know that to be the prior limb by which the beginning [is made], for that is posterior; / but from a conjunct one should know the posterior to be the chief of the conjunct.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃyuktasya tu varṇasya tatparaṃ pūrvamakṣaram /
anusvāraḥ padāntaśca kramajaṃ pratyaye svake //
meaning:
संयुक्तस्य तु वर्णस्य तत्परं पूर्वमक्षरम् /
अनुस्वारः पदान्तश्च क्रमजं प्रत्यये स्वके //
text_mt: The syllable prior to a conjunct sound follows it; / the anusvāra and word-ending arise from the krama when followed by their own conditioning sound.

sanskrit_iast:
svarabhaktistathārephaḥ pūrvapūrvāṅgamucyate /
pādādau cāpādādau saṃyogāvagraheṣu ca //
meaning:
स्वरभक्तिस्तथारेफः पूर्वपूर्वाङ्गमुच्यते /
पादादौ चापादादौ संयोगावग्रहेषु च //
text_mt: The svarabhakti vowel-fragment and the sound r are called the preceding limb of each prior [sound], / both at the beginning of a verse-quarter and not at the beginning of a verse-quarter, and in conjuncts and pauses (avagraha).

sanskrit_iast:
yaśabda iti vijñeyo yo 'nyaḥsaya iti smṛtaḥ /
pādādāvapyavicchedesaṃyogānte ca tiṣṭatām //
meaning:
यशब्द इति विज्ञेयो यो ऽन्यःसय इति स्मृतः /
पादादावप्यविच्छेदेसंयोगान्ते च तिष्टताम् //
text_mt: It should be known as the sound ya, while that which is other is remembered as saya, / occurring even at the beginning of a verse-quarter without break, and standing at the end of a conjunct.

sanskrit_iast:
varjayitvā rahapāṇāmupādeśaḥ pradṛśyate /
svasaṃyukto gururjñeyaḥ sānusvārā grimaḥ sphuṭaḥ /
aṇuśeṣo hrigo vāpi yugalādiravisphuṭaḥ //
meaning:
वर्जयित्वा रहपाणामुपादेशः प्रदृश्यते /
स्वसंयुक्तो गुरुर्ज्ञेयः सानुस्वारा ग्रिमः स्फुटः /
अणुशेषो ह्रिगो वापि युगलादिरविस्फुटः //
text_mt: Excluding r and h, the instruction is demonstrated: / one conjoined with itself should be known as heavy; accompanied by an anusvāra, the preceding [syllable] is clear; / having an atomic remnant, or […], the beginning of a pair is indistinct.

sanskrit_iast:
yadudāttamudāttaṃ tadyatsvaritaṃ tatpade bhavati /
yannīcaṃ nīcameva tadyatpracayasthaṃ tadapi nīcam //
meaning:
यदुदात्तमुदात्तं तद्यत्स्वरितं तत्पदे भवति /
यन्नीचं नीचमेव तद्यत्प्रचयस्थं तदपि नीचम् //
text_mt: What is high-pitched (udātta) is udātta; what is circumflex (svarita) is in that word; / what is low-pitched (anudātta) is indeed low; what stands in the monotone (pracaya) is also low.

sanskrit_iast:
agniḥ suto mitramidaṃ tathā vayamayāvahāḥ /
priyaṃ dūtaṃ ghṛtaṃ cittamatiśabdastu nīcataḥ //
meaning:
अग्निः सुतो मित्रमिदं तथा वयमयावहाः /
प्रियं दूतं घृतं चित्तमतिशब्दस्तु नीचतः //
text_mt: ‘Agniḥ’, ‘sutaḥ’, ‘mitram’, ‘idam’, likewise ‘vayam’, ‘ayāvahāḥ’, / ‘priyam’, ‘dūtam’, ‘ghṛtam’, ‘cittam’: the word ‘ati’ is from the low [tone].

sanskrit_iast:
akveṣveva suteṣveva yajñeṣu kalaśeṣu ca /
śateṣu sapavitreṣu nīcāduñcāryate śrutiḥ //
meaning:
अक्वेष्वेव सुतेष्वेव यज्ञेषु कलशेषु च /
शतेषु सपवित्रेषु नीचादुञ्चार्यते श्रुतिः //
text_mt: In words such as ‘akveṣu’, ‘suteṣu’, ‘yajñeṣu’, and ‘kalaśeṣu’, / in ‘śateṣu’, and ‘sapavitreṣu’, the Vedic sound is pronounced from the low [tone].

sanskrit_iast:
hārivaruṇavareṇyeṣu dhārāpuruṣeṣu svaratirephaḥ /
viśvānaronakāraśca śeṣāstusvaritā narāḥ //
meaning:
हारिवरुणवरेण्येषु धारापुरुषेषु स्वरतिरेफः /
विश्वानरोनकारश्च शेषास्तुस्वरिता नराः //
text_mt: In ‘hāri’, ‘varuṇa’, ‘vareṇyeṣu’, ‘dhārā’, ‘puruṣeṣu’, the sound r is accented; / ‘viśvānaraḥ’ has the letter na, and the remaining ‘narāḥ’ are circumflex.

sanskrit_iast:
dvau varuṇau vasvarata uduttamantvaṃ varuṇadhāra caurudhārāmurudhāresvadohate /
mātrikaṃ vā dvimātraṃ vā svaryate yadihākṣaram /
tasyāditor'ddhamātraṃ vai śeṣaṃ tu parato bhavet /
adīrghaṃ dīrghavatkuryāddvisvaraṃ yatprayujyate //
meaning:
द्वौ वरुणौ वस्वरत उदुत्तमन्त्वं वरुणधार चौरुधारामुरुधारेस्वदोहते /
मात्रिकं वा द्विमात्रं वा स्वर्यते यदिहाक्षरम् /
तस्यादितोर्ऽद्धमात्रं वै शेषं तु परतो भवेत् /
अदीर्घं दीर्घवत्कुर्याद्द्विस्वरं यत्प्रयुज्यते //
text_mt: Two ‘varuṇas’ are accented: [in the passages] ‘uduttamam tvam varuṇa...’, [and] ‘dhāracaurudhārām...’ / If a syllable of one mora or two morae is accented here, / half a mora of it belongs to the beginning, and the remainder belongs to what follows; / one should make what is non-long like a long [syllable] when two vowels are employed.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṃpotsvaritābhigītaṃ hrasvakarṣaṇameva ca /
nimeṣakālo mātrā syādvidyutkāleti cāpare //
meaning:
कंपोत्स्वरिताभिगीतं ह्रस्वकर्षणमेव च /
निमेषकालो मात्रा स्याद्विद्युत्कालेति चापरे //
text_mt: Tremor, elevated tone, singing out, and the dragging of a short vowel: / the measure of a mora is the time of a wink of the eye, and others say the duration of a lightning flash.

sanskrit_iast: ṛksvarā tulyayogā vā kaiścidevamudīryate //
meaning: ऋक्स्वरा तुल्ययोगा वा कैश्चिदेवमुदीर्यते //
text_mt: Vowels of the Ṛgveda or those of equal conjunction are described thus by some.

sanskrit_iast:
samāse 'vagrahaṃ kuryātpadaṃ cātrānusaṃhitam /
yetīkṣarādikaraṇaṃ padāntasyeti taṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
समासे ऽवग्रहं कुर्यात्पदं चात्रानुसंहितम् /
येतीक्षरादिकरणं पदान्तस्येति तं विदुः //
text_mt: One should make a pause (avagraha) in a compound, and the word here is joined in saṃhitā; / they know the operation beginning with the letter ‘iti’ as belonging to the end of a word.

sanskrit_iast:
(sarvatra mitraputrasakhiśabdā ahiśatakratoravagrāhyāḥ /
ādityaviprajātavedāśca satpatigopativṛtrahāsamudrāśca /
svarayupuvodevayavaścāritaṃ devatātape ) cikitiśca dhacaiva nāvagṛhṇanti paṇḍitāḥ /
vivṛtayaścatasro vai vijñeyā iti me matam //
meaning:
(सर्वत्र मित्रपुत्रसखिशब्दा अहिशतक्रतोरवग्राह्याः /
आदित्यविप्रजातवेदाश्च सत्पतिगोपतिवृत्रहासमुद्राश्च /
स्वरयुपुवोदेवयवश्चारितं देवतातपे ) चिकितिश्च धचैव नावगृह्णन्ति पण्डिताः /
विवृतयश्चतस्रो वै विज्ञेया इति मे मतम् //
text_mt: Everywhere the words ‘mitra’, ‘putra’, and ‘sakhi’ are to be separated by avagraha from ‘ahi’ and ‘śatakratu’; / and ‘āditya’, ‘vipra’, ‘jātavedas’, ‘satpati’, ‘gopati’, ‘vṛtrahā’, and ‘samudra’; / [in the forms] ‘svarayu...’ […] and ‘cikitiḥ’ and ‘dha’: the learned do not separate these with avagraha; / four hiatuses (vivṛti) are indeed to be known, such is my view.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣarāṇāṃ niyogena tāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu /
hrasvādivatsānusṛtā vatsānusāriṇī cāgre //
meaning:
अक्षराणां नियोगेन तासां नामानि मे शृणु /
ह्रस्वादिवत्सानुसृता वत्सानुसारिणी चाग्रे //
text_mt: Hear from me their names according to the deployment of syllables: / beginning with a short vowel is the ‘vatsānusṛtā’ (‘calf-followed’), and before it the ‘vatsānusāriṇī’ (‘calf-following’);

sanskrit_iast:
pākavatyubhayorhrasvā dīrghā vṛddhā pipīlikāḥ /
catasṛṇāṃ vivṛtīnā mantaraṃ mātrikaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
पाकवत्युभयोर्ह्रस्वा दीर्घा वृद्धा पिपीलिकाः /
चतसृणां विवृतीना मन्तरं मात्रिकं भवेत् //
text_mt: The ‘pākavatī’ has short [vowels] in both; the ‘pipīlikā’ has long [vowels] increased. / The interval between the four hiatuses should be of one mora,

sanskrit_iast: arddhamātrikamanyeṣāmanyeṣāmaṇumātrikam //
meaning: अर्द्धमात्रिकमन्येषामन्येषामणुमात्रिकम् //
text_mt: or half a mora according to others, or of an atomic mora according to others.

sanskrit_iast:
āpadyate makāro rephoṣmasu pratyaye 'pyanusvāram /
paveṣu parasavarṇaṃ sparśeṣu cottamāpatim //
meaning:
आपद्यते मकारो रेफोष्मसु प्रत्यये ऽप्यनुस्वारम् /
पवेषु परसवर्णं स्पर्शेषु चोत्तमापतिम् //
text_mt: The sound m becomes an anusvāra when followed by r or a sibilant; / before labials it becomes the sound homogenous with the following, and before stop consonants it becomes the nasal stop.

sanskrit_iast:
nakārānte padā pūrve svare ca parataḥ sthite /
akāraṃ raktamityāhustakāreṇa tu rajyate //
meaning:
नकारान्ते पदा पूर्वे स्वरे च परतः स्थिते /
अकारं रक्तमित्याहुस्तकारेण तु रज्यते //
text_mt: When a prior word ends in the letter n and a vowel follows, / they say the vowel a is coloured, and it is nasalised by the letter t.

sanskrit_iast:
nakārānte pade pūrve vyañjanaiśca yavohiṣu /
arddhamātrā tu pūrvasya rajyate tvaṇumātrayā //
meaning:
नकारान्ते पदे पूर्वे व्यञ्जनैश्च यवोहिषु /
अर्द्धमात्रा तु पूर्वस्य रज्यते त्वणुमात्रया //
text_mt: When a prior word ends in the letter n and consonants such as y, v, and h [follow], / half a mora of the preceding [sound] is nasalised by an atomic mora.

sanskrit_iast:
nakārasvarasaṃyuktaścaturyukto vidhīyate /
repho raṅgaśca lopaśca sānusvaro 'pi vā kvacit //
meaning:
नकारस्वरसंयुक्तश्चतुर्युक्तो विधीयते /
रेफो रङ्गश्च लोपश्च सानुस्वरो ऽपि वा क्वचित् //
text_mt: The sound n conjoined with a vowel is prescribed with fourfold modification: / r, a nasal colouration (raṅga), elision, or sometimes accompanied by an anusvāra.

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdayāduttiṣṭateraṅgaḥ kāṃsyena tu samanvitaḥ /
mṛduścaiva dvimātraśca dadhanvāṃ iti nidarśanam //
meaning:
हृदयादुत्तिष्टतेरङ्गः कांस्येन तु समन्वितः /
मृदुश्चैव द्विमात्रश्च दधन्वां इति निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: The raṅga arises from the heart, accompanied by the tone of a bronze vessel; / it is soft and of two morae, as illustrated by ‘dadhanvāṃ’.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā saurāṣṭrikā nārī arāṃ ityabhibhāṣate /
evaṃ raṅgaḥ prayoktavyo nāradaitanmataṃ mama //
meaning:
यथा सौराष्ट्रिका नारी अरां इत्यभिभाषते /
एवं रङ्गः प्रयोक्तव्यो नारदैतन्मतं मम //
text_mt: Just as a woman of Saurāṣṭra says ‘arāṃ’, / in this way the raṅga should be articulated; O Nārada, this is my view.

sanskrit_iast:
svarā gaḍadabāścaiva ṅaṇanamāḥ sahoṣmabhiḥ /
caturṇāṃ padajātīnāṃ padāntā daśa kīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
स्वरा गडदबाश्चैव ङणनमाः सहोष्मभिः /
चतुर्णां पदजातीनां पदान्ता दश कीर्तिताः //
text_mt: The vowels, g, ḍ, d, b, and ṅ, ṇ, n, m, together with the spirants: / these ten are declared to be word-finals of the four classes of words.

sanskrit_iast:
svara uccaḥ svaro nīcaḥ svaraḥ svarita eva ca /
vyañjanā na tu vartante yatra tiṣṭati sa svaraḥ //
meaning:
स्वर उच्चः स्वरो नीचः स्वरः स्वरित एव च /
व्यञ्जना न तु वर्तन्ते यत्र तिष्टति स स्वरः //
text_mt: A vowel is high-pitched, a vowel is low-pitched, and a vowel is circumflex; / consonants do not exist independently where that vowel stands.

sanskrit_iast:
svarapradhānaṃ traisvaryamācāryāḥ pratijānate /
maṇivadvyañjanaṃ vidyātsūtra vañca svaraṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
स्वरप्रधानं त्रैस्वर्यमाचार्याः प्रतिजानते /
मणिवद्व्यञ्जनं विद्यात्सूत्र वञ्च स्वरं विदुः //
text_mt: The teachers maintain that the threefold accent is primarily vowel-based; / one should know the consonant to be like a jewel, and they know the vowel to be like the thread.

sanskrit_iast:
durbalasya yathā rāṣṭraṃ harate balavānnṛpaḥ /
durbalaṃ vyajanaṃ tadvaddhareta balavānsvaraḥ //
meaning:
दुर्बलस्य यथा राष्ट्रं हरते बलवान्नृपः /
दुर्बलं व्यजनं तद्वद्धरेत बलवान्स्वरः //
text_mt: Just as a strong king seizes the realm of a weak one, / even so a strong vowel seizes a weak consonant.

sanskrit_iast:
ubhāvaśca vivṛttiśca śaṣasārepha eva ca /
jihvāmūlamupadhmā ca gatiraṣṭavidhoṣmaṇaḥ //
meaning:
उभावश्च विवृत्तिश्च शषसारेफ एव च /
जिह्वामूलमुपध्मा च गतिरष्टविधोष्मणः //
text_mt: Becoming the sound u, hiatus (vivṛtti), ś, ṣ, s, and r, / the jihvāmūlīya and upadhmānīya: such is the eightfold course of the spirant.

sanskrit_iast:
svarapratyayāvivṛtiḥ saṃhitāyāṃ tu yā bhavet /
visargastatra mantavyaratālavyaścātra jāyate //
meaning:
स्वरप्रत्ययाविवृतिः संहितायां तु या भवेत् /
विसर्गस्तत्र मन्तव्यरतालव्यश्चात्र जायते //
text_mt: Whatever hiatus with a vocalic conditioner occurs in continuous recitation (saṃhitā), / a visarga is to be considered there, and a palatal [sound] is produced here.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃdhyakṣare pare saṃdhau prāptasuptau yavau yadi /
vyañjanākhyā vivṛttistu svarākhyā pratisaṃhitā //
meaning:
संध्यक्षरे परे संधौ प्राप्तसुप्तौ यवौ यदि /
व्यञ्जनाख्या विवृत्तिस्तु स्वराख्या प्रतिसंहिता //
text_mt: When a diphthong is followed in sandhi, if y and v have lapsed into elision, / that hiatus is designated as consonantal, while that joined in sandhi is designated as vocalic.

sanskrit_iast:
ūṣmāntaṃ virate yatra saṃbhāvo bhavati kvacit /
vivṛttiryā bhavettatra svarākhyāṃ tāṃ vinirddiśet //
meaning:
ऊष्मान्तं विरते यत्र संभावो भवति क्वचित् /
विवृत्तिर्या भवेत्तत्र स्वराख्यां तां विनिर्द्दिशेत् //
text_mt: Where a pause ends in a spirant and assimilation (saṃbhāva) occurs anywhere, / whatever hiatus occurs there, one should declare it to be vocalic.

sanskrit_iast:
yadyobhāvaprasaṃdhānamṛkārādiparaṃ padam /
svarāntaṃ tādṛśaṃ vidyādyadanyavdyaktamūṣmaṇaḥ //
meaning:
यद्योभावप्रसंधानमृकारादिपरं पदम् /
स्वरान्तं तादृशं विद्याद्यदन्यव्द्यक्तमूष्मणः //
text_mt: If there is the joining of a transition to o followed by a word beginning with ṛ, / one should know such [a word] to end in a vowel, whereas the other is the clear form of a spirant.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamā uttamāścaiva padānteṣu yadi sthitāḥ /
dvitīyaṃ sthānamāpannāḥ śaṣasapratyayā yadi //
meaning:
प्रथमा उत्तमाश्चैव पदान्तेषु यदि स्थिताः /
द्वितीयं स्थानमापन्नाः शषसप्रत्यया यदि //
text_mt: If the first and fifth [stops] stand at word-ends, / they attain the second place when conditioned by ś, ṣ, or s.

sanskrit_iast:
prathamānūṣmasaṃyuktān dvitīyāniva darśayet /
na caitānpratijānīyādyathā matsyaḥ kṣuropsarāḥ //
meaning:
प्रथमानूष्मसंयुक्तान् द्वितीयानिव दर्शयेत् /
न चैतान्प्रतिजानीयाद्यथा मत्स्यः क्षुरोप्सराः //
text_mt: One should pronounce the first [stops] conjoined with spirants as if they were second [aspirates]; / but one must not recognise them [as such] in cases like ‘matsyaḥ’, ‘kṣuraḥ’, and ‘apsarāḥ’.

sanskrit_iast:
chandomānaṃ ca vṛttaṃ ca pādasthānaṃ trikāraṇam /
ṛcaḥ svacchandavṛttāstu pādāstvakṣaramānataḥ //
meaning:
छन्दोमानं च वृत्तं च पादस्थानं त्रिकारणम् /
ऋचः स्वच्छन्दवृत्तास्तु पादास्त्वक्षरमानतः //
text_mt: Metrical measure, rhythm, and verse-quarter position: these are the threefold cause. / The verses of the Ṛgveda are self-metered rhythms, but their verse-quarters are by syllable count.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛgvaryyān svarabhaktiṃ ca chandomānena nirddiśet /
pratyayeta sahārephamimīte svarabhaktayā //
meaning:
ऋग्वर्य्यान् स्वरभक्तिं च छन्दोमानेन निर्द्दिशेत् /
प्रत्ययेत सहारेफमिमीते स्वरभक्तया //
text_mt: One should determine the Ṛgvedic sounds and the svarabhakti vowel-fragment by metrical measure; / when conditioned along with the sound r, one measures it by the svarabhakti.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛvarṇe tu pṛthagrephaḥ pratyayastu vṛthā bhaveta /
vidyāllaghumṛkāraṃ tu yadi tūṣmāṇasaṃyutaḥ //
meaning:
ऋवर्णे तु पृथग्रेफः प्रत्ययस्तु वृथा भवेत /
विद्याल्लघुमृकारं तु यदि तूष्माणसंयुतः //
text_mt: In the vocalic ṛ, the sound r is distinct, but a separate conditioning is superfluous; / one should know the vocalic ṛ to be light, unless it is conjoined with a spirant.

sanskrit_iast:
ūṣmaṇaiva hi saṃyukta ṛkāro yatra pīḍyate /
guruvarṇaḥ sa vijñeyastṛcaṃ cātra nidarśanam //
meaning:
ऊष्मणैव हि संयुक्त ऋकारो यत्र पीड्यते /
गुरुवर्णः स विज्ञेयस्तृचं चात्र निदर्शनम् //
text_mt: For where the vocalic ṛ is compressed when conjoined with a spirant, / that sound is to be known as heavy; the word ‘tṛcam’ is the example here.

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣabhaṃ ca gṛhītaṃ ca bṛhaspatiṃ pṛthivyāṃ ca /
nirṛtipañcamā hyatra ṛkārā nātra saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
ऋषभं च गृहीतं च बृहस्पतिं पृथिव्यां च /
निरृतिपञ्चमा ह्यत्र ऋकारा नात्र संशयः //
text_mt: In ‘ṛṣabham’, ‘gṛhītam’, ‘bṛhaspatim’, and ‘pṛthivyām’, / and with ‘nirṛti’ as fifth: these are indeed vocalic ṛ sounds, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṣasaha rādau rephaḥ sparabhaktirjāyate dvipadasaṃdhau /
iuvarṇābhyāṃ hīnā kvacidekapadākramaviyuktā //
meaning:
शषसह रादौ रेफः स्परभक्तिर्जायते द्विपदसंधौ /
इउवर्णाभ्यां हीना क्वचिदेकपदाक्रमवियुक्ता //
text_mt: When r precedes ś, ṣ, s, or h, the svarabhakti vowel-fragment is produced at the junction of two words; / it is free from the vowels i and u, and sometimes detached from the krama in a single word.

sanskrit_iast:
svarabhaktirdvidhā proktāṛkāre repha eva ca /
svarodā vyañjanodā ca vihitākṣaracintakaiḥ //
meaning:
स्वरभक्तिर्द्विधा प्रोक्ताऋकारे रेफ एव च /
स्वरोदा व्यञ्जनोदा च विहिताक्षरचिन्तकैः //
text_mt: The svarabhakti vowel-fragment is declared to be of two kinds: in the vocalic ṛ and in the sound r; / it has a vocalic onset and a consonantal onset, as determined by analysts of syllables.

sanskrit_iast:
śaṣaseṣu svarodayāṃ hakāre vyañjanodayām /
śaṣaseṣu vivṛtāṃ tu hakāre saṃvṛtāṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
शषसेषु स्वरोदयां हकारे व्यञ्जनोदयाम् /
शषसेषु विवृतां तु हकारे संवृतां विदुः //
text_mt: Before ś, ṣ, and s, it has a vocalic onset; before the sound h, it has a consonantal onset; / they know it to be open before ś, ṣ, and s, but closed before the sound h.

sanskrit_iast:
svarabhaktiṃ prayuñjāna srīndoṣānparivarjayet /
ikāraṃ cāpyukāraṃ grastadoṣaṃ tathaiva ca //
meaning:
स्वरभक्तिं प्रयुञ्जान स्रीन्दोषान्परिवर्जयेत् /
इकारं चाप्युकारं ग्रस्तदोषं तथैव च //
text_mt: Employing the svarabhakti vowel-fragment, one should avoid three faults: / the vowel i, the vowel u, and likewise the fault of swallowing (grasta).

sanskrit_iast:
saṃyogaparaṃ chaparaṃ visarjanīyaṃ dvimātrakaṃ caiva /
atha sāntika ca naṅmasānusvāraṃ ghuṭataṃ ca //
meaning:
संयोगपरं छपरं विसर्जनीयं द्विमात्रकं चैव /
अथ सान्तिक च नङ्मसानुस्वारं घुटतं च //
text_mt: Followed by a conjunct, followed by ch, the visarga has two morae; / then when proximate, accompanied by anusvāra, and [...].

sanskrit_iast:
yasyāḥ pādaḥ prathamo dvādaśamātrastathā tṛtīyo 'pi /
aṣṭādaśo dvitīyaḥ samāpannaḥ pañcadaśamātraḥ /
yasyā lakṣaṇamuktaṃ yā tvanyā sā smṛtā vipulā //
meaning:
यस्याः पादः प्रथमो द्वादशमात्रस्तथा तृतीयो ऽपि /
अष्टादशो द्वितीयः समापन्नः पञ्चदशमात्रः /
यस्या लक्षणमुक्तं या त्वन्या सा स्मृता विपुला //
text_mt:
[That metre] whose first quarter contains twelve morae and likewise the third,
whose second consists of eighteen, and whose [fourth] is finished with fifteen morae,
is that whose definition has been stated; but that which is otherwise is recorded as vipulā.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣarāṇāṃ laghuhrasvamasaṃyogaparaṃ yadi /
tatsaṃyogottaraṃ vidyādgurudārghākṣarāṇi tu //
meaning:
अक्षराणां लघुह्रस्वमसंयोगपरं यदि /
तत्संयोगोत्तरं विद्याद्गुरुदार्घाक्षराणि तु //
text_mt:
Among syllables, a short [syllable] is light if it is not followed by a conjunct [consonant];
if it is followed by a conjunct, one should know it to be heavy, as are long syllables.

sanskrit_iast: vivṛttir yatra dṛśyate svārasyaivāgrataḥ sthitaḥ //
meaning: विवृत्तिर् यत्र दृश्यते स्वारस्यैवाग्रतः स्थितः //
text_mt: Where hiatus is seen standing right before a svāra [accent],

sanskrit_iast:
gurusvāraḥ savijñeyaḥ kṣaiprastatra na vidyate //a
aṣṭaprakāraṃ vijñeyaṃ padānāṃ svaralakṣaṇam //
meaning:
गुरुस्वारः सविज्ञेयः क्षैप्रस्तत्र न विद्यते //अ
अष्टप्रकारं विज्ञेयं पदानां स्वरलक्षणम् //
text_mt:
it should be recognized as a heavy svāra; the kṣaipra accent is not found there.
One should know the accentual characteristics of words to be of eight kinds:

sanskrit_iast:
anto dāttamādyudāttamudāttamanudāttaṃ nīcasvaritam /
madhyodāttaṃ svaritaṃ dvirudāttamityetā aṣṭau padasaṃjñāḥ //
meaning:
अन्तो दात्तमाद्युदात्तमुदात्तमनुदात्तं नीचस्वरितम् /
मध्योदात्तं स्वरितं द्विरुदात्तमित्येता अष्टौ पदसंज्ञाः //
text_mt:
Having the udātta at the end, having the udātta at the beginning, [entirely] udātta, anudātta, the low svarita,
having the udātta in the middle, svarita, and having two udāttas—these are the eight designations of words.

sanskrit_iast:
agniḥ somaḥ pravo vīryaṃ haviṣā svarvanaspatiḥ /
antarmadhyamayotāmyudamanunipātya ādyātsvaritamupasarge dvirnnīcamākhyāta iti svaritātparāṇi yāni syurddhārāpakṣarāṇi tu /
sarvāṇi pracayasthānyupodāttaṃ nihanyate //
meaning:
अग्निः सोमः प्रवो वीर्यं हविषा स्वर्वनस्पतिः /
अन्तर्मध्यमयोताम्युदमनुनिपात्य आद्यात्स्वरितमुपसर्गे द्विर्न्नीचमाख्यात इति स्वरितात्पराणि यानि स्युर्द्धारापक्षराणि तु /
सर्वाणि प्रचयस्थान्युपोदात्तं निहन्यते //
text_mt:
"Agniḥ", "somaḥ", "pra vaḥ", "vīryam", "haviṣā", "svar", "vanaspatiḥ":
[these exemplify] the final, medial, [...],
and following a svarita, whatever syllables occur in succession,
all belong to the pracaya accent; the pre-udātta is depressed.

sanskrit_iast:
pracayo yatra dṛśyeta tatra hanyātsvaraṃ budhaḥ /
svaritaḥ kevalo yatra mṛdustatra nipātayet //
meaning:
प्रचयो यत्र दृश्येत तत्र हन्यात्स्वरं बुधः /
स्वरितः केवलो यत्र मृदुस्तत्र निपातयेत् //
text_mt:
Where pracaya is observed, the wise man should there suppress the accent;
where there is a solitary svarita, he should drop it gently there.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcavidhamācāryakaṃ nāma sukhaṃ nyāsaḥ karaṇaṃ pratijñoccāraṇā /
atrocyate śreyaḥ khalu vaiśyāḥ pratijñātoccāraṇā yasya kasyacidvarṇasya karaṇaṃ nopalabhyate pratijñā tatra voḍhavyākaraṇaṃ hi tadātmakam //
meaning:
पञ्चविधमाचार्यकं नाम सुखं न्यासः करणं प्रतिज्ञोच्चारणा /
अत्रोच्यते श्रेयः खलु वैश्याः प्रतिज्ञातोच्चारणा यस्य कस्यचिद्वर्णस्य करणं नोपलभ्यते प्रतिज्ञा तत्र वोढव्याकरणं हि तदात्मकम् //
text_mt:
The role of the teacher is fivefold: comfort, placement, articulatory effort, the enunciated rule, and delivery.
Here it is said: that is superior indeed; [...] when the articulatory effort for any sound whatsoever is not obtained, the rule must be maintained there, for the effort is identical with it.

sanskrit_iast:
tuṃburubhavadviśiṣṭaviśvāvasvādayaśca gandharvāḥ /
sāmasu nibhṛtaṃ karaṇaṃ svarasaukṣmyānnaiva jānīyuḥ //
meaning:
तुंबुरुभवद्विशिष्टविश्वावस्वादयश्च गन्धर्वाः /
सामसु निभृतं करणं स्वरसौक्ष्म्यान्नैव जानीयुः //
text_mt:
Even the Gandharvas, beginning with Viśvāvasu and Tuṃburu, who are distinguished among beings,
could never perceive the concealed articulatory effort in the sāmans, because of the subtlety of the accent.

sanskrit_iast:
kaukṣeyāgniṃ sadā rakṣedaśrīpādarśanaṃ hetum /
jīrṇo hāraḥ prabuddhaḥ khalūṣasinbrahma cintayet //
meaning:
कौक्षेयाग्निं सदा रक्षेदश्रीपादर्शनं हेतुम् /
जीर्णो हारः प्रबुद्धः खलूषसिन्ब्रह्म चिन्तयेत् //
text_mt:
One should always guard the gastric fire, avoiding whatever causes the appearance of disease;
when food is digested and one is awake, one should indeed meditate on Brahman at dawn.

sanskrit_iast:
śaradviṣuvatotītāduṣasyutthānamiṣyate /
yāvadvāsaṃtikī rātrirmadhyamā paryupasthitā //
meaning:
शरद्विषुवतोतीतादुषस्युत्थानमिष्यते /
यावद्वासंतिकी रात्रिर्मध्यमा पर्युपस्थिता //
text_mt:
Rising at dawn is prescribed after the autumn equinox,
until the middle night of spring has arrived.

sanskrit_iast:
āmrapālāśabilvānāmapāmārgaśirīṣayoḥ /
vāgyataḥ prātarutthāya bhakṣayeddvatadhāvanam //
meaning:
आम्रपालाशबिल्वानामपामार्गशिरीषयोः /
वाग्यतः प्रातरुत्थाय भक्षयेद्द्वतधावनम् //
text_mt:
Having risen in the morning, holding one's speech in check, one should chew a tooth-stick
from the mango, palāśa, bilva, apāmārga, or sirīṣa [trees],

sanskrit_iast:
khādiraśca kadambaśca karavīrakarañjayoḥ /
sarve kaṇṭakinaḥ puṇyāḥ kṣīriṇaśca yaśasvinaḥ //
meaning:
खादिरश्च कदम्बश्च करवीरकरञ्जयोः /
सर्वे कण्टकिनः पुण्याः क्षीरिणश्च यशस्विनः //
text_mt:
or from khadira, kadamba, karavīra, or karañja.
All thorny trees are auspicious, and milky trees bring renown.

sanskrit_iast:
tenāsya karaṇe saukṣmyaṃ mādhuryaṃ copa jāyate /
varṇāṃśca kurute samyakprācīnaudavatiryathā //
meaning:
तेनास्य करणे सौक्ष्म्यं माधुर्यं चोप जायते /
वर्णांश्च कुरुते सम्यक्प्राचीनौदवतिर्यथा //
text_mt:
By this, subtlety and sweetness are produced in his articulation,
and he utters the sounds properly, just like the flow of water eastward.

sanskrit_iast:
triphalāṃ lavaṇākhyena bhakṣayecchiṣaayakaḥ sadā /
agnimedhājananyeṣā svaravarṇakarī tathā //
meaning:
त्रिफलां लवणाख्येन भक्षयेच्छिषअयकः सदा /
अग्निमेधाजनन्येषा स्वरवर्णकरी तथा //
text_mt:
A student should always consume triphalā with what is called salt;
this generates digestive fire and intellect, and similarly improves voice and pronunciation.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtvā cāvaśyakāndharmāñjāṭharaṃ paryupāsya ca /
pītvā madhuṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva śucirbhūtvā tato vadet //
meaning:
कृत्वा चावश्यकान्धर्माञ्जाठरं पर्युपास्य च /
पीत्वा मधुं घृतं चैव शुचिर्भूत्वा ततो वदेत् //
text_mt:
Having performed the obligatory duties and attended to the gastric fire,
and having drunk honey and clarified butter, becoming pure, he should then speak.

sanskrit_iast:
mandreṇopakrametpūrvaṃ sarvaśākhāsvayaṃ vidhiḥ /
saptamantrānatikramya yatheṣṭāṃ vācamutsṛjet //
meaning:
मन्द्रेणोपक्रमेत्पूर्वं सर्वशाखास्वयं विधिः /
सप्तमन्त्रानतिक्रम्य यथेष्टां वाचमुत्सृजेत् //
text_mt:
He should begin first in a low tone; this is the rule in all Vedic recensions.
Passing beyond seven mantras, he may emit his voice as he desires.

sanskrit_iast:
na tāṃ samīrayedvācaṃ na prāṇamuparodhayet /
prāṇānāmuparodhena vaisvaryaṃ copajāyate /
svaravyaṇḍajanamādhuryaṃ lupyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
न तां समीरयेद्वाचं न प्राणमुपरोधयेत् /
प्राणानामुपरोधेन वैस्वर्यं चोपजायते /
स्वरव्यण्डजनमाधुर्यं लुप्यते नात्र संशयः //

sanskrit_iast:
kutīrthādāgataṃ dagdhamapavarṇaiśca bhakṣitam //
na tasya parimokṣo 'sti pāpāheriva kilbiṣāt //
meaning:
कुतीर्थादागतं दग्धमपवर्णैश्च भक्षितम् //
न तस्य परिमोक्षो ऽस्ति पापाहेरिव किल्बिषात् //
text_mt:
What is received from a bad teacher is burnt and ruined by corrupted sounds;
there is no deliverance for him from that sin, just as from a venomous serpent.

sanskrit_iast:
sutīrthādāgataṃ jagdhuṃ svāmnātaṃ supratiṣṭitam /
susvareṇa svavakreṇa prayuktaṃ brahma rājati //
na takālo na laṃboṣṭo na ca sarvānunāsikaḥ //
meaning:
सुतीर्थादागतं जग्धुं स्वाम्नातं सुप्रतिष्टितम् /
सुस्वरेण स्ववक्रेण प्रयुक्तं ब्रह्म राजति //
न तकालो न लंबोष्टो न च सर्वानुनासिकः //
text_mt:
What is received from a good teacher, properly digested, correctly recited, well established,
and pronounced with a good tone from one's own mouth—that Brahman shines forth.
He who is neither late in cadence, nor pendulous-lipped, nor entirely nasal,

sanskrit_iast: gadgado baddhajihvaśca prayogānvaktumarhati //
meaning: गद्गदो बद्धजिह्वश्च प्रयोगान्वक्तुमर्हति //
text_mt: nor stammering, nor tongue-tied, is fit to recite the sacred formulas.

sanskrit_iast:
ekacitto niruddhāntaḥ snāto gānavivarjjitaḥ /
sa tu varṇānprayuñjīta detoṣṭhaṃ yasya śobhanam //
meaning:
एकचित्तो निरुद्धान्तः स्नातो गानविवर्ज्जितः /
स तु वर्णान्प्रयुञ्जीत देतोष्ठं यस्य शोभनम् //
text_mt:
Single-minded, his inner senses restrained, bathed, free from frivolous chanting,
he whose teeth and lips are handsome should indeed articulate the sounds.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcavidyāṃ na gṛhṇanti caṇḍā stabdhāśca ye narāḥ /
alasāśca sarogāśca yeṣāṃ ca visṛtaṃ manaḥ //
meaning:
पञ्चविद्यां न गृह्णन्ति चण्डा स्तब्धाश्च ये नराः /
अलसाश्च सरोगाश्च येषां च विसृतं मनः //
text_mt:
Men do not acquire knowledge in five cases: the fierce, the obstinate,
the indolent, the diseased, and those whose minds are distracted.

sanskrit_iast:
śanairvidyāṃ śanairarthānārohetparvataṃ śanaiḥ /
śanairadhvasu varteta yojanānna paraṃ vrajet //
meaning:
शनैर्विद्यां शनैरर्थानारोहेत्पर्वतं शनैः /
शनैरध्वसु वर्तेत योजनान्न परं व्रजेत् //
text_mt:
Slowly should one acquire knowledge, slowly acquire wealth, slowly climb a mountain;
slowly should one proceed on paths; one should not walk beyond a yojana [at once].

sanskrit_iast:
yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu śanairyāti pipīlikā /
agacchanvainateyo 'pi padamekaṃ na gacchati //
meaning:
योजनानां सहस्रं तु शनैर्याति पिपीलिका /
अगच्छन्वैनतेयो ऽपि पदमेकं न गच्छति //
text_mt:
Even an ant goes a thousand yojanas slowly,
[yet] even Garuḍa, if he does not move, does not advance a single step.

sanskrit_iast:
nahi pāpahatā vāṇī prayogānvaktumarhati /
badhirasyeva jalpasya vidagdhā vāmalocanā //
meaning:
नहि पापहता वाणी प्रयोगान्वक्तुमर्हति /
बधिरस्येव जल्पस्य विदग्धा वामलोचना //
text_mt:
A voice ruined by sin is not fit to utter the sacred formulas,
just as a clever, fair-eyed woman cannot converse with a deaf man.

sanskrit_iast:
upāṃśucaritaṃ caiva yo 'dhīte vitrasanniva /
api rūpasahasreṣu saṃdeheṣveva vartate //
meaning:
उपांशुचरितं चैव यो ऽधीते वित्रसन्निव /
अपि रूपसहस्रेषु संदेहेष्वेव वर्तते //
text_mt:
He who studies what should be recited in a whisper as if trembling in fear,
remains only in doubts, even through a thousand forms.

sanskrit_iast:
pustakapratyayādhītaṃ nādhītaṃ gurusannidhau /
rājate na sabhāmadhyejāragarbheva kāminī //
meaning:
पुस्तकप्रत्ययाधीतं नाधीतं गुरुसन्निधौ /
राजते न सभामध्येजारगर्भेव कामिनी //
text_mt:
Knowledge acquired relying on books, not studied in the presence of a guru,
does not shine in the midst of an assembly, like a wanton woman pregnant by a paramour.

sanskrit_iast:
añjanasya kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā valmīkasya tu saṃcayam /
avandhyaṃ divasaṃ kuryāddānādhyayanakarmasu //
meaning:
अञ्जनस्य क्षयं दृष्ट्वा वल्मीकस्य तु संचयम् /
अवन्ध्यं दिवसं कुर्याद्दानाध्ययनकर्मसु //
text_mt:
Seeing the depletion of collyrium and the accumulation of an anthill,
one should make the day fruitful in deeds of giving and study.

sanskrit_iast:
yatkīṭaiḥ pāṃśubhiḥ ślakṣṇairvalmīkaḥ kriyate mahān /
na tatra balasāmarthyamudyogasgatatra kāraṇam //
meaning:
यत्कीटैः पांशुभिः श्लक्ष्णैर्वल्मीकः क्रियते महान् /
न तत्र बलसामर्थ्यमुद्योगस्गतत्र कारणम् //
text_mt:
Since a great anthill is built by insects with fine particles of dust,
it is not physical strength that is the cause there, but persistent effort.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasraguṇitā vidyā śataśaḥ parikīrtitā /
āgamiṣyati jihvāgre sthalānnimnamivodakam //
meaning:
सहस्रगुणिता विद्या शतशः परिकीर्तिता /
आगमिष्यति जिह्वाग्रे स्थलान्निम्नमिवोदकम् //
text_mt:
Knowledge repeated a thousand times and recited hundreds of times
will come to the tip of the tongue, like water [flowing] from high ground to a low place.

sanskrit_iast:
hayanāmiva jātyānāmarddharātrārddhaśāyinām /
nahi vādyārthināṃ nidrā ciraṃ netreṣu tiṣṭati //
meaning:
हयनामिव जात्यानामर्द्धरात्रार्द्धशायिनाम् /
नहि वाद्यार्थिनां निद्रा चिरं नेत्रेषु तिष्टति //
text_mt:
Just as with thoroughbred horses who sleep only half of midnight,
sleep does not long linger in the eyes of those who seek learning.

sanskrit_iast:
na bhojanabilaṃvī syānna ca nārīnivandhanaḥ /
samudramapi vidyārthī vrajedgaruḍahaṃsavat //
meaning:
न भोजनबिलंवी स्यान्न च नारीनिवन्धनः /
समुद्रमपि विद्यार्थी व्रजेद्गरुडहंसवत् //
text_mt:
One should not linger over meals, nor be bound to women;
a seeker of knowledge should cross even the ocean like Garuḍa or a swan.

sanskrit_iast:
ahiriva gaṇādbhitaḥ sāhityānnarakādiva /
rākṣasībhya iva sribhyaḥ sa vidyāmadhigacchati //
meaning:
अहिरिव गणाद्भितः साहित्यान्नरकादिव /
राक्षसीभ्य इव स्रिभ्यः स विद्यामधिगच्छति //
text_mt:
Fearing crowds like a serpent, fearing worldly literature like hell,
and fearing women like demonesses, he attains knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
na śaṭhāḥ prānpuvantyarthānna klibā na ca māninaḥ /
na ca lokaravā dīnā na ca svasvapratīkṣakāḥ //
meaning:
न शठाः प्रान्पुवन्त्यर्थान्न क्लिबा न च मानिनः /
न च लोकरवा दीना न च स्वस्वप्रतीक्षकाः //
text_mt:
The deceitful do not attain their aims, nor the impotent, nor the arrogant,
nor those distressed by public gossip, nor those waiting for favorable moments for everything.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā khananankhanitreṇa bhūpalaṃ vāri vindati /
