text_mt: Learning, action, heroism, and widely extensive knowledge / are worn away for the sake of wealth, but one who has achieved the true goal is liberated.

sanskrit_iast:
nibandhinī rajjureṣā yā grāme vasato ratiḥ /
chitvaināṃ sukṛto yānti naināṃ chindanti duṣkṛtaḥ //
meaning:
निबन्धिनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः /
छित्वैनां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः //
text_mt: This attachment to living in a village is a binding rope; / cutting it, the virtuous depart, but the evil-doers do not cut it.

sanskrit_iast:
tulyajātivayorūpān hṛtānpasyasi mṛtyunā /
na ca nāmāsti nirvedo lohaṃ hi hṛdayaṃ tava //
meaning:
तुल्यजातिवयोरूपान् हृतान्पस्यसि मृत्युना /
न च नामास्ति निर्वेदो लोहं हि हृदयं तव //
text_mt: You see those of equal caste, age, and appearance snatched away by death, / and yet there is no disgust in you; your heart is surely made of iron!

sanskrit_iast:
rūpakūlāṃ manaḥ srotāṃ sparśadvīpāṃ rasāvahām /
gandhapaṅkāṃ śabdajalāṃ svargamārgadurāruhām //
meaning:
रूपकूलां मनः स्रोतां स्पर्शद्वीपां रसावहाम् /
गन्धपङ्कां शब्दजलां स्वर्गमार्गदुरारुहाम् //
text_mt: With forms as its banks, the mind as its current, touch as its islands, taste as its flow, / smell as its mud, sound as its water, difficult to ascend on the path to heaven,

sanskrit_iast:
kṣamāritrāṃ satyamayīṃ dharmasthairyakarākarām /
tyāgavātādhvagāṃ śīghrāṃ buddhināvaṃ nadīṃ taret //
meaning:
क्षमारित्रां सत्यमयीं धर्मस्थैर्यकराकराम् /
त्यागवाताध्वगां शीघ्रां बुद्धिनावं नदीं तरेत् //
text_mt: one should cross the river with the swift boat of intellect, having forbearance as its rudder, consisting of truth, made of the steady mines of righteousness, and driven by the wind of renunciation.

sanskrit_iast:
tyaktvā dharmamadharmaṃ ca hyubhe satyānṛte tyaja /
tyaja dharmamasaṃkalpādadharmaṃ cāpyahiṃsayā //
meaning:
त्यक्त्वा धर्ममधर्मं च ह्युभे सत्यानृते त्यज /
त्यज धर्ममसंकल्पादधर्मं चाप्यहिंसया //
text_mt: Abandoning both righteousness and unrighteousness, renounce both truth and falsehood; / abandon righteousness through non-intention, and unrighteousness through non-injury;

sanskrit_iast:
ubhe satyānṛte buddhiṃ paramaniścayāt /
asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam //
meaning:
उभे सत्यानृते बुद्धिं परमनिश्चयात् /
अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम् //
text_mt: [abandon] both truth and falsehood by intellect, through supreme ascertainment. / Having bones for pillars, bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood,

sanskrit_iast:
dharmāvanaddhaṃ durgandhiṃ pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ /
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamasthiram //
meaning:
धर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धिं पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः /
जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमस्थिरम् //
text_mt: covered with skin, foul-smelling, filled with urine and feces, / overcome by old age and grief, an abode of disease, unstable,

sanskrit_iast:
rajasvalamanityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsaṃ samutsṛja /
idaṃ viśvaṃ jagatsarvamajagañcāpi yadbhavet //
meaning:
रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासं समुत्सृज /
इदं विश्वं जगत्सर्वमजगञ्चापि यद्भवेत् //
text_mt: subject to defilement and transient, cast off this dwelling of the elements! / This entire universe, both moving and unmoving, that exists,

sanskrit_iast:
mahābhūtātmakaṃ sarvamasmādyatparamāṇumat /
indriyāṇi ca pañcaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā //
meaning:
महाभूतात्मकं सर्वमस्माद्यत्परमाणुमत् /
इन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा //
text_mt: all consists of the great elements, and what is subtler than this; / the five sense-organs, and tamas, sattva, and rajas,

sanskrit_iast:
ityeṣa saptadaśako rāśikhyaktasaṃjñakaḥ /
sarvairihendriyārthaiśca vyaktāvyaktairhi hitam //
meaning:
इत्येष सप्तदशको राशिख्यक्तसंज्ञकः /
सर्वैरिहेन्द्रियार्थैश्च व्यक्ताव्यक्तैर्हि हितम् //
text_mt: thus this group of seventeen is known as the manifest; / along with all sense-objects here, manifest and unmanifest, it is established.

sanskrit_iast:
pañcaviṃśaka ityeṣa vyaktāvyaktamayo gaṇaḥ /
etaiḥ sarvaiḥ samāyuktamanityamabhidhīyate //
meaning:
पञ्चविंशक इत्येष व्यक्ताव्यक्तमयो गणः /
एतैः सर्वैः समायुक्तमनित्यमभिधीयते //
text_mt: This group of twenty-five consists of the manifest and unmanifest; / combined with all these, it is declared to be impermanent.

sanskrit_iast:
trivargo 'tra sukhaṃ duḥkha jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ tathā /
ya idaṃ veda tattvena sasa veda prabhavāpyayau //
meaning:
त्रिवर्गो ऽत्र सुखं दुःख जीवितं मरणं तथा /
य इदं वेद तत्त्वेन सस वेद प्रभवाप्ययौ //
text_mt: Herein lie the three aims of life, pleasure, pain, life, and death. / He who knows this in truth, knows the origin and dissolution [of all].’

sanskrit_iast:
indriyairgṛhyate yadyattadvyaktamabhidhīyate /
avyaktamatha tajjñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyamatīndriyam //
meaning:
इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद्यत्तद्व्यक्तमभिधीयते /
अव्यक्तमथ तज्ज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् //
text_mt: Whatever is grasped by the senses is called the manifest; / but that which is to be grasped by inference, beyond the senses, should be known as the unmanifest.

sanskrit_iast:
indriyairniyatairdehī dhārābhiriva tarpyate /
loke vihitamātmānaṃ lokaṃ cātmani paśyati //
meaning:
इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्देही धाराभिरिव तर्प्यते /
लोके विहितमात्मानं लोकं चात्मनि पश्यति //
text_mt: When the senses are restrained, the embodied soul is satisfied as if by streams [of rain]; / he sees himself established in the world and the world in himself.

sanskrit_iast:
parāvaradṛśaḥ śaktirjñānavelāṃ na paśyati /
paśyataḥ sarvabhūtāni sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā //
meaning:
परावरदृशः शक्तिर्ज्ञानवेलां न पश्यति /
पश्यतः सर्वभूतानि सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा //
text_mt: The power of one who sees the higher and the lower sees no boundary to knowledge, / as he sees all beings in all states at all times.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmabhūtasya saṃyogo nāśubhenopapadyate /
jñānena vividhātkleśānna nivṛttiśca dehajāt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मभूतस्य संयोगो नाशुभेनोपपद्यते /
ज्ञानेन विविधात्क्लेशान्न निवृत्तिश्च देहजात् //
text_mt: For one who has become Brahman, association with what is inauspicious does not occur; / nor through knowledge is there failure of cessation from the manifold afflictions born of the body.

sanskrit_iast:
lokabuddhiprakāśena lokamārgo na riṣyati /
anādinidhanaṃ jantumātmani sthitamavyayam //
meaning:
लोकबुद्धिप्रकाशेन लोकमार्गो न रिष्यति /
अनादिनिधनं जन्तुमात्मनि स्थितमव्ययम् //
text_mt: By the light of worldly understanding, the course of the world is not impaired; / the living being, without beginning or end, stands undecaying within the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
akartāramamūḍhaṃ ca bhagavānāha tīrtavit /
yo jantuḥ svakṛtaistaistaiḥ karmabhirnityaduḥkhitaḥ //
meaning:
अकर्तारममूढं च भगवानाह तीर्तवित् /
यो जन्तुः स्वकृतैस्तैस्तैः कर्मभिर्नित्यदुःखितः //
text_mt: A non-agent and undeluded, the Lord, knower of the sacred fords, has said. / Whichever creature is perpetually tormented by its various deeds performed by itself,

sanskrit_iast:
svaduḥkhapratighātārthaṃ hṝnti janturanekadhā /
tataḥ karma samādatte punaranyannavaṃ bahu //
meaning:
स्वदुःखप्रतिघातार्थं हॄन्ति जन्तुरनेकधा /
ततः कर्म समादत्ते पुनरन्यन्नवं बहु //
text_mt: To counteract its own sorrow, that creature struggles in various ways; / then it undertakes again another vast, new karma.

sanskrit_iast:
tapyate 'tha punastena bhuktvāpathyamivāturaḥ /
ajasrameva mohānto duḥkheṣu sukhasaṃjñitaḥ //
meaning:
तप्यते ऽथ पुनस्तेन भुक्त्वापथ्यमिवातुरः /
अजस्रमेव मोहान्तो दुःखेषु सुखसंज्ञितः //
text_mt: Tormented then again by that, like a sick person who has eaten unwholesome food, / perpetually blinded by delusion, having notions of happiness amidst sorrows,

sanskrit_iast:
vadhyate tapyate caiva bhayavatyarmabhiḥ sadā /
tato nivṛtto bandhātsvātkarmaṇāmudayādiha //
meaning:
वध्यते तप्यते चैव भयवत्यर्मभिः सदा /
ततो निवृत्तो बन्धात्स्वात्कर्मणामुदयादिह //
text_mt: One is slain and tormented always by fearful actions; / having ceased from that, one is freed here from the bondage of one's own actions through their fruition.

sanskrit_iast:
paribhramati saṃsāre cakravadbāhuvarjitaḥ /
saṃyamena ca saṃbandhānnivṛttyā tapaso balāt //
meaning:
परिभ्रमति संसारे चक्रवद्बाहुवर्जितः /
संयमेन च संबन्धान्निवृत्त्या तपसो बलात् //
text_mt: It wanders in saṃsāra like a wheel, deprived of arms. / But through self-restraint and detachment from attachments, by the power of asceticism,

sanskrit_iast:
samprāptā bahavaḥ siddhiṃ avyābādhāṃ sukhodayām //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bṛhadupākhyāne ṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
सम्प्राप्ता बहवः सिद्धिं अव्याबाधां सुखोदयाम् //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे बृहदुपाख्याने षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Many have attained perfection, unhindered and yielding happiness.

Thus ends the sixtieth chapter in the Great Narrative, in the second quarter of the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca
aśokaṃ śokanāśārthaṃ śāstraṃ śāntikaraṃ śivam /
niśamya labhyate buddhirlabdhāyāṃ sukhamedhate //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अशोकं शोकनाशार्थं शास्त्रं शान्तिकरं शिवम् /
निशम्य लभ्यते बुद्धिर्लब्धायां सुखमेधते //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / Hearing the griefless, auspicious scripture that destroys sorrow and brings peace, / understanding is obtained; when it is obtained, happiness flourishes.

sanskrit_iast:
harṣasthānasahasrāṇi śokasthānaśatāni ca /
divase divase mūḍhamāviśanti na paṇḍitam //
meaning:
हर्षस्थानसहस्राणि शोकस्थानशतानि च /
दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम् //
text_mt: Thousands of occasions for joy and hundreds of occasions for sorrow / enter day after day into the fool, but not into the wise man.

sanskrit_iast:
aniṣṭasaṃpraṃyogāśca viprayogātpriyasya ca /
manuṣyā mānasairduḥkhairyujyante ye 'lpabuddhayaḥ //
meaning:
अनिष्टसंप्रंयोगाश्च विप्रयोगात्प्रियस्य च /
मनुष्या मानसैर्दुःखैर्युज्यन्ते ये ऽल्पबुद्धयः //
text_mt: From association with what is unpleasant and separation from what is dear, / men of small intellect are joined to mental griefs.

sanskrit_iast:
dravyeṣu samatīteṣu ye guṇāstenna cindayet /
tānanādriyamāṇaśca snehabandhādvimucyate //
meaning:
द्रव्येषु समतीतेषु ये गुणास्तेन्न चिन्दयेत् /
ताननाद्रियमाणश्च स्नेहबन्धाद्विमुच्यते //
text_mt: When possessions are gone, one should not contemplate the qualities they had; / and by disregarding them, one is freed from the bond of affection.

sanskrit_iast:
doṣadarśī bhavettatra yatra rāgaḥ pravarttate /
aniṣṭabuddhitāṃ yacchettataḥ kṣipraṃ virājate //
meaning:
दोषदर्शी भवेत्तत्र यत्र रागः प्रवर्त्तते /
अनिष्टबुद्धितां यच्छेत्ततः क्षिप्रं विराजते //
text_mt: One should see faults where attachment arises; / one should view it as undesirable, and then quickly shines forth.

sanskrit_iast:
nārtho na dharmo na yaśo yo 'tītamanuśocati /
asyābhāvena yujyetaṃ tañcāsya tu nivartate //
meaning:
नार्थो न धर्मो न यशो यो ऽतीतमनुशोचति /
अस्याभावेन युज्येतं तञ्चास्य तु निवर्तते //
text_mt: Neither wealth, nor dharma, nor fame comes to him who grieves over the past; / he would be afflicted by its absence, yet it does not return to him.

sanskrit_iast:
guṇairbhūtāni yujyante tathaiva ca na yujyate /
sarvāṇi naitadekasya śokasthānaṃ hi vidyate //
meaning:
गुणैर्भूतानि युज्यन्ते तथैव च न युज्यते /
सर्वाणि नैतदेकस्य शोकस्थानं हि विद्यते //
text_mt: Beings are joined with qualities, and likewise they are not joined; / this entire state is not an occasion of grief for a single person alone.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtaṃ vā yadi vā naṣṭaṃ yo 'tītamanuśocati /
duḥkhena labhate duḥkhaṃ mahānarthe prapadyate //
meaning:
मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं यो ऽतीतमनुशोचति /
दुःखेन लभते दुःखं महानर्थे प्रपद्यते //
text_mt: Whoever grieves over the past, whether dead or lost, / gains sorrow from sorrow, and falls into a great calamity.

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhopaghāte śārīre mānase cāpyupasthite /
yasminna śakyate kartuṃ yatnastannānurcitayet //
meaning:
दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे चाप्युपस्थिते /
यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुर्चितयेत् //
text_mt: When physical pain or mental affliction is present, / in whatever matter effort cannot be made, one should not brood upon it.

sanskrit_iast:
bhaiṣajyametaddaḥkhasya yadetannānucintayet /
cintyamānaṃ hi na vyeti bhūyaścābhipravarddhate //
meaning:
भैषज्यमेतद्दःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् /
चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चाभिप्रवर्द्धते //
text_mt: This is the medicine for sorrow: that one should not dwell upon it; / for when dwelled upon, it does not depart, but grows even more.

sanskrit_iast:
prajñayā mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ hanyācchārīramauṣadhaiḥ /
etadvijñāya sāmarthyaṃ na vānyaiḥ samatāmiyāt //
meaning:
प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः /
एतद्विज्ञाय सामर्थ्यं न वान्यैः समतामियात् //
text_mt: One should slay mental sorrow with wisdom, and physical [pain] with medicines; / knowing this capacity, one would not attain equality with others.

sanskrit_iast:
anityaṃ jīvitaṃ rūpaṃ yauvanaṃ dravyasañcayaḥ /
ārogyaṃ priyasaṃvāsaṃ na mṛdhyetpaṇḍitaḥ kvacit //
meaning:
अनित्यं जीवितं रूपं यौवनं द्रव्यसञ्चयः /
आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासं न मृध्येत्पण्डितः क्वचित् //
text_mt: Life, beauty, youth, accumulation of wealth, / health, and living with loved ones are impermanent; a wise man should never take pleasure in them.

sanskrit_iast:
nājñānaprabhavaṃ duḥkhamekaṃ śocitumarhati /
aśocanpratikurvīta yadi paśyedupakramam //
meaning:
नाज्ञानप्रभवं दुःखमेकं शोचितुमर्हति /
अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम् //
text_mt: One ought not to grieve over a single sorrow born of ignorance; / without grieving, one should counter it if one perceives a remedy.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhātpriyataraṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvite nātra saṃśayaḥ /
jarāmaraṇaduḥkhebhyaḥ priyamātmānamuddharet //
meaning:
सुखात्प्रियतरं दुःखं जीविते नात्र संशयः /
जरामरणदुःखेभ्यः प्रियमात्मानमुद्धरेत् //
text_mt: In life, sorrow is dearer than happiness, without doubt here; / from the sorrows of old age and death, one should deliver one's dear self.

sanskrit_iast:
bhajanti hi śārīrāṇi rogāḥ śarīramānasāḥ /
sāyakā iva tīkṣṇāgrāḥ prayuktā dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ //
meaning:
भजन्ति हि शारीराणि रोगाः शरीरमानसाः /
सायका इव तीक्ष्णाग्राः प्रयुक्ता दृढधन्विभिः //
text_mt: For bodily and mental illnesses afflict physical beings, / like sharp-pointed arrows shot by sturdy archers.

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhitasya cikitsābhistrasyato jīvitaiṣiṇaḥ /
āmayasya vināśāya śarīramanukṛṣyate //
meaning:
व्याधितस्य चिकित्साभिस्त्रस्यतो जीवितैषिणः /
आमयस्य विनाशाय शरीरमनुकृष्यते //
text_mt: Through medical treatments for the diseased person who trembles and longs for life, / the body is dragged down in order to destroy the sickness.

sanskrit_iast:
sraṃsaṃti na nivartante srotāṃsi saritāmiva /
āyurādāya martyānāṃ rātryahāni punaḥpunaḥ //
meaning:
स्रंसंति न निवर्तन्ते स्रोतांसि सरितामिव /
आयुरादाय मर्त्यानां रात्र्यहानि पुनःपुनः //
text_mt: Nights and days fall away and do not turn back, like the currents of rivers, / taking away the lifespan of mortals again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
apayantyayamatyantaṃ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ /
jātaṃ martyaṃ jarayati nimiṣaṃ nāvatiṣṭate //
meaning:
अपयन्त्ययमत्यन्तं पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः /
जातं मर्त्यं जरयति निमिषं नावतिष्टते //
text_mt: This departure of the bright and dark fortnights is absolute; / it ages the born mortal, pausing not even for a twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaduḥkhābhibhūtānāmajaro jarayatyasūn /
ādityo hyastamabhyeti punaḥ punarudeti ca //
meaning:
सुखदुःखाभिभूतानामजरो जरयत्यसून् /
आदित्यो ह्यस्तमभ्येति पुनः पुनरुदेति च //
text_mt: The ageless [sun] wears away the lives of those overcome by happiness and sorrow; / for the sun sets, and rises again and again.

sanskrit_iast:
adṛṣṭapūrvānādāya bhāvānapariśaṅkitān /
iṣṭāniṣṭā manuṣyāṇāṃ mataṃ gacchanti rātrayaḥ //
meaning:
अदृष्टपूर्वानादाय भावानपरिशङ्कितान् /
इष्टानिष्टा मनुष्याणां मतं गच्छन्ति रात्रयः //
text_mt: Bringing about states never seen before and unforeseen, / pleasant and unpleasant, the nights pass according to men's destiny.

sanskrit_iast:
yo yadicchedyathākāmaṃ kāmānāṃ tattadāpnuyāt /
yadi syānna parādhīnaṃ puruṣasya kriyāphalam //
meaning:
यो यदिच्छेद्यथाकामं कामानां तत्तदाप्नुयात् /
यदि स्यान्न पराधीनं पुरुषस्य क्रियाफलम् //
text_mt: Whatever desires one wished at will, those very desires one would attain, / if the fruit of an action of a person were not dependent on another.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃyatāścaiva takṣāśca matimantaśca mānavāḥ /
dṛśyante niṣphalāḥ saṃtaḥ prahīnāśca svakarmabhiḥ //
meaning:
संयताश्चैव तक्षाश्च मतिमन्तश्च मानवाः /
दृश्यन्ते निष्फलाः संतः प्रहीनाश्च स्वकर्मभिः //
text_mt: Restrained, skillful, and intelligent men / are seen to be destitute of results, ruined by their own deeds.

sanskrit_iast:
apare niṣphalāḥ santo nirguṇāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ /
āśābhiraṇyasaṃyuktā dṛśyante sarvakāminaḥ //
meaning:
अपरे निष्फलाः सन्तो निर्गुणाः पुरुषाधमाः /
आशाभिरण्यसंयुक्ता दृश्यन्ते सर्वकामिनः //
text_mt: Others, destitute of good deeds, devoid of virtue, the lowest of men, / are seen possessing hopes and gold, fulfilling every desire.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtānāmaparaḥ kaściddhiṃsāyāṃ satatotthitaḥ /
vañcanāyāṃ ca lokeṣu sasukheṣveva jīyate //
meaning:
भूतानामपरः कश्चिद्धिंसायां सततोत्थितः /
वञ्चनायां च लोकेषु ससुखेष्वेव जीयते //
text_mt: Another person is constantly intent upon harm to living beings / and upon deceit in the world, yet lives in mere pleasure.

sanskrit_iast:
aceṣṭamānamāsīnaṃ śrīḥ kañcidupatiṣṭati /
kaścitkarmāṇi kurute na prāpyamadhigacchati //
meaning:
अचेष्टमानमासीनं श्रीः कञ्चिदुपतिष्टति /
कश्चित्कर्माणि कुरुते न प्राप्यमधिगच्छति //
text_mt: Prosperity attends someone who sits inactive; / another performs actions and does not attain what is to be reached.

sanskrit_iast:
aparādhānsamācṣṭuṃ puruṣasya svabhāvataḥ /
śukramanyatra saṃbhūtaṃ punaranyatra gacchati //
meaning:
अपराधान्समाच्ष्टुं पुरुषस्य स्वभावतः /
शुक्रमन्यत्र संभूतं पुनरन्यत्र गच्छति //
text_mt: To announce the offences of a man by nature, / semen produced in one place goes again to another.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya yonau prasaktasya garbho bhavati mānavaḥ /
āmrapuṣpopamā yasya nivṛttirupalabhyate //
meaning:
तस्य योनौ प्रसक्तस्य गर्भो भवति मानवः /
आम्रपुष्पोपमा यस्य निवृत्तिरुपलभ्यते //
text_mt: From its attachment in the womb, an embryo becomes a human being, / whose cessation is seen to be like a mango flower.

sanskrit_iast:
keṣāñcitputrakāmānāmanusantānamicchatām /
siddhau prayatamānānāṃ naivāṇḍamupajāyate //
meaning:
केषाञ्चित्पुत्रकामानामनुसन्तानमिच्छताम् /
सिद्धौ प्रयतमानानां नैवाण्डमुपजायते //
text_mt: For some who desire sons and long for a lineage, / though striving for success, not even an embryo is born.

sanskrit_iast:
garbhādudvijamānānāṃ kruddhādaśīviṣādiva /
āyuṣmān jāyate putraḥ kathaṃ pretaḥ piteva saḥ //
meaning:
गर्भादुद्विजमानानां क्रुद्धादशीविषादिव /
आयुष्मान् जायते पुत्रः कथं प्रेतः पितेव सः //
text_mt: For those who shrink from the womb as from an angry venomous snake, / a long-lived son is born, while the father is like one departed.

sanskrit_iast:
devāniṣṭvā tapastaptvā kṛpaṇaiḥ putrahetubhiḥ /
daśamāsānparidhṛtā jāyate kulapāṃsanāḥ //
meaning:
देवानिष्ट्वा तपस्तप्त्वा कृपणैः पुत्रहेतुभिः /
दशमासान्परिधृता जायते कुलपांसनाः //
text_mt: Having sacrificed to the gods and performed austerities for the sake of sons, by wretched people, / those borne for ten months are born as disgrace to the family.

sanskrit_iast:
apare dhanadhānyāni bhogāṃśca pitṛsaṃcitān /
vimalānabhijāyante labdhvā taireva maṅgalaiḥ //
meaning:
अपरे धनधान्यानि भोगांश्च पितृसंचितान् /
विमलानभिजायन्ते लब्ध्वा तैरेव मङ्गलैः //
text_mt: Others are born having obtained immaculate wealth, grains, / and pleasures accumulated by their fathers through those very auspicious merits.

sanskrit_iast:
anyonya samabhipretya maithunasya samāgame /
upadravaivādṛṣṭo yonau garbhaḥ prapadyate //
meaning:
अन्योन्य समभिप्रेत्य मैथुनस्य समागमे /
उपद्रवैवादृष्टो योनौ गर्भः प्रपद्यते //
text_mt: Mutually desiring one another in the union of sexual intercourse, / an unseen calamity, as it were, enters the womb as an embryo.

sanskrit_iast:
snigdhatvādindriyārtheṣu mohānmaraṇamapriyam /
parityajati yo duḥkhaṃ sukhamapyubhayaṃ naraḥ //
meaning:
स्निग्धत्वादिन्द्रियार्थेषु मोहान्मरणमप्रियम् /
परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखमप्युभयं नरः //
text_mt: Because of attachment to sense objects, death is unwelcome due to delusion; / the man who abandons both sorrow and happiness,

sanskrit_iast:
atyeti brahma so 'tyantaṃ sukhamapyaśnute param /
duḥkhamarthā hi tyajyante pālane ca na te sukhāḥ //
meaning:
अत्येति ब्रह्म सो ऽत्यन्तं सुखमप्यश्नुते परम् /
दुःखमर्था हि त्यज्यन्ते पालने च न ते सुखाः //
text_mt: He completely transcends to Brahman, and enjoys supreme bliss; / for worldly goods are abandoned with sorrow, and they are not pleasant in guarding them.

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvaiva nādhigamanaṃ nāśameṣāṃ na cintayet /
anyāmanyāṃ dhanāvasthāṃ prāpya vaiśeṣikā narāḥ //
meaning:
श्रुत्वैव नाधिगमनं नाशमेषां न चिन्तयेत् /
अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिका नराः //
text_mt: Merely upon hearing it, one should not think of non-attainment nor of their destruction; / men having distinctions, upon attaining various states of wealth,

sanskrit_iast:
atṛptā yānti vidhvaṃsaṃ santoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ /
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ //
meaning:
अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं सन्तोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः /
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः //
text_mt: being unsatisfied, go to destruction, while the wise find contentment. / All accumulations end in depletion; all elevations end in a fall.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam /
anto nāsti pipāsāyāstuṣṭistu paramaṃ sukham //
meaning:
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम् /
अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् //
text_mt: Unions end in separation, and life indeed ends in death; / there is no end to thirst, but contentment is supreme happiness.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsaṃtoṣameveha dhanaṃ śaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ /
nimeṣamātramapi hi yo 'dhigacchanna tiṣṭati //
meaning:
तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं शंसन्ति पण्डिताः /
निमेषमात्रमपि हि यो ऽधिगच्छन्न तिष्टति //
text_mt: Therefore, the wise praise contentment alone as wealth in this world. / For he who, attaining [objects], does not remain stable even for the twinkling of an eye,

sanskrit_iast:
saśarīreṣvanityeṣu nityaṃ kimanucintayet /
bhūteṣu bhāvaṃ saṃcintya ye buddhyā tamasaḥ param //
meaning:
सशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत् /
भूतेषु भावं संचिन्त्य ये बुद्ध्या तमसः परम् //
text_mt: what eternal thing could he contemplate in non-eternal bodies? / Having contemplated the true state among beings, those who through intellect [see] beyond darkness,

sanskrit_iast:
na śocanti gatādhvānaḥ paśyanti paramāṃ gatim /
saṃcinvannekamevainaṃ kāmānāvitṛptakam //
meaning:
न शोचन्ति गताध्वानः पश्यन्ति परमां गतिम् /
संचिन्वन्नेकमेवैनं कामानावितृप्तकम् //
text_mt: having reached the end of the road, do not grieve; they see the supreme goal. / Accumulating only this one thing, an insatiable consumer of desires,

sanskrit_iast:
vyāghra paśumivāsādya mṛtyurādāya gacchati /
athāpyupāyaṃ saṃpaśyedduḥkhasyāsya vimokṣaṇe //
meaning:
व्याघ्र पशुमिवासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति /
अथाप्युपायं संपश्येद्दुःखस्यास्य विमोक्षणे //
text_mt: Death, having approached like a tiger toward a beast, takes him and departs. / Yet one should perceive the means for deliverance from this sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
aśocannārabhennaiva yuktaścāvyasanī bhavet /
śabde sparśe rase rūpe gandhe ca paramaṃ tathā //
meaning:
अशोचन्नारभेन्नैव युक्तश्चाव्यसनी भवेत् /
शब्दे स्पर्शे रसे रूपे गन्धे च परमं तथा //
text_mt: not grieving, he should never undertake [fruitless acts]; disciplined, he should be free of addiction. / In sound, touch, taste, form, and smell—likewise in the highest—

sanskrit_iast:
nopabhogātparaṃ kiñciddhanino vādhanasya vā /
vāksaṃprayogādbhṛtānāṃ nāsti duḥkhamanāmayam //
meaning:
नोपभोगात्परं किञ्चिद्धनिनो वाधनस्य वा /
वाक्संप्रयोगाद्भृतानां नास्ति दुःखमनामयम् //
text_mt: there is nothing beyond enjoyment, whether for the wealthy or the poor. / For those sustained by the exercise of speech, there is no pain without disease.

sanskrit_iast:
viprayogaśca sarvasya na vācā na ca vidyayā /
praṇayaṃ parisaṃhṛtya saṃstuteṣvitareṣu ca //
meaning:
विप्रयोगश्च सर्वस्य न वाचा न च विद्यया /
प्रणयं परिसंहृत्य संस्तुतेष्वितरेषु च //
text_mt: And separation belongs to everything, not prevented by speech nor by learning. / Withdrawing affection both toward those who are praised and toward others,

sanskrit_iast:
vicaredasamunnaddhaḥ sa sukhī sa ca paṇḍitaḥ /
adhyātmagatamālīno nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ //
meaning:
विचरेदसमुन्नद्धः स सुखी स च पण्डितः /
अध्यात्मगतमालीनो निरपेक्षो निरामिषः //
text_mt: one who walks about without haughtiness is happy, and he is wise. / Resting in what pertains to the self, impartial, free of greed,

sanskrit_iast:
ātmanaiva sahāyena caścaretsa sukhī bhavet /
sukhaduḥkhaviparyāso yadā samupapadyate //
meaning:
आत्मनैव सहायेन चश्चरेत्स सुखी भवेत् /
सुखदुःखविपर्यासो यदा समुपपद्यते //
text_mt: he who walks with the Self alone as his companion becomes happy. / When the reversal of pleasure and pain occurs,

sanskrit_iast:
nainaṃ prajñā suniyataṃ trāyate nāpi pauruṣam /
svabhāvādyatnamātiṣṭhedyatnavānnāvasīdati //
meaning:
नैनं प्रज्ञा सुनियतं त्रायते नापि पौरुषम् /
स्वभावाद्यत्नमातिष्ठेद्यत्नवान्नावसीदति //
text_mt: neither well-disciplined wisdom nor human effort protects him. / By nature one should undertake exertion; one endowed with effort does not sink down.

sanskrit_iast:
upadrava ivāniṣṭo yoniṃ garbhaḥ prapadyate /
tāni pūrvaśarīrāṇi nityamekaṃ śarīriṇam //
meaning:
उपद्रव इवानिष्टो योनिं गर्भः प्रपद्यते /
तानि पूर्वशरीराणि नित्यमेकं शरीरिणम् //
text_mt: Like an unwanted calamity, the embryo enters the womb. / Those previous bodies [belong] always to a single embodied being.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇināṃ prāṇasaṃrodhe māṃsaśleṣmaviceṣṭitam /
nirdagdhaṃ paradehena paradeṃhaṃ balābalam //
meaning:
प्राणिनां प्राणसंरोधे मांसश्लेष्मविचेष्टितम् /
निर्दग्धं परदेहेन परदेंहं बलाबलम् //
text_mt: When the breath of living beings is obstructed, agitated by flesh and phlegm, / burned up by another body, another body is strong or weak;

sanskrit_iast:
vinaśyati vināśānte nāvi nāvamivācalām /
saṃgatyā jaṭhare nyastaṃ retobindumacetanam //
meaning:
विनश्यति विनाशान्ते नावि नावमिवाचलाम् /
संगत्या जठरे न्यस्तं रेतोबिन्दुमचेतनम् //
text_mt: it perishes at the end of destruction, like an unsteady boat upon a boat. / Deposited in the womb by intercourse, an unconscious drop of semen—

sanskrit_iast:
kena yatnena jīvantaṃ garbhaṃ tvamiha paśyasi /
annapānāni jīryante yatra bhakṣyāśca bhakṣitāḥ //
meaning:
केन यत्नेन जीवन्तं गर्भं त्वमिह पश्यसि /
अन्नपानानि जीर्यन्ते यत्र भक्ष्याश्च भक्षिताः //
text_mt: by what effort do you see the embryo living here? / Where food and drink, and whatever foods are eaten, are digested,

sanskrit_iast:
tasminnevodare garbhaḥ kiṃ nānnamiva jīryati /
garbhe mūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ svabhāvaniyatā gatiḥ //
meaning:
तस्मिन्नेवोदरे गर्भः किं नान्नमिव जीर्यति /
गर्भे मूत्रपुरीषाणां स्वभावनियता गतिः //
text_mt: in that very belly, why does the embryo not digest like food? / In the womb, the course of urine and feces is determined by nature;

sanskrit_iast:
dhāraṇe vā visarge ca na kartuṃ vidyate 'vaśaḥ /
prabhavantyudare garbhā jāyamānāstathāpare //
meaning:
धारणे वा विसर्गे च न कर्तुं विद्यते ऽवशः /
प्रभवन्त्युदरे गर्भा जायमानास्तथापरे //
text_mt: helpless, one has no power to retain or discharge them. / Embryos develop in the belly, and others are born;

sanskrit_iast:
āgamena mahānyeṣāṃ vināśa upapadyate /
etasmādyonisaṃbandhādyo jīvanparimucyate //
meaning:
आगमेन महान्येषां विनाश उपपद्यते /
एतस्माद्योनिसंबन्धाद्यो जीवन्परिमुच्यते //
text_mt: with their arrival, great destruction falls upon others. / He who, while living, is freed from this connection with the womb,

sanskrit_iast:
pūjāṃ na labhate kāñcitpunarddhandveṣu majjati /
garbhasya saha jātasya saptamīmīdṛśīṃ daśām //
meaning:
पूजां न लभते काञ्चित्पुनर्द्धन्द्वेषु मज्जति /
गर्भस्य सह जातस्य सप्तमीमीदृशीं दशाम् //
text_mt: receives no honor [here], and sinks back into the pairs of opposites. / Of the embryo born along with it, [the wise reach] such a seventh state;

sanskrit_iast:
prāpnuvanti tataḥ pañca na bhavanti śatāyuṣaḥ /
nābhyutthāne manuṣyāṇāṃ yogāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ //
meaning:
प्राप्नुवन्ति ततः पञ्च न भवन्ति शतायुषः /
नाभ्युत्थाने मनुष्याणां योगाः स्युर्नात्र संशयः //
text_mt: then the five reach [death], not living to a hundred years. / In human enterprise there would be successes, no doubt about it;

sanskrit_iast:
vyādhibhiśca vivadhyante vyāghraiḥ kṣudramṛgā iva /
vyādhibhirbhakṣyamāṇānāṃ tyajatāṃ vipulandhanam //
meaning:
व्याधिभिश्च विवध्यन्ते व्याघ्रैः क्षुद्रमृगा इव /
व्याधिभिर्भक्ष्यमाणानां त्यजतां विपुलन्धनम् //
text_mt: yet they are struck down by diseases, like small deer by tigers. / For those being devoured by diseases, even as they spend abundant wealth,

sanskrit_iast: vedanā nāpakarṣanti yatamānāścikitsakāḥ //
meaning: वेदना नापकर्षन्ति यतमानाश्चिकित्सकाः //
text_mt: physicians, though striving, do not take away the pain.

sanskrit_iast:
te cāpi vividhā vaidyāḥ kuśalā saṃmatauṣadhāḥ /
vyādhibhiḥ parikṛṣyante mṛgā jyāghrairivārditāḥ //
meaning:
ते चापि विविधा वैद्याः कुशला संमतौषधाः /
व्याधिभिः परिकृष्यन्ते मृगा ज्याघ्रैरिवार्दिताः //
text_mt: And even those various skillful physicians, experienced in medicines, / are dragged down by diseases, like deer tormented by tigers.

sanskrit_iast:
te pibanti kaṣāyāṃśca sarpīṣi vividhāni ca /
dṛśyante jarayā bhagnā nāgairnāgā ivottamāḥ //
meaning:
ते पिबन्ति कषायांश्च सर्पीषि विविधानि च /
दृश्यन्ते जरया भग्ना नागैर्नागा इवोत्तमाः //
text_mt: They drink decoctions and various kinds of clarified butter, / yet they are seen broken by old age, like excellent elephants by [other] elephants.

sanskrit_iast:
kairvā bhuvi cikitsyenta rogārttā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ /
śvāpadāśca daridrāśca prāyo nārtā bhavanti te //
meaning:
कैर्वा भुवि चिकित्स्येन्त रोगार्त्ता मृगपक्षिणः /
श्वापदाश्च दरिद्राश्च प्रायो नार्ता भवन्ति ते //
text_mt: Or by whom on earth are beasts and birds, afflicted with sickness, treated? / And beasts of prey and the destitute are generally not afflicted.

sanskrit_iast:
ghorānapi durādharṣānnṛpatīnugratejasa /
ākramya roga ādatte paśūnpaśupaco yathā //
meaning:
घोरानपि दुराधर्षान्नृपतीनुग्रतेजस /
आक्रम्य रोग आदत्ते पशून्पशुपचो यथा //
text_mt: Attacking even terrible, invincible kings of fierce splendor, / disease seizes them, as a butcher does beasts.

sanskrit_iast:
iti lokamanākrandaṃ mohaśokapariplutam /
srotasā mahasā kṣipraṃ hriyamāṇaṃ balīyasā //
meaning:
इति लोकमनाक्रन्दं मोहशोकपरिप्लुतम् /
स्रोतसा महसा क्षिप्रं ह्रियमाणं बलीयसा //
text_mt: Thus the world, destitute of refuge, overwhelmed by delusion and grief, / is quickly swept away by a great, mighty current.

sanskrit_iast:
na dhanena na rājyena nogreṇa tapasā tathā /
svabhāvā hyativartante ye nirmuktāḥ śarīriṣu //
meaning:
न धनेन न राज्येन नोग्रेण तपसा तथा /
स्वभावा ह्यतिवर्तन्ते ये निर्मुक्ताः शरीरिषु //
text_mt: Neither by wealth nor by kingdom, nor by fierce austerity, / do inborn natures surpass those [afflictions] that are released upon embodied beings.

sanskrit_iast:
uparyapari lokasya sarvo bhavitumicchati /
yatate ca yathāśakti na ca tadvartate tathā //
meaning:
उपर्यपरि लोकस्य सर्वो भवितुमिच्छति /
यतते च यथाशक्ति न च तद्वर्तते तथा //
text_mt: Everyone wishes to be higher and higher than the world, / and strives according to his power; yet it does not turn out so.

sanskrit_iast:
na mriyerannajīryeransarve syuḥ sārvakāmikāḥ /
nāpriyaṃ pratipadyerannutthānasya phalaṃ prati //
meaning:
न म्रियेरन्नजीर्येरन्सर्वे स्युः सार्वकामिकाः /
नाप्रियं प्रतिपद्येरन्नुत्थानस्य फलं प्रति //
text_mt: They would not die, they would not age, all would have all desires fulfilled, / and they would never encounter what is unpleasant as the fruit of their enterprise!

sanskrit_iast:
aiśvaryamadamattāśca mānānmayamadena ca /
apramattāḥ śaṭhāḥ krūrā vikrāntāḥ paryupāsate //
meaning:
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्ताश्च मानान्मयमदेन च /
अप्रमत्ताः शठाः क्रूरा विक्रान्ताः पर्युपासते //
text_mt: Drunk with the pride of sovereignty and with the pride of conceit, / the vigilant, the deceitful, the cruel, and the valiant wait upon [rulers].

sanskrit_iast:
śokāḥ pratinivartante keṣāñcidasamīkṣatām /
svaṃ svaṃ ca punaranyeṣāṃ na kañcidatigacchati //
meaning:
शोकाः प्रतिनिवर्तन्ते केषाञ्चिदसमीक्षताम् /
स्वं स्वं च पुनरन्येषां न कञ्चिदतिगच्छति //
text_mt: For some, griefs turn back without their having anticipated them; / and each [destiny] of others does not bypass anyone.

sanskrit_iast:
mahañca phalavaiṣamyaṃ dṛśyate karmasaṃdhiṣu /
vahṝnti śibikāmanye yāntyanye śibikāruhaḥ //
meaning:
महञ्च फलवैषम्यं दृश्यते कर्मसंधिषु /
वहॄन्ति शिबिकामन्ये यान्त्यन्ये शिबिकारुहः //
text_mt: A great disparity of fruits is seen in the junctures of actions: / some carry a palanquin, while others ride upon the palanquin.

sanskrit_iast:
sarveṣāmṛddhikāmānāmanye rathapuraḥ sarāḥ /
manujāśca gataśrīkāḥ śataśo vividhāḥ striyāḥ //
meaning:
सर्वेषामृद्धिकामानामन्ये रथपुरः सराः /
मनुजाश्च गतश्रीकाः शतशो विविधाः स्त्रियाः //
text_mt: While all desire prosperity, others run before chariots; / and there are men bereft of fortune, and hundreds of diverse women.

sanskrit_iast:
dvandvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu gacchantyekaikaśo narāḥ /
idamanyatparaṃ paśya nātra mohaṃ kariṣyasi //
meaning:
द्वन्द्वारामेषु भूतेषु गच्छन्त्येकैकशो नराः /
इदमन्यत्परं पश्य नात्र मोहं करिष्यसि //
text_mt: Among beings delighting in pairs of opposites, men depart one by one. / See this other, supreme truth; herein you will not fall into delusion:

sanskrit_iast:
dharmaṃ cāpi tyajā dharmaṃ tyaja satyānṛtāṃ dhiyam /
sarvaṃ tyaktvā svarūpasthaḥ sukhī bhava nirāmayaḥ //
meaning:
धर्मं चापि त्यजा धर्मं त्यज सत्यानृतां धियम् /
सर्वं त्यक्त्वा स्वरूपस्थः सुखी भव निरामयः //
text_mt: Renounce righteousness and unrighteousness; renounce the intellect bound to truth and falsehood; / having abandoned everything, established in your own nature, be happy and free from disease.

sanskrit_iast:
etatte paramaṃ guhyamākhyātamṛṣisattama /
yena devāḥ parityajya bhartyalokaṃ divaṃ gatāḥ //
meaning:
एतत्ते परमं गुह्यमाख्यातमृषिसत्तम /
येन देवाः परित्यज्य भर्त्यलोकं दिवं गताः //
text_mt: This supreme secret has been declared to you, O best of sages, / by which the gods, having abandoned the mortal world, went to heaven.

sanskrit_iast:
sanandana uvāca
ityuktvā vyāsatanayaṃ samāpṛcchya mahāmuniḥ /
sanatkumāraḥ prayayau pūjitastena sādaram //
meaning:
सनन्दन उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा व्यासतनयं समापृच्छ्य महामुनिः /
सनत्कुमारः प्रययौ पूजितस्तेन सादरम् //
text_mt: Sanandana said: / Having spoken thus to Vyāsa's son and taken his leave, the great sage / Sanatkumāra departed, respectfully honored by him.

sanskrit_iast:
śuko 'pi yogināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ samyagjñātvā hyavasthitam /
brahmaṇaḥ padamanveṣṭumutsukaḥ pitaraṃ yayau //
meaning:
शुको ऽपि योगिनां श्रेष्ठः सम्यग्ज्ञात्वा ह्यवस्थितम् /
ब्रह्मणः पदमन्वेष्टुमुत्सुकः पितरं ययौ //
text_mt: Śuka too, the best of yogins, having fully known what is established, / went to his father, eager to seek the state of Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pitrā samāgamya praṇamya ca mahāmuniḥ /
śukaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yayau kailāsaparvatam //
meaning:
ततः पित्रा समागम्य प्रणम्य च महामुनिः /
शुकः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ययौ कैलासपर्वतम् //
text_mt: Then, having met his father and bowed to him, the great sage / Śuka circumambulated him and went to Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāsastadvirahāddūnaḥ putrasnehasamāvṛtaḥ /
kṣaṇaikaṃ sthīyatāṃ putra iti ca krośa durmanāḥ //
meaning:
व्यासस्तद्विरहाद्दूनः पुत्रस्नेहसमावृतः /
क्षणैकं स्थीयतां पुत्र इति च क्रोश दुर्मनाः //
text_mt: Vyāsa, distressed by separation from him and overcome with affection for his son, / cried out, dejected in mind: "Stay for a single moment, my son!"

sanskrit_iast:
nirapekṣaḥ śuko bhūtvā niḥsneho muktabandhanaḥ /
mokṣamevānusaṃcitya gata eva paraṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde ekaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
निरपेक्षः शुको भूत्वा निःस्नेहो मुक्तबन्धनः /
मोक्षमेवानुसंचित्य गत एव परं पदम् //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे एकषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Becoming detached, free of affection, his bonds severed, / meditating only upon liberation, Śuka went indeed to the supreme abode.

Thus ends the sixty-first chapter in the Second Quarter of the Great Narrative in the First Part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
etacchrṛtvā tu vacanaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
punaḥ papraccha taṃ vipra śukābhipatanaṃ munim //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
एतच्छ्रृत्वा तु वचनं नारदो भगवानृषिः /
पुनः पप्रच्छ तं विप्र शुकाभिपतनं मुनिम् //
text_mt: Sūta said: / Hearing this speech, the lordly sage Nārada / questioned that muni once again, O brāhmaṇa, concerning Śuka's flight.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvamākhyātaṃ tvayātikaruṇātmanā /
yacchrṛtvā mānasaṃ me 'dya śāntimagryāmupāgatam //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वमाख्यातं त्वयातिकरुणात्मना /
यच्छ्रृत्वा मानसं मे ऽद्य शान्तिमग्र्यामुपागतम् //
text_mt: Nārada said: / O lord, everything has been related by you, whose nature is exceedingly compassionate; / hearing this today, my mind has attained supreme peace.

sanskrit_iast:
punaśca mokṣaśāstraṃ me tvamādiśa mahāmune /
nahi sampūrṇatāmeti tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇaguṇārṇave //
meaning:
पुनश्च मोक्षशास्त्रं मे त्वमादिश महामुने /
नहि सम्पूर्णतामेति तृष्णा कृष्णगुणार्णवे //
text_mt: Teach me once again, O great sage, the treatise on liberation; / thirst never reaches fulfillment in the ocean of Kṛṣṇa's virtues.

sanskrit_iast:
ye tu saṃsāranirmuktā mokṣa śāstraparāyaṇāḥ /
kutra te nivasaṃtīha saṃśayo me mahānayam //
meaning:
ये तु संसारनिर्मुक्ता मोक्ष शास्त्रपरायणाः /
कुत्र ते निवसंतीह संशयो मे महानयम् //
text_mt: Those who are released from saṃsāra and dedicated to the scripture of liberation, / where do they dwell here? This is my great doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ chindhi sumahābhāgatvatto nānyo vidāṃvaraḥ /
sanaṃ.u
dhārayāmāsa cātmānaṃ yathāśāstraṃ mahāmuniḥ //
meaning:
तं छिन्धि सुमहाभागत्वत्तो नान्यो विदांवरः /
सनं.उ
धारयामास चात्मानं यथाशास्त्रं महामुनिः //
text_mt: Cut through it, O highly fortunate one; none other is best among the knowers than you. / Sanatkumāra said: / The great sage held his self [in meditation] according to the sacred precepts,

sanskrit_iast:
pādātprabhṛti gātreṣu krameṇa kramayogavit /
tataḥ sa prāṅmukho vidvānādityena virocite //
meaning:
पादात्प्रभृति गात्रेषु क्रमेण क्रमयोगवित् /
ततः स प्राङ्मुखो विद्वानादित्येन विरोचिते //
text_mt: beginning from the feet through the limbs in succession, knowing the successive yoga. / Then, facing east, that wise one, in [the spot] illuminated by the sun,

sanskrit_iast:
pāṇipādaṃ samādhāya vinītavadupāviśat /
na tatra pakṣisaṃghāto na śabdo na ca darśanam //
meaning:
पाणिपादं समाधाय विनीतवदुपाविशत् /
न तत्र पक्षिसंघातो न शब्दो न च दर्शनम् //
text_mt: composed his hands and feet and sat down like one disciplined. / There was no flock of birds there, no sound, and no sight,

sanskrit_iast:
yatra vaiyāsakirddhāmni yoktuṃ samupacakrame /
sa dadarśa tadātmānaṃ sarvasaṃgaviniḥsṛtaḥ //
meaning:
यत्र वैयासकिर्द्धाम्नि योक्तुं समुपचक्रमे /
स ददर्श तदात्मानं सर्वसंगविनिःसृतः //
text_mt: where the son of Vyāsa in his radiant abode undertook to practice yoga. / Then, freed from all attachments, he beheld the Self.

sanskrit_iast:
prajahāsa tato hāsaṃ śukaḥ samprekṣya bhāskaram /
sa punaryogamāsthāya mokṣamārgopalabdhaye //
meaning:
प्रजहास ततो हासं शुकः सम्प्रेक्ष्य भास्करम् /
स पुनर्योगमास्थाय मोक्षमार्गोपलब्धये //
text_mt: Then Śuka laughed a laugh, gazing upon the sun; / once more having resorted to yoga for the attainment of the path of liberation,

sanskrit_iast:
mahāyogīśvaro bhūtvā so 'tyakrāmadvihāyasam /
antarīkṣacaraḥ śrīmānvyāsaputraḥ suniścitaḥ //
meaning:
महायोगीश्वरो भूत्वा सो ऽत्यक्रामद्विहायसम् /
अन्तरीक्षचरः श्रीमान्व्यासपुत्रः सुनिश्चितः //
text_mt: becoming a master of great yoga, he crossed beyond the sky. / Moving through the atmosphere, the glorious son of Vyāsa was firmly resolved.

sanskrit_iast:
tamundyantaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ vainateyasamadyutim /
dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni manomārutaraṃhasam //
meaning:
तमुन्द्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम् /
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि मनोमारुतरंहसम् //
text_mt: All beings beheld that best of the twice-born ascending, / having a splendor equal to the son of Vinatā, with the speed of mind and wind.

sanskrit_iast:
yathāśakti yathānyāyaṃ pūjayāñcakrire tathā /
puṣpa varṣaiśca divyaistamavacakrurdivaukasaḥ //
meaning:
यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे तथा /
पुष्प वर्षैश्च दिव्यैस्तमवचक्रुर्दिवौकसः //
text_mt: According to their ability and according to propriety, they worshipped him thus, / and the denizens of heaven showered him with celestial showers of flowers.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitāḥ sarve gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ /
ṛṣayaścaiva saṃsiddhāḥ ko 'yaṃ siddhimupāgataḥ //
meaning:
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः /
ऋषयश्चैव संसिद्धाः को ऽयं सिद्धिमुपागतः //
text_mt: Seeing him, all the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases were astonished, / as well as the accomplished sages: “Who is this that has attained perfection?”

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'sau svāhrayaṃ tebhyaḥ kathayāmāsa nārada /
uvāca ca mahātejāstānṛṣīnsaṃpraharṣitaḥ //
meaning:
ततो ऽसौ स्वाह्रयं तेभ्यः कथयामास नारद /
उवाच च महातेजास्तानृषीन्संप्रहर्षितः //
text_mt: Then he proclaimed his own name to them, O Nārada, / and, possessing great splendor, addressed those sages, fully delighted:

sanskrit_iast:
pitā yadyanugacchenmāṃ krośamānaḥ śuketi vai /
tasmai prativacodeyaṃ bhavadbhistu samāhitaiḥ //
meaning:
पिता यद्यनुगच्छेन्मां क्रोशमानः शुकेति वै /
तस्मै प्रतिवचोदेयं भवद्भिस्तु समाहितैः //
text_mt: “If my father should follow me, crying out indeed, ‘O Śuka!’, / an answer should be given to him by you with composed minds.”

sanskrit_iast:
bāḍhamuktastatastaistu lokānhitvā caturvidhān /
tamo hyaṣṭavidhaṃ tyaktvā jahau pañcavidhaṃ rajaḥ //
meaning:
बाढमुक्तस्ततस्तैस्तु लोकान्हित्वा चतुर्विधान् /
तमो ह्यष्टविधं त्यक्त्वा जहौ पञ्चविधं रजः //
text_mt: Being told “Certainly” by them, having abandoned the four types of worlds, / having cast off the eightfold darkness, he discarded the fivefold passion.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ satvaṃ jahau dhīmāṃstadadbhutamivābhavat /
tatastasminpade nitye nirguṇe liṅgapūjite //
meaning:
ततः सत्वं जहौ धीमांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् /
ततस्तस्मिन्पदे नित्ये निर्गुणे लिङ्गपूजिते //
text_mt: Then the wise one discarded purity; that was like a wonder. / Then, in that eternal, attributeless realm worshipped by the signs—

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ sa śṛṅge 'pratime himavanmerusannibhe /
saṃśliṣṭe śvetapīte ca rukmarūpyamaye śubhe //
meaning:
ततः स शृङ्गे ऽप्रतिमे हिमवन्मेरुसन्निभे /
संश्लिष्टे श्वेतपीते च रुक्मरूप्यमये शुभे //
text_mt: then he, [facing] the two peerless peaks resembling the Himālaya and Meru, / joined together, white and yellow, auspicious, composed of gold and silver,

sanskrit_iast:
śatayojanavistāre tiryāgūrddhca nārada /
so 'viśaṅkena manasā tathaivābhyapatacchukaḥ //
meaning:
शतयोजनविस्तारे तिर्यागूर्द्ध्च नारद /
सो ऽविशङ्केन मनसा तथैवाभ्यपतच्छुकः //
text_mt: a hundred yojanas in extent across and upwards, O Nārada, / Śuka flew straight against them with a fearless mind.

sanskrit_iast:
te śṛṅge 'tyantasaṃśliṣṭe sahasaiva dvidhākṛte /
adṛśyetāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha tadadbhutamivābhavat //
meaning:
ते शृङ्गे ऽत्यन्तसंश्लिष्टे सहसैव द्विधाकृते /
अदृश्येतां द्विजश्रेष्ठ तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् //
text_mt: Those two peaks, tightly conjoined, were suddenly split in two; / they were seen [so], O best of the twice-born; that was like a wonder.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ parvataśṛṅgābhyāṃ sahasaiva viniḥsṛtaḥ /
na ca pratijaghānāsya sa gatiṃ parvatottamaḥ //
meaning:
ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाभ्यां सहसैव विनिःसृतः /
न च प्रतिजघानास्य स गतिं पर्वतोत्तमः //
text_mt: Then, having suddenly issued from the two mountain peaks, / that best of mountains did not obstruct his path.

sanskrit_iast:
tato mandākinīṃ divyā mupariṣṭādabhivrajan /
śuko dadarśa dharmātmā puṣpitadrumakānanam //
meaning:
ततो मन्दाकिनीं दिव्या मुपरिष्टादभिव्रजन् /
शुको ददर्श धर्मात्मा पुष्पितद्रुमकाननम् //
text_mt: Then, proceeding above the celestial Mandākinī, / the righteous Śuka saw a grove of flowering trees.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāṃ krīḍāsu niratāḥ snānti caivāpsarogaṇāḥ /
nirākāraṃ tu sākārādadṛśustaṃ vivāsasaḥ //
meaning:
तस्यां क्रीडासु निरताः स्नान्ति चैवाप्सरोगणाः /
निराकारं तु साकाराददृशुस्तं विवाससः //
text_mt: In it, devoted to amusements, the hosts of apsarases were bathing; / they, possessing forms and naked, beheld him who was formless.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ prakramantamājñāya pitā snehasamanvitaḥ /
uttamāṃ gatimāsthāya pṛṣṭato 'nusasāra ha //
meaning:
तं प्रक्रमन्तमाज्ञाय पिता स्नेहसमन्वितः /
उत्तमां गतिमास्थाय पृष्टतो ऽनुससार ह //
text_mt: Knowing that he was departing, his father, filled with affection, / resorting to an excellent course, followed behind.

sanskrit_iast:
śukastu mārutādūrddhvaṃ gatiṃ kṛtvāṃ tarikṣagām /
darśayitvā prabhāvaṃ svaṃ sarvabhūto 'bhavattadā //
meaning:
शुकस्तु मारुतादूर्द्ध्वं गतिं कृत्वां तरिक्षगाम् /
दर्शयित्वा प्रभावं स्वं सर्वभूतो ऽभवत्तदा //
text_mt: Śuka, however, taking a path moving through the sky above the wind, / having displayed his power, then became the self of all beings.

sanskrit_iast:
atha yogagatiṃ vyāsaḥ samāsthāya mahātapāḥ /
nimeṣāntaramātreṇa śukābhipatanaṃ yayau //
meaning:
अथ योगगतिं व्यासः समास्थाय महातपाः /
निमेषान्तरमात्रेण शुकाभिपतनं ययौ //
text_mt: Then Vyāsa of great austerities, resorting to the course of yoga, / went in the mere interval of a twinkling of an eye to Śuka's place of ascent.

sanskrit_iast:
sa dadarśa dvidhā kṛtvā parvatāgraṃ gataṃ śukam /
śaśaṃsurmunayaḥ siddhā gatiṃ tasmai sutasya tām //
meaning:
स ददर्श द्विधा कृत्वा पर्वताग्रं गतं शुकम् /
शशंसुर्मुनयः सिद्धा गतिं तस्मै सुतस्य ताम् //
text_mt: He saw that Śuka had gone, having split the mountain crest in two; / the perfected sages declared that course of his son to him.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ śuketiśabdena dīrgheṇa kranditaṃ tadāḥ /
svayaṃ pitrā svareṇoñcaistrīṃllokānanunādya vai //
meaning:
ततः शुकेतिशब्देन दीर्घेण क्रन्दितं तदाः /
स्वयं पित्रा स्वरेणोञ्चैस्त्रींल्लोकाननुनाद्य वै //
text_mt: Then, with the long cry “O Śuka!”, a weeping was made then / by the father himself with a loud voice, making the three worlds resound.

sanskrit_iast:
śukaḥ sarvagatirbhūtvā sarvātmā sarvatomukhaḥ /
pratyabhāṣata dharmātmā bhoḥ śabdenānunādayan //
meaning:
शुकः सर्वगतिर्भूत्वा सर्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः /
प्रत्यभाषत धर्मात्मा भोः शब्देनानुनादयन् //
text_mt: Śuka, having become the goal of all, the self of all, facing everywhere, / the righteous one answered, making [the worlds] resound with the sound “bhoḥ”.

sanskrit_iast:
tata ekākṣaraṃ nādaṃ bhorityevamudīrayan /
pratyāharajjagatsarvamuñcaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamam //
meaning:
तत एकाक्षरं नादं भोरित्येवमुदीरयन् /
प्रत्याहरज्जगत्सर्वमुञ्चैः स्थावरजङ्गमम् //
text_mt: Then, uttering that single-syllable sound, “bhoḥ!”, / the entire universe, moving and unmoving, echoed loudly in return.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛti vādyāpi śabdānuñcāritānpṛthak /
girigahvarapṛṣṭeṣu vyājahāra śukaṃ prati //
meaning:
ततः प्रभृति वाद्यापि शब्दानुञ्चारितान्पृथक् /
गिरिगह्वरपृष्टेषु व्याजहार शुकं प्रति //
text_mt: From that time onwards, even today, the separate uttered sounds / in mountain caves and mountain ridges reply in response to Śuka.

sanskrit_iast:
antarhitaprabhāvaṃ taṃ darśayitvā śukastadā /
guṇānsaṃtyajya sattvādīnpadamadhyagamatparam //
meaning:
अन्तर्हितप्रभावं तं दर्शयित्वा शुकस्तदा /
गुणान्संत्यज्य सत्त्वादीन्पदमध्यगमत्परम् //
text_mt: Having shown that hidden power, Śuka then, / having discarded the qualities such as sattva, attained the supreme abode.

sanskrit_iast:
mahimānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā putrasyāmitatejasaḥ /
so 'nunīto bhagavatā vyāso rudreṇa nārada //
meaning:
महिमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः /
सो ऽनुनीतो भगवता व्यासो रुद्रेण नारद //
text_mt: Seeing that greatness of his son of boundless splendor, / that Vyāsa was consoled, O Nārada, by the lord Rudra:

sanskrit_iast:
kimu tvaṃ tāmyasi mune putraṃ prati samākulaḥ /
paśyasi vipra nāyāntaṃ brahmabhūtaṃ nijāntire //
meaning:
किमु त्वं ताम्यसि मुने पुत्रं प्रति समाकुलः /
पश्यसि विप्र नायान्तं ब्रह्मभूतं निजान्तिरे //
text_mt: “Why do you grieve, O sage, agitated on account of your son? / Do you not see, O brāhmaṇa, that he who has become Brahman is not returning, [though] within yourself?”

sanskrit_iast:
ityevamanunīto 'sau vyāsaḥ punaruprāvrajat /
śvāśramaṃ sa śuko brahmabhūto lokāṃścacāra ha //
meaning:
इत्येवमनुनीतो ऽसौ व्यासः पुनरुप्राव्रजत् /
श्वाश्रमं स शुको ब्रह्मभूतो लोकांश्चचार ह //
text_mt: Consoled in this manner, that Vyāsa returned / to his own hermitage, while that Śuka, having become Brahman, roamed the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
tata kālāntare brahmanvyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ /
naranārāyaṇau draṣṭuṃ yayau badarikāśramam //
meaning:
तत कालान्तरे ब्रह्मन्व्यासः सत्यवतीसुतः /
नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं ययौ बदरिकाश्रमम् //
text_mt: Then, in the course of time, O brāhmaṇa, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī / went to Badarikāśrama to see Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra dṛṣṭvā tu tau devau tapyamāno mahattapaḥ /
svayaṃ ca tatra tapasi sthitaḥ śukamanusmaran //
meaning:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा तु तौ देवौ तप्यमानो महत्तपः /
स्वयं च तत्र तपसि स्थितः शुकमनुस्मरन् //
text_mt: Seeing those two gods there, practicing great austerities, / he himself remained there in asceticism, remembering Śuka.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvattatra sthito vyāsaḥ śukaḥ paramayogavit /
śvetadvīpaṃ gatastāta yatra tvamagamaḥ purā //
meaning:
यावत्तत्र स्थितो व्यासः शुकः परमयोगवित् /
श्वेतद्वीपं गतस्तात यत्र त्वमगमः पुरा //
text_mt: While Vyāsa remained there, Śuka, the knower of supreme yoga, / went to Śvetadvīpa, dear one, where you had gone of old.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra dṛṣṭaprabhāvastu śrīmānnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
dṛṣṭaḥ śrutivimṛgyo hi devadevo janārdanaḥ //
meaning:
तत्र दृष्टप्रभावस्तु श्रीमान्नारायणः प्रभुः /
दृष्टः श्रुतिविमृग्यो हि देवदेवो जनार्दनः //
text_mt: There, the glorious Lord Nārāyaṇa, whose power was witnessed, / was seen—the god of gods, Janārdana, who is sought by the Vedic scriptures.

sanskrit_iast:
stutaśca śukadevena prasannaḥ prāha nārada /
śrībhagavānuvāca
tvayā dṛṣṭo 'smi yogīndra sarvadevarahaḥsthitaḥ //
meaning:
स्तुतश्च शुकदेवेन प्रसन्नः प्राह नारद /
श्रीभगवानुवाच
त्वया दृष्टो ऽस्मि योगीन्द्र सर्वदेवरहःस्थितः //
text_mt: Praised by Śukadeva, being pleased, he said, O Nārada: / The Holy Lord said: / “I have been seen by you, O lord of yogins, I who dwell in secret from all gods.

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumārādiṣṭena siddho yogena vāḍava /
tvaṃ sadāgatimārgastho lokānpaśya yathecchayā //
meaning:
सनत्कुमारादिष्टेन सिद्धो योगेन वाडव /
त्वं सदागतिमार्गस्थो लोकान्पश्य यथेच्छया //
text_mt: You have become perfected through the yoga instructed by Sanatkumāra, O brāhmaṇa; / standing on the path of the wind, behold the worlds as you please.”

sanskrit_iast:
ityukto vāsudevena taṃ natvāraṇisaṃbhavaḥ /
vaikuṇṭhaṃ prayayau vipra sarvalokanamaskṛtam //
meaning:
इत्युक्तो वासुदेवेन तं नत्वारणिसंभवः /
वैकुण्ठं प्रययौ विप्र सर्वलोकनमस्कृतम् //
text_mt: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, bowing to him, the one born from the fire-kindling stick / set out for Vaikuṇṭha, O brāhmaṇa, which is worshipped by all the worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
vaimānikaiḥ surairjuṣṭaṃ virajāpariceṣṭitam /
yaṃ bhāntamanubhāntyete lokāḥ sarve 'pi nārada //
meaning:
वैमानिकैः सुरैर्जुष्टं विरजापरिचेष्टितम् /
यं भान्तमनुभान्त्येते लोकाः सर्वे ऽपि नारद //
text_mt: served by gods in celestial chariots, surrounded by the Virajā, / in whose shining all these worlds shine after, O Nārada;

sanskrit_iast:
yatra vidumasopānāḥ svarṇaratnavicitritāḥ /
vāpya utpalaṃsaṃchannāḥ surastrīkrīḍanākulāḥ //
meaning:
यत्र विदुमसोपानाः स्वर्णरत्नविचित्रिताः /
वाप्य उत्पलंसंछन्नाः सुरस्त्रीक्रीडनाकुलाः //
text_mt: where there are coral steps variegated with gold and gems, / ponds covered with blue lotuses and crowded with the sports of celestial women,

sanskrit_iast:
divyairhaṃsakulairghuṣṭāḥ svacchāṃbunibhṛtāḥ sadā /
tatra dvāḥsthaiścaturhastenārnābharaṇabhūṣitaiḥ //
meaning:
दिव्यैर्हंसकुलैर्घुष्टाः स्वच्छांबुनिभृताः सदा /
तत्र द्वाःस्थैश्चतुर्हस्तेनार्नाभरणभूषितैः //
text_mt: resounded by flocks of heavenly swans, always filled with clear water. / There, by the four-armed gatekeepers adorned with various ornaments,

sanskrit_iast:
viṣvaksenānugaiḥ siddhaiḥ kumudādyairavā ritaḥ /
praviśyābhyāntaraṃ tatra devadevaṃ caturbhujam //
meaning:
विष्वक्सेनानुगैः सिद्धैः कुमुदाद्यैरवा रितः /
प्रविश्याभ्यान्तरं तत्र देवदेवं चतुर्भुजम् //
text_mt: the perfected followers of Viṣvaksena such as Kumuda and others, unimpeded, / entering inside, [he saw] there the four-armed god of gods,

sanskrit_iast:
śāntaṃ prasannavadanaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam /
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmairmūrtimadbhirupāsitam //
meaning:
शान्तं प्रसन्नवदनं पीतकौशेयवाससम् /
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मैर्मूर्तिमद्भिरुपासितम् //
text_mt: peaceful, with a cheerful face, clad in yellow silk, / served by his conch, discus, mace, and lotus in personified forms.

sanskrit_iast:
vakṣasthalasthayā lakṣmyā kaustubhena virājitam /
kaṭīsūtrabrahmasūtrakaṭakāṅgadabhūṣitam //
meaning:
वक्षस्थलस्थया लक्ष्म्या कौस्तुभेन विराजितम् /
कटीसूत्रब्रह्मसूत्रकटकाङ्गदभूषितम् //
text_mt: resplendent with Lakṣmī resting upon his chest and with the Kaustubha jewel, / adorned with a waist-cord, sacred thread, bracelets, and armlets,

sanskrit_iast:
bhrājatkirīṭavalayaṃ maṇinūpuraśobhitam /
dadarśa siddhani karaiḥ sevyamānamaharniśam //
meaning:
भ्राजत्किरीटवलयं मणिनूपुरशोभितम् /
ददर्श सिद्धनि करैः सेव्यमानमहर्निशम् //
text_mt: wearing a radiant crown and wristlets, adorned with gemmed anklets; / he saw him being served day and night by hosts of Siddhas.

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktibhāvena tuṣṭāva madhusūdanam /
śuka uvāca
namaste vāsudevāya sarvalokaikasākṣiṇe //
meaning:
तं दृष्ट्वा भक्तिभावेन तुष्टाव मधुसूदनम् /
शुक उवाच
नमस्ते वासुदेवाय सर्वलोकैकसाक्षिणे //
text_mt: Having seen him, he praised Madhusūdana with devotion: / Śuka said: / "Obeisance to you, Vāsudeva, sole witness of all worlds,

sanskrit_iast:
jagadbījasvarūpāya pūrṇāya nibhṛtātmane /
haraye vāsukisthāya śvetadvīpanivāsine //
meaning:
जगद्बीजस्वरूपाय पूर्णाय निभृतात्मने /
हरये वासुकिस्थाय श्वेतद्वीपनिवासिने //
text_mt: whose essential nature is the seed of the universe, complete, composed of self, / to Hari who rests upon Vāsuki, dweller in Śvetadvīpa!

sanskrit_iast:
haṃsāya matsyarūpāya vārāhatanudhāriṇe /
nṛsiṃhāya dhruvejyāya sāṃkhyayogeśvarāya ca //
meaning:
हंसाय मत्स्यरूपाय वाराहतनुधारिणे /
नृसिंहाय ध्रुवेज्याय सांख्ययोगेश्वराय च //
text_mt: To Haṃsa, to him whose form is the Fish, who bears the boar's body, / to Nṛsiṃha, to him who is constantly worshipped, and master of Sāṅkhya and Yoga!

sanskrit_iast:
catuḥsanāya kūrmāya pṛthave svasuravātmane /
nābheyāya jagaddhātre vidhātreṃ'takāraya ca //
meaning:
चतुःसनाय कूर्माय पृथवे स्वसुरवात्मने /
नाभेयाय जगद्धात्रे विधात्रेंऽतकारय च //
text_mt: To the four Sanas, to Kūrma, to Pṛthu, the self-existent spirit, / to the son of Nābhi, sustainer of the world, creator, and bringer of the end!

sanskrit_iast:
bhārgavendrāya rāmāya rāghavāya parāya ca /
kṛṣṇāya vedakartre ca buddhakalkisvarūpiṇe //
meaning:
भार्गवेन्द्राय रामाय राघवाय पराय च /
कृष्णाय वेदकर्त्रे च बुद्धकल्किस्वरूपिणे //
text_mt: To the foremost descendant of Bhṛgu, to Rāma, to Rāghava, and to the Supreme, / to Kṛṣṇa, creator of the Vedas, having the forms of Buddha and Kalkin!

sanskrit_iast:
caturvyuhāya vedyāya dhyeyāya paramātmane /
naranārāyaṇākhyāya śiṣiviṣṭāya viṣṇave //
meaning:
चतुर्व्युहाय वेद्याय ध्येयाय परमात्मने /
नरनारायणाख्याय शिषिविष्टाय विष्णवे //
text_mt: To him of fourfold manifestation, to be known, to be meditated upon, the Supreme Self, / known as Nara-Nārāyaṇa, to Śipiviṣṭa, to Viṣṇu!

sanskrit_iast:
ṛtadhāmne vidhāmne ca suparṇāya svarociṣe /
ṛbhave suvratākhyāya sudhāmne cājitāya ca //
meaning:
ऋतधाम्ने विधाम्ने च सुपर्णाय स्वरोचिषे /
ऋभवे सुव्रताख्याय सुधाम्ने चाजिताय च //
text_mt: To him whose abode is truth, whose abode is manifold, to Suparṇa, self-luminous, / to Ṛbhu, named Suvrata, Sudhāman, and the unconquered Ajita!

sanskrit_iast:
viśvarūpāya viśvāya sṛṣṭisthityantakāriṇe /
yajñāya yajñabhokte ca sthaviṣṭhāyāṇave 'rthine //
meaning:
विश्वरूपाय विश्वाय सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारिणे /
यज्ञाय यज्ञभोक्ते च स्थविष्ठायाणवे ऽर्थिने //
text_mt: To him whose form is all, to the universe, author of creation, maintenance, and destruction, / to the sacrifice, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the grossest, the subtlest, the seeker!

sanskrit_iast:
ādityasomanetrāya sahaojobalāya ca /
ījyāya sākṣiṇe 'jāyabahuśīrṣāṅghribāhave //
meaning:
आदित्यसोमनेत्राय सहओजोबलाय च /
ईज्याय साक्षिणे ऽजायबहुशीर्षाङ्घ्रिबाहवे //
text_mt: To him whose eyes are sun and moon, possessing endurance, strength, and power, / worthy of worship, the witness, unborn, having many heads, feet, and arms!

sanskrit_iast:
śrīśāya śrīnivāsāya bhaktavaśyāya śārṅgiṇe /
aṣṭaprakṛtyadhīśāya brahmaṇe 'nantasaktaye //
meaning:
श्रीशाय श्रीनिवासाय भक्तवश्याय शार्ङ्गिणे /
अष्टप्रकृत्यधीशाय ब्रह्मणे ऽनन्तसक्तये //
text_mt: To the Lord of Śrī, abode of Śrī, conquered by devotion, wielder of the bow Śārṅga, / sovereign of the eightfold material nature, to Brahman of infinite power!

sanskrit_iast:
bṛhadāraṇyavedyāya hṛṣīkeśāya vedhase /
puṇḍarīkanibhākṣāya kṣetrajñāya vibhāsine //
meaning:
बृहदारण्यवेद्याय हृषीकेशाय वेधसे /
पुण्डरीकनिभाक्षाय क्षेत्रज्ञाय विभासिने //
text_mt: To him known through the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, to Hṛṣīkeśa, to the Ordainer, / whose eyes resemble lotuses, the knower of the field, the radiant one!

sanskrit_iast:
govindāya jagatkartre jagannāthāya yogine /
satyāya satyasaṃdhāya vaikuṇṭhāyācyutāya ca //
meaning:
गोविन्दाय जगत्कर्त्रे जगन्नाथाय योगिने /
सत्याय सत्यसंधाय वैकुण्ठायाच्युताय च //
text_mt: To Govinda, maker of the universe, lord of the universe, yogin, / truth, true to his promise, to Vaikuṇṭha, and to Acyuta!

sanskrit_iast:
adhokṣajāya dharmāya vāmanāya tridhātave /
ghṛtārciṣe viṣṇave te 'nantāya kapilāyaya ca //
meaning:
अधोक्षजाय धर्माय वामनाय त्रिधातवे /
घृतार्चिषे विष्णवे ते ऽनन्ताय कपिलायय च //
text_mt: To Adhokṣaja, to Dharma, to Vāmana, to the threefold element, / whose rays are butter, to Viṣṇu, to infinite Kapila!

sanskrit_iast:
viriñcaye trikakude ṛgyajuḥsāmarūpiṇe /
ekaśṛṅgāya ca śuciśravase śāstrayonaye //
meaning:
विरिञ्चये त्रिककुदे ऋग्यजुःसामरूपिणे /
एकशृङ्गाय च शुचिश्रवसे शास्त्रयोनये //
text_mt: To Viriñci, three-crested, embodied as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, / to the one-horned, of pure fame, the source of sacred teachings!

sanskrit_iast:
vṛṣākapaya ṛddhāya prabhave viśvakarmaṇe /
bhūrbhuvuḥsvaḥsvarūpāya daityaghne nirguṇāya ca //
meaning:
वृषाकपय ऋद्धाय प्रभवे विश्वकर्मणे /
भूर्भुवुःस्वःस्वरूपाय दैत्यघ्ने निर्गुणाय च //
text_mt: To Vṛṣākapi, prosperous, powerful, Viśvakarman, / whose nature is earth, atmosphere, and heaven, slayer of Daityas, beyond qualities!

sanskrit_iast:
nirañjanāya nityāya hyavyayāyākṣarāya ca /
namaste pāhi māmīśa śaraṇāgatavatsala //
meaning:
निरञ्जनाय नित्याय ह्यव्ययायाक्षराय च /
नमस्ते पाहि मामीश शरणागतवत्सल //
text_mt: To the untainted, eternal, imperishable, and immutable! / Obeisance to you! Protect me, O Lord, compassionate to those seeking refuge!"

sanskrit_iast:
iti stutaḥ sa bhagavāñcchaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
āraṇeyamuvācedaṃ bhṛśaṃ praṇatavatsalaḥ //
meaning:
इति स्तुतः स भगवाञ्च्छङ्खचक्रगदाधरः /
आरणेयमुवाचेदं भृशं प्रणतवत्सलः //
text_mt: Thus praised, the Blessed One, holding conch, discus, and mace, / deeply affectionate to the bowed, spoke thus to the son of Araṇī:

sanskrit_iast:
śrībhagavānuvāca
vyāsaputra mahābhāga prīto 'smi tava suvrata /
vidyāmāpnuhi bhaktiṃ ca jñānī tvaṃ mama rūpadhṛk //
meaning:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
व्यासपुत्र महाभाग प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव सुव्रत /
विद्यामाप्नुहि भक्तिं च ज्ञानी त्वं मम रूपधृक् //
text_mt: The Blessed One said: / "O son of Vyāsa, highly fortunate, faithful to vows, I am pleased with you; / obtain knowledge and devotion; you are a sage bearing my form.

sanskrit_iast:
yadrūpaṃ mama dṛṣṭaṃ prāk śvetadvīpe tvayā dvija /
so 'hamevāvatārārthaṃ sthito viśvaṃbharātmakaḥ //
meaning:
यद्रूपं मम दृष्टं प्राक् श्वेतद्वीपे त्वया द्विज /
सो ऽहमेवावतारार्थं स्थितो विश्वंभरात्मकः //
text_mt: The form of mine that was seen formerly by you in Śvetadvīpa, O twice-born, / that very one am I, abiding as the sustainer of the world for the sake of incarnation.

sanskrit_iast:
siddho 'si tvaṃ mahābhāga mokṣadharmānunucintayā /
varalokānyathā vāyuryathā ravaṃ savitā tathā //
meaning:
सिद्धो ऽसि त्वं महाभाग मोक्षधर्मानुनुचिन्तया /
वरलोकान्यथा वायुर्यथा रवं सविता तथा //
text_mt: You are perfected, O highly fortunate one, through meditation on the duties of liberation, / moving through the excellent worlds like the wind, as the sun moves through space.

sanskrit_iast:
nityamuktasvarūpastvaṃ pūjyamānaḥ surairnaraiḥ /
bhaktirhi durlabhā loke mayi sarvaparāyaṇe //
meaning:
नित्यमुक्तस्वरूपस्त्वं पूज्यमानः सुरैर्नरैः /
भक्तिर्हि दुर्लभा लोके मयि सर्वपरायणे //
text_mt: Your nature is ever-liberated, worshipped by gods and men; / devotion indeed is rare in the world toward me, the supreme refuge of all.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ labdhvā nāparaṃ kiñcillabdhavyamavaśiṣyate /
ākalpāntaḥ tapaḥ saṃsthau naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī //
meaning:
तां लब्ध्वा नापरं किञ्चिल्लब्धव्यमवशिष्यते /
आकल्पान्तः तपः संस्थौ नरनारायणावृषी //
text_mt: Having obtained it, nothing else remains to be attained; / abiding in austerity until the end of the aeon are the two ṛṣis, Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
tayornideśato vyāso janaka stava suvrataḥ /
kartā bhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ tadadhīṣva bhuvaṃ vraja //
meaning:
तयोर्निदेशतो व्यासो जनक स्तव सुव्रतः /
कर्ता भागवतं शास्त्रं तदधीष्व भुवं व्रज //
text_mt: By their command, your father Vyāsa, faithful to vows, / will compose the Bhāgavata scripture; study that and go to earth.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tapyati tapastvadya parvate gandhamādane /
tvadviyogena khinnātmā taṃ prasādaya matpriyam //
meaning:
स तप्यति तपस्त्वद्य पर्वते गन्धमादने /
त्वद्वियोगेन खिन्नात्मा तं प्रसादय मत्प्रियम् //
text_mt: He now performs austerity on Mount Gandhamādana, / dejected in heart through separation from you; propitiate him who is dear to me."

sanskrit_iast:
evamuktaḥ śuko vipra namaskṛtya caturbhujam /
yathāgataṃ nivṛtto 'sau piturantikamāgamat //
meaning:
एवमुक्तः शुको विप्र नमस्कृत्य चतुर्भुजम् /
यथागतं निवृत्तो ऽसौ पितुरन्तिकमागमत् //
text_mt: Thus addressed, O brāhmaṇa, Śuka bowed to the four-armed [Lord], / and returning the way he had come, went into the presence of his father.

sanskrit_iast:
atha taṃ svantike dṛṣṭvā pārāśaryyaḥ pratāpavān /
putraṃ prāpya prahṛṣṭātmā tapaso nivavarta ha //
meaning:
अथ तं स्वन्तिके दृष्ट्वा पाराशर्य्यः प्रतापवान् /
पुत्रं प्राप्य प्रहृष्टात्मा तपसो निववर्त ह //
text_mt: Then, seeing him near him, the glorious son of Parāśara, / rejoiced in heart on regaining his son, ceased from his austerity.

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam /
āraṇeyasamāyuktaḥ svāśramaṃ samupāgamat //
meaning:
नारायणं नमस्कृत्य नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् /
आरणेयसमायुक्तः स्वाश्रमं समुपागमत् //
text_mt: Having bowed to Nārāyaṇa and to Nara, best of men, / accompanied by the son of Araṇī, he came to his own hermitage.

sanskrit_iast:
nārāyaṇaniyogāttu tvanmukhena munīśvara /
cakāra saṃhitāṃ divyāṃ nānākhyānasamanvitām //
meaning:
नारायणनियोगात्तु त्वन्मुखेन मुनीश्वर /
चकार संहितां दिव्यां नानाख्यानसमन्विताम् //
text_mt: By Nārāyaṇa's appointment, however, through your mouth, O best of sages, / he composed a divine collection filled with diverse tales,

sanskrit_iast:
vedatulyāṃ bhāgavatīṃ haribhaktivivarddhinīm /
nivṛttinirataṃ putraṃ śukamadhyāpayañca tām //
meaning:
वेदतुल्यां भागवतीं हरिभक्तिविवर्द्धिनीम् /
निवृत्तिनिरतं पुत्रं शुकमध्यापयञ्च ताम् //
text_mt: equal to the Vedas, related to the Lord, promoting devotion to Hari, / and he taught it to his son Śuka, devoted to renunciation.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmārāmo 'pi bhagavānpārāśaryātmajaḥ śukaḥ /
adhītavānsaṃhitāṃ vai nityaṃ viṣṇujanapriyām //
meaning:
आत्मारामो ऽपि भगवान्पाराशर्यात्मजः शुकः /
अधीतवान्संहितां वै नित्यं विष्णुजनप्रियाम् //
text_mt: Though rejoicing in the Self, the blessed Śuka, son of Parāśara, / studied this collection, ever dear to the people of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
evamete samākhyātā mokṣadharmāstavānadha /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ cāpi haribhaktivivarddhanāḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bṛhadupākhyāne mokṣadharṃmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
एवमेते समाख्याता मोक्षधर्मास्तवानध /
पठतां शृण्वतां चापि हरिभक्तिविवर्द्धनाः //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे बृहदुपाख्याने मोक्षधर्ंमनिरूपणं नाम द्विषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
Thus these duties of liberation have been proclaimed to you, O sinless one; / they promote devotion to Hari for both those who recite and those who listen.

Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, named 'Ascertainment of the Duties of Liberation' in the Great Narrative in the second quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
samāptaścāyaṃ dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ /
śaunaka uvāca
sūta sādho ciraṃ jīva sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ /
yattvayā pāyitā vidvanvayaṃ kṛṣṇakathāmṛtam //
meaning:
समाप्तश्चायं द्वितीयः पादः /
शौनक उवाच
सूत साधो चिरं जीव सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः /
यत्त्वया पायिता विद्वन्वयं कृष्णकथामृतम् //
text_mt: And concluded is this second quarter. / Śaunaka said: / "O virtuous Sūta, adept in all scriptures, live long, / since by you, O learned one, we have been made to drink the nectar of tales of Kṛṣṇa!

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā tu mokṣadharmānvai nārado bhagavatpriyaḥ /
sanandanamukhodgītānkiṃ papracchaṃ tataḥ param //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा तु मोक्षधर्मान्वै नारदो भगवत्प्रियः /
सनन्दनमुखोद्गीतान्किं पप्रच्छं ततः परम् //
text_mt: Having heard the duties of liberation, dear to the Blessed One, / sung from the mouth of Sanandana, what did Nārada ask after that?

sanskrit_iast:
mānasā brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ sanakādyā munīśvarāḥ /
caranti lokānantasiddhā lokoddharaṇatatparāḥ //
meaning:
मानसा ब्रह्मणः पुत्राः सनकाद्या मुनीश्वराः /
चरन्ति लोकानन्तसिद्धा लोकोद्धरणतत्पराः //
text_mt: The mind-born sons of Brahmā, Sanaka and the other foremost sages, / perfected ones, roam the infinite worlds, intent on elevating the world.

sanskrit_iast:
nārado 'pi mahābhāga nityaṃ kṛṣṇaparāyaṇaḥ /
teṣāṃ samāgame bhadrā kā kathā lokapāvanī //
meaning:
नारदो ऽपि महाभाग नित्यं कृष्णपरायणः /
तेषां समागमे भद्रा का कथा लोकपावनी //
text_mt: Nārada too, O highly fortunate one, is ever devoted to Kṛṣṇa; / at their meeting, what auspicious tale, purifying the world, [took place]?"

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ mahābhāga tvayā lokopakāriṇā /
kathayiṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ yatpṛṣṭa nāradarṣiṇā //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
साधु पृष्टं महाभाग त्वया लोकोपकारिणा /
कथयिष्यामि तत्सर्वं यत्पृष्ट नारदर्षिणा //
text_mt: Sūta said: / "Well asked by you, O highly fortunate one, benefactor of the world! / I will relate all that was asked by the sage Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā sanandanaproktānmokṣadharmānsanātanān /
nārado bhārgavaśreṣṭha punaḥ papraccha tānmunīn //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा सनन्दनप्रोक्तान्मोक्षधर्मान्सनातनान् /
नारदो भार्गवश्रेष्ठ पुनः पप्रच्छ तान्मुनीन् //
text_mt: Having heard the eternal duties of liberation spoken by Sanandana, / Nārada, O best of the descendants of Bhṛgu, questioned those sages again.

sanskrit_iast:
nārada uvāca
sarvadeveśvaro viṣṇurvede tantre ca kīrtitaḥ /
samārādhyaḥ sa evātra sarvaiḥ sarvārthakāṅkṣibhiḥ //
meaning:
नारद उवाच
सर्वदेवेश्वरो विष्णुर्वेदे तन्त्रे च कीर्तितः /
समाराध्यः स एवात्र सर्वैः सर्वार्थकाङ्क्षिभिः //
text_mt: Nārada said: / 'Viṣṇu, Lord of all gods, is celebrated in the Veda and the Tantra; / he alone is to be propitiated here by all who desire all ends.

sanskrit_iast:
kairmantrairbhagavānviṣṇuḥ samārādhyo munīśvarāḥ /
ke devāḥ pūjanīyāśca viṣṇupādaparāyaṇaiḥ //
meaning:
कैर्मन्त्रैर्भगवान्विष्णुः समाराध्यो मुनीश्वराः /
के देवाः पूजनीयाश्च विष्णुपादपरायणैः //
text_mt: With which mantras is the Blessed Viṣṇu to be propitiated, O best of sages? / And which deities are to be worshipped by those devoted to Viṣṇu's feet?

sanskrit_iast:
tantraṃ bhāgavataṃ viprā guruśiṣyaprayojakam /
dīkṣaṇaṃ prātarādyaṃ ca kṛtyaṃ syādyattaducyatām //
meaning:
तन्त्रं भागवतं विप्रा गुरुशिष्यप्रयोजकम् /
दीक्षणं प्रातराद्यं च कृत्यं स्याद्यत्तदुच्यताम् //
text_mt: O brāhmaṇas, explain the Bhāgavata tantra regarding the preceptor and disciple, / the initiation, and what the duty beginning in the morning should be.

sanskrit_iast:
yairmāsaiḥ karmabhiryairvā japyairhemādibhistathā /
prīyeta paramātmā vai tadbrūta mama mānadāḥ //
meaning:
यैर्मासैः कर्मभिर्यैर्वा जप्यैर्हेमादिभिस्तथा /
प्रीयेत परमात्मा वै तद्ब्रूत मम मानदाः //
text_mt: Tell me, O givers of honor, through which months, which rites, / which recitations, and such [rites] as fire oblations, the Supreme Self is pleased.'"

sanskrit_iast:
sūta uvāca
etacchrutvā vacastasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ /
sanatkumāro bhagavānuvācārkasamadyutiḥ //
meaning:
सूत उवाच
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य नारदस्य महात्मनः /
सनत्कुमारो भगवानुवाचार्कसमद्युतिः //
text_mt: Sūta said: / Having heard these words of the great-souled Nārada, / the blessed Sanatkumāra, radiant as the sun, spoke:

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi tantraṃ bhāgavataṃ tava /
yajjñātvāmalayā bhaktyā sādhayedviṣṇumavyayam //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि तन्त्रं भागवतं तव /
यज्ज्ञात्वामलया भक्त्या साधयेद्विष्णुमव्ययम् //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / "Listen, Nārada; I shall declare to you the Bhāgavata tantra, / knowing which with pure devotion one may attain the imperishable Viṣṇu.

sanskrit_iast:
tripadārthaṃ catuṣpādaṃ mahātantraṃ pracakṣate /
bhogamokṣakriyācaryāhvayā pādāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
meaning:
त्रिपदार्थं चतुष्पादं महातन्त्रं प्रचक्षते /
भोगमोक्षक्रियाचर्याह्वया पादाः प्रकीर्तिताः //
text_mt: They declare the great tantra to have three subject matters and four quarters; / enjoyment, liberation, ritual practice, and conduct are proclaimed as the names of the quarters.

sanskrit_iast:
pādārthāstu paśupatiḥ paśupāśāstraya eva hi /
patistatra śivohyeko jīvāstu paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
पादार्थास्तु पशुपतिः पशुपाशास्त्रय एव हि /
पतिस्तत्र शिवोह्येको जीवास्तु पशवः स्मृताः //
text_mt: The categories of the padas are indeed just three: the Lord of the bound (Paśupati), the bound souls (paśu), and the fetters (pāśa). / There, the Lord is Śiva alone, whereas living beings are remembered as the bound souls.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvanmohādisaṃyogāḥ svarūpābodhalakṣaṇāḥ /
tāvatpaśutvameteṣāṃ dvaitavatpaśya nārada //
meaning:
यावन्मोहादिसंयोगाः स्वरूपाबोधलक्षणाः /
तावत्पशुत्वमेतेषां द्वैतवत्पश्य नारद //
text_mt: As long as there are connections with delusion and the like, characterized by ignorance of one's essential nature, / for that long does their state of being a bound soul endure; look upon them as characterized by duality, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
pāśāḥ pañcavidhāstveṣāṃ pratyekaṃ teṣu lakṣaṇam /
paśavastrividhāścāpi vijñātāḥ kalasaṃjñikāḥ //
meaning:
पाशाः पञ्चविधास्त्वेषां प्रत्येकं तेषु लक्षणम् /
पशवस्त्रिविधाश्चापि विज्ञाताः कलसंज्ञिकाः //
text_mt: Their fetters are of five kinds, each having its own characteristic definition among them; / and the bound souls are understood to be threefold, designated according to their association with the limiting principles (kala):

sanskrit_iast:
talapākalasaṃjñaśca sakalaśceti nāmataḥ /
tatrādyo malasaṃyukto malakarmayutaḥ paraḥ //
meaning:
तलपाकलसंज्ञश्च सकलश्चेति नामतः /
तत्राद्यो मलसंयुक्तो मलकर्मयुतः परः //
text_mt: Known by the names Vijñānākala, Pralayākala, and Sakala. / Among them, the first is endowed with impurity (mala); the second is endowed with impurity and karma;

sanskrit_iast:
malamāyākarmayutastṛtīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
ādyastu dvividhastatra samāsakaluṣastathā //
meaning:
मलमायाकर्मयुतस्तृतीयः परिकीर्तितः /
आद्यस्तु द्विविधस्तत्र समासकलुषस्तथा //
text_mt: The third is declared to be endowed with impurity, māyā, and karma. / There, the first is of two kinds: having compounded blemish,

sanskrit_iast:
asamāsamalaśceti dvitīyo 'pi punastathā /
pakvāpakvamalenaiva dvividhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
असमासमलश्चेति द्वितीयो ऽपि पुनस्तथा /
पक्वापक्वमलेनैव द्विविधः परिकीर्तितः //
text_mt: And having uncompounded blemish; and the second is also likewise / declared to be of two kinds according to mature and immature impurity.

sanskrit_iast:
śuddhe 'dhvani gatāvetau vijñānapralayākalau /
kalāditattvaniyataḥ sakalaḥ paryaṭatyayam //
meaning:
शुद्धे ऽध्वनि गतावेतौ विज्ञानप्रलयाकलौ /
कलादितत्त्वनियतः सकलः पर्यटत्ययम् //
text_mt: These two, the Vijñānākala and the Pralayākala, have entered the pure course (śuddhādhvan); / [while] this Sakala soul, constrained by the tattvas beginning with kalā, wanders about

sanskrit_iast:
karmānugaśarīreṣu tattadbhuvanageṣu ca /
pāśāḥ pañca tathā tatra prathamau malakarmajau //
meaning:
कर्मानुगशरीरेषु तत्तद्भुवनगेषु च /
पाशाः पञ्च तथा तत्र प्रथमौ मलकर्मजौ //
text_mt: In bodies conforming to karma, and in the various worlds. / Likewise, the fetters there are five, the first two being produced from mala and karma;

sanskrit_iast:
māyeyaśca tirodhānaśaktijo bindujaḥ paraḥ /
eko 'pyanekaśaktirdṛkkriyācchādanakomalaḥ //
meaning:
मायेयश्च तिरोधानशक्तिजो बिन्दुजः परः /
एको ऽप्यनेकशक्तिर्दृक्क्रियाच्छादनकोमलः //
text_mt: The next arise from māyā, from the power of concealment (tirodhānaśakti), and from bindu. / [Mala,] though single, possesses manifold powers, concealing sight and action softly;

sanskrit_iast:
tuṣakañcukavaddehanimittaṃ cātmanāmiha /
dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma vicitraphalabhogadam //
meaning:
तुषकञ्चुकवद्देहनिमित्तं चात्मनामिह /
धर्माधर्मात्मकं कर्म विचित्रफलभोगदम् //
text_mt: Like a husk or a sheath, it is the cause of embodiment for souls here. / Karma consists of merit and demerit, granting the experience of diverse fruits;

sanskrit_iast:
pravāhanityaṃ tadbījāṅkuranyāyena saṃsthitam /
ityetau prathamau cātha māyeyādyān śṛṇudvija //
meaning:
प्रवाहनित्यं तद्बीजाङ्कुरन्यायेन संस्थितम् /
इत्येतौ प्रथमौ चाथ मायेयाद्यान् शृणुद्विज //
text_mt: It is eternal as a stream, continuing according to the maxim of the seed and the sprout. / Thus these two are the first; now hear of those beginning with māyā, O twice-born one.

sanskrit_iast:
sañcidānandavibhavaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ /
patirjayati sarveṣāmeko bījaṃ vibhuḥ param //
meaning:
सञ्चिदानन्दविभवः परमात्मा सनातनः /
पतिर्जयति सर्वेषामेको बीजं विभुः परम् //
text_mt: The eternal supreme Self, whose magnificence is consciousness and bliss, / the one Lord over all, the supreme omnipresent seed, reigns supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
manasyati na codeti nivṛttiṃ ca prayacchati /
varvarti dṛkkriyārūpaṃ tattejaḥ śāṃbhavaṃ param //
meaning:
मनस्यति न चोदेति निवृत्तिं च प्रयच्छति /
वर्वर्ति दृक्क्रियारूपं तत्तेजः शांभवं परम् //
text_mt: He neither desires nor rises, and grants cessation; / that supreme splendor belonging to Śambhu perpetually exists in the form of seeing and acting.

sanskrit_iast:
śakto mayā harau bhukto paśugaṇasya hi /
tacchaktimādyāmekāntāṃ vidrūpākhyāṃ vadanti hi //
meaning:
शक्तो मया हरौ भुक्तो पशुगणस्य हि /
तच्छक्तिमाद्यामेकान्तां विद्रूपाख्यां वदन्ति हि //
text_mt: It is capable of granting experience to the host of bound souls in Hari; / indeed, they speak of His primal, exclusive power as consisting of consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
tayā cojjṛṃbhito bindurdikkriyātmā śivābhidhaḥ /
aśeṣatattvajātasya kāraṇaṃ vibhuravyayam //
meaning:
तया चोज्जृंभितो बिन्दुर्दिक्क्रियात्मा शिवाभिधः /
अशेषतत्त्वजातस्य कारणं विभुरव्ययम् //
text_mt: And awakened by Her, the bindu, which is the nature of vision and action, is named Śiva, / the omnipresent, imperishable cause of the entire collection of tattvas.

sanskrit_iast:
asminnilīnā nikhilā icchāyāḥ śaktayaḥ svakam /
kṛtyaṃ kurvanti tenedaṃ sarvānugrāhakaṃ mune //
meaning:
अस्मिन्निलीना निखिला इच्छायाः शक्तयः स्वकम् /
कृत्यं कुर्वन्ति तेनेदं सर्वानुग्राहकं मुने //
text_mt: All the powers of will, merged within this [bindu], perform their own / task; therefore, O sage, this is the bestower of grace upon all.

sanskrit_iast:
cijjaḍānugrahārthāya yasya viśvaṃ sisṛkṣataḥ /
ādyonmeṣo 'sya nādātmā śāntyādibhuvanātmakaḥ //
meaning:
चिज्जडानुग्रहार्थाय यस्य विश्वं सिसृक्षतः /
आद्योन्मेषो ऽस्य नादात्मा शान्त्यादिभुवनात्मकः //
text_mt: For Him who wishes to emanate the universe in order to bestow grace upon the conscious and the insentient, / His initial unfoldment consists of nāda, comprising the worlds beginning with Śānti.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchaktitattvaṃ viprendra proktaṃ sāvayavaṃ param /
tato jñānakriyāśaktyostathotkarṣāpakarṣayoḥ //
meaning:
तच्छक्तितत्त्वं विप्रेन्द्र प्रोक्तं सावयवं परम् /
ततो ज्ञानक्रियाशक्त्योस्तथोत्कर्षापकर्षयोः //
text_mt: That power-principle (śaktitattva), O best of brahmins, is declared to be composite and supreme. / Then, from the increase and decrease of the powers of knowledge and action,

sanskrit_iast:
prasaraścāpyabhāvena tattvaṃ caitatsadāśivam /
dṛkśaktiryatra nyagbhūtā kriyāśaktirviśiṣyate //
meaning:
प्रसरश्चाप्यभावेन तत्त्वं चैतत्सदाशिवम् /
दृक्शक्तिर्यत्र न्यग्भूता क्रियाशक्तिर्विशिष्यते //
text_mt: And their unfolding without absence, arises this tattva named Sadāśiva. / Where the power of seeing is subordinated and the power of action is prominent,

sanskrit_iast:
īśvarākhyaṃ tu tattattvaṃ proktaṃ sarvārthakartṛkam /
yatra kriyā hi nyagbhūtā jñānākhyodrekamaśnute //
meaning:
ईश्वराख्यं तु तत्तत्त्वं प्रोक्तं सर्वार्थकर्तृकम् /
यत्र क्रिया हि न्यग्भूता ज्ञानाख्योद्रेकमश्नुते //
text_mt: That tattva is indeed called Īśvara, the agent of all purposes. / Where action is subordinated and [the power] called knowledge attains prominence,

sanskrit_iast:
tattattvaṃ caiva vidyākhyaṃ jñānarūpaṃ prakāśakam /
nādo binduśca sakalaḥ sadākhyaṃ tattvamāśritau //
meaning:
तत्तत्त्वं चैव विद्याख्यं ज्ञानरूपं प्रकाशकम् /
नादो बिन्दुश्च सकलः सदाख्यं तत्त्वमाश्रितौ //
text_mt: That tattva is known as Vidyā, having the nature of knowledge, illuminating. / Nāda and bindu, possessing parts, have resorted to the tattva called Sadāśiva.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyeśāḥ punaraiśaṃ tu mantrā vidyābhidhaṃ punaḥ /
imāni caiva tattvāni śuddhādhveti prakīrtitam //
meaning:
विद्येशाः पुनरैशं तु मन्त्रा विद्याभिधं पुनः /
इमानि चैव तत्त्वानि शुद्धाध्वेति प्रकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: The lords of knowledge (vidyeśas) belong to Īśa, and the mantras belong to the Vidyā tattva. / And these tattvas are proclaimed as the pure course (śuddhādhvan).

sanskrit_iast:
sākṣānnimittamīśo 'tretyupādānasabindurāṭ /
pañcānāṃ kālarāhityākramo nāstīti niścitam //
meaning:
साक्षान्निमित्तमीशो ऽत्रेत्युपादानसबिन्दुराट् /
पञ्चानां कालराहित्याक्रमो नास्तीति निश्चितम् //
text_mt: Here, the Lord is the direct efficient cause, and the king of bindus is the material cause. / Due to the absence of time among the five, it is certain that there is no temporal sequence.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāpāravasato hyeṣāṃ vihitā khalu kalpanā /
tattvaṃ vastuta ekaṃ tu śivākhyaṃ citraśaktikam //
meaning:
व्यापारवसतो ह्येषां विहिता खलु कल्पना /
तत्त्वं वस्तुत एकं तु शिवाख्यं चित्रशक्तिकम् //
text_mt: Indeed, their conceptual distinction is made only on account of their activities; / in reality, the principle is one, named Śiva, possessing manifold powers.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktaṃ yāṃ vṛttibhedāttuvihitāḥ khalu kalpanāḥ /
cijjaḍānugrahārthāya kṛtvā rūpāṇi vai prabhuḥ //
meaning:
शक्तं यां वृत्तिभेदात्तुविहिताः खलु कल्पनाः /
चिज्जडानुग्रहार्थाय कृत्वा रूपाणि वै प्रभुः //
text_mt: According to the differences in Her activities, conceptual distinctions are made. / Having assumed forms in order to bestow grace upon the conscious and the insentient, the Lord

sanskrit_iast:
anādimalaruddhānāṃ kurute 'nugrahaṃ citām /
muktiṃ ca viśveṣāṃ svavyāpāre samarthetām //
meaning:
अनादिमलरुद्धानां कुरुते ऽनुग्रहं चिताम् /
मुक्तिं च विश्वेषां स्वव्यापारे समर्थेताम् //
text_mt: Bestows grace upon conscious souls obstructed by beginningless impurity; / and liberation for all souls that are capable in their own activity

sanskrit_iast:
vidhatte jaḍavargasya sarvānugrāhakaḥ śivaḥ /
śivasāmānyarūpo hi mokṣastu cidanugrahaḥ //
meaning:
विधत्ते जडवर्गस्य सर्वानुग्राहकः शिवः /
शिवसामान्यरूपो हि मोक्षस्तु चिदनुग्रहः //
text_mt: Śiva, the gracious bestower of all, arranges for the category of the insentient. / For liberation, which has the common nature of Śiva, is grace upon the conscious soul.

sanskrit_iast:
so 'nāditvātkarmaṇo hi tattadbhogaṃ vinā bhavet /
tenānugrāhakaḥ śambhustadbhuktyai prabhurvyayaḥ //
meaning:
सो ऽनादित्वात्कर्मणो हि तत्तद्भोगं विना भवेत् /
