text_mt: He should place in the four-petalled mūlādhāra; / Śrīviṣṇu joined with Rākiṇī, preceded by the letters from ba to la,

sanskrit_iast:
svādhiṣṭhanābhidhe cakre liṅgasthe ṣaḍdale nyaset /
rudraṃ tu ḍākinīyuktaṃ ḍādiphaāntārṇapūrvakam //
meaning:
स्वाधिष्ठनाभिधे चक्रे लिङ्गस्थे षड्दले न्यसेत् /
रुद्रं तु डाकिनीयुक्तं डादिफआन्तार्णपूर्वकम् //
text_mt: He should place in the six-petalled cakra named svādhiṣṭhāna situated at the genitals; / Rudra joined with Lākinī, preceded by the letters from ḍa to pha,

sanskrit_iast:
cakre daśadale nyasyennābhisthe maṇipūrake /
īśvaraṃ kādiṭhāntārṇapūrvakaṃ śākinīyutam //
meaning:
चक्रे दशदले न्यस्येन्नाभिस्थे मणिपूरके /
ईश्वरं कादिठान्तार्णपूर्वकं शाकिनीयुतम् //
text_mt: He should place in the ten-petalled cakra situated at the navel, the maṇipūraka; / Īśvara accompanied by Kākinī, preceded by the letters from ka to ṭha,

sanskrit_iast:
vinyaseddvādaśadalehṛdayasthe tvanāhate /
sadāśivaṃ śākinīṃ ca ṣoḍaśasvarapūrvakam //
meaning:
विन्यसेद्द्वादशदलेहृदयस्थे त्वनाहते /
सदाशिवं शाकिनीं च षोडशस्वरपूर्वकम् //
text_mt: One should place in the twelve-petalled [cakra], the anāhata situated in the heart, / Sadāśiva and Śākinī, preceded by the sixteen vowels.

sanskrit_iast:
kaṇṭhasthe ṣoḍaśadale viśuddhākhye pravinyaset /
ājñācakre paraśivaṃ hākinīsaṃyutaṃ nyaset //
meaning:
कण्ठस्थे षोडशदले विशुद्धाख्ये प्रविन्यसेत् /
आज्ञाचक्रे परशिवं हाकिनीसंयुतं न्यसेत् //
text_mt: one should place them in the sixteen-petalled [lotus] in the throat named the Viśuddha; / in the ājñā-cakra, one should place Paraśiva accompanied by Hākinī.

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣārṇapūvaṃ bhrūmadhyasaṃsthite 'timanohare /
tārādipañcamaṃ nyāsaṃ kuryātsarveṣṭasiddhaye //
meaning:
लक्षार्णपूवं भ्रूमध्यसंस्थिते ऽतिमनोहरे /
तारादिपञ्चमं न्यासं कुर्यात्सर्वेष्टसिद्धये //
text_mt: In that most captivating [centre] situated between the eyebrows, preceded by the syllables of lakṣa, / one should perform the fifth ritual placement beginning with Tārā for the attainment of all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭau vargānsvaradvandvapūrvakān bījasaṃyutān /
tārādyā nyāsapūrvāśca prayojyā aṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
meaning:
अष्टौ वर्गान्स्वरद्वन्द्वपूर्वकान् बीजसंयुतान् /
ताराद्या न्यासपूर्वाश्च प्रयोज्या अष्टशक्तयः //
text_mt: The eight groups preceded by pairs of vowels, combined with seed-syllables / and preceded by the Tārā-seed, are to be used in the ritual placement of the eight energies:

sanskrit_iast:
tārāthogrā mahogrāpi vajrā kālī sarasvatī /
kāmeśvarī ca cāmuṇḍā ityaṣṭau tārikāḥ smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
ताराथोग्रा महोग्रापि वज्रा काली सरस्वती /
कामेश्वरी च चामुण्डा इत्यष्टौ तारिकाः स्मृताः //
text_mt: Tārā, then Ugrā, and Mahogrā, Vajrā, Kālī, Sarasvatī, / Kāmeśvarī, and Cāmuṇḍā—these are remembered as the eight saviouresses.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmarandhre lalāṭe ca bhrūmadhye kaṇṭhadeśataḥ /
hṛdi nābhau phale mūlādhāre cetāḥ kramānnyaset //
meaning:
ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे ललाटे च भ्रूमध्ये कण्ठदेशतः /
हृदि नाभौ फले मूलाधारे चेताः क्रमान्न्यसेत् //
text_mt: At the aperture of Brahman, on the forehead, between the eyebrows, in the region of the throat, / in the heart, at the navel, on the sexual organ, and at the mūlādhāra—one should place these in order.

sanskrit_iast:
aṅganyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryātpīṭhākhyaṃ sarvasiddhidam /
ādhāre kāmarūpākhyaṃ bījaṃ hrasvārṇapūrvakam //
meaning:
अङ्गन्यासं ततः कुर्यात्पीठाख्यं सर्वसिद्धिदम् /
आधारे कामरूपाख्यं बीजं ह्रस्वार्णपूर्वकम् //
text_mt: Then one should perform the ritual placement of the limbs called that of the sacred seats, which grants all perfections: / at the base, the seed-syllable named Kāmarūpa, preceded by short vowels;

sanskrit_iast:
hṛdi jālandharaṃ bījaṃ dīrghapūrvaṃ pravinyaset /
lalāṭe pūrṇagiryākhyaṃ kavargādyaṃ nyasetsudhīḥ //
meaning:
हृदि जालन्धरं बीजं दीर्घपूर्वं प्रविन्यसेत् /
ललाटे पूर्णगिर्याख्यं कवर्गाद्यं न्यसेत्सुधीः //
text_mt: in the heart, the wise man should place the seed-syllable Jālandhara, preceded by long vowels; / on the forehead, that named Pūrṇagiri, beginning with the ka-group;

sanskrit_iast:
uḍḍīyānaṃ cavargādyaṃ keśasandhau pravinyaset /
kaṇṭhe tu mathurāpīṭhaṃ daśama yādikaṃ nyaset //
meaning:
उड्डीयानं चवर्गाद्यं केशसन्धौ प्रविन्यसेत् /
कण्ठे तु मथुरापीठं दशम यादिकं न्यसेत् //
text_mt: at the hairline, one should place Uḍḍīyāna, beginning with the ca-group; / and in the throat, one should place the sacred seat Mathurā, [beginning with] the tenth syllable, ya and so on.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍhā nyāsastu tārāyāḥ prokto 'bhīṣṭapradāyakaḥ /
hṛdi śrīmadekajaṭāṃ tāriṇīṃ śirasi nyaset //
meaning:
षोढा न्यासस्तु तारायाः प्रोक्तो ऽभीष्टप्रदायकः /
हृदि श्रीमदेकजटां तारिणीं शिरसि न्यसेत् //
text_mt: The sixfold ritual placement of Tārā is declared as granting desires: / one should place the glorious Ekajaṭā on the heart, and Tāriṇī on the head;

sanskrit_iast:
vajrodake śikhāṃ pātu ugratārāṃ tu varmaṇi /
mahogrā vatsare netre piṅgāgraikajaṭāstrake //
meaning:
वज्रोदके शिखां पातु उग्रतारां तु वर्मणि /
महोग्रा वत्सरे नेत्रे पिङ्गाग्रैकजटास्त्रके //
text_mt: 'May Vajrodakā protect the crest; and Ugratārā on the armour; / Mahogrā on the chest; [Tārā] on the eyes; Piṅgāgraikajaṭā on the weapon.'

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍradīrgayuktamāyāyā etānyaṣṭau ṣaḍaṅgake /
aṅguṣṭhādiṣvaṅgulīṣu pūrvaṃ vinyasya yatnataḥ //
meaning:
षड्रदीर्गयुक्तमायाया एतान्यष्टौ षडङ्गके /
अङ्गुष्ठादिष्वङ्गुलीषु पूर्वं विन्यस्य यत्नतः //
text_mt: With the māyā-seed joined to the six long vowels, these eight in the six limbs: / having first placed them with care on the fingers, beginning with the thumb,

sanskrit_iast:
tarjanīmadhyamābhyāṃ tu kṛtvā tālatrayaṃ tataḥ /
choṭikāmudrāyā kuryāddigbandhaṃ devatāṃ smaran //
meaning:
तर्जनीमध्यमाभ्यां तु कृत्वा तालत्रयं ततः /
छोटिकामुद्राया कुर्याद्दिग्बन्धं देवतां स्मरन् //
text_mt: and then clapping thrice with the forefinger and middle finger, / one should perform the boundary-sealing with the snapping mudrā while remembering the deity.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyayā tārapuṭayā vyāpakaṃ saptadhā caret /
ugratārāṃ tato dhyāyetsadyo vāde 'tisiddhidām //
meaning:
विद्यया तारपुटया व्यापकं सप्तधा चरेत् /
उग्रतारां ततो ध्यायेत्सद्यो वादे ऽतिसिद्धिदाम् //
text_mt: Enclosed by the vidyā and the syllable oṃ, one should perform the pervasion seven times; / then one should meditate upon Ugratārā, who grants immediate great success in debate:

sanskrit_iast:
layābdhāvaṃbujanmasthāṃ nīlābhāṃ divyabhūṣaṇām /
kambuṃ khaḍgaṃ kapālaṃ ca nīlābjaṃ dadhatīṃ karaiḥ //
meaning:
लयाब्धावंबुजन्मस्थां नीलाभां दिव्यभूषणाम् /
कम्बुं खड्गं कपालं च नीलाब्जं दधतीं करैः //
text_mt: standing on a lotus in the ocean of dissolution, shining blue, with divine ornaments, / holding a conch, a sword, a skull-cup, and a blue lotus in her hands;

sanskrit_iast:
nāgaśreṣṭhālaṅkṛtāṅgīṃ raktanetratrayāṃ smaret /
japellakṣacatuṣkaṃ hi daśāṃśaṃ raktapadmakaiḥ //
meaning:
नागश्रेष्ठालङ्कृताङ्गीं रक्तनेत्रत्रयां स्मरेत् /
जपेल्लक्षचतुष्कं हि दशांशं रक्तपद्मकैः //
text_mt: her limbs adorned by the best of serpents, having three red eyes, he should meditate upon her. / He should indeed recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth part in oblation with red lotuses,

sanskrit_iast:
hunetkṣīrājyasaṃmiśraiḥ śaṅkhaṃ saṃsthāpya saṃjapet /
nārīṃ paśyanspṛśangacchanmahāniśi baliṃ caret //
meaning:
हुनेत्क्षीराज्यसंमिश्रैः शङ्खं संस्थाप्य संजपेत् /
नारीं पश्यन्स्पृशन्गच्छन्महानिशि बलिं चरेत् //
text_mt: mixed with milk and clarified butter; having established the conch, he should recite thoroughly. / Looking upon a woman, touching, and approaching, he should offer a sacrificial offering at midnight,

sanskrit_iast:
śmaśāne śūnyasadane devāgāre 'tha nirjane /
parvate vanamadhye vā śavamāruhya mantravit //
meaning:
श्मशाने शून्यसदने देवागारे ऽथ निर्जने /
पर्वते वनमध्ये वा शवमारुह्य मन्त्रवित् //
text_mt: in a cremation ground, an abandoned house, a temple, or a deserted place, / on a mountain, or in the midst of a forest, mounting a corpse, the knower of mantras,

sanskrit_iast:
samare śatrunihataṃ yadvā ṣāṇyāsikaṃ śiśum /
vidyāṃ sādhayataḥ śīghraṃ sādhitaivaṃ prasiddhyati //
meaning:
समरे शत्रुनिहतं यद्वा षाण्यासिकं शिशुम् /
विद्यां साधयतः शीघ्रं साधितैवं प्रसिद्ध्यति //
text_mt: [a corpse] slain by an enemy in battle, or else a six-month-old infant. / For one mastering the vidyā swiftly, when mastered in this way, it brings success.

sanskrit_iast:
medhā prajñā prabhā vidyā dhīvṛttismṛtibuddhayaḥ /
viśveśvarīti saṃproktāḥ pīṭhasya nava śaktayaḥ //
meaning:
मेधा प्रज्ञा प्रभा विद्या धीवृत्तिस्मृतिबुद्धयः /
विश्वेश्वरीति संप्रोक्ताः पीठस्य नव शक्तयः //
text_mt:
Medhā, Prajñā, Prabhā, Vidyā, Dhī, Vṛtti, Smṛti, Buddhi,
and Viśveśvarī: these are declared as the nine powers of the seat.

sanskrit_iast:
bhṛgumanvindusaṃyuktaṃ meghavartma sarasvatī /
yogapīṭhātmane hārddaṃ pīṭhasya manurīritaḥ //
meaning:
भृगुमन्विन्दुसंयुक्तं मेघवर्त्म सरस्वती /
योगपीठात्मने हार्द्दं पीठस्य मनुरीरितः //
text_mt:
Joined with Bhṛgu, Manu, and Bindu, the path of clouds, Sarasvatī,
followed by 'to the soul of the yoga-seat' ending in the heart-mantra: this is stated as the seat-mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
dattvānenāsanaṃ mūrtiṃ mūlamantreṇa kalpayet /
pūjayedvidhivaddevīṃ tadvidhānamathocyate //
meaning:
दत्त्वानेनासनं मूर्तिं मूलमन्त्रेण कल्पयेत् /
पूजयेद्विधिवद्देवीं तद्विधानमथोच्यते //
text_mt:
Having offered the seat with this, he should fashion the form with the root-mantra.
He should worship the Goddess according to rule; that procedure is now explained:

sanskrit_iast:
tāro māyā bhagaṃ brahmā jaṭe sūryaḥ sadīrghakam /
yakṣādhipataye tandrīsopanītaṃ baliṃ tataḥ //
meaning:
तारो माया भगं ब्रह्मा जटे सूर्यः सदीर्घकम् /
यक्षाधिपतये तन्द्रीसोपनीतं बलिं ततः //
text_mt:
The praṇava, Māyā, Bhaga, Brahmā, on matted locks the Sun with a long [vowel],
'to the lord of the Yakṣas, the slumber... the brought bali' then,

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhayugmaṃ śivā svāhā balimantro 'yamīritaḥ /
dadyānnityaṃ baliṃ tena madhyarātre catuṣpathe //
meaning:
गृहयुग्मं शिवा स्वाहा बलिमन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः /
दद्यान्नित्यं बलिं तेन मध्यरात्रे चतुष्पथे //
text_mt:
a pair of Gṛha, Śivā, Svāhā: this is declared as the bali-mantra.
With it he should daily offer a bali at midnight at a crossroads.

sanskrit_iast:
jaladānādikaṃ mantrairvidadhyāddaśabhistataḥ /
dhruvo vajrodake varma phaṭsaptārṇo jalagrahe //
meaning:
जलदानादिकं मन्त्रैर्विदध्याद्दशभिस्ततः /
ध्रुवो वज्रोदके वर्म फट्सप्तार्णो जलग्रहे //
text_mt:
Then, with ten mantras, he should perform the offering of water and the rest:
Dhruva, Vajrodake, Varma, Phaṭ: this seven-syllable [mantra] is for taking water.

sanskrit_iast:
tārādyā vahnijāyāntā māyā hi kṣālane matā /
tāro māyāḥ bhṛguḥ karṇoviśuddhaṃ dharmavarmataḥ //
meaning:
ताराद्या वह्निजायान्ता माया हि क्षालने मता /
तारो मायाः भृगुः कर्णोविशुद्धं धर्मवर्मतः //
text_mt:
Māyā beginning with the praṇava and ending with the wife of Agni is held for washing.
The praṇava, Māyā, Bhṛgu, Karṇa, purified from Dharma-varma,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpāni śāmyante cheto netrayutaṃ jalam /
kalpāntanayanasvāhā mantra ācamane mataḥ //
meaning:
सर्वपापानि शाम्यन्ते छेतो नेत्रयुतं जलम् /
कल्पान्तनयनस्वाहा मन्त्र आचमने मतः //
text_mt:
'may all sins be subdued', Cheto, Jala joined with Netra,
ending in Kalpāntanayana-svāhā: this is considered the mantra for sipping water.

sanskrit_iast:
dhruvo maṇidharītyante vajriṇyakṣiyutā mṛtiḥ /
kharividyāyugrijaśva sarvavānte bako 'bjavān //
meaning:
ध्रुवो मणिधरीत्यन्ते वज्रिण्यक्षियुता मृतिः /
खरिविद्यायुग्रिजश्व सर्ववान्ते बको ऽब्जवान् //
text_mt:
Dhruva, followed by Maṇidhari, Vajriṇī endowed with Akṣi, Mṛti,
Kharividyāyugrijaśva, after Sarvavā the heron endowed with a lotus,

sanskrit_iast:
kāriṇyante dīrghavarma astraṃ vahnipriyāntimaḥ /
trayoviṃśativarṇātmā śikhāyā bandhane manuḥ //
meaning:
कारिण्यन्ते दीर्घवर्म अस्त्रं वह्निप्रियान्तिमः /
त्रयोविंशतिवर्णात्मा शिखाया बन्धने मनुः //
text_mt:
ending in Kāriṇī, the long armor, the weapon, and last the beloved of Agni:
consisting of twenty-three syllables, this is the mantra for tying the topknot.

sanskrit_iast:
praṇavo rakṣayugalaṃ dīrghavarmāstraṭhadvayam /
navārṇenāmunā mantrī kuryādbhūmiviśodhanam //
meaning:
प्रणवो रक्षयुगलं दीर्घवर्मास्त्रठद्वयम् /
नवार्णेनामुना मन्त्री कुर्याद्भूमिविशोधनम् //
text_mt:
The praṇava, a pair of 'protect', the long armor, weapon, and a pair of Ṭha:
with this nine-syllable mantra the practitioner should purify the ground.

sanskrit_iast:
nārānte sarvavighnānutsārayeti padaṃ tataḥ /
huṃ phaṭ svāhā guṇendvarṇo manurvighnanivāraṇam //
meaning:
नारान्ते सर्वविघ्नानुत्सारयेति पदं ततः /
हुं फट् स्वाहा गुणेन्द्वर्णो मनुर्विघ्ननिवारणम् //
text_mt:
Then, after Nārā, the words 'drive away all obstacles',
Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā: this mantra of thirteen syllables wards off obstacles.

sanskrit_iast:
māyābījaṃ japāpuṣpanibhaṃ nābhau viciṃyet /
tadutthenāgninā dehaṃ dahetsāddhasvapāpmanā //
meaning:
मायाबीजं जपापुष्पनिभं नाभौ विचिंयेत् /
तदुत्थेनाग्निना देहं दहेत्साद्धस्वपाप्मना //
text_mt:
He should visualize the Māyā seed-syllable resembling a hibiscus flower in the navel;
with the fire born from that, he should burn his body together with his sin.

sanskrit_iast:
tārābījaṃ suvarṇābhaṃ cintayeddhṛdi mantravit /
pavanena tadutthena pāpabhasma kṣipedbhuvi //
meaning:
ताराबीजं सुवर्णाभं चिन्तयेद्धृदि मन्त्रवित् /
पवनेन तदुत्थेन पापभस्म क्षिपेद्भुवि //
text_mt:
The practitioner should visualize the Tārā seed-syllable, golden-hued, in the heart;
with the wind born from that, he should cast the ash of sin onto the earth.

sanskrit_iast:
turīyaṃ candrakundābhaṃ bījaṃ dhyātvālalāṭataḥ /
tadutthasudhayāde haṃ svayaṃ vai devatānibham //
meaning:
तुरीयं चन्द्रकुन्दाभं बीजं ध्यात्वाललाटतः /
तदुत्थसुधयादे हं स्वयं वै देवतानिभम् //
text_mt:
Having meditated on the fourth seed-syllable resembling the moon and kunda flower at the forehead,
he himself, with the nectar born from that, becomes a body resembling the deity.

sanskrit_iast:
anayā bhūtaśuddhyā tu devīsādṛśyamāpnuyāt /
tāro 'nanto bhaguḥ karṇo padmanābhayuto balī //
meaning:
अनया भूतशुद्ध्या तु देवीसादृश्यमाप्नुयात् /
तारो ऽनन्तो भगुः कर्णो पद्मनाभयुतो बली //
text_mt:
By this purification of elements, he attains resemblance to the Goddess.
The praṇava, Ananta, Bhagu, Karṇa, the mighty one joined with Padmanābha,

sanskrit_iast:
khe vajrarekhe krodhākhyaṃ bījaṃ pāvakallabhā /
amunā dvādaśārṇena racayenmaṇḍalaṃ śubham //
meaning:
खे वज्ररेखे क्रोधाख्यं बीजं पावकल्लभा /
अमुना द्वादशार्णेन रचयेन्मण्डलं शुभम् //
text_mt:
Kha, Vajrarekhe, the seed-syllable named Krodha, and the beloved of Pāvaka:
with this twelve-syllable mantra he should fashion an auspicious maṇḍala.

sanskrit_iast:
tāro yathāgatā nidrā sadṛkṣekabhṛgurviṣam /
sadīrghasmṛtirau sākṣau mahākālo bhagānvitaḥ //
meaning:
तारो यथागता निद्रा सदृक्षेकभृगुर्विषम् /
सदीर्घस्मृतिरौ साक्षौ महाकालो भगान्वितः //
text_mt:
The praṇava, Nidrā as arrived, Bhṛgu with eyes and Eka, Viṣa,
Smṛti with a long [vowel], Rau, endowed with eyes, Mahākāla joined with Bhaga,

sanskrit_iast:
krodho 'straṃ manuvarṇo 'yaṃ manuḥ puṣpādiśodhane /
tāraḥ pāśaḥ parā svāhā pañcārṇaścittaśodhane //
meaning:
क्रोधो ऽस्त्रं मनुवर्णो ऽयं मनुः पुष्पादिशोधने /
तारः पाशः परा स्वाहा पञ्चार्णश्चित्तशोधने //
text_mt:
Krodha, weapon: this mantra consists of [sixteen] syllables for purifying flowers and the like.
The praṇava, Pāśa, Parā, Svāhā: a five-syllable [mantra] for purifying the mind.

sanskrit_iast:
manavo daśa saṃproktā ardhyasthāpanamucyate /
seṃdubhyāṃ māsato māyā bhuvaṃ saṃsṛjya bhūgṛham //
meaning:
मनवो दश संप्रोक्ता अर्ध्यस्थापनमुच्यते /
सेंदुभ्यां मासतो माया भुवं संसृज्य भूगृहम् //
text_mt:
Ten mantras have been proclaimed; the placement of the offering-water is now explained:
With two moons, Māyā from the moon, having created the earth, an earth-enclosure,

sanskrit_iast:
vṛtaṃ trikoṇasaṃyuktaṃ kuryānmaṇḍalamantrataḥ /
yajettatrādhāraśaktiṃ vahnimaṇḍalamadhyagām /
vahnimaṇḍalamabhyarcya mahāśaṅkhaṃ nidhāpayet //
meaning:
वृतं त्रिकोणसंयुक्तं कुर्यान्मण्डलमन्त्रतः /
यजेत्तत्राधारशक्तिं वह्निमण्डलमध्यगाम् /
वह्निमण्डलमभ्यर्च्य महाशङ्खं निधापयेत् //

sanskrit_iast:
vāmakarṇenduyuktena phaḍantena vihāyasā /
prakṣālitaṃ bhṛgurdaṇḍī trimūrtīntuyutaṃ paṭhet //
meaning:
वामकर्णेन्दुयुक्तेन फडन्तेन विहायसा /
प्रक्षालितं भृगुर्दण्डी त्रिमूर्तीन्तुयुतं पठेत् //
text_mt:
Washed by space endowed with the left ear and moon, ending in Phaṭ,
he should recite Bhṛgu, the staff-bearer, endowed with the three forms and moon.

sanskrit_iast:
tator'cayenmahāśaṅkhaṃ japanmantracatuṣṭayam /
dīrghatrayānvitā māyā kālī sṛṣṭiḥ sadīrghasaḥ //
meaning:
ततोर्ऽचयेन्महाशङ्खं जपन्मन्त्रचतुष्टयम् /
दीर्घत्रयान्विता माया काली सृष्टिः सदीर्घसः //
text_mt:
Then he should worship the great conch, reciting the four mantras:
Māyā endowed with three longs, Kālī, Sṛṣṭi, along with the long Sa,

sanskrit_iast:
pratimāsaṃyutaṃ māsaṃ yavanaṃ hṛdayaṃ tataḥ /
ekādhaśārṇaḥ prathamo mahāśaṅkhārcane manuḥ //
meaning:
प्रतिमासंयुतं मासं यवनं हृदयं ततः /
एकाधशार्णः प्रथमो महाशङ्खार्चने मनुः //
text_mt:
joined with the image, month, Yavana, then Hṛdaya:
this eleven-syllable [mantra] is the first mantra in worshiping the great conch.

sanskrit_iast:
haṃso haribhujaṅgeśayukto dīrghantrayenduyuk /
tāriṇyante kapālāya namonto dvādaśākṣaraḥ //
meaning:
हंसो हरिभुजङ्गेशयुक्तो दीर्घन्त्रयेन्दुयुक् /
तारिण्यन्ते कपालाय नमोन्तो द्वादशाक्षरः //
text_mt:
Haṃsa joined with Hari and the lord of serpents, endowed with three longs and moon,
ending in Tāriṇī, Kapālāya Namaḥ: this is the twelve-syllable mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
svaṃ dīrghatrayamanvāḍhyameṣo vāmadaganvitaḥ /
lokapālāya hṛdayaṃ tṛtīyo 'yaṃ śivākṣaraḥ //
meaning:
स्वं दीर्घत्रयमन्वाढ्यमेषो वामदगन्वितः /
लोकपालाय हृदयं तृतीयो ऽयं शिवाक्षरः //
text_mt:
Sva endowed with three longs and Manu, a ram endowed with the left eye,
'to the world-guardian', Hṛdaya: this third [mantra] has the syllables of Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
māyāstrībījamarddhaiduyutaṃ svaṃ svargakhādimaḥ /
pālāya sarvādhārāya sarvaḥ sarvodbhavastathā //
meaning:
मायास्त्रीबीजमर्द्धैदुयुतं स्वं स्वर्गखादिमः /
पालाय सर्वाधाराय सर्वः सर्वोद्भवस्तथा //
text_mt:
Māyā, Strī seed-syllable joined with a half-moon, Sva, the first of sky and heaven,
to the protector, to the foundation of all, all, born of all, and so on,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaśuddhimayaśceti ṅeṃtāḥ sarvāsurāntikam /
rudhirā ratidīrghā ca vāyuḥ śubhrānilaḥ surā //
meaning:
सर्वशुद्धिमयश्चेति ङेंताः सर्वासुरान्तिकम् /
रुधिरा रतिदीर्घा च वायुः शुभ्रानिलः सुरा //
text_mt:
consisting of all purity, ending in the dative, near all demons,
Rudhirā, Rati with a long [vowel], Vāyu, white wind, wine,

sanskrit_iast:
bhājanāya bhagī satyā vikapālāya hṛnmanuḥ /
turyo raseṣu varṇo 'yaṃ mahāśaṅkhaprapūjane //
meaning:
भाजनाय भगी सत्या विकपालाय हृन्मनुः /
तुर्यो रसेषु वर्णो ऽयं महाशङ्खप्रपूजने //
text_mt:
Bhājanāya, Bhagī, Satyā, Vikapālāya, the Hṛd mantra:
this fourth mantra of six syllables is used in worshiping the great conch.

sanskrit_iast:
navārkamaṇḍalaṃ ceṣṭvā salilaṃ mūlamantrataḥ /
prapūrayetsudhābuddhyā gandhapuṣpākṣatādibhiḥ //
meaning:
नवार्कमण्डलं चेष्ट्वा सलिलं मूलमन्त्रतः /
प्रपूरयेत्सुधाबुद्ध्या गन्धपुष्पाक्षतादिभिः //
text_mt:
Having envisioned the circle of nine suns, he should fill the water with the root-mantra,
conceiving it as nectar, with fragrant paste, flowers, unhusked barley, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
mudrāṃ trikhaṇḍāṃ saṃdarśya pūjayeccandramaṇḍalam /
vāksatyapadmāgagane rephaānugrahabinduyuk //
meaning:
मुद्रां त्रिखण्डां संदर्श्य पूजयेच्चन्द्रमण्डलम् /
वाक्सत्यपद्मागगने रेफआनुग्रहबिन्दुयुक् //
text_mt:
Displaying the three-part mudrā, he should worship the moon-circle:
Speech, Satyā, Padmā, in the sky the letter Ra joined with grace and Bindu,

sanskrit_iast:
mūlamantro vipaddhvaṃsamanusargasamanvitam /
aṣṭakṛtvo 'munā mantrī mantrayetprayato jalam //
meaning:
मूलमन्त्रो विपद्ध्वंसमनुसर्गसमन्वितम् /
अष्टकृत्वो ऽमुना मन्त्री मन्त्रयेत्प्रयतो जलम् //
text_mt:
the root-mantra joined with the mantra that destroys misfortune and with emission:
with this the practitioner, restrained, should consecrate the water eight times.

sanskrit_iast:
māyayā madiśaṃ kṣiptvā khaṃ yoniṃ ca pradarśayet /
tatra vṛttāṣṭaṣaṭkoṇaṃ dhyātvā devīṃ vicintayet //
meaning:
मायया मदिशं क्षिप्त्वा खं योनिं च प्रदर्शयेत् /
तत्र वृत्ताष्टषट्कोणं ध्यात्वा देवीं विचिन्तयेत् //
text_mt:
Throwing wine with the Māyā-mantra, he should display the womb-mudrā and the sky;
having meditated there on a circular, six-cornered [figure] with eight [petals], he should envision the Goddess.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvoktāṃ pūjayettvenāṃ mūlenātha pratarpayet /
tarjanūmadhyamānāmākaniṣṭhābhirmaheśvarīm //
meaning:
पूर्वोक्तां पूजयेत्त्वेनां मूलेनाथ प्रतर्पयेत् /
तर्जनूमध्यमानामाकनिष्ठाभिर्महेश्वरीम् //
text_mt:
He should worship the previously mentioned Great Goddess and then offer libation with the root-mantra,
with the forefinger, middle finger, ring finger, and little finger,

sanskrit_iast:
sāṃguṣṭhāniścuturvāraṃ mahāśaṅkhasthite jale /
khaṃrephamanubindvāḍhyāṃ bhṛgumanvinduyuktayā //
meaning:
सांगुष्ठानिश्चुतुर्वारं महाशङ्खस्थिते जले /
खंरेफमनुबिन्द्वाढ्यां भृगुमन्विन्दुयुक्तया //
text_mt:
with the thumb, four times, in the water placed in the great conch.
With [the syllable] endowed with Kha, Repha, Manu, and Bindu, joined with Bhṛgu, Manu, and the moon,

sanskrit_iast:
dhruvādyena namontena tarpyādānandabhairavam /
tatastenārdhatoyena prokṣetpūjanasādhanam //
meaning:
ध्रुवाद्येन नमोन्तेन तर्प्यादानन्दभैरवम् /
ततस्तेनार्धतोयेन प्रोक्षेत्पूजनसाधनम् //
text_mt:
beginning with Dhruva and ending with Namaḥ, having offered libations to Ānandabhairava,
he should then sprinkle the implements of worship with half that water.

sanskrit_iast:
yomimudrāṃ pradarśyāpi praṇamedbhavatāriṇīm /
vidhānamarghe saṃproktaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam //
meaning:
योमिमुद्रां प्रदर्श्यापि प्रणमेद्भवतारिणीम् /
विधानमर्घे संप्रोक्तं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् //
text_mt:
Displaying the womb-mudrā, he should also bow to the Savior from existence.
This procedure for the offering-water has been proclaimed, bestowing all accomplishments.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvokte pūjayetpīṭhe padme ṣaṭkoṇakarṇike /
dharāgṛhāvṛte ramye devīṃ ramyopacārakaiḥ //
meaning:
पूर्वोक्ते पूजयेत्पीठे पद्मे षट्कोणकर्णिके /
धरागृहावृते रम्ये देवीं रम्योपचारकैः //
text_mt:
On the previously mentioned seat, on a lotus with a pericarp of six corners,
enclosed in an earth-house, charming, he should worship the Goddess with delightful offerings.

sanskrit_iast:
mahīgṛhe caturdikṣu gaṇeśādīnprapūjayet /
pāśāṅkuśau kapālaṃ ca triśūlaṃ dadhataṃ karaiḥ //
meaning:
महीगृहे चतुर्दिक्षु गणेशादीन्प्रपूजयेत् /
पाशाङ्कुशौ कपालं च त्रिशूलं दधतं करैः //
text_mt:
In the earth-house in the four directions he should worship Gaṇeśa and the others;
holding a noose, goad, skull-cup, and trident with his hands,

sanskrit_iast:
alaṅkāracayopetaṃ gaṇeśaṃ prāktamarcayet /
kapālaśūle hastābhyāṃ dadhataṃ sarpabhūṣaṇam //
meaning:
अलङ्कारचयोपेतं गणेशं प्राक्तमर्चयेत् /
कपालशूले हस्ताभ्यां दधतं सर्पभूषणम् //
text_mt:
endowed with an array of ornaments, he should first worship Gaṇeśa in the east;
holding a skull-cup and spear with his hands, adorned with serpents,

sanskrit_iast:
svayūthaveṣṭitaṃ ramyaṃ baṭukaṃ dakṣiṇer'cayet /
asiśūlakapālāni ḍamaruṃ dadhataṃ karaiḥ //
meaning:
स्वयूथवेष्टितं रम्यं बटुकं दक्षिणेर्ऽचयेत् /
असिशूलकपालानि डमरुं दधतं करैः //
text_mt:
surrounded by his own troop, charming, he should worship Baṭuka in the south;
holding a sword, spear, skull-cup, and hourglass-drum in his hands,

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣṇaṃ digaṃbaraṃ krūraṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca paścime /
kapālaṃ ḍamaruṃ pāśaṃ liṅgaṃ śaṃbibhratīṃ karaiḥ //
meaning:
कृष्णं दिगंबरं क्रूरं क्षेत्रपालं च पश्चिमे /
कपालं डमरुं पाशं लिङ्गं शंबिभ्रतीं करैः //
text_mt:
dark, sky-clad, and fierce, he should worship Kṣetrapāla in the west;
holding a skull-cup, hourglass-drum, noose, and auspicious linga in her hands,

sanskrit_iast:
adhyākanyā raktavastrā yoginīruttare yajet /
akṣobhyaṃ prayajenmūrdhni devyā mantraṛṣiṃ śubham //
meaning:
अध्याकन्या रक्तवस्त्रा योगिनीरुत्तरे यजेत् /
अक्षोभ्यं प्रयजेन्मूर्ध्नि देव्या मन्त्रऋषिं शुभम् //
text_mt:
a primeval maiden clad in red garments, he should worship the Yoginī in the north.
On the head of the Goddess, he should worship Akṣobhya, the auspicious seer of the mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
akṣobhyaṃ vastrapuṣpaṃ ca pratīcchānavallabhā /
akṣobhyapūjane mantraḥ ṣaṭkogakam //
meaning:
अक्षोभ्यं वस्त्रपुष्पं च प्रतीच्छानवल्लभा /
अक्षोभ्यपूजने मन्त्रः षट्कोगकम् //
text_mt:
'O Akṣobhya, accept the garment and flower, Svāhā':
this is the six-limbed mantra in the worship of Akṣobhya.

sanskrit_iast:
vairācanaṃ cāmitābhaṃ padmanābhibhidhaṃ tathā /
śaṅkhaṃ pāṇḍurasaṃjñaṃ ca digdaleṣu prapūjayet //
meaning:
वैराचनं चामिताभं पद्मनाभिभिधं तथा /
शङ्खं पाण्डुरसंज्ञं च दिग्दलेषु प्रपूजयेत् //
text_mt:
Vairācana, Amitābha, the one named Padmanābhi,
Śaṅkha, and the one named Pāṇḍura: these he should worship on the directional petals.

sanskrit_iast:
lābhakāṃ mānakāṃ caiva pāṇḍurāṃ tārakāṃ tathā /
vidiggatābjapatreṣu pūjayediṣṭasiddhaye //
meaning:
लाभकां मानकां चैव पाण्डुरां तारकां तथा /
विदिग्गताब्जपत्रेषु पूजयेदिष्टसिद्धये //
text_mt:
Lābhakā, Mānakā, Pāṇḍurā, and Tārakā:
he should worship these on the intermediate lotus petals for the attainment of desired ends.

sanskrit_iast:
bindunāmādivarṇādyāḥ saṃbuddhyantāstathābhidhāḥ /
vrajapuṣpaṃ pratīcchāgnipriyāntāḥ praṇavādikāḥ //
meaning:
बिन्दुनामादिवर्णाद्याः संबुद्ध्यन्तास्तथाभिधाः /
व्रजपुष्पं प्रतीच्छाग्निप्रियान्ताः प्रणवादिकाः //
text_mt:
Beginning with Bindu and the initial phoneme of the name, ending in the vocative case,
'accept the thunderbolt-flower', ending in Svāhā and beginning with the praṇava.

sanskrit_iast:
vairācanādi pūjāyāṃ manavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
bhūdharaśca caturdvārṣu padmāntakayamāntakau //
meaning:
वैराचनादि पूजायां मनवः परिकीर्तिताः /
भूधरश्च चतुर्द्वार्षु पद्मान्तकयमान्तकौ //
text_mt: The mantras are declared for the worship of Vairācana and the others. / Bhūdhara and, at the four gates, Padmāntaka and Yamāntaka,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyāntakābhidhaḥ paścānnarāntaka imānyajet /
śakrādīṃścaiva vajrādīnprajapettadanantaram //
meaning:
विद्यान्तकाभिधः पश्चान्नरान्तक इमान्यजेत् /
शक्रादींश्चैव वज्रादीन्प्रजपेत्तदनन्तरम् //
text_mt: then the one named Vidyāntaka, and Narāntaka: one should worship these. / Immediately thereafter one should recite [the mantras of] Śakra and the others, and the vajra and the other [weapons].

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ saṃpūjayandevīṃ pāṇḍityaṃ dhanamadbhutam /
putrānpautrāñchubhāṃ kīrtiṃ labhate janavaśyatām //
meaning:
एवं संपूजयन्देवीं पाण्डित्यं धनमद्भुतम् /
पुत्रान्पौत्राञ्छुभां कीर्तिं लभते जनवश्यताम् //
text_mt: Worshipping the goddess thus, he obtains learning, wondrous wealth, / sons, grandsons, auspicious renown, and the subjugation of people.

sanskrit_iast:
tāro māyā śrīmadakajaṭe nīlasarasvatī /
mahopratāre devāsaḥ sanetro gadiyugmakam //
meaning:
तारो माया श्रीमदकजटे नीलसरस्वती /
महोप्रतारे देवासः सनेत्रो गदियुग्मकम् //
text_mt: Tāra, māyā, ‘śrīmadakajaṭe nīlasarasvatī’, / ‘mahopratāre’, ‘devāsaḥ’, accompanied by netra, the pair of ‘gadi’,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvadevapiśākarmo dīrghogrirmarusānmasa /
abhragumama jāḍyaṃ ca chedayadvitayaṃ ramā //
meaning:
सर्वदेवपिशाकर्मो दीर्घोग्रिर्मरुसान्मस /
अभ्रगुमम जाड्यं च छेदयद्वितयं रमा //
text_mt: ‘sarvadevapiśākarmo dīrghogrirmarusānmasa’, / ‘abhragumama’, and ‘jāḍyaṃ chedaya’ twice, ‘ramā’,

sanskrit_iast:
māyāstrāgnipriyānto 'yaṃ dvipañcāśallipirmanuḥ /
anena nityaṃ pūjati'nvahaṃ devyai baliṃ haret //
meaning:
मायास्त्राग्निप्रियान्तो ऽयं द्विपञ्चाशल्लिपिर्मनुः /
अनेन नित्यं पूजतिऽन्वहं देव्यै बलिं हरेत् //
text_mt: ending with māyā, astra, and the beloved of Agni (svāhā)—this is the fifty-two-syllable mantra. / Worshipping constantly with this, he should offer a bali-oblation every day to the goddess.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī prayogānvidadhāti ca /
jātamātrasya bālasya divasatritayādadhaḥ //
meaning:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री प्रयोगान्विदधाति च /
जातमात्रस्य बालस्य दिवसत्रितयादधः //
text_mt: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner performs applications: / within three days of an infant’s birth,

sanskrit_iast:
jihvāyāṃ vilikhenmantraṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ śalākayā /
suvarṇa kṛtayā yadvā mantrī dhavaladūrvayā //
meaning:
जिह्वायां विलिखेन्मन्त्रं मध्वाज्याभ्यां शलाकया /
सुवर्ण कृतया यद्वा मन्त्री धवलदूर्वया //
text_mt: the practitioner should write the mantra on its tongue with honey and ghee using a gold probe, / or alternatively with white dūrvā grass.

sanskrit_iast:
gate 'ṣṭame 'bde bālo 'pi jāyate kaviradbutam /
tathāparairajeyo 'pi bhūpasaṃghairddhanārcitaḥ //
meaning:
गते ऽष्टमे ऽब्दे बालो ऽपि जायते कविरद्बुतम् /
तथापरैरजेयो ऽपि भूपसंघैर्द्धनार्चितः //
text_mt: When the eighth year has passed, that child becomes a wondrous poet; / likewise, though invincible to others, he is worshipped with wealth by multitudes of kings.

sanskrit_iast:
uparāge datānīva naradārusarojale /
nirmāya kīlakaṃ tena tailamadhvamṛtairlikhet //
meaning:
उपरागे दतानीव नरदारुसरोजले /
निर्माय कीलकं तेन तैलमध्वमृतैर्लिखेत् //
text_mt: During an eclipse, in lotus-water with cedar-wood [paste] as if given [in ritual], / fashioning a peg, with that one should write with oil, honey, and nectar

sanskrit_iast:
sarojinīdale mantraṃ veṣṭayenmātṛkākṣaraiḥ /
nikhāya tadalaṃ kuṇḍe caturasre samekhale //
meaning:
सरोजिनीदले मन्त्रं वेष्टयेन्मातृकाक्षरैः /
निखाय तदलं कुण्डे चतुरस्रे समेखले //
text_mt: the mantra on a lotus leaf, and surround it with the mātṛkā syllables. / Having buried that leaf in a four-sided fire-pit provided with girdles,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsthāpya pāvakaṃ tatra juhuyānmanunāmunā /
sahasraṃ raktapadmānāṃ dhenudugdhajalāplutam //
meaning:
संस्थाप्य पावकं तत्र जुहुयान्मनुनामुना /
सहस्रं रक्तपद्मानां धेनुदुग्धजलाप्लुतम् //
text_mt: and establishing the sacred fire there, one should offer with this mantra / a thousand red lotuses moistened with cow’s milk and water.

sanskrit_iast:
homānte vivadhai ratnaiḥ palairapi baliṃ haret /
baliṃ mantreṇa vidhivadbalimantraḥ prakāśyate //
meaning:
होमान्ते विवधै रत्नैः पलैरपि बलिं हरेत् /
बलिं मन्त्रेण विधिवद्बलिमन्त्रः प्रकाश्यते //
text_mt: At the end of the fire oblation, he should offer a bali with various jewels and meat / according to rule with the bali mantra; the bali mantra is now revealed:

sanskrit_iast:
tāraḥ padme yuga tandrī viyaddīrghaṃ ca lohitaḥ /
atrirviṣabhagārūḍho vadatpadmāvatīpadam //
meaning:
तारः पद्मे युग तन्द्री वियद्दीर्घं च लोहितः /
अत्रिर्विषभगारूढो वदत्पद्मावतीपदम् //
text_mt: Tāra, padme, the pair of tandrī, long viyat, and lohita, / Atri mounted on the viṣa-bhaga, the word ‘vadatpadmāvatī’,

sanskrit_iast:
jhiṇṭīśāḍhyonilasvāhā ṣoḍaśārṇo balermanuḥ /
tato niśīthe ca baliṃ pūrvoktamanunā haret //
meaning:
झिण्टीशाढ्योनिलस्वाहा षोडशार्णो बलेर्मनुः /
ततो निशीथे च बलिं पूर्वोक्तमनुना हरेत् //
text_mt: jhiṇṭīśa combined with anila, and svāhā: this is the sixteen-syllable bali mantra. / Then at midnight he should offer the bali with the previously stated mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kṛte paṇḍitānāṃ sa jayī kavirāḍ bhavet /
nivāso bhāratīlakṣmyorjanatārañjanakṣamaḥ //
meaning:
एवं कृते पण्डितानां स जयी कविराड् भवेत् /
निवासो भारतीलक्ष्म्योर्जनतारञ्जनक्षमः //
text_mt: When this is done, he becomes victorious among scholars, a king of poets, / an abode of Bhāratī and Lakṣmī, and able to delight people.

sanskrit_iast:
śatābhijaptyā yo mantrī rocanāṃ mastāke dharet /
yaṃ yaṃ paśyati tasyāsau dāsavajjāyate kṣaṇāt //
meaning:
शताभिजप्त्या यो मन्त्री रोचनां मस्ताके धरेत् /
यं यं पश्यति तस्यासौ दासवज्जायते क्षणात् //
text_mt: The practitioner who places rocanā upon his head after reciting it a hundred times— / whomever he looks upon becomes like his servant in an instant.

sanskrit_iast:
śmaśānāṅgāramāśritya pūrvāyāṃ kujavāsare /
tena matreṇa saṃveṣṭya nibaddhaṃ raktatantubhiḥ //
meaning:
श्मशानाङ्गारमाश्रित्य पूर्वायां कुजवासरे /
तेन मत्रेण संवेष्ट्य निबद्धं रक्ततन्तुभिः //
text_mt: Taking charcoal from a cremation ground on a Tuesday under the Pūrvā asterism, / surrounded with that mantra and bound with red threads,

sanskrit_iast:
śatābhijaptaṃ mūlena nikṣipedvairiveśmani /
uccāṭayati saptāhātsakuṇṭubānvirodhinaḥ //
meaning:
शताभिजप्तं मूलेन निक्षिपेद्वैरिवेश्मनि /
उच्चाटयति सप्ताहात्सकुण्टुबान्विरोधिनः //
text_mt: recited over a hundred times with the root mantra, one should throw it into an enemy’s dwelling; / within seven days it expels the adversaries along with their families.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīrāḍhyayā niśāmantraṃ likhitvā pauruṣe 'sthani /
ravivāre niśīthinyāṃ sahasramabhimantrayet //
meaning:
क्षीराढ्यया निशामन्त्रं लिखित्वा पौरुषे ऽस्थनि /
रविवारे निशीथिन्यां सहस्रमभिमन्त्रयेत् //
text_mt: Writing the mantra with turmeric mixed with milk on a human bone / on a Sunday at midnight, one should consecrate it a thousand times.

sanskrit_iast:
tatkṣiptaṃ śatrusadane maṇḍalādbhraṃśakaṃ bhavet /
kṣetre kṣiptaṃ sasyahānyojavahṛtturamālayet //
meaning:
तत्क्षिप्तं शत्रुसदने मण्डलाद्भ्रंशकं भवेत् /
क्षेत्रे क्षिप्तं सस्यहान्योजवहृत्तुरमालयेत् //
text_mt: Thrown into an enemy’s house, it causes his expulsion from the region; / thrown into a field, it destroys the crops, robs vigor, and ruins horses.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭkoṇāntarlikhenmūlaṃ sādhyārṇaṃ keśare svaraiḥ /
bāhye 'ṣṭavargayukpatraṃ padmabhūmiparāvṛtam //
meaning:
षट्कोणान्तर्लिखेन्मूलं साध्यार्णं केशरे स्वरैः /
बाह्ये ऽष्टवर्गयुक्पत्रं पद्मभूमिपरावृतम् //
text_mt: One should write the root mantra inside a hexagon, with the name of the target in the filaments surrounded by vowels, / and on the outside, [eight] petals endowed with the eight classes [of consonants], surrounded by a lotus-earth [figure].

sanskrit_iast:
yantraṃ bhūrje jahurasairlikhetpūtāmbarāvṛtam /
paṭṭasūtreṇa sannaddhaṃ śiśukaṇṭhagataṃ dhruvam //
meaning:
यन्त्रं भूर्जे जहुरसैर्लिखेत्पूताम्बरावृतम् /
पट्टसूत्रेण सन्नद्धं शिशुकण्ठगतं ध्रुवम् //
text_mt: One should draw this yantra on birch bark with marking-nut juice, cover it with a purified cloth, / bind it with silk thread, and place it on a child’s neck; certainly,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtabhītiharaṃ vāmavāhau strīṇāṃ ca putradam /
nṛṇāṃ dakṣiṇabāhusthaṃ nirdhanānāṃ dhanapradam //
meaning:
भूतभीतिहरं वामवाहौ स्त्रीणां च पुत्रदम् /
नृणां दक्षिणबाहुस्थं निर्धनानां धनप्रदम् //
text_mt: it removes fear of spirits; on the left arm of women it grants sons; / placed on the right arm of men, it gives wealth to the destitute;

sanskrit_iast:
jñānadaṃ jñānamicchūnāṃ rājñāṃ tu vijayapradam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde yakṣiṇīmantrabhedanirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
ज्ञानदं ज्ञानमिच्छूनां राज्ञां तु विजयप्रदम् //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे यक्षिणीमन्त्रभेदनिरूपणं नाम पञ्चाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
it gives knowledge to those desiring knowledge, and victory to kings.

Thus ends the eighty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Varieties of Yakṣiṇī Mantras', in the third quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca
sarasvatyavatārāste kathitāḥ siddhidā nṛṇām /
atha lakṣmyavatārāṃste vakṣye sarvārthasiddhidān //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
सरस्वत्यवतारास्ते कथिताः सिद्धिदा नृणाम् /
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारांस्ते वक्ष्ये सर्वार्थसिद्धिदान् //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / The incarnations of Sarasvatī that grant success to mortals have been declared to you; / now I shall speak to you of the incarnations of Lakṣmī that grant success in all aims.

sanskrit_iast:
vāṇīmanmathaśaktyākhyaṃ bījatritayamīritam /
ṛṣiḥ syāddakṣiṇāmūrtiḥ paṅktiśchandaḥ prakīrtitam //
meaning:
वाणीमन्मथशक्त्याख्यं बीजत्रितयमीरितम् /
ऋषिः स्याद्दक्षिणामूर्तिः पङ्क्तिश्छन्दः प्रकीर्तितम् //
text_mt: The triad of seed-syllables named after Vāṇī, Manmatha, and Śakti is stated. / The seer is Dakṣiṇāmūrti, and the meter is declared to be paṅkti.

sanskrit_iast:
devatā tripurā bālā madhyānte śaktibījake /
nābherāpādamādyaṃ tu nābhyantaṃ hṛdayātparam //
meaning:
देवता त्रिपुरा बाला मध्यान्ते शक्तिबीजके /
नाभेरापादमाद्यं तु नाभ्यन्तं हृदयात्परम् //
text_mt: The deity is Tripurā Bālā; in the middle and at the end are the śakti-seeds. / The first [extends] from the navel down to the feet; the second, from the heart down to the navel;

sanskrit_iast:
mṛrdhno hradantaṃ tartīyaṃ kramāddeheṣu vinyaset /
ādyaṃ vāmakare dakṣakare tadubhayoḥ param //
meaning:
मृर्ध्नो ह्रदन्तं तर्तीयं क्रमाद्देहेषु विन्यसेत् /
आद्यं वामकरे दक्षकरे तदुभयोः परम् //
text_mt: the third, from the crown of the head to the heart: one should place these successively in the body. / The first in the left hand, [the second] in the right hand, and the subsequent one in both.

sanskrit_iast:
punarbījatrayaṃ nyasya mūrdhni guhye ca vakṣasi /
nava yonpābhidhaṃ nyāse navakṛtvo manuṃ nyaset //
meaning:
पुनर्बीजत्रयं न्यस्य मूर्ध्नि गुह्ये च वक्षसि /
नव योन्पाभिधं न्यासे नवकृत्वो मनुं न्यसेत् //
text_mt: Having placed the triad of seed-syllables again on the crown, the private parts, and the chest, / in the ritual placement called the nine yonis, one should place the mantra nine times:

sanskrit_iast:
karṇayościbuke nyasyecchaṅkhayormukhapaṅkaje /
netrayornāsikāyāṃ ca skandhayorudare tathā //
meaning:
कर्णयोश्चिबुके न्यस्येच्छङ्खयोर्मुखपङ्कजे /
नेत्रयोर्नासिकायां च स्कन्धयोरुदरे तथा //
text_mt: one should place it on the two ears, on the chin, on the two temples, on the lotus-face, / on the two eyes, on the nose, on the two shoulders, and on the belly;

sanskrit_iast:
nyasetkūrparayornābhau jānunorliṅgamastake /
pādayorapi guhye ca pārśvayorhṛdaye punaḥ //
meaning:
न्यसेत्कूर्परयोर्नाभौ जानुनोर्लिङ्गमस्तके /
पादयोरपि गुह्ये च पार्श्वयोर्हृदये पुनः //
text_mt: one should place it on the two elbows, on the navel, on the two knees, on the head of the phallus, / on the two feet, on the private parts, on the two sides, and again on the heart,

sanskrit_iast:
stanayoḥ kaṇṭhadeśe ca vāmāṅgādiṣu vinyaset /
vāgbhavādyāṃ ratiṃ guhye prītimatyādikāṃ hṛdi //
meaning:
स्तनयोः कण्ठदेशे च वामाङ्गादिषु विन्यसेत् /
वाग्भवाद्यां रतिं गुह्ये प्रीतिमत्यादिकां हृदि //
text_mt: on the two breasts, in the region of the neck, and on the left limbs and others. / One should place Rati preceded by the vāgbhava seed in the private parts, Prītimatī and the others in the heart;

sanskrit_iast:
kāmabījādikānpaśyedbhūmadhye tu manobhavām /
punarvāgakātmamādyāstisraeva ca vinyaset //
meaning:
कामबीजादिकान्पश्येद्भूमध्ये तु मनोभवाम् /
पुनर्वागकात्ममाद्यास्तिस्रएव च विन्यसेत् //
text_mt: one should see those beginning with the kāma-seed [there], and Manobhavā between the eyebrows. / Again one should place the three beginning with the essence of speech;

sanskrit_iast:
amṛteśīṃ ca yogeśīṃ viśvayoniṃ tṛtīyakām /
mūrdhniṃ vaktre hṛdi nyasyedguhye caraṇayorapi //
meaning:
अमृतेशीं च योगेशीं विश्वयोनिं तृतीयकाम् /
मूर्ध्निं वक्त्रे हृदि न्यस्येद्गुह्ये चरणयोरपि //
text_mt: Amṛteśī, Yogeśī, and the third, Viśvayoni, / one should place on the crown of the head, on the mouth, on the heart, on the private parts, and on the two feet.

sanskrit_iast:
kāmeśī pañcabījāḍhyāṃ smarātpañcanyasetkramāt /
māyākāmau ca vāglakṣmī kāmeśī pañcabījakam //
meaning:
कामेशी पञ्चबीजाढ्यां स्मरात्पञ्चन्यसेत्क्रमात् /
मायाकामौ च वाग्लक्ष्मी कामेशी पञ्चबीजकम् //
text_mt: Endowed with five seed-syllables, one should place the five Kāmeśīs successively after Smara. / Māyā, Kāma, Vāc, and Lakṣmī: these are the five seeds of Kāmeśī.

sanskrit_iast:
manobhavaśca makaradhvajakandarpamanmathāḥ /
kāmadevaḥ smaraḥ pañca kīrtitānyāsasiddhidāḥ //
meaning:
मनोभवश्च मकरध्वजकन्दर्पमन्मथाः /
कामदेवः स्मरः पञ्च कीर्तितान्याससिद्धिदाः //
text_mt: Manobhava, Makaradhvaja, Kandarpa, Manmatha, / and Kāmadeva: these five Smaras are declared to grant success in ritual placement.

sanskrit_iast:
śiraḥpanmukhāguhyeṣu hṛdaye bāṇadevatāḥ /
drāviṇyādyāḥ kramānnyasyedvāṇeśībījapūrvakaḥ //
meaning:
शिरःपन्मुखागुह्येषु हृदये बाणदेवताः /
द्राविण्याद्याः क्रमान्न्यस्येद्वाणेशीबीजपूर्वकः //
text_mt: On the head, feet, face, private parts, and heart, one should place the arrow-deities, / Drāviṇī and the others, in order, preceded by the seed-syllables of the goddess of the arrows.

sanskrit_iast:
drāndrīṃ klīñjūṃsa iti vaibāṇeśabījakaṃ ca kam /
drāviṇī kṣobhiṇī vaśīkaraṇyāṅkarṣaṇī tathā //
meaning:
द्रान्द्रीं क्लीञ्जूंस इति वैबाणेशबीजकं च कम् /
द्राविणी क्षोभिणी वशीकरण्याङ्कर्षणी तथा //
text_mt: ‘Drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ’—these are the seed-syllables of the lord of the arrows. / Drāviṇī, Kṣobhiṇī, Vaśīkaraṇī, Ākarṣaṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃmohanī ca bāṇānāṃ devatāḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ /
tārtīyavāgmadhyagena kāmena syātṣaḍaṅgakam //
meaning:
संमोहनी च बाणानां देवताः पञ्च कीर्तिताः /
तार्तीयवाग्मध्यगेन कामेन स्यात्षडङ्गकम् //
text_mt: and Saṃmohanī: these are declared to be the five deities of the arrows. / With the Kāma-seed located between the third [seed] and speech, the six limbs are formed,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍdīrghasvarayuktena tato devīṃ vicintayet /
dhyāyedraktasarojasthāṃ raktavastrāṃ trilocanam //
meaning:
षड्दीर्घस्वरयुक्तेन ततो देवीं विचिन्तयेत् /
ध्यायेद्रक्तसरोजस्थां रक्तवस्त्रां त्रिलोचनम् //
text_mt: provided with the six long vowels. Then one should meditate on the goddess: / one should meditate on her as standing on a red lotus, wearing red garments, three-eyed,

sanskrit_iast:
udyadarkanibhāṃ vidyāṃ mālābhayavarodvahām /
lakṣatrayaṃ japenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ kiṃśukodbhavaiḥ //
meaning:
उद्यदर्कनिभां विद्यां मालाभयवरोद्वहाम् /
लक्षत्रयं जपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं किंशुकोद्भवैः //
text_mt: resembling the rising sun, bearing a book, a rosary, and the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons. / One should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times, and make a tenth part as a fire oblation with flowers

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpairhayārijairvāpi juhuyānmadhurānvitaiḥ /
navayonyātmakaṃ yantraṃ bahiraṣṭadalāvṛtam //
meaning:
पुष्पैर्हयारिजैर्वापि जुहुयान्मधुरान्वितैः /
नवयोन्यात्मकं यन्त्रं बहिरष्टदलावृतम् //
text_mt: of kiṃśuka or oleander mixed with sweet substances. / A yantra consisting of nine yonis, surrounded on the outside by eight petals,

sanskrit_iast:
kesareṣu svarānnyasyedvargānaṣṭaudaleṣvapi /
dalāgreṣu triśūlāni padma tu mātṛkāvṛtam //
meaning:
केसरेषु स्वरान्न्यस्येद्वर्गानष्टौदलेष्वपि /
दलाग्रेषु त्रिशूलानि पद्म तु मातृकावृतम् //
text_mt: one should place the vowels in the filaments, and the eight consonant classes on the petals; / on the petal-tips trident-figures, and the lotus surrounded by the mātṛkā letters.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ vilikhite yantre pīṭhaśaktīḥ prapūjayet /
icchā jñānā kriyā caiva kāminī kāmadāyinī //
meaning:
एवं विलिखिते यन्त्रे पीठशक्तीः प्रपूजयेत् /
इच्छा ज्ञाना क्रिया चैव कामिनी कामदायिनी //
text_mt: When the yantra has been drawn in this manner, one should worship the powers of the ritual seat: / Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Kāminī, Kāmadāyinī,

sanskrit_iast:
ratī ratipriyā nandā manonmanyapi coditāḥ /
pīṭhaśaktīrimā iṣṭvā pīṭhaṃ tanmanunā diśet //
meaning:
रती रतिप्रिया नन्दा मनोन्मन्यपि चोदिताः /
पीठशक्तीरिमा इष्ट्वा पीठं तन्मनुना दिशेत् //
text_mt: Ratī, Ratipriyā, Nandā, and Manonmanī are proclaimed. / Having worshipped these powers of the ritual seat, one should assign the seat with its mantra:

sanskrit_iast:
vyomapūrve tu tārtīyaṃ sadāśivamahāpadam /
pretapadmāsanaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ namontaḥ pīṭhamantrakaḥ //
meaning:
व्योमपूर्वे तु तार्तीयं सदाशिवमहापदम् /
प्रेतपद्मासनं ङेंतं नमोन्तः पीठमन्त्रकः //
text_mt: Viyat preceding the third, the great word Sadāśiva, / pretapadmāsana ending in the dative case, and namaḥ at the end: this is the seat mantra.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍaśārṇastato mūrtauṃ kḷptāyāṃ mūlamantrataḥ /
āvāhya prajapeddevīmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
meaning:
षोडशार्णस्ततो मूर्तौं कॢप्तायां मूलमन्त्रतः /
आवाह्य प्रजपेद्देवीमुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः //
text_mt: Then, having fashioned the sixteen-syllabled [form] upon the physical image by means of the root-mantra, / having invoked the Goddess, he should recite with various kinds of ritual services.

sanskrit_iast:
devīmiṣṭvā madhyayonau trikoṇe ratipūrvikām /
vāmakoṇe ratiṃ dakṣe prītimagre manobhavām //
meaning:
देवीमिष्ट्वा मध्ययोनौ त्रिकोणे रतिपूर्विकाम् /
वामकोणे रतिं दक्षे प्रीतिमग्रे मनोभवाम् //
text_mt: Having worshiped the Goddess in the central triangle, [along with] the ones beginning with Rati in the triangle: / Rati in the left angle, Prīti in the right, and Manobhavā in front;

sanskrit_iast:
yonyantarvahnikoṇādavaṅgānyagnervidikṣvapi /
madhyayomerhahiḥ pūrvādiṣu cāgre smarānapi //
meaning:
योन्यन्तर्वह्निकोणादवङ्गान्यग्नेर्विदिक्ष्वपि /
मध्ययोमेर्हहिः पूर्वादिषु चाग्रे स्मरानपि //
text_mt: inside the triangle, beginning from the southeast corner, the limbs [of the mantra] in the intermediate directions of Agni, / and outside the central triangle in the east and other [cardinal points], and in front the [forms of] Smara;

sanskrit_iast:
vāṇadevīstadvadeva śaktīraṣṭasu yoniṣu /
subhagākhyā bhāgā paścāttṛtīyā bhagasarpiṇī //
meaning:
वाणदेवीस्तद्वदेव शक्तीरष्टसु योनिषु /
सुभगाख्या भागा पश्चात्तृतीया भगसर्पिणी //
text_mt: likewise the Bāṇadevīs, the Śaktis in the eight triangles: / the one named Subhagā, then Bhāgā, the third Bhagasarpiṇī,

sanskrit_iast:
bhagamālā tathānaṅgā nagādyā kusumāparā /
anaṅgamekhalānaṅgamadanetyaṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
meaning:
भगमाला तथानङ्गा नगाद्या कुसुमापरा /
अनङ्गमेखलानङ्गमदनेत्यष्टशक्तयः //
text_mt: Bhagamālā, likewise Anaṅgā, Nagādyā, Kusumā another, / Anaṅgamekhalā, and Anaṅgamadanā—these are the eight Śaktis.

sanskrit_iast:
padmakeśaragā brāhmī mukhāḥ patreṣu bhairavāḥ /
dīrghādyā mātaraḥ pūjyā hrasvādyāścāṣṭabhairavāḥ //
meaning:
पद्मकेशरगा ब्राह्मी मुखाः पत्रेषु भैरवाः /
दीर्घाद्या मातरः पूज्या ह्रस्वाद्याश्चाष्टभैरवाः //
text_mt: The [Mātṛkās] headed by Brāhmī residing on the lotus filaments, and the Bhairavas on the petals: / the Mothers beginning with long [vowels] are to be worshiped, and the eight Bhairavas beginning with short [vowels].

sanskrit_iast:
dalāgreṣvaṣṭapīṭhāni kāmarūpākhyamādimam /
malayaṃ kollagiryyākhyaṃ cauhārākhyaṃ kulāntakam //
meaning:
दलाग्रेष्वष्टपीठानि कामरूपाख्यमादिमम् /
मलयं कोल्लगिर्य्याख्यं चौहाराख्यं कुलान्तकम् //
text_mt: At the tips of the petals are the eight seats: the first named Kāmarūpa, / Malaya, the one called Kollagiri, the one called Cauhāra, Kulāntaka,

sanskrit_iast:
jālandharaṃ tathonnāsaṃ koṭapīṭhamathāṣṭamam /
bhūgṛhe daśadikṣvarceddhetukaṃ tripurāntakam //
meaning:
जालन्धरं तथोन्नासं कोटपीठमथाष्टमम् /
भूगृहे दशदिक्ष्वर्चेद्धेतुकं त्रिपुरान्तकम् //
text_mt: Jālandhara, likewise Unnāsa, and Koṭapīṭha as the eighth. / In the earth-enclosure, in the ten directions, one should worship Hetuka, Tripurāntaka,

sanskrit_iast:
vaitālamagni jihvaṃ ca kamalāntakālinau /
ekapādaṃ bhīmarūpaṃ vimalaṃ hāṭakeśvaram //
meaning:
वैतालमग्नि जिह्वं च कमलान्तकालिनौ /
एकपादं भीमरूपं विमलं हाटकेश्वरम् //
text_mt: Vetāla, Agnijihva, and the pair Kamalāntaka and Kālin, / Ekapāda, Bhīmarūpa, Vimala, and Hāṭakeśvara,

sanskrit_iast:
śakrādyānāyudhaiḥ sārddhaṃ svasvadikṣu samarcayet /
tadbahirdikṣu baṭukaṃ yoginīṃ kṣetranāyakam //
meaning:
शक्राद्यानायुधैः सार्द्धं स्वस्वदिक्षु समर्चयेत् /
तद्बहिर्दिक्षु बटुकं योगिनीं क्षेत्रनायकम् //
text_mt: along with Śakra and the others with their weapons, in their respective directions, one should worship. / Outside that, in the directions, [one should worship] Baṭuka, Yoginī, Kṣetranāyaka,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇeśaṃ vidiśāsvarcedvasūnsūryācchivāṃstathā /
bhūtāṃścetthaṃ bhajanbālāmīśaḥ syāddhanavidyayoḥ //
meaning:
गणेशं विदिशास्वर्चेद्वसून्सूर्याच्छिवांस्तथा /
भूतांश्चेत्थं भजन्बालामीशः स्याद्धनविद्ययोः //
text_mt: and Gaṇeśa; in the intermediate directions one should worship the Vasus, Sūryas, Śivas, / and the Bhūtas. Worshiping Bālā in this way, one becomes a master of wealth and knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
raktāṃbhojairhuternāryovaśyāḥ syuḥ sarṣapairnṛpāḥ /
nandyāvartai rājavṛkṣaiḥ kundaiḥ pāṭalacaṃpakaiḥ //
meaning:
रक्तांभोजैर्हुतेर्नार्योवश्याः स्युः सर्षपैर्नृपाः /
नन्द्यावर्तै राजवृक्षैः कुन्दैः पाटलचंपकैः //
text_mt: By offering red lotuses, women become subjugated; by mustard seeds, kings. / With nandyāvarta flowers, rājavṛkṣa, kunda, pāṭala, and campaka,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpairbilvaphalairvāpi homāllakṣmīḥ sthirā bhavet /
apamṛtyuṃ jayenmantrī guḍūcyā dugdhayuktayā //
meaning:
पुष्पैर्बिल्वफलैर्वापि होमाल्लक्ष्मीः स्थिरा भवेत् /
अपमृत्युं जयेन्मन्त्री गुडूच्या दुग्धयुक्तया //
text_mt: with flowers or with bilva fruits, from fire oblation wealth becomes firm. / The mantra-practitioner conquers premature death with guḍūcī mixed with milk;

sanskrit_iast:
yathoktadūrvāhomena nīrogāyuḥ samaśnute /
jñānaṃ kavitvaṃ labhate candrāgurusurairhutaiḥ //
meaning:
यथोक्तदूर्वाहोमेन नीरोगायुः समश्नुते /
ज्ञानं कवित्वं लभते चन्द्रागुरुसुरैर्हुतैः //
text_mt: by fire oblation of dūrvā grass as prescribed, he enjoys a healthy life. / He gains knowledge and poetic skill through oblations of moon-plant, aguru, and devdāru.

sanskrit_iast:
palāśapuṣpairvāksiddhirannāptiścānnahomataḥ /
surabhikṣīradadhyaktāṃllājānhutvā rujo jayet //
meaning:
पलाशपुष्पैर्वाक्सिद्धिरन्नाप्तिश्चान्नहोमतः /
सुरभिक्षीरदध्यक्तांल्लाजान्हुत्वा रुजो जयेत् //
text_mt: With palāśa flowers comes mastery of speech, and obtaining food through fire oblation of food. / Having offered parched grain smeared with milk and curd from a fragrant cow, he conquers diseases.

sanskrit_iast:
raktacandanakarpūrakarcūrāgururocanāḥ /
candanaṃ keśaraṃ māṃsīṃ kramādbhāgainiṃyojayet //
meaning:
रक्तचन्दनकर्पूरकर्चूरागुरुरोचनाः /
चन्दनं केशरं मांसीं क्रमाद्भागैनिंयोजयेत् //
text_mt: Red sandalwood, camphor, karcūra, aguru, rocanā, / white sandalwood, saffron, and jaṭāmāṃsī: he should combine them in sequence with parts

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmicandraikanandābdhidiksaptanigamonmitaiḥ /
śmaśāne kṛṣṇabhūtasya niśi nīhārapāthasā //
meaning:
भूमिचन्द्रैकनन्दाब्धिदिक्सप्तनिगमोन्मितैः /
श्मशाने कृष्णभूतस्य निशि नीहारपाथसा //
text_mt: measuring earth [one], moon [one], one [one], bliss [nine], ocean [four], direction [ten], seven, and Veda [four], / in a cremation ground, in the dark [fortnight] of the fourteenth day, at night, with dew-water.

sanskrit_iast:
kumāryā peṣayettāni mantreṇāthābhimantrya ca /
vidaddhyāttilakaṃ tena darśanādvaśayejjanān //
meaning:
कुमार्या पेषयेत्तानि मन्त्रेणाथाभिमन्त्र्य च /
विदद्ध्यात्तिलकं तेन दर्शनाद्वशयेज्जनान् //
text_mt: He should have a maiden grind them, and having consecrated [the paste] with the mantra, / he should apply a sectarian mark with it: by sight he can subjugate people,

sanskrit_iast:
gajasiṃhādibhūtāni rākṣasāñchākinīrapi /
prayojanānāṃ siddhyai tu devyāḥ śāpaṃ nivartya ca //
meaning:
गजसिंहादिभूतानि राक्षसाञ्छाकिनीरपि /
प्रयोजनानां सिद्ध्यै तु देव्याः शापं निवर्त्य च //
text_mt: beings such as elephants and lions, Rākṣasas, and Śākinīs. / But for the attainment of objectives, having reversed the curse of the Goddess,

sanskrit_iast:
vidhāyotkīlitāṃ paścājjapamasya samācaret /
yo japedādime bīje varāhabhṛgupāvakān //
meaning:
विधायोत्कीलितां पश्चाज्जपमस्य समाचरेत् /
यो जपेदादिमे बीजे वराहभृगुपावकान् //
text_mt: and having performed the unpinning, he should thereafter practice the recitation of this [mantra]. / One who recites Varāha, Bhṛgu, and Pāvaka in the first seed-syllable,

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamādau nabhohaṃsau madhyamānte tu pāvakam /
ādāvante ca tārtūyakramātsvaṃ dhūmraketanam //
meaning:
मध्यमादौ नभोहंसौ मध्यमान्ते तु पावकम् /
आदावन्ते च तार्तूयक्रमात्स्वं धूम्रकेतनम् //
text_mt: Nabhas and Haṃsa in the beginning of the middle, and Pāvaka at the end of the middle, / and at the beginning and the end the third, respectively one's own [seed] and Dhūmraketana,

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ japtvā śataṃ vidyā śāpahīnā phalapradā /
yadvādye carame bīje naiva rephaṃ viyojayet //
meaning:
एवं जप्त्वा शतं विद्या शापहीना फलप्रदा /
यद्वाद्ये चरमे बीजे नैव रेफं वियोजयेत् //
text_mt: having recited thus a hundred times, the vidyā becomes free from curses and bestows results. / Or else, in the first and the last seed-syllable, one should not apply the letter 'r'.

sanskrit_iast:
śāpoddhāraprakāro 'nyo yadvāyaṃ kīrtito budhaiḥ /
ādyamādyaṃ hi tārtīyaṃ kāmaḥ kāmo 'tha vāgbhavam //
meaning:
शापोद्धारप्रकारो ऽन्यो यद्वायं कीर्तितो बुधैः /
आद्यमाद्यं हि तार्तीयं कामः कामो ऽथ वाग्भवम् //
text_mt: Or this other method of removing the curse is proclaimed by the wise: / the first, the first, indeed the third, Kāma, Kāma, then Vāgbhava,

sanskrit_iast:
antyamantthamanaṅgaśca navārṇaḥ kīrtito manuḥ /
japto 'yaṃ śatadhā śāpaṃ bālāyā vinivartayet //
meaning:
अन्त्यमन्त्थमनङ्गश्च नवार्णः कीर्तितो मनुः /
जप्तो ऽयं शतधा शापं बालाया विनिवर्तयेत् //
text_mt: the last, the last, and Anaṅga—the nine-syllabled mantra is proclaimed. / Recited a hundred times, this reverses the curse of Bālā.

sanskrit_iast:
caitanyāhlādinūmantrau japtau niṣkīlatākarau /
trisvarāścetanaṃ mantrī dharaḥ śāntiranugrahaḥ //
meaning:
चैतन्याह्लादिनूमन्त्रौ जप्तौ निष्कीलताकरौ /
त्रिस्वराश्चेतनं मन्त्री धरः शान्तिरनुग्रहः //
text_mt: The two mantras of Caitanyā and Āhlādinī, when recited, produce the unpinning. / The three vowels, Cetana, the mantra-practitioner, Dhara, Śānti, Anugraha,

sanskrit_iast:
tārādihṛdayāntaḥ syātkāma āhlādinīmanuḥ /
tathā trayāṇāṃ bījānāṃ dīpanairmanubhistribhiḥ //
meaning:
तारादिहृदयान्तः स्यात्काम आह्लादिनीमनुः /
तथा त्रयाणां बीजानां दीपनैर्मनुभिस्त्रिभिः //
text_mt: beginning with Tāra and ending with 'hṛdaya', Kāma is the Āhlādinī mantra. / Likewise, having thoroughly illuminated the three seed-syllables / with the three illuminating mantras at first, he should recite them for attaining desires:

sanskrit_iast:
sudīptāni vidhāyādau japettānīṣṭasiddhaye /
vadayugmaṃ sadīrghāṃbu smṛtivālāvanaṅgatau //
meaning:
सुदीप्तानि विधायादौ जपेत्तानीष्टसिद्धये /
वदयुग्मं सदीर्घांबु स्मृतिवालावनङ्गतौ //
text_mt: 'vada' twice, accompanied by long water, Smṛti, Vālā, to Anaṅga,

sanskrit_iast:
satyaḥ sanetro nastādṛgvā vāgvarṇādyadīpinī /
klinne kledini vaikuṇṭho dīrghaṃ svaṃ sadyagontimaḥ //
meaning:
सत्यः सनेत्रो नस्तादृग्वा वाग्वर्णाद्यदीपिनी /
क्लिन्ने क्लेदिनि वैकुण्ठो दीर्घं स्वं सद्यगोन्तिमः //
text_mt: Satya, with eyes, 'na' such, or the first illuminator of the speech syllable. / 'klinne kledini', Vaikuṇṭha, long self, Sadyoga, the last,

sanskrit_iast:
nidrā sacandrā kurvīta śivārṇā madhyadīpinī /
tāro mokṣaṃ ca kurute nāyaṃ varṇāsyadīpinī //
meaning:
निद्रा सचन्द्रा कुर्वीत शिवार्णा मध्यदीपिनी /
तारो मोक्षं च कुरुते नायं वर्णास्यदीपिनी //
text_mt: Nidrā with the moon, one should make; the Śiva syllable is the middle illuminator. / Tāra, and makes liberation, Nāyā—this is the illuminator of the syllable mouth.

sanskrit_iast:
dīpinīmantarā bālā sādhitāpi na siddhyati /
vāgantyakāmān prajayedarīṇā kṣobhahetave //
meaning:
दीपिनीमन्तरा बाला साधितापि न सिद्ध्यति /
वागन्त्यकामान् प्रजयेदरीणा क्षोभहेतवे //
text_mt: Without the illuminator, Bālā, even if accomplished, is not perfected. / One should recite the speech, last, and Kāma [seeds] for the agitation of enemies;

sanskrit_iast:
kāmavāgantyabījāni trailokyasya vaśīkṛtau /
kāmāntyavāṇībījāni muktaye niyato japet //
meaning:
कामवागन्त्यबीजानि त्रैलोक्यस्य वशीकृतौ /
कामान्त्यवाणीबीजानि मुक्तये नियतो जपेत् //
text_mt: the Kāma, speech, and last seed-syllables are for the subjugation of the three worlds; / the Kāma, last, and speech seed-syllables, disciplined, he should recite for liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
pūjāraṃbhe tu bālāyāstrividhānarcayedgurūn /
divyaughaścaiva siddhaugho mānavaugha iti tridhā //
meaning:
पूजारंभे तु बालायास्त्रिविधानर्चयेद्गुरून् /
दिव्यौघश्चैव सिद्धौघो मानवौघ इति त्रिधा //
text_mt: At the beginning of the worship of Bālā, he should worship the three kinds of gurus: / the divine group, the accomplished group, and the human group—thus three kinds.

sanskrit_iast:
paraprakāśaḥ parame śānaḥ paraśivastathā /
kāmeśvarastato mokṣaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ kāmo 'mṛtoṃ'timaḥ //
meaning:
परप्रकाशः परमे शानः परशिवस्तथा /
कामेश्वरस्ततो मोक्षः षष्ठः कामो ऽमृतोंऽतिमः //
text_mt: Paraprakāśa, Parameśāna, likewise Paraśiva, / Kāmeśvara, then Mokṣa, the sixth Kāma, and Amṛta the last:

sanskrit_iast:
ete daptaiva divyaughā ānandapadapaścimāḥ /
īśānākhyastatpuruṣo 'ghorākhyovāmadevakaḥ //
meaning:
एते दप्तैव दिव्यौघा आनन्दपदपश्चिमाः /
ईशानाख्यस्तत्पुरुषो ऽघोराख्योवामदेवकः //
text_mt: these are the seven of the divine group, ending with the word 'ānanda'. / The one named Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, the one named Aghora, Vāmadevaka,

sanskrit_iast:
sadyojāta ime pañca siddhaudhākhyāḥ smṛtā mune /
mānavaughāḥ parijñeyāḥ svaguroḥ sampradāyataḥ //
meaning:
सद्योजात इमे पञ्च सिद्धौधाख्याः स्मृता मुने /
मानवौघाः परिज्ञेयाः स्वगुरोः सम्प्रदायतः //
text_mt: and Sadyojāta: these five are remembered as the accomplished group, O sage. / The human groups are to be known from the tradition of one's own guru.

sanskrit_iast:
navayonyātmake yantre vilikhenmadhyayonitaḥ /
prādakṣiṇyena bījāni trivāraṃ sādhakottamaḥ //
meaning:
नवयोन्यात्मके यन्त्रे विलिखेन्मध्ययोनितः /
प्रादक्षिण्येन बीजानि त्रिवारं साधकोत्तमः //
text_mt: In a diagram consisting of nine triangles, beginning from the central triangle, / the excellent practitioner should write the seed-syllables clockwise three times.

sanskrit_iast:
trīṃstrīnvarṇāṃstu gāyatryā aṣṭapatreṣu saṃlikhet /
bahirmātṛkayā'veṣṭya tadbahirbhūpuradvayam //
meaning:
त्रींस्त्रीन्वर्णांस्तु गायत्र्या अष्टपत्रेषु संलिखेत् /
बहिर्मातृकयाऽवेष्ट्य तद्बहिर्भूपुरद्वयम् //
text_mt: He should write three letters each of the gāyatrī on the eight petals, / having encircled on the outside with the Mātṛkā, and outside that two earth-enclosures,

sanskrit_iast:
kāmabījalasatkoṇana vyatibhinnaṃ parasparam /
patre traipuramākhyātaṃ japasaṃpātasādhitam //
meaning:
कामबीजलसत्कोणन व्यतिभिन्नं परस्परम् /
पत्रे त्रैपुरमाख्यातं जपसंपातसाधितम् //
text_mt: mutually intersected, with corners shining with the Kāma seed-syllable. / It is declared as the Traipura [yantra] on a sheet, accomplished by the infusion of recitation;

sanskrit_iast:
bāhunā vidhṛte dadyāddhanaṃ kīrtiṃ sukhaṃ sutān /
kāmānte tripurā devī vidmahe kaviṣaṃ bhahim //
meaning:
बाहुना विधृते दद्याद्धनं कीर्तिं सुखं सुतान् /
कामान्ते त्रिपुरा देवी विद्महे कविषं भहिम् //
text_mt: worn on the arm, it bestows wealth, fame, happiness, and sons. / After Kāma, 'tripurāyai devyai vidmahe', 'kaviṣaṃbhahim',

sanskrit_iast:
bakaḥ khaḍgī samārūḍhaḥ sanetro 'gniśca dhīmahi /
tatra klinne pracodānte yādityeṣā prakīrtitā //
meaning:
बकः खड्गी समारूढः सनेत्रो ऽग्निश्च धीमहि /
तत्र क्लिन्ने प्रचोदान्ते यादित्येषा प्रकीर्तिता //
text_mt: Baka, holding a sword, mounted, with eyes, and Agni 'dhīmahi'; / there 'tannaḥ klinne pracodayāt'—thus is proclaimed

sanskrit_iast:
gāyatrī traipurā sarsiddhidā surasevitā /
atha lakṣmyavatāro 'nyaḥ kīrtyate siddhido nṛṇām //
meaning:
गायत्री त्रैपुरा सर्सिद्धिदा सुरसेविता /
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारो ऽन्यः कीर्त्यते सिद्धिदो नृणाम् //
text_mt: the Traipurā Gāyatrī, bestowing all accomplishments, served by the gods. / Now another incarnation of Lakṣmī is proclaimed, bestowing accomplishments upon men.

sanskrit_iast:
vedādirgirijā padmā manyatho hṛdayaṃ bhṛguḥ /
bhagavati māheśvarī ṅente 'nnapūrṇe dahanāṅganā //
meaning:
वेदादिर्गिरिजा पद्मा मन्यथो हृदयं भृगुः /
भगवति माहेश्वरी ङेन्ते ऽन्नपूर्णे दहनाङ्गना //
text_mt: The beginning of the Veda, Girijā, Padmā, Manmatha, hṛdaya, Bhṛgu, / 'bhagavati māheśvari', ending in the dative case 'annapūrṇe', and the wife of fire [svāhā]:

sanskrit_iast:
proktā viṃśativarṇeyaṃ vidyā syāddruhiṇo muniḥ /
dhṛtiśchando 'nnapūrṇeśī devatā parikīrtitā //
meaning:
प्रोक्ता विंशतिवर्णेयं विद्या स्याद्द्रुहिणो मुनिः /
धृतिश्छन्दो ऽन्नपूर्णेशी देवता परिकीर्तिता //
text_mt: this twenty-syllabled vidyā is proclaimed; its sage is Druhiṇa, / the meter is Dhṛti, and the deity is proclaimed to be the ruler Annapūrṇā.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍdīrghāḍhyena hṛllekhābī'jena syātṣaḍaṅgakam /
mukhanāsākṣikarṇāṃsagudeṣu navasu nyaset //
meaning:
षड्दीर्घाढ्येन हृल्लेखाबीऽजेन स्यात्षडङ्गकम् /
मुखनासाक्षिकर्णांसगुदेषु नवसु न्यसेत् //
text_mt: With the Hṛllekhā seed-syllable enriched with the six long [vowels] is the six-limbed [rite]. / He should place the nine words in the nine: mouth, nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, and anus.

sanskrit_iast:
padāni nava tadvarṇasaṃkhyedānīmudīryate /
bhūmicandradharaikākṣivedābdhiyugabāhubhiḥ //
meaning:
पदानि नव तद्वर्णसंख्येदानीमुदीर्यते /
भूमिचन्द्रधरैकाक्षिवेदाब्धियुगबाहुभिः //
text_mt: The number of letters of those nine words is now spoken: / earth [one], moon [one], bearer [one], one [one], eye [two], Veda [four], ocean [four], pair [two], arms [two]—

sanskrit_iast:
padasaṃkhyāmitā varṇaistato dhyāyetsureśvarīm /
svarṇābhāṅgāṃ trinayanāṃ vastrālaṅkāraśobhitām //
meaning:
पदसंख्यामिता वर्णैस्ततो ध्यायेत्सुरेश्वरीम् /
स्वर्णाभाङ्गां त्रिनयनां वस्त्रालङ्कारशोभिताम् //
text_mt: measured by these syllable counts for each word. Then he should meditate on the ruler of goddesses: / her limbs having the radiance of gold, three-eyed, adorned with garments and ornaments,

sanskrit_iast:
bhūramāsaṃ yutāṃ devīṃ svarṇāmatrakarāṃbujām /
lakṣaṃ japo 'yutaṃ homo ghṛtāktacaruṇā tathā //
meaning:
भूरमासं युतां देवीं स्वर्णामत्रकरांबुजाम् /
लक्षं जपो ऽयुतं होमो घृताक्तचरुणा तथा //
text_mt: the Goddess accompanied by Bhū and Ramā, holding a golden vessel in her lotus hands. / One hundred thousand recitations, and a fire oblation of ten thousand with sacrificial offering smeared with ghee;

sanskrit_iast:
jayādinavaśaktayāḍhye pīṭhe pūjā samīritā /
trikoṇā vedapatrāṣṭapatraṣoḍaśapatrake //
meaning:
जयादिनवशक्तयाढ्ये पीठे पूजा समीरिता /
त्रिकोणा वेदपत्राष्टपत्रषोडशपत्रके //
text_mt: the worship is proclaimed on the seat enriched with the nine Śaktis beginning with Jayā, / in [a diagram of] a triangle, four petals, eight petals, and sixteen petals.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūpureṇa yute yantre pradadyānmāyayā manum /
agnyādikoṇatritaye śivavārāhamādhavān //
meaning:
भूपुरेण युते यन्त्रे प्रदद्यान्मायया मनुम् /
अग्न्यादिकोणत्रितये शिववाराहमाधवान् //
text_mt: In the yantra endowed with an earth-city, one should impart the mantra along with Māyā. / In the triad of corners beginning with fire, [one should worship] Śiva, Varāha, and Mādhava;

sanskrit_iast:
acaryayetsvasvamantraistu procyante manavastu te /
praṇavo manucandrāḍhyaṃ gaganaṃ hṛdayaṃ śivā //
meaning:
अचर्ययेत्स्वस्वमन्त्रैस्तु प्रोच्यन्ते मनवस्तु ते /
प्रणवो मनुचन्द्राढ्यं गगनं हृदयं शिवा //
text_mt: One should worship them with their respective mantras; those mantras are now stated: / The praṇava, the sky-letter endowed with the fourteen vowels and the crescent moon, the heart, Śivā,

sanskrit_iast:
mārutaḥ śivamantro 'yaṃ saptārṇaḥ śivapūjane /
vārāhanārāyaṇayormantrau pūrvamudīrayet //
meaning:
मारुतः शिवमन्त्रो ऽयं सप्तार्णः शिवपूजने /
वाराहनारायणयोर्मन्त्रौ पूर्वमुदीरयेत् //
text_mt: And the wind-letter: this seven-syllable Śiva-mantra is used in the worship of Śiva. / One should state the two mantras of Varāha and Nārāyaṇa as mentioned before.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaḍaṅgāni tato 'bhyarcya vāme dakṣe dharāṃ ramām /
yajetsvasvamanubhyāṃ tu tāvucyete munīśvara //
meaning:
षडङ्गानि ततो ऽभ्यर्च्य वामे दक्षे धरां रमाम् /
यजेत्स्वस्वमनुभ्यां तु तावुच्येते मुनीश्वर //
text_mt: Then, having worshipped the six limbs, one should worship the Earth on the left and Ramā on the right / With their respective mantras; O lord of sages, both are now spoken:

sanskrit_iast:
annaṃ mahyannamityuktvā me dehyannādhiporṇakāḥ /
nayemamannaṃ prāṇānte dāpayānalasuṃdarī //
meaning:
अन्नं मह्यन्नमित्युक्त्वा मे देह्यन्नाधिपोर्णकाः /
नयेममन्नं प्राणान्ते दापयानलसुंदरी //
text_mt: Having said, 'annam mahyannam,' [then] 'me dehyannādhiporṇakāḥ' / 'Nayemamannaṃ prāṇānte,' [and] 'dāpayānalasundarī'—

sanskrit_iast:
dvāviṃśatyakṣaro mantro bhūmīṣṭau bhūmisaṃpuṭaḥ /
lakṣmīṣṭau śrīpuṭo vipra snṛtirlabhanucandrayuk //
meaning:
द्वाविंशत्यक्षरो मन्त्रो भूमीष्टौ भूमिसंपुटः /
लक्ष्मीष्टौ श्रीपुटो विप्र स्नृतिर्लभनुचन्द्रयुक् //
text_mt: This twenty-two-syllable mantra is encased with the earth-bīja for Earth's desire. / For Lakṣmī's desire, it is encased with the śrī-bīja, O twice-born one. The letter sa, combined with ṛ, la, bha, the sun, and the moon,

sanskrit_iast:
bhuvo bījamiti proktaṃ śrībījaṃ prāgudāhṛtam /
mantrādisthacaturbījapūrvikāḥ paripūjayet //
meaning:
भुवो बीजमिति प्रोक्तं श्रीबीजं प्रागुदाहृतम् /
मन्त्रादिस्थचतुर्बीजपूर्विकाः परिपूजयेत् //
text_mt: Is declared to be the earth-bīja; the śrī-bīja was stated previously. / Preceded by the four bījas placed at the beginning of the mantra, one should fully worship

sanskrit_iast:
śaktīścatasro vedāsre parā ca bhuvaneśvarī /
kamalā subhagā cati brāhmyādyā aṣṭapatragāḥ //
meaning:
शक्तीश्चतस्रो वेदास्रे परा च भुवनेश्वरी /
कमला सुभगा चति ब्राह्म्याद्या अष्टपत्रगाः //
text_mt: The four Śaktis in the four corners: Parā, Bhuvaneśvarī, / Kamalā, and Subhagā; and Brāhmī and the others situated in the eight petals.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣoḍaśāre smṛte cava mānadātuṣṭipuṣṭayaḥ /
prītī ratirhnīḥ śrīścāpi svadhā svāhā daśamyatha //
meaning:
षोडशारे स्मृते चव मानदातुष्टिपुष्टयः /
प्रीती रतिर्ह्नीः श्रीश्चापि स्वधा स्वाहा दशम्यथ //
text_mt: In the sixteen spokes are traditionally taught: Mānadā, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, / Prīti, Rati, Hrī, Śrī, Svadhā, Svāhā, and as the tenth,

sanskrit_iast:
jyotsnā haimavatī chāyā pūrṇimā saṃhatistathā /
amāvāsyeti saṃpūjyā mantreśe prāṇapūrvikā //
meaning:
ज्योत्स्ना हैमवती छाया पूर्णिमा संहतिस्तथा /
अमावास्येति संपूज्या मन्त्रेशे प्राणपूर्विका //
text_mt: Jyotsnā, Haimavatī, Chāyā, Pūrṇimā, Saṃhati, / And Amāvāsyā; these should be worshipped in the master of mantras preceded by Prāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
bhūpure lokapālāḥ syustadastrāṇi tadagrataḥ /
itthaṃ japādibhiḥ siddhe mantre 'smindhanasaṃcayaiḥ //
meaning:
भूपुरे लोकपालाः स्युस्तदस्त्राणि तदग्रतः /
इत्थं जपादिभिः सिद्धे मन्त्रे ऽस्मिन्धनसंचयैः //
text_mt: In the earth-city are the world-guardians, with their weapons before them. / When this mantra is accomplished in this way through recitation and other rites, through heaps of wealth

sanskrit_iast:
kuberasadṛśo mantrī jāyate janavanditaḥ /
atha lakṣmyavatāro 'nyaḥ kīrtyate munisattama //
meaning:
कुबेरसदृशो मन्त्री जायते जनवन्दितः /
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारो ऽन्यः कीर्त्यते मुनिसत्तम //
text_mt: The practitioner of mantras becomes equal to Kubera and praised by people. / Now, another incarnation of Lakṣmī is celebrated, O best of sages:

sanskrit_iast:
praṇavaḥ śāntiraruṇākriyāḍhyācandrabhūṣitāḥ /
bagalāmukhasarvānte indhikāhrādinīyutā //
meaning:
प्रणवः शान्तिररुणाक्रियाढ्याचन्द्रभूषिताः /
बगलामुखसर्वान्ते इन्धिकाह्रादिनीयुता //
text_mt: The praṇava, Śānti, Aruṇā combined with Kriyā, adorned with the moon; / At the end of the whole phrase 'bagalāmukha,' endowed with Indhikā and Hrādinī;

sanskrit_iast:
pītājarāyukpratiṣṭhā punardīrdhodasaṃyutā /
vācaṃ mukhaṃ padaṃ staṃbhayānte jihvāpadaṃ vadet //
meaning:
पीताजरायुक्प्रतिष्ठा पुनर्दीर्धोदसंयुता /
वाचं मुखं पदं स्तंभयान्ते जिह्वापदं वदेत् //
text_mt: Endowed with Pītā and Ajarā, Pratiṣṭhā, again joined with the long water-vowel; / One should say, 'vācaṃ mukhaṃ padaṃ stambhaya,' and at the end of the word 'jihvā,'

sanskrit_iast:
kīlayeti ca buddhiṃ vināśayānte svabījakam /
tāro 'gnisuṃdarī mantro bagalāyāḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
कीलयेति च बुद्धिं विनाशयान्ते स्वबीजकम् /
तारो ऽग्निसुंदरी मन्त्रो बगलायाः प्रकीर्तितः //
text_mt: And 'kīlaya,' and at the end of 'buddhiṃ vināśaya,' its own bīja, / The tāra, and the fire-beauty [svāhā]: this is declared to be the mantra of Bagalā.

sanskrit_iast:
munistu nāradaśchado bṛhatī bagalāmukhī /
devatā netrapañceṣunavapañcadigarṇakaiḥ //
meaning:
मुनिस्तु नारदश्छदो बृहती बगलामुखी /
देवता नेत्रपञ्चेषुनवपञ्चदिगर्णकैः //
text_mt: The sage is Nārada; the metre is Bṛhatī; Bagalāmukhī / Is the deity. With two, five, five, nine, five, and ten syllables,

sanskrit_iast:
aṅgāni kalpayitvā ca dhyāyetpītāmbarāṃ tataḥ /
svarṇāsanasthāṃ hemābhāṃ staṃbhinīminduśekharām //
meaning:
अङ्गानि कल्पयित्वा च ध्यायेत्पीताम्बरां ततः /
स्वर्णासनस्थां हेमाभां स्तंभिनीमिन्दुशेखराम् //
text_mt: Having arranged the limbs, one should then meditate upon her dressed in yellow garments, / Seated on a golden throne, having a golden luster, the paralyzer, wearing the crescent moon on her crest,

sanskrit_iast:
dadhatīṃ mudgaraṃ pāśaṃ vajraṃ ca rasanāṃ karaiḥ /
evaṃ dhyātvājapellakṣamayutaṃ caṃpakodbhavaiḥ //
meaning:
दधतीं मुद्गरं पाशं वज्रं च रसनां करैः /
एवं ध्यात्वाजपेल्लक्षमयुतं चंपकोद्भवैः //
text_mt: Holding a club, a noose, a thunderbolt, and a tongue with her hands. / Having meditated thus, one should recite [the mantra] a hundred thousand times, and make ten thousand oblations

sanskrit_iast:
kusumairjuhuyātpīṭhe bālāyāḥ pūjayedimām /
candanāgurucandrādyaiḥ pūjārthaṃ yantramālikhet //
meaning:
कुसुमैर्जुहुयात्पीठे बालायाः पूजयेदिमाम् /
चन्दनागुरुचन्द्राद्यैः पूजार्थं यन्त्रमालिखेत् //
text_mt: With flowers born of the campaka tree; on the seat of Bālā one should worship her. / For the sake of worship, one should draw a yantra with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, and other substances;

sanskrit_iast:
trikoṇaṣaḍdalāṣṭāsraṣoḍaśāre yajedimām /
maṅgalā staṃbhinī caiva jṛṃbhiṇī mohinī tathā //
meaning:
त्रिकोणषड्दलाष्टास्रषोडशारे यजेदिमाम् /
मङ्गला स्तंभिनी चैव जृंभिणी मोहिनी तथा //
text_mt: In a triangle, six petals, eight corners, and sixteen spokes, one should worship her: / Maṅgalā, Stambhinī, Jṛmbhiṇī, Mohinī,

sanskrit_iast:
vaśyā calā balākā ca bhūdharā kalmaṣābhidhā /
dhātrī ca kalanā kālakarṣiṇī bhrāmikāpi ca //
meaning:
वश्या चला बलाका च भूधरा कल्मषाभिधा /
धात्री च कलना कालकर्षिणी भ्रामिकापि च //
text_mt: Vaśyā, Calā, Balākā, Bhūdharā, Kalmaṣā, / Dhātrī, Kalanā, Kālakarṣiṇī, Bhrāmikā,

sanskrit_iast:
mandagāpi ca bhogasthā bhāvikā ṣoḍaśī smṛtā /
bhūgṛhasya caturdikṣu pūrvādiṣu yajetkramāt //
meaning:
मन्दगापि च भोगस्था भाविका षोडशी स्मृता /
भूगृहस्य चतुर्दिक्षु पूर्वादिषु यजेत्क्रमात् //
text_mt: Mandagā, Bhogasthā, and Bhāvikā is remembered as the sixteenth. / In the four directions of the earth-enclosure, beginning with the east, one should worship in order:

sanskrit_iast:
gaṇeśaṃ baṭukaṃ cāpi yoginīḥ kṣetrapālakam /
indrādīṃśca tato bāhye nijāyudhasamanvitān //
meaning:
गणेशं बटुकं चापि योगिनीः क्षेत्रपालकम् /
इन्द्रादींश्च ततो बाह्ये निजायुधसमन्वितान् //
text_mt: Gaṇeśa, Baṭuka, the Yoginīs, and the field-protector, / And outside them Indra and the others, accompanied by their own weapons.

sanskrit_iast:
itthaṃ siddhe manau mantrī staṃbhayeddevatādikān /
pītavastrapadāsīnaḥ pītamālyānulepanaḥ //
meaning:
इत्थं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री स्तंभयेद्देवतादिकान् /
पीतवस्त्रपदासीनः पीतमाल्यानुलेपनः //
text_mt: When the mantra is thus accomplished, the practitioner can paralyze deities and others. / Seated on a yellow cloth, wearing yellow garlands and unguents,

sanskrit_iast:
pītapuṣpairyajeddevīṃ haridrotthasrajā japet /
pītāṃ dhyāyanbhagavatīṃ payomadhye 'yutaṃ japet //
meaning:
पीतपुष्पैर्यजेद्देवीं हरिद्रोत्थस्रजा जपेत् /
पीतां ध्यायन्भगवतीं पयोमध्ये ऽयुतं जपेत् //
text_mt: One should worship the goddess with yellow flowers and recite with a rosary made of turmeric. / Meditating on the yellow Goddess, one should recite ten thousand times while in water.

sanskrit_iast:
trimadhvā jyatilairhemo nṝṇāṃ vaśyakaro mataḥ /
madhuratritayāktaiḥ syādākarṣo lavarṇairdhruvam //
meaning:
त्रिमध्वा ज्यतिलैर्हेमो नॄणां वश्यकरो मतः /
मधुरत्रितयाक्तैः स्यादाकर्षो लवर्णैर्ध्रुवम् //
text_mt: Fire oblation with the three sweets, ghee, and sesame seeds is held to subjugate men. / Attraction [of others] will certainly occur with salt smeared with the three sweets.

sanskrit_iast:
tailābhyaktairnimbapatrairhemo vidveṣakārakaḥ /
tālaloṇaharidrābhirdviṣāṃ saṃstaṃbhanaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
तैलाभ्यक्तैर्निम्बपत्रैर्हेमो विद्वेषकारकः /
ताललोणहरिद्राभिर्द्विषां संस्तंभनं भवेत् //
text_mt: Fire oblation with neem leaves smeared with oil causes hatred [between enemies]. / Total paralysis of enemies is effected with yellow orpiment, salt, and turmeric.

sanskrit_iast:
āgāradhūmaṃ rājīśca māhiṣaṃ guggulaṃ niśi /
śmaśāne pāvake hutvā nāśayedacirādarīn //
meaning:
आगारधूमं राजीश्च माहिषं गुग्गुलं निशि /
श्मशाने पावके हुत्वा नाशयेदचिरादरीन् //
text_mt: Having offered into fire soot from the house, black mustard, buffalo ghee, and bdellium at night / In a cremation-ground fire, one quickly destroys enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
garuto gṛdhrakākānāṃ kaṭutailaṃ vibhītakam /
gṛhadhūmaṃ citāvahnau hutvā proccāṭayedripūn //
meaning:
गरुतो गृध्रकाकानां कटुतैलं विभीतकम् /
गृहधूमं चितावह्नौ हुत्वा प्रोच्चाटयेद्रिपून् //
text_mt: Having offered vulture and crow feathers, mustard oil, bibhītaka [seeds], / And house-soot into the funeral-pyre fire, one drives away enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
dūvārguḍūcīlājānyo madhuratritayānvitān /
juhoti so 'khilān rogān śamayeddarśanādapi //
meaning:
दूवार्गुडूचीलाजान्यो मधुरत्रितयान्वितान् /
जुहोति सो ऽखिलान् रोगान् शमयेद्दर्शनादपि //
text_mt: One who makes fire oblation of dūrvā grass, guḍūcī, and puffed rice combined with the three sweets / Calms all diseases, even by his mere sight.

sanskrit_iast:
parvatāgre mahāraṇye nadīsaṃge śivālaye /
brahmacaryarato lakṣaṃ japedakhilasiddhaye //
meaning:
पर्वताग्रे महारण्ये नदीसंगे शिवालये /
ब्रह्मचर्यरतो लक्षं जपेदखिलसिद्धये //
text_mt: On a mountain peak, in a great forest, at a river confluence, or in a temple of Śiva, / Devoted to celibacy, one should recite a hundred thousand times for all accomplishments.

sanskrit_iast:
eka varṇagavīdugdhaṃ śarkarāmadhusaṃyutam /
triśataṃ mantritaṃ pītaṃ hanyādviṣaparābhavam //
meaning:
एक वर्णगवीदुग्धं शर्करामधुसंयुतम् /
त्रिशतं मन्त्रितं पीतं हन्याद्विषपराभवम् //
text_mt: The milk of a cow of single color combined with sugar and honey, / Consecrated three hundred times with the mantra and drunk, destroys the defeat caused by poison.

sanskrit_iast:
śvetapālaśakāṣṭhena racite ramyapādake /
alaktarañjite lakṣaṃ mantrayenmanunāmunā //
meaning:
श्वेतपालशकाष्ठेन रचिते रम्यपादके /
अलक्तरञ्जिते लक्षं मन्त्रयेन्मनुनामुना //
text_mt: On charming wooden sandals crafted from the wood of the white palāśa / And colored with red lac, one should recite this mantra a hundred thousand times.

sanskrit_iast:
tadārūḍhaḥ pumān gacchatkṣaṇena śatayojanam /
pāradaṃ ca śilāṃ tālaṃ piṣṭaṃ madhusamanvitam //
meaning:
तदारूढः पुमान् गच्छत्क्षणेन शतयोजनम् /
पारदं च शिलां तालं पिष्टं मधुसमन्वितम् //
text_mt: A man mounted upon them traverses a hundred yojanas in an instant. / Mercury, realgar, and yellow orpiment ground together with honey,

sanskrit_iast:
manunā mantrayellakṣaṃ liṃpettenākhilāṃ tanum /
adṛśyaḥ syānnṛṇāmeṣa āścaryyaṃ dṛśyatāmidam //
meaning:
मनुना मन्त्रयेल्लक्षं लिंपेत्तेनाखिलां तनुम् /
अदृश्यः स्यान्नृणामेष आश्चर्य्यं दृश्यतामिदम् //
text_mt: One should consecrate with the mantra a hundred thousand times, and smear it over one's entire body; / He becomes invisible to men; behold this wonder!

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭkoṇaṃ vilikhadbījaṃ sādhyanāmānvitaṃ manoḥ /
haritālaniśācūrṇairunmatturasasaṃyutaiḥ //
meaning:
षट्कोणं विलिखद्बीजं साध्यनामान्वितं मनोः /
हरितालनिशाचूर्णैरुन्मत्तुरससंयुतैः //
text_mt: Drawing a six-pointed figure, [one should write] the bīja along with the name of the one to be subdued in the mantra / With the powder of yellow orpiment and turmeric mixed with the juice of the thorn apple,

sanskrit_iast:
śeṣākṣaraiḥ samānītaṃ dharāgehavirājitam /
tadyantraṃ sthāpitaprāṇaṃ pītasūtreṇa veṣṭayet //
meaning:
शेषाक्षरैः समानीतं धरागेहविराजितम् /
तद्यन्त्रं स्थापितप्राणं पीतसूत्रेण वेष्टयेत् //
text_mt: Supplied with the remaining syllables, adorned with an earth-house. / Having established the life-breath in that yantra, one should bind it with yellow thread.

sanskrit_iast:
bhrāmyatkulālacakrasthāṃ gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ tathā /
racayedṛṣabhaṃ ramyaṃ yantraṃ tanmadhyataḥ kṣipet //
meaning:
भ्राम्यत्कुलालचक्रस्थां गृहीत्वा मृत्तिकां तथा /
रचयेदृषभं रम्यं यन्त्रं तन्मध्यतः क्षिपेत् //
text_mt: Taking clay situated upon a rotating potter's wheel, / One should fashion a beautiful bull and cast the yantra into its center.

sanskrit_iast:
haritālena saṃlipya vṛṣaṃ pratyahamarcayet /
staṃbhayedvidviṣāṃ vācaṃ gatiṃ kāryaparaṃparām //
meaning:
हरितालेन संलिप्य वृषं प्रत्यहमर्चयेत् /
स्तंभयेद्विद्विषां वाचं गतिं कार्यपरंपराम् //
text_mt: Having smeared the bull with yellow orpiment, one should worship it every day; / One paralyzes the speech, movement, and continuous actions of enemies.

sanskrit_iast:
ādāya vāmahastena pretabhūsthitakarparam /
aṅgāreṇa citāsthena tatra yantraṃ samālikhet //
meaning:
आदाय वामहस्तेन प्रेतभूस्थितकर्परम् /
अङ्गारेण चितास्थेन तत्र यन्त्रं समालिखेत् //
text_mt: Taking with the left hand a skull situated in a cremation ground, / With charcoal from a funeral pyre one should write the yantra there.

sanskrit_iast:
mantritaṃ nihitaṃ bhūmau ripūṇāṃ staṃbhayedgatim /
pretavastre likhedyantraṃ aṅgāreṇaiva tatpunaḥ //
meaning:
मन्त्रितं निहितं भूमौ रिपूणां स्तंभयेद्गतिम् /
प्रेतवस्त्रे लिखेद्यन्त्रं अङ्गारेणैव तत्पुनः //
text_mt: Consecrated with the mantra and buried in the earth, it paralyzes the movement of enemies. / Again, one should write the yantra on a shroud with charcoal,

sanskrit_iast:
maṇḍūkavadane nyasyetpītasūtreṇa veṣṭitam /
pūjitaṃ pītapuṣpaistadvācaṃ saṃstaṃbhayeddviṣām //
meaning:
मण्डूकवदने न्यस्येत्पीतसूत्रेण वेष्टितम् /
पूजितं पीतपुष्पैस्तद्वाचं संस्तंभयेद्द्विषाम् //
text_mt: Place it inside the mouth of a frog, bound with yellow thread; / Worshipped with yellow flowers, it completely paralyzes the speech of adversaries.

sanskrit_iast:
yadbhūmau bhavitā divyaṃ tatra yantraṃ samālikhet /
mārjitaṃ taddviṣāṃ pātrairdivyastambhanakṛdbhavet //
meaning:
यद्भूमौ भविता दिव्यं तत्र यन्त्रं समालिखेत् /
मार्जितं तद्द्विषां पात्रैर्दिव्यस्तम्भनकृद्भवेत् //
text_mt: Where an ordeal will take place on earth, there one should write the yantra; / Cleaned with vessels of the enemies, it paralyzes the ordeal.

sanskrit_iast:
indravāruṇikāmūlaṃ saptaśo manumantritam /
kṣiptaṃ jale divyakṛtaṃ jalastaṃbhanakārakam //
meaning:
इन्द्रवारुणिकामूलं सप्तशो मनुमन्त्रितम् /
क्षिप्तं जले दिव्यकृतं जलस्तंभनकारकम् //
text_mt: The root of indravāruṇī consecrated seven times with the mantra / And thrown into the water of an ordeal causes the paralysis of water.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ bahūktyā sādhakena mantraḥ samyagupāsitaḥ /
śatrūṇāṃ gatibuddhyādeḥ staṃbhano nātra saṃśayaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde yakṣiṇīmantrasādhananirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaḍaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
meaning:
किं बहूक्त्या साधकेन मन्त्रः सम्यगुपासितः /
शत्रूणां गतिबुद्ध्यादेः स्तंभनो नात्र संशयः //
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे यक्षिणीमन्त्रसाधननिरूपणं नाम षडशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
text_mt:
What need of many words? When the mantra is properly worshipped by the practitioner, / It paralyzes the movement, intellect, and other faculties of enemies; there is no doubt about this.

Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, named 'Expounding the Accomplishment of the Yakṣiṇī Mantra,' in the third quarter of the great narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
sanatkumāra uvāca
avatāratrayaṃ lakṣmyāḥ kathita te dvijottama /
durgāyāścābhidhāsyāmi sarvalokopakārakān //
meaning:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अवतारत्रयं लक्ष्म्याः कथित ते द्विजोत्तम /
दुर्गायाश्चाभिधास्यामि सर्वलोकोपकारकान् //
text_mt: Sanatkumāra said: / Three incarnations of Lakṣmī have been spoken to you, O best of the twice-born; / And I shall declare those of Durgā that are beneficent to all the worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
praṇavaḥ śrīḥ śivāyugmaṃ vāṇīvairocanīpadam /
vajrādyaṃ kṣudhitā sūkṣmā mṛtā svāgnīndusaṃyutā //
meaning:
प्रणवः श्रीः शिवायुग्मं वाणीवैरोचनीपदम् /
वज्राद्यं क्षुधिता सूक्ष्मा मृता स्वाग्नीन्दुसंयुता //
text_mt: The praṇava, Śrī, a pair of Śivās, the word Vāṇīvairocanī, / [the word] beginning with Vajra, Kṣudhitā, Sūkṣmā, Mṛtā, conjoined with their fire and moon,

sanskrit_iast:
pratiṣṭhāpya śivā phaṭ ca svāhānto 'tyaṣṭivarṇavān /
bhairavo 'sya muniḥ samrāṭ chando mantrasya devatā //
meaning:
प्रतिष्ठाप्य शिवा फट् च स्वाहान्तो ऽत्यष्टिवर्णवान् /
भैरवो ऽस्य मुनिः सम्राट् छन्दो मन्त्रस्य देवता //
text_mt: Having placed [the word] Śivā, and phaṭ, ending with svāhā, [this mantra] has twenty-eight syllables. / Bhairava is its seer; the meter is Samrāṭ; the deity of the mantra is [Chinnamastā];

sanskrit_iast:
chinnamastā ramā bījaṃ svāhā śaktirudīritā /
āṃ khaḍgāya hṛdākhyātamīṃ khaḍgāya śiraḥ smṛtam //
meaning:
छिन्नमस्ता रमा बीजं स्वाहा शक्तिरुदीरिता /
आं खड्गाय हृदाख्यातमीं खड्गाय शिरः स्मृतम् //
